REGISTER: cycle
NUMBER: 0xc00
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: Implicit reads of the cycle CSR are ordered as device input.
RULE 2: A read of the cycle CSR is classified as device input for the purposes of the FENCE instruction.
RULE 3: A write to the cycle CSR is classified as device output for the purposes of the FENCE instruction.
RULE 4: Accesses to the cycle CSR are weakly ordered by default under the RVWMO memory consistency model.
RULE 5: For base ISAs with XLEN ≥ 64, the RDCYCLE pseudoinstruction reads the full 64-bit value of the cycle CSR.
RULE 6: The cycle counter can be read using the canonical csrrs rd, cycle, x0 instruction as well as the read-only CSRRC, CSRRSI, and CSRRCI forms.
RULE 7: The RDCYCLE pseudoinstruction reads the low XLEN bits of the cycle CSR.
RULE 8: If the entire core is paused (clock-gated or powered-down), the cycle count should not increase.
RULE 9: On some simple platforms, the cycle counter might serve as the real-time clock, causing RDTIME and RDCYCLE to return identical values.
RULE 10: The presented code sequence ensures that a consistent 64-bit cycle counter value is read even if the lower half overflows between the reads.
RULE 11: The cycle CSR is located at address 0xC00 and is designated as unprivileged read-only (URO).
RULE 12: The cycleh CSR is located at address 0xC80 and is designated as unprivileged read-only (URO).
RULE 13: The cycle CSR provides a cycle counter that is accessed by the RDCYCLE instruction.
RULE 14: When the RDCYCLE instruction reads CSR 0xC00, the value returned equals the current cycle counter.
RULE 15: The mcycle register is located at address 0xB00 and provides the Machine cycle counter.
RULE 16: The mcyclecfg register is located at address 0x321 and provides the Machine cycle counter configuration register.
RULE 17: In S-mode, when the indirect CSR mapping entry has siselect equal to 0x40, the first mapped register (sireg) is the cycle register.
RULE 18: In S-mode, when the indirect CSR mapping entry has siselect equal to 0x40, the second mapped register (sireg2) is the cyclecfg register.
RULE 19: In S-mode, when the indirect CSR mapping entry has siselect equal to 0x40, the third mapped register (sireg3) selects none and therefore does not select a cycle-related register.
RULE 20: In S-mode, when the indirect CSR mapping entry has siselect equal to 0x40, the fourth mapped register (sireg4) is the cycleh register.
RULE 21: In S-mode, when the indirect CSR mapping entry has siselect equal to 0x40, the fifth mapped register (sireg5) is the cyclecfgh register.
RULE 22: In S-mode, when the indirect CSR mapping entry has siselect equal to 0x40, the sixth mapped register (sireg6) selects none and therefore does not select a cycle-related register.
RULE 23: The mcycle CSR counts the number of clock cycles executed by the processor core on which the hart is running.
RULE 24: After a hart reset, the mcycle register contains an arbitrary value.
RULE 25: A write to the mcycle CSR stores the specified value into the register.
RULE 26: A write to the mcycle CSR takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 27: If the mcycle CSR is shared between harts on the same core, writes to the mcycle CSR are visible to all those harts.
RULE 28: The cycle counter continues to increment regardless of any reads or writes to the mcounteren register.
RULE 29: When the CY bit in mcounteren is clear, attempts to read the cycle CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 30: When the CY bit in mcounteren is set, access to the cycle CSR is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 31: The cycle CSR is a read-only shadow of the mcycle register.
RULE 32: In harts that support U-mode, the CY field of the mcounteren register, which controls access to the cycle CSR, must be implemented, is WARL, and may be read-only zero.
RULE 33: In harts that support U-mode, when the CY field of mcounteren is read-only zero, reads of the cycle CSR from a less-privileged mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 34: When the CY bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mcycle CSR increments on each cycle.
RULE 35: When the CY bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mcycle CSR does not increment on any cycle.
RULE 36: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as if the CY bit were clear, causing the mcycle CSR to increment on each cycle.
RULE 37: When the mcycle CSR is shared between harts on the same core, the mcountinhibit.CY field is also shared, and writes to mcountinhibit.CY are visible to those harts, thereby controlling whether the shared mcycle CSR increments on each cycle.
RULE 38: By default the cycle counter is not filtered by privilege mode.
RULE 39: The privilege-mode filtering applied to the cycle counter is the same as that applied to the instret counter.
RULE 40: Bit 62 of mcyclecfg, named MINH, when set inhibits counting of cycle events while the processor is executing in machine mode.
RULE 41: Bit 61 of mcyclecfg, named SINH, when set inhibits counting of cycle events while the processor is executing in supervisor or hypervisor mode.
RULE 42: Bit 60 of mcyclecfg, named UINH, when set inhibits counting of cycle events while the processor is executing in user mode.
RULE 43: Bit 59 of mcyclecfg, named VSINH, when set inhibits counting of cycle events while the processor is executing in virtual-supervisor mode.
RULE 44: Bit 58 of mcyclecfg, named VUINH, when set inhibits counting of cycle events while the processor is executing in virtual-user mode.
RULE 45: If all INH bits (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in mcyclecfg are zero, counting of cycle events is enabled in all privilege modes.
RULE 46: For any INH bit in positions 61 through 58 of mcyclecfg, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, that bit is read-only zero.
RULE 47: The cycle counter will increment for each CPU cycle while the CPU is executing in a non-inhibited privilege mode.
RULE 48: When mcounteren[0] = 1 and menvcfg.CDE = 1, the cycle register may be read or written via the indirect CSRs while siselect = 0x40.
RULE 49: When siselect = 0x40, accesses to sireg select the low 32 bits of the cycle counter (cycle).
RULE 50: When siselect = 0x40, accesses to sireg4 select the high half of the cycle counter (cycleh).
RULE 51: When siselect = 0x40, accesses to sireg2 select the cycle configuration register (cyclecfg).
RULE 52: When siselect = 0x40, accesses to sireg5 select the high half of the cycle configuration register (cyclecfgh).
RULE 53: If menvcfg.CDE = 0, any access to the cycle register via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 54: If XLEN = 64, any access to the cycleh register via sireg4 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 55: If XLEN = 64, any access to the cyclecfgh register via sireg5 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 56: If mcounteren[0] = 0, any access to the cycle register, cycleh, cyclecfg, or cyclecfgh via the indirect CSRs raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 57: If the Smcntrpmf extension is implemented, bit 62 of the cyclecfg register accessed via sireg* is read-only, reads as 0, and writes to that bit have no effect.
RULE 58: If the Smcntrpmf extension is implemented, bit 62 of the cyclecfgh register accessed via sireg* is read-only, reads as 0, and writes to that bit have no effect.
RULE 59: If any required extension for the cycle register state is not implemented, attempts from M-mode or S-mode to access the cycle register via the indirect CSRs raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 60: If any required extension for the cycleh register state is not implemented, attempts from M-mode or S-mode to access the cycleh register via the indirect CSRs raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 61: In VU-mode, any access to the cycle register via sireg* raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 62: When vsiselect = 0x40, any access to the cycle register via vsireg* from M-mode or S-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 63: In VS-mode, an access to the cycle register via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception when menvcfg.CDE = 0.
RULE 64: In VS-mode, an access to the cycle register via sireg* raises a virtual-instruction exception when menvcfg.CDE = 1.
RULE 65: The SCTRCLR instruction must set the cycle counter field of the CTR register to zero and must also set the CCV field to zero.
RULE 66: Any read of the cycle-related registers ctrsource, ctrtarget, or ctrdata that occurs after execution of SCTRCLR and before the next qualified control transfer must return zero.
RULE 67: The first recorded control transfer after execution of SCTRCLR must have its CCV field in the cycle data (ctrdata.CCV) equal to zero.
RULE 68: The elapsed cycle counter (CtrCycleCounter) increments at the same rate as the mcycle counter.
RULE 69: Only cycles while CTR is active are counted, where active implies that the current privilege mode is enabled for recording and CTR is not frozen.
RULE 70: The cycle count exponent CCE holds 0 if the CtrCycleCounter value is less than 4096; otherwise CCE holds the index of the most significant one bit in the CtrCycleCounter value minus 11.
RULE 71: The cycle count mantissa CCM holds the CtrCycleCounter bits CCE+10 down to CCE-1.
RULE 72: The CtrCycleCounter is reset on writes to x ctrctl and on execution of SCTRCLR to ensure that any accumulated cycle counts do not persist across a context switch.
RULE 73: Unimplemented CCE bits, which are part of the cycle count exponent, are read-only 0.
RULE 74: When CCE>1, the granularity of the reported cycle count is reduced.
RULE 75: When CCE=3, the bottom 2 bits of the cycle counter are not reported, and thus the reported value increments only every 4 cycles.
RULE 76: The cycle count (CC) value saturates when all implemented bits in CCM and CCE are 1.
RULE 77: The next record will have CCV=0 after a write to x ctrctl or execution of SCTRCLR, since the cycle counter is reset.
RULE 78: The implementation should provide a mechanism to modify counter values, and this mechanism must also apply to the cycle counter.
RULE 79: If the CY bit in scounteren is clear, a read of the cycle register while executing in U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 80: If the CY bit in scounteren is set, access to the cycle register from U-mode is permitted.
RULE 81: If the CY bit in scounteren is read-only zero, a U-mode read of the cycle register causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 82: The writability of the CY bit in scounteren is not affected by the setting of the CY bit in mcounteren.
RULE 83: A U-mode read of the cycle register causes an illegal-instruction exception unless both the CY bit in scounteren and the CY bit in mcounteren are set.
RULE 84: If both the CY bit in scounteren and the CY bit in mcounteren are set, a U-mode read of the cycle register is permitted.
RULE 85: When the CY bit in the hcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the cycle register while V=1 will cause a virtual-instruction exception if the CY bit in mcounteren is 1.
RULE 86: When the CY bit in the hcounteren register is set, access to the cycle register is permitted while V=1 unless prevented for some other reason.
RULE 87: In VU-mode, the cycle register is readable only if the CY bit is set in both hcounteren and scounteren.
RULE 88: The CY bit in hcounteren may be implemented as read-only zero, which causes reads of the cycle register to cause an exception when V=1.
RULE 89: When the 64-bit cycle counter wraps, the mcause or scause register is set to exception code 13 (counter-overflow interrupt).
RULE 90: When V=1 and an attempt to access a cycle counter CSR is HS-qualified but is prevented by insufficient privilege or by a supervisor or hypervisor CSR such as scounteren or hcounteren, a virtual-instruction exception with code 22 is taken.
RULE 91: When XLEN>32, any attempt to access a high-half cycle CSR (e.g., cycleh) raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 92: In VS-mode, accessing a non-high-half cycle CSR (cycle) while the corresponding hcounteren bit is 0 and the corresponding mcounteren bit is 1 raises a virtual-instruction exception with code 22.
RULE 93: In VU-mode, accessing a non-high-half cycle CSR (cycle) while the corresponding bit in either hcounteren or scounteren is 0 and the corresponding mcounteren bit is 1 raises a virtual-instruction exception with code 22.
RULE 94: When a virtual-instruction exception is taken due to any of the above cycle-counter conditions, the mtval or stval register is written in the same manner as for an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 95: In M-mode, accessing cycle register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc00; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 96: In S-mode, accessing cycle register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc00; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 97: In U-mode, accessing cycle register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc00; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 98: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the cycle register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc00, a0; csrr a1, 0xc00; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: fcsr
NUMBER: 0x003
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 32
FIELDS: 7..5=FRM, 4..4=NV, 3..3=DZ, 2..2=OF, 1..1=UF, 0..0=NX
EXTENSIONS: D, F, Q, Zdinx, Zfinx, Zhinx
RULE 1: The fcsr register is not visible to other harts.
RULE 2: Bits 4, 3, 2, 1, and 0 of the fcsr register are aliases of the corresponding bits in the fflags CSR and are tracked as independent units.
RULE 3: The whole fcsr register is an alias of the frm CSR and is tracked as a single independent unit.
RULE 4: Bits 7, 6, and 5 of the fcsr register are aliases of the frm CSR and are tracked as independent units.
RULE 5: Bits 31-8 of fcsr are reserved for other standard extensions, and if those extensions are not present implementations shall ignore writes to these bits and shall return zero for these bits when fcsr is read.
RULE 6: The FSCSR instruction swaps the value in fcsr by copying the original fcsr value into integer register rd and then writing a new value taken from integer register rs1 into fcsr.
RULE 7: The FRRM instruction reads the rounding-mode field frm (bits 7-5 of fcsr) and copies it into the least-significant three bits of integer register rd, setting all other bits of rd to zero.
RULE 8: The FSRM instruction swaps the rounding-mode field frm by copying the original bits 7-5 of fcsr into integer register rd and then writing the three least-significant bits of integer register rs1 into bits 7-5 of fcsr.
RULE 9: The FRFLAGS instruction reads the accrued-exception-flags field fflags (bits 4-0 of fcsr) and copies it into integer register rd, zero-extending the value to the full width of rd.
RULE 10: The FSFLAGS instruction swaps the accrued-exception-flags field by copying the original bits 4-0 of fcsr into integer register rd and then writing the five least-significant bits of integer register rs1 into bits 4-0 of fcsr.
RULE 11: Floating-point operations use either a static rounding mode encoded in the instruction or the dynamic rounding mode held in frm, and an instruction encoding of rm=111 selects the dynamic rounding mode held in frm.
RULE 12: The behavior of floating-point instructions that depend on rounding mode is reserved when executed with a reserved static rounding mode (encodings 101-110) or a reserved dynamic rounding mode (encodings 101-111).
RULE 13: Implementations may raise an illegal-instruction exception when a floating-point instruction is executed with a reserved dynamic rounding mode, and such behavior remains valid under the weakened specification.
RULE 14: The accrued exception flags in fcsr indicate which exception conditions have arisen on any floating-point arithmetic instruction since the flags were last reset by software.
RULE 15: The base RISC-V ISA does not provide a mechanism to generate a trap on the setting of any floating-point exception flag in fcsr.
RULE 16: Bits 7-5 of fcsr encode the rounding mode with the following meanings: 000 = round to nearest, ties to even (RNE); 001 = round towards zero (RTZ); 010 = round down towards –∞ (RDN); 011 = round up towards +∞ (RUP); 100 = round to nearest, ties to max magnitude (RMM); 101 and 110 are reserved for future use; 111 is reserved in the register and is used in an instruction's rm field to select the dynamic rounding mode.
RULE 17: Bits 4-0 of fcsr encode the accrued exception flags with the following bit assignments: bit 4 = Invalid Operation (NV); bit 3 = Divide by Zero (DZ); bit 2 = Overflow (OF); bit 1 = Underflow (UF); bit 0 = Inexact (NX).
RULE 18: When the Zfinx extension is implemented, the mstatus.FS field is hard-wired to 0, and this hard-wiring removes any effect of the FS field on the trapping behavior of fcsr accesses.
RULE 19: When the mstatus.FS field is hard-wired to 0, the FS field no longer affects the trapping behavior of floating-point instructions or fcsr accesses.
RULE 20: The fcsr has URW privilege, meaning it is readable and writable in unprivileged mode.
RULE 21: The fflags component of the fcsr is URW (unprivileged read/write).
RULE 22: The frm component of the fcsr is URW (unprivileged read/write).
RULE 23: When an instruction explicitly or implicitly writes the fcsr without altering its contents while FS is Initial or Clean, it is implementation-defined whether FS transitions to Dirty.
RULE 24: Changing the FS field has no effect on the contents of the fcsr.
RULE 25: Setting FS=Off does not destroy the contents of the fcsr.
RULE 26: Setting FS=Initial does not clear the contents of the fcsr.
RULE 27: The FCSR bit of a state-enable CSR determines whether accesses to the fcsr register are permitted when floating-point instructions operate on integer (x) registers under the Zfinx, Zdinx, and related extensions.
RULE 28: When misa.F=1, the FCSR bit of mstateen0, hstateen0, and sstateen0 is read-only zero, pertaining to the fcsr register.
RULE 29: When state-enable CSRs are implemented, misa.F=0, and the FCSR bit of a controlling stateen0 CSR is zero, every floating-point instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception or, if applicable, a virtual-instruction exception as if it accessed the fcsr register, regardless of the actual access.
RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing fcsr register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 31: In S-mode, accessing fcsr register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 32: In U-mode, accessing fcsr register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 33: In M-mode, setting fcsr.FRM (bit 5) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x20) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x20; csrs 0x003, a0; csrr a1, 0x003; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x20].
RULE 34: In M-mode, setting fcsr.NV (bit 4) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x10) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x10; csrs 0x003, a0; csrr a1, 0x003; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x10].
RULE 35: In M-mode, setting fcsr.DZ (bit 3) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8; csrs 0x003, a0; csrr a1, 0x003; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8].
RULE 36: In M-mode, setting fcsr.OF (bit 2) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x4) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4; csrs 0x003, a0; csrr a1, 0x003; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x4].
RULE 37: In M-mode, setting fcsr.UF (bit 1) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2; csrs 0x003, a0; csrr a1, 0x003; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2].
RULE 38: In M-mode, setting fcsr.NX (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x003, a0; csrr a1, 0x003; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 39: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the fcsr register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x003, a0; csrr a1, 0x003; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 40: In M-mode, accessing fcsr register while D extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: D; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 41: In M-mode, accessing fcsr register while F extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: F; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 42: In M-mode, accessing fcsr register while Q extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Q; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 43: In M-mode, accessing fcsr register while Zdinx extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zdinx; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 44: In M-mode, accessing fcsr register while Zfinx extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zfinx; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 45: In M-mode, accessing fcsr register while Zhinx extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zhinx; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: fflags
NUMBER: 0x001
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 32
FIELDS: 4..4=NV, 3..3=DZ, 2..2=OF, 1..1=UF, 0..0=NX
EXTENSIONS: D, F, Q, V
RULE 1: An access to the fcsr CSR also affects the fflags CSR.
RULE 2: The Accrued Exception Flags field named fflags occupies bits 4-0 of the floating-point control and status register (fcsr).
RULE 3: The FRFLAGS instruction reads the current value of fflags and copies it into integer register rd, placing the flag bits in rd bits 4-0 and clearing all other bits of rd to zero.
RULE 4: The FSFLAGS instruction returns the original value of fflags in integer register rd.
RULE 5: The FSFLAGS instruction writes a new value to fflags using the three least-significant bits of integer register rs1 as the source value.
RULE 6: The FSFLAGS instruction updates fflags with the low five bits of rs1, replacing the previous flag contents.
RULE 7: Whenever a floating-point arithmetic instruction encounters an exception condition, the corresponding bit(s) in fflags become set.
RULE 8: Once set, the bits in fflags remain set until software resets the field.
RULE 9: Each of the five bits in fflags (bits 4-0) corresponds to one of the exception mnemonics NV, DZ, OF, UF, and NX, representing Invalid Operation, Divide by Zero, Overflow, Underflow, and Inexact respectively.
RULE 10: Setting a flag bit in fflags never generates a trap in the base RISC-V ISA.
RULE 11: A vector floating-point exception occurring at any active floating-point element sets the standard FP exception flags in the fflags register.
RULE 12: An inactive floating-point element does not set the FP exception flags in the fflags register.
RULE 13: The fflags CSR is accessible with unprivileged read/write (URW) privilege.
RULE 14: The fcsr CSR, which incorporates the fflags field, is accessible with unprivileged read/write (URW) privilege.
RULE 15: Changing the setting of the FS field has no effect on the contents of the fflags CSR.
RULE 16: Setting FS=Off does not destroy the contents of the fflags CSR.
RULE 17: Setting FS=Initial does not clear the contents of the fflags CSR.
RULE 18: In M-mode, accessing fflags register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x001; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 19: In S-mode, accessing fflags register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x001; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 20: In U-mode, accessing fflags register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x001; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 21: In M-mode, setting fflags.NV (bit 4) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x10) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x10; csrs 0x001, a0; csrr a1, 0x001; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x10].
RULE 22: In M-mode, setting fflags.DZ (bit 3) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8; csrs 0x001, a0; csrr a1, 0x001; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8].
RULE 23: In M-mode, setting fflags.OF (bit 2) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x4) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4; csrs 0x001, a0; csrr a1, 0x001; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x4].
RULE 24: In M-mode, setting fflags.UF (bit 1) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2; csrs 0x001, a0; csrr a1, 0x001; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2].
RULE 25: In M-mode, setting fflags.NX (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x001, a0; csrr a1, 0x001; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 26: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the fflags register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x001, a0; csrr a1, 0x001; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 27: In M-mode, accessing fflags register while D extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: D; csrr a0, 0x001; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing fflags register while F extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: F; csrr a0, 0x001; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 29: In M-mode, accessing fflags register while Q extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Q; csrr a0, 0x001; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing fflags register while V extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: V; csrr a0, 0x001; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: frm
NUMBER: 0x002
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 32
FIELDS: 2..0=ROUNDINGMODE
EXTENSIONS: F, V, Zvfbfmin, Zvfbfwma
RULE 1: The frm register is listed as an alias of the fcsr CSR.
RULE 2: The fcsr CSR lists frm as one of its aliases.
RULE 3: Bits 7-5 of the fcsr CSR are an alias of the frm register.
RULE 4: Modifying bits 7-5 of the fcsr CSR changes the value of the frm register.
RULE 5: The FRRM instruction reads the frm field and copies its value into the least-significant three bits of integer register rd while zeroing all other bits of rd.
RULE 6: The FSRM instruction first copies the original frm value into integer register rd and then writes a new value taken from the three least-significant bits of integer register rs1 into the frm field.
RULE 7: When the rm field of a floating-point instruction is binary 111, the instruction selects the dynamic rounding mode held in frm.
RULE 8: When frm holds the binary value 000, it specifies the rounding mode RNE – Round to Nearest, ties to Even.
RULE 9: When frm holds the binary value 001, it specifies the rounding mode RTZ – Round towards Zero.
RULE 10: When frm holds the binary value 010, it specifies the rounding mode RDN – Round Down (towards –∞).
RULE 11: When frm holds the binary value 011, it specifies the rounding mode RUP – Round Up (towards +∞).
RULE 12: When frm holds the binary value 100, it specifies the rounding mode RMM – Round to Nearest, ties to Max Magnitude.
RULE 13: When frm holds the binary value 101, it is a reserved value for future use.
RULE 14: When frm holds the binary value 110, it is a reserved value for future use.
RULE 15: When frm holds the binary value 111, it is a reserved value and is used for dynamic rounding-mode selection in the rm field.
RULE 16: The binary values 101, 110, and 111 of frm are reserved rounding modes.
RULE 17: If a floating-point instruction that depends on rounding mode is executed with a reserved rounding mode, including any of the reserved frm values, the behavior of the instruction is reserved.
RULE 18: When the rm field of a scalar floating-point instruction is encoded as DYN (binary 111), the instruction uses the rounding mode specified in the frm CSR.
RULE 19: The sum is rounded according to the frm register.
RULE 20: All vector floating-point operations use the dynamic rounding mode specified in the frm register.
RULE 21: If the frm field contains an invalid rounding mode, any vector floating-point instruction, including those that do not depend on the rounding mode, causes the operation to be reserved.
RULE 22: If the vector length register (vl) equals zero, any use of the frm field by a vector floating-point instruction is reserved.
RULE 23: If the vector start register (vstart) is greater than or equal to vl, any use of the frm field by a vector floating-point instruction is reserved.
RULE 24: The vector floating-point/integer conversion instructions vfcvt.xu.f.v, vfcvt.x.f.v, vfcvt.rtz.xu.f.v, vfcvt.rtz.x.f.v, vfcvt.f.xu.v, and vfcvt.f.x.v use the dynamic rounding mode specified in the frm register.
RULE 25: The rtz variants vfcvt.rtz.xu.f.v and vfcvt.rtz.x.f.v do not use the rounding mode in the frm register and instead round towards zero.
RULE 26: The frm register has privilege level URW (User-Read/Write).
RULE 27: In M-mode, accessing frm register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x002; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 28: In S-mode, accessing frm register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x002; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 29: In U-mode, accessing frm register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x002; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 30: In M-mode, setting frm.ROUNDINGMODE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x002, a0; csrr a1, 0x002; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 31: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the frm register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x002, a0; csrr a1, 0x002; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing frm register while F extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: F; csrr a0, 0x002; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 33: In M-mode, accessing frm register while V extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: V; csrr a0, 0x002; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 34: In M-mode, accessing frm register while Zvfbfmin extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zvfbfmin; csrr a0, 0x002; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 35: In M-mode, accessing frm register while Zvfbfwma extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zvfbfwma; csrr a0, 0x002; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

RULE 1: The hcounteren CSR is readable and writable in hypervisor privilege mode (HRW).
RULE 2: Access to the vstimecmp register via stimecmp in VS-mode is permitted only if the TM bit in hcounteren does not prevent such access and the register is implemented.
RULE 3: In VS-mode, a scountovf bit X is readable only if the corresponding hcounteren bit X is set.
RULE 4: If the hcounteren bit X is clear in VS-mode, reads of scountovf bit X return zero.
RULE 5: hcounteren is a CSR that is provided to HS-mode.
RULE 6: hcounteren is not provided to VS-mode.
RULE 7: If a CY, TM, IR, or HPM n bit in hcounteren is clear, a read of the corresponding cycle, time, instret, or hpmcounter n register while V=1 causes a virtual-instruction exception provided the same bit in mcounteren is 1.
RULE 8: If a CY, TM, IR, or HPM n bit in hcounteren is set, access to the corresponding register is permitted while V=1 unless some other condition prevents it.
RULE 9: In VU-mode, a counter register is readable only if the applicable bits are set in both hcounteren and scounteren.
RULE 10: If the TM bit in hcounteren is clear, an access to the vstimecmp register (via stimecmp) while executing in VS-mode causes a virtual-instruction exception when the TM bit in mcounteren is set.
RULE 11: If the TM bit in hcounteren and the TM bit in mcounteren are both set, access to the vstimecmp register (if implemented) is permitted in VS-mode.
RULE 12: Any bit in hcounteren may be read-only zero, and reads of the associated counter cause a virtual-instruction exception when V=1.
RULE 13: All bits in hcounteren are WARL fields.
RULE 14: When V=1, if an HS-qualified instruction is prevented from executing because it is expressly disabled by the hypervisor CSR hcounteren, a virtual-instruction exception with cause 22 is raised instead of an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 15: In VS-mode, if a non-high-half counter CSR is accessed and the corresponding bit in hcounteren is 0 while the corresponding bit in mcounteren is 1, a virtual-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 16: In VU-mode, if a non-high-half counter CSR is accessed and the corresponding bit in either hcounteren or scounteren is 0 while the corresponding bit in mcounteren is 1, a virtual-instruction exception is raised.

REGISTER: henvcfg
NUMBER: 0x60a
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=STCE, 62..62=PBMTE, 61..61=ADUE, 7..7=CBZE, 6..6=CBCFE, 5..4=CBIE, 3..3=SSE, 0..0=FIOM
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: If the current privilege mode is VS and henvcfg.CBIE is 00, a virtual-instruction exception is raised for the CBO.INVAL instruction.
RULE 2: If the current privilege mode is VU and either henvcfg.CBIE is 00 or senvcfg.CBIE is 00, a virtual-instruction exception is raised for the CBO.INVAL instruction.
RULE 3: If the current privilege mode is VS and henvcfg.CBIE is 01, the CBO.INVAL instruction is executed and a flush operation is performed.
RULE 4: If the current privilege mode is VU and either henvcfg.CBIE is 01 or senvcfg.CBIE is 01, the CBO.INVAL instruction is executed and a flush operation is performed.
RULE 5: If the current privilege mode is VS and henvcfg.CBCFE is zero, a virtual-instruction exception is raised for the CBO.CLEAN or CBO.FLUSH instruction.
RULE 6: If the current privilege mode is VU and either henvcfg.CBCFE is zero or senvcfg.CBCFE is zero, a virtual-instruction exception is raised for the CBO.CLEAN or CBO.FLUSH instruction.
RULE 7: If neither the VS-mode henvcfg.CBCFE-zero condition nor the VU-mode condition that henvcfg.CBCFE or senvcfg.CBCFE is zero holds, the CBO.CLEAN or CBO.FLUSH instruction is executed.
RULE 8: If the current privilege mode is VS and henvcfg.CBZE is zero, a virtual-instruction exception is raised for the CBO.ZERO instruction.
RULE 9: If the current privilege mode is VU and either henvcfg.CBZE is zero or senvcfg.CBZE is zero, a virtual-instruction exception is raised for the CBO.ZERO instruction.
RULE 10: If none of the virtual-instruction exception conditions involving henvcfg.CBZE are true, the CBO.ZERO instruction is executed.
RULE 11: Writes to henvcfg.CBIE, henvcfg.CBCFE, or henvcfg.CBZE do not affect the corresponding fields of menvcfg or senvcfg, and reads of those fields in other xenvcfg registers are independent of henvcfg.
RULE 12: The henvcfg register is a hypervisor-read/write (HRW) CSR.
RULE 13: The hypervisor CSR henvcfg contains a FIOM bit that is equivalent to the FIOM bit in menvcfg.
RULE 14: henvcfg.PBMTE is read-only zero if the implementation has the hypervisor extension and menvcfg.PBMTE is zero.
RULE 15: henvcfg.ADUE is read-only zero if the implementation has the hypervisor extension and menvcfg.ADUE is zero.
RULE 16: If the Sstc extension is implemented and menvcfg.STCE is zero, an attempt to access stimecmp in any mode other than M-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 17: If the Sstc extension is implemented and menvcfg.STCE is zero, henvcfg.STCE is read-only zero.
RULE 18: If menvcfg.SSE is zero, henvcfg.SSE is read-only zero.
RULE 19: The ENVCFG bit in mstateen0 controls access to the henvcfg, henvcfgh, and senvcfg CSRs.
RULE 20: If the hypervisor extension is implemented, the henvcfg .ADUE field is writable.
RULE 21: The henvcfg CSR includes an STCE bit when the Sstc extension is implemented.
RULE 22: The henvcfg register is provided to HS-mode but not to VS-mode.
RULE 23: Setting henvcfg.PMM enables pointer masking for HLV.* and HSV.* when their explicit memory access is performed as though in VS-mode.
RULE 24: When henvcfg.PMM is not set, pointer masking for HLV.* and HSV.* is disabled when their explicit memory access is performed as though in VS-mode.
RULE 25: When the FIOM bit in henvcfg is 1 and V=1, FENCE instructions executed in V=1 are modified so that ordering device I/O accesses also orders main memory accesses.
RULE 26: When the FIOM bit in henvcfg is 1, V=1, and an atomic instruction that accesses a region ordered as device I/O has its aq and/or rl bit set, that atomic instruction is ordered as though it accesses both device I/O and memory.
RULE 27: When FIOM=1 in henvcfg and V=1, setting the PI bit in a FENCE instruction means predecessor device input and memory reads (PR is implied).
RULE 28: When FIOM=1 in henvcfg and V=1, setting the PO bit in a FENCE instruction means predecessor device output and memory writes (PW is implied).
RULE 29: When FIOM=1 in henvcfg and V=1, setting the SI bit in a FENCE instruction means successor device input and memory reads (SR is implied).
RULE 30: When FIOM=1 in henvcfg and V=1, setting the SO bit in a FENCE instruction means successor device output and memory writes (SW is implied).
RULE 31: When the PBMTE bit in henvcfg is 1, the Svpbmt extension is available for use in VS-stage address translation.
RULE 32: When the PBMTE bit in henvcfg is 0, the implementation behaves as though Svpbmt were not implemented for VS-stage address translation.
RULE 33: If the Svpbmt extension is not implemented, the PBMTE field in henvcfg is read-only zero.
RULE 34: When the ADUE bit in henvcfg is 1 and the Svadu extension is implemented, hardware updating of PTE A/D bits is enabled during VS-stage address translation, and the implementation behaves as though the Svade extension were not implemented for VS-mode address translation.
RULE 35: When the ADUE bit in henvcfg is 0 and the Svadu extension is implemented, the implementation behaves as though Svade were implemented for VS-stage address translation.
RULE 36: If the Svadu extension is not implemented, the ADUE field in henvcfg is read-only zero.
RULE 37: If the Sstc extension is not implemented, the STCE bit in henvcfg is read-only zero.
RULE 38: When the STCE bit in henvcfg is 1, it enables vstimecmp for VS-mode.
RULE 39: When the STCE bit in henvcfg is 0, V=1, and an attempt is made to access stimecmp (vstimecmp), a virtual-instruction exception is raised and VSTIP in hip reverts to its defined behavior as if the Sstc extension is not implemented.
RULE 40: If the Zicboz extension is not implemented, the CBZE field in henvcfg is read-only zero.
RULE 41: When CBO.ZERO is executed in VS or VU privilege mode, the instruction is HS-qualified, and CBZE=1 in henvcfg, the instruction is enabled for execution.
RULE 42: When CBO.ZERO is executed in VS or VU privilege mode, the instruction is HS-qualified, and CBZE=0 in henvcfg, a virtual-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 43: When CBO.ZERO is executed and the instruction is not HS-qualified, an illegal-instruction exception is raised regardless of the CBZE setting in henvcfg.
RULE 44: If the Zicbom extension is not implemented, the CBCFE field in henvcfg is read-only zero.
RULE 45: When V=1 and CBO.CLEAN or CBO.FLUSH is executed and the instruction is not HS-qualified, an illegal-instruction exception is raised regardless of the CBCFE setting in henvcfg.
RULE 46: When V=1 and CBO.CLEAN or CBO.FLUSH is executed, the instruction is HS-qualified, and CBCFE=1 in henvcfg, the instructions are enabled for execution.
RULE 47: When V=1 and CBO.CLEAN or CBO.FLUSH is executed, the instruction is HS-qualified, and CBCFE=0 in henvcfg, a virtual-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 48: If the Zicbom extension is not implemented, the CBIE field in henvcfg is read-only zero.
RULE 49: When V=1 and CBO.INVAL is executed and the instruction is not HS-qualified, an illegal-instruction exception is raised regardless of the CBIE setting in henvcfg.
RULE 50: When V=1 and CBO.INVAL is HS-qualified and CBIE=01b or CBIE=11b in henvcfg, the instruction is enabled for execution.
RULE 51: When V=1 and CBO.INVAL is HS-qualified and CBIE has any value other than 01b or 11b in henvcfg, a virtual-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 52: If CBO.INVAL is enabled in HS-mode and is executed in VS or VU mode, it performs a flush operation even if CBIE=11b in henvcfg.
RULE 53: When CBO.INVAL is enabled for execution and CBIE=01b in henvcfg, the instruction is executed and performs a flush operation even if VS-mode configures it to perform an invalidate operation.
RULE 54: When CBO.INVAL is enabled for execution and CBIE=11b in henvcfg, the instruction is executed and performs an invalidate operation unless VS-mode configures it to perform a flush operation.
RULE 55: If the Ssnpm extension is not implemented, the PMM field in henvcfg is read-only zero.
RULE 56: When PMM in henvcfg takes the legal WARL value 00, pointer masking is disabled (PMLEN=0).
RULE 57: When PMM in henvcfg takes the legal WARL value 01, the value is reserved.
RULE 58: When PMM in henvcfg takes the legal WARL value 10, pointer masking is enabled with PMLEN=XLEN-57 (PMLEN=7 on RV64).
RULE 59: When PMM in henvcfg takes the legal WARL value 11, pointer masking is enabled with PMLEN=XLEN-48 (PMLEN=16 on RV64).
RULE 60: When the LPE bit in henvcfg is 1, the Zicfilp extension is enabled in VS-mode.
RULE 61: When the LPE bit in henvcfg is 0, the Zicfilp extension is not enabled in VS-mode and the hart does not update the ELP state, which remains NO_LP_EXPECTED.
RULE 62: When the LPE bit in henvcfg is 0, the LPAD instruction operates as a no-op.
RULE 63: When the SSE bit in henvcfg is 1, the Zicfiss extension is activated in VS-mode.
RULE 64: When the SSE bit in henvcfg is 0 and V=1, 16-bit Zicfiss instructions revert to their behavior defined by Zcmop.
RULE 65: When the SSE bit in henvcfg is 0 and V=1, the pte.xwr=010b encoding in VS-stage page tables becomes reserved.
RULE 66: When the SSE bit in henvcfg is 0 and V=1, the senvcfg.SSE field reads as zero and is read-only.
RULE 67: When the SSE bit in henvcfg is 0, V=1, and menvcfg.SSE is 1, SSAMOSWAP.W/D raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 68: When the DTE bit in henvcfg is 0, the implementation behaves as though the Ssdbltrp extension is not implemented for VS-mode and the vsstatus.SDT bit is read-only zero.
RULE 69: When the PBMTE or ADUE bits in henvcfg are changed, executing an HFENCE.VVMA instruction with rs1=x0 and rs2=x0 suffices to synchronize with respect to the altered interpretation of VS-stage PTEs' PBMT and A/D bit fields for the currently active VMID.
RULE 70: When the sequence "zero vsatp, switch henvcfg.PBMTE/ADUE, write new vsatp" is used, an HFENCE.VVMA instruction is not required.
RULE 71: When running with virtualization in VS or VU mode and vsatp.MODE is Bare, the two extra GPA bits may be subject to pointer masking depending on hgatp.MODE and either senvcfg.PMM or henvcfg.PMM for VU/VS mode.
RULE 72: If the privilege mode is VS-mode and henvcfg.SSE is 0, a virtual-instruction exception is raised on attempts to access the ssp CSR.
RULE 73: If the privilege mode is VU-mode and henvcfg.SSE is 0 (or senvcfg.SSE is 0), a virtual-instruction exception is raised on attempts to access the ssp CSR.
RULE 74: When S-mode is implemented and the current privilege mode is VS, the value of xSSE is defined to equal the SSE field of henvcfg (xSSE = henvcfg.SSE).
RULE 75: When V = 1 and henvcfg.SSE = 0, the shadow-stack page encoding R = 0, W = 1, X = 0 remains reserved at the VS and VU levels.
RULE 76: In M-mode, accessing henvcfg register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x60a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 77: In S-mode, accessing henvcfg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x60a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 78: In U-mode, accessing henvcfg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x60a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 79: In M-mode, setting henvcfg.STCE (bit 63) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x60a, a0; csrr a1, 0x60a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 80: In M-mode, setting henvcfg.PBMTE (bit 62) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4000000000000000; csrs 0x60a, a0; csrr a1, 0x60a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 81: In M-mode, setting henvcfg.CBZE (bit 7) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x80) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x80; csrs 0x60a, a0; csrr a1, 0x60a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x80].
RULE 82: In M-mode, setting henvcfg.CBCFE (bit 6) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x40) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x40; csrs 0x60a, a0; csrr a1, 0x60a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x40].
RULE 83: In M-mode, setting henvcfg.CBIE (bit 4) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x10) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x10; csrs 0x60a, a0; csrr a1, 0x60a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x10].
RULE 84: In M-mode, setting henvcfg.SSE (bit 3) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8; csrs 0x60a, a0; csrr a1, 0x60a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8].
RULE 85: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the henvcfg register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x60a, a0; csrr a1, 0x60a; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: hgatp
NUMBER: 0x680
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: 63..60=MODE, 57..44=VMID, 43..0=PPN
EXTENSIONS: H, Smcdeleg, Smnpm, Ssdbltrp, Sstc, Svade, Svadu, Svpbmt, Zicbom, Zicboz, Zicfilp, Zicfiss
RULE 1: The hgatp register is a hypervisor read/write CSR.
RULE 2: The hgatp register is assigned to the Hypervisor Protection and Translation privilege level.
RULE 3: When the PBMTE bit in hgatp is 1, the Svpbmt extension is available for S-mode and G-stage address translation.
RULE 4: When the PBMTE bit in hgatp is 0, the implementation behaves as though the Svpbmt extension were not implemented.
RULE 5: If the Svpbmt extension is not implemented, the PBMTE bit in hgatp is read-only zero.
RULE 6: When the ADUE bit in hgatp is 1, hardware updating of PTE A/D bits is enabled during S-mode address translation, and the implementation behaves as though the Svade extension were not implemented for S-mode address translation.
RULE 7: When the hypervisor extension is implemented and the ADUE bit in hgatp is 1, hardware updating of PTE A/D bits is enabled during G-stage address translation, and the implementation behaves as though the Svade extension were not implemented for G-stage address translation.
RULE 8: When the ADUE bit in hgatp is 0, the implementation behaves as though the Svade extension were implemented for S-mode and G-stage address translation.
RULE 9: If the Svadu extension is not implemented, the ADUE bit in hgatp is read-only zero.
RULE 10: If the hypervisor extension is implemented, the hgatp.MODE field is reset to 0.
RULE 11: If two-stage address translation is enabled within the H extension and hgatp.MODE is not zero, then non-zero G-stage PTE PBMT bits override the attributes in the PMA to produce an intermediate set of attributes.
RULE 12: If two-stage address translation is enabled within the H extension and hgatp.MODE is zero, then the PMA attributes serve as the intermediate attributes.
RULE 13: The CSR hgatp is provided to software executing in HS-mode.
RULE 14: The CSR hgatp is not provided to software executing in VS-mode.
RULE 15: The hgatp register holds the physical page number (PPN) of the guest-physical root page table.
RULE 16: When mstatus.TVM = 1 and the processor is executing in HS-mode, any attempt to read or write hgatp must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 17: Bits 63-60 of hgatp form the MODE field and are WARL (4 bits).
RULE 18: Bits 59-58 of hgatp are reserved and are WARL (2 bits).
RULE 19: Bits 43-30 of hgatp are reserved and are WARL (14 bits).
RULE 20: Bits 29-0 of hgatp contain the PPN field and are WARL (44 bits).
RULE 21: For HSXLEN = 64, a MODE value of 0 in hgatp selects Bare, which provides no translation or protection.
RULE 22: For HSXLEN = 64, MODE values 1-7 in hgatp are reserved.
RULE 23: For HSXLEN = 64, a MODE value of 8 in hgatp selects Sv39x4, which provides page-based 41-bit virtual addressing.
RULE 24: For HSXLEN = 64, a MODE value of 9 in hgatp selects Sv48x4, which provides page-based 50-bit virtual addressing.
RULE 25: For HSXLEN = 64, a MODE value of 10 in hgatp selects Sv57x4, which provides page-based 59-bit virtual addressing.
RULE 26: For HSXLEN = 64, MODE values 11-15 in hgatp are reserved.
RULE 27: When HSXLEN = 64, Sv39x4, Sv48x4, and Sv57x4 are defined MODE values in hgatp, and the remaining MODE values are reserved for future use and may define different interpretations of the other fields in hgatp.
RULE 28: A write to hgatp with an unsupported MODE value is not ignored, and the fields of hgatp are WARL in the normal way, when so indicated.
RULE 29: When MODE = Bare in hgatp, guest physical addresses are equal to supervisor physical addresses and no further memory protection is provided beyond the physical-memory protection scheme of Section 3.7.
RULE 30: When MODE = Bare in hgatp, software must write zero to the remaining fields (PPN, VMID, etc.) in hgatp.
RULE 31: When hgatp selects a paged virtual-memory scheme (Sv32x4, Sv39x4, Sv48x4, Sv57x4), the root page table must be 16 KiB and must be aligned to a 16-KiB boundary.
RULE 32: In paged virtual-memory schemes selected by hgatp, the lowest two bits of the PPN field in hgatp always read as zeros.
RULE 33: An implementation that supports only the defined paged virtual-memory schemes and/or Bare may make PPN[1:0] in hgatp read-only zero.
RULE 34: The number of implemented VMID bits (VMIDLEN) may be determined by writing one to every bit position in the VMID field of hgatp, then reading back hgatp to see which bit positions retain a one.
RULE 35: The least-significant bits of the VMID field in hgatp are implemented first; if VMIDLEN > 0, then VMID[VMIDLEN-1:0] in hgatp is writable.
RULE 36: The maximal value of VMIDLEN for hgatp is 7 for Sv32x4, or 14 for Sv39x4, Sv48x4, and Sv57x4.
RULE 37: hgatp is considered active for the address-translation algorithm unless the effective privilege mode is U and hstatus.HU = 0.
RULE 38: Executing an HFENCE.VVMA guarantees that any prior stores already visible to the current hart are ordered before all implicit reads performed by that hart for VS-stage address translation of instructions that follow the HFENCE.VVMA, provided that hgatp.VMID has the same setting as it did when the HFENCE.VVMA executed.
RULE 39: The ordering guarantee of HFENCE.VVMA does not apply when hgatp.VMID differs from its value at the time the HFENCE.VVMA instruction executed.
RULE 40: Implicit reads for VS-stage address translation need not be ordered by HFENCE.VVMA when hgatp.VMID is different than at the time the HFENCE.VVMA executed.
RULE 41: An HFENCE.VVMA instruction applies only to the single virtual machine identified by the value of hgatp.VMID at the moment the HFENCE.VVMA instruction executes.
RULE 42: If hgatp.MODE is changed for a given VMID, software must execute an HFENCE.GVMA with rs1 = x0 and rs2 set to either x0 or that VMID to order subsequent guest translations with the MODE change, even if the old MODE or the new MODE is Bare.
RULE 43: When the TVM field in mstatus is set to 1, HS-mode MUST NOT access hgatp.
RULE 44: When the TVM field in mstatus is set to 1, HS-mode MUST NOT execute the HFENCE.GVMA instruction.
RULE 45: When the TVM field in mstatus is set to 1, HS-mode MUST NOT execute the HINVAL.GVMA instruction.
RULE 46: The TVM field's restriction on hgatp access applies only while executing in HS-mode and does not affect VS-mode.
RULE 47: When the current virtualization mode V is 1, the hgatp register performs the second-stage G-stage address translation, converting a guest physical address into a supervisor physical address.
RULE 48: Zeroing the hgatp register disables G-stage address translation.
RULE 49: When V is 1, memory accesses that would normally bypass address translation are subject only to G-stage address translation performed by the hgatp register, including reads and writes of VS-level page tables.
RULE 50: If hgatp.MODE is Bare then guest physical addresses are equal to supervisor physical addresses without modification.
RULE 51: If hgatp.MODE is Bare then no memory protection applies to the translation.
RULE 52: If hgatp.MODE specifies Sv32x4, Sv39x4, Sv48x4, or Sv57x4 then the root page table must be aligned to a 16 KiB boundary.
RULE 53: If hgatp.MODE is Sv39x4 then address bits 63:41 must be zero, otherwise a guest-page-fault exception occurs.
RULE 54: If hgatp.MODE is Sv48x4 then address bits 63:50 must be zero, otherwise a guest-page-fault exception occurs.
RULE 55: If hgatp.MODE is Sv57x4 then address bits 63:59 must be zero, otherwise a guest-page-fault exception occurs.
RULE 56: Translation using an hgatp-selected G-stage scheme begins only if the effective privilege mode is VS-mode or VU-mode.
RULE 57: When checking the U bit during hgatp-controlled translation, the current privilege mode is always taken to be U-mode.
RULE 58: Guest-page-fault exceptions are raised instead of regular page-fault exceptions when translation is performed by hgatp.
RULE 59: When hgatp selects a G-stage scheme, all memory accesses are treated as user-level accesses as if executed in U-mode.
RULE 60: When hgatp selects a G-stage scheme, access-type permissions are checked during G-stage translation the same as for VS-stage translation.
RULE 61: When hgatp selects a G-stage scheme and a memory access supports VS-stage address translation, permissions and A/D-bit requirements at the G-stage level are checked as for an implicit load or store, not for the original access type.
RULE 62: When hgatp selects a G-stage scheme, any exception is reported for the original access type (instruction, load, or store/AMO).
RULE 63: When hgatp selects a G-stage scheme, the G bit in all G-stage PTEs is currently not used.
RULE 64: When hgatp selects a G-stage scheme, hardware must ignore the G bit in G-stage PTEs.
RULE 65: The SFENCE.VMA instruction orders stores to VS-level address-translation structures with subsequent VS-stage address translations.
RULE 66: The SFENCE.VMA ordering applies only when hgatp.VMID at the time of the translation matches hgatp.VMID at the time SFENCE.VMA was executed.
RULE 67: Executing an HFENCE.VVMA with rs1 = x0 and rs2 = x0 suffices to synchronize the altered interpretation of VS-stage PTE PBMT and A/D bit fields for the currently active VMID identified by hgatp.VMID.
RULE 68: In VS/VU mode when vsatp.MODE is Bare, the two extra bits of a guest physical address may be subject to pointer masking, and this depends on the hgatp.MODE and the senvcfg.PMM (for VU) or henvcfg.PMM (for VS) settings.
RULE 69: When vsatp.MODE is not Bare, the two extra bits of a guest physical address are not subject to pointer masking regardless of the hgatp.MODE or any PMM settings.
RULE 70: In M-mode, accessing hgatp register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x680; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 71: In HS-mode, accessing hgatp register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x680; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 72: In U-mode, accessing hgatp register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x680; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 73: In M-mode, setting hgatp.MODE (bit 60) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1000000000000000; csrs 0x680, a0; csrr a1, 0x680; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 74: In M-mode, setting hgatp.VMID (bit 44) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x100000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x100000000000; csrs 0x680, a0; csrr a1, 0x680; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x100000000000].
RULE 75: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hgatp register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x680, a0; csrr a1, 0x680; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 76: In M-mode, accessing hgatp register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x680; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 77: In M-mode, accessing hgatp register while Smcdeleg extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smcdeleg; csrr a0, 0x680; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 78: In M-mode, accessing hgatp register while Smnpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smnpm; csrr a0, 0x680; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 79: In M-mode, accessing hgatp register while Ssdbltrp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssdbltrp; csrr a0, 0x680; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 80: In M-mode, accessing hgatp register while Sstc extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sstc; csrr a0, 0x680; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 81: In M-mode, accessing hgatp register while Svade extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Svade; csrr a0, 0x680; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 82: In M-mode, accessing hgatp register while Svadu extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Svadu; csrr a0, 0x680; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 83: In M-mode, accessing hgatp register while Svpbmt extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Svpbmt; csrr a0, 0x680; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 84: In M-mode, accessing hgatp register while Zicbom extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicbom; csrr a0, 0x680; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 85: In M-mode, accessing hgatp register while Zicboz extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicboz; csrr a0, 0x680; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 86: In M-mode, accessing hgatp register while Zicfilp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicfilp; csrr a0, 0x680; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 87: In M-mode, accessing hgatp register while Zicfiss extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicfiss; csrr a0, 0x680; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hgeie
NUMBER: 0x607
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: 63..1=GUEST_EXTERNAL_INTERRUPTS, 0..0=HSXLEN
EXTENSIONS: H
RULE 1: The hgeie register has HRW privilege/access, meaning it is readable and writable in hypervisor mode.
RULE 2: hip.SGEIP is read-only and is 1 if and only if the bitwise logical-AND of hgeip and hgeie is non-zero in any bit.
RULE 3: Guest external interrupt number i is mapped to bit i of the hgeie register.
RULE 4: If GEILEN is nonzero, bits GEILEN down to 1 of the hgeie register shall be writable.
RULE 5: If GEILEN is nonzero, all bit positions of the hgeie register other than bits GEILEN down to 1 shall be read-only zeros.
RULE 6: The enable bits in the hgeie register do not affect the VS-level external interrupt signal selected from hgeip by hstatus.VGEIN.
RULE 7: In M-mode, accessing hgeie register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x607; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 8: In HS-mode, accessing hgeie register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x607; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hgeip
NUMBER: 0xe12
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: UNKNOWN..UNKNOWN=WPRI, UNKNOWN..UNKNOWN=GEIP, 0..0=WPRI
EXTENSIONS: H
RULE 1: The hgeip CSR holds the Hypervisor guest external interrupt pending status.
RULE 2: The hgeip CSR is readable and writable (HRW).
RULE 3: The hgeip CSR is provided to HS-mode.
RULE 4: The hgeip CSR is not provided to VS-mode.
RULE 5: hip.SGEIP is read-only in the hip register and equals 1 if and only if the bitwise logical-AND of hgeip and hgeie is non-zero in any bit.
RULE 6: The bit of hgeip selected by hstatus.VGEIN is one of the sources logically ORed to form hip.VSEIP.
RULE 7: hgeip is an HSXLEN-bit read-only register.
RULE 8: In hgeip, guest external interrupt number i corresponds to bit i.
RULE 9: If GEILEN is nonzero, all bit positions of hgeip that are not within bits GEILEN:1 shall read as zero.
RULE 10: The enable bits in hgeie do not affect the VS-level external interrupt signal selected from hgeip by hstatus.VGEIN.
RULE 11: In hgeip, the HSXLEN field occupies bit 0.
RULE 12: In M-mode, accessing hgeip register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xe12; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 13: In HS-mode, accessing hgeip register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xe12; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 14: In U-mode, accessing hgeip register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xe12; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 15: In M-mode, setting hgeip.WPRI (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0xe12, a0; csrr a1, 0xe12; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].

REGISTER: hideleg
NUMBER: 0x603
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..16=WPRI, 15..14=WPRI, 13..13=LCOFI, 12..12=S-EXTERNAL, 11..11=WPRI, 10..10=VSEIP, 9..9=S-TIMER, 8..7=WPRI, 6..6=VSTIP, 5..5=S-SOFTWARE, 4..3=WPRI, 2..2=VSSIP, 1..0=WPRI

RULE 1: If the LCOFI bit in hideleg is implemented, setting this bit allows all LCOFIs to be delegated to VS-mode.
RULE 2: hideleg is provided to HS-mode.
RULE 3: hideleg is not provided to VS-mode.
RULE 4: The hideleg CSR is an HSXLEN-bit read/write register.
RULE 5: An interrupt that has been delegated to HS-mode using mideleg is further delegated to VS-mode if the corresponding hideleg bit is set.
RULE 6: When a virtual supervisor external interrupt (code 10) is delegated to VS-mode via hideleg, the machine automatically translates it into a supervisor external interrupt (code 9) for VS-mode, including the value written to vscause on an interrupt trap.
RULE 7: When a virtual supervisor timer interrupt (code 6) is delegated to VS-mode via hideleg, the machine automatically translates it into a supervisor timer interrupt (code 5) for VS-mode.
RULE 8: When a virtual supervisor software interrupt (code 2) is delegated to VS-mode via hideleg, the machine automatically translates it into a supervisor software interrupt (code 1) for VS-mode.
RULE 9: The interrupt fields of hideleg are WARL.
RULE 10: An interrupt i will trap to HS-mode only if bit i in hideleg is clear.
RULE 11: If the Shlcofideleg extension is implemented, hideleg bit 13 is writable.
RULE 12: If the Shlcofideleg extension is not implemented, hideleg bit 13 is read-only zero.
RULE 13: When hideleg bit 13 is zero, vsip.LCOFIP and vsie.LCOFIE are read-only zeros.
RULE 14: When hideleg bit 13 is non-zero, vsip.LCOFIP and vsie.LCOFIE alias sip.LCOFIP and sie.LCOFIE respectively.
RULE 15: When hideleg bit 10 is zero, vsip.SEIP and vsie.SEIE are read-only zeros.
RULE 16: When hideleg bit 10 is non-zero, vsip.SEIP and vsie.SEIE alias hip.VSEIP and hie.VSEIE respectively.
RULE 17: When hideleg bit 6 is zero, vsip.STIP and vsie.STIE are read-only zeros.
RULE 18: When hideleg bit 6 is non-zero, vsip.STIP and vsie.STIE alias hip.VSTIP and hie.VSTIE respectively.
RULE 19: When hideleg bit 2 is zero, vsip.SSIP and vsie.SSIE are read-only zeros.
RULE 20: When hideleg bit 2 is non-zero, vsip.SSIP and vsie.SSIE alias hip.VSSIP and hie.VSSIE respectively.
RULE 21: For any bit position where the corresponding bit in the mideleg register is zero, the same-position bit in the hideleg register is a read-only zero.
RULE 22: hideleg is consulted to decide whether a trap that has been delegated to HS-mode is further delegated to VS-mode.
RULE 23: If hideleg delegates a trap that would otherwise be taken to HS-mode, the trap is taken to VS-mode.

REGISTER: hie

FIELDS: 63..16=UNKNOWN, 15..14=WPRI, 13..13=SGEIE, 12..11=WPRI, 10..10=VSEIE, 9..8=WPRI, 7..7=WPRI, 6..6=VSTIE, 5..3=WPRI, 2..2=VSSIE, 1..0=WPRI

RULE 1: The hie CSR has the HRW attribute, indicating that it is both readable and writable.
RULE 2: A bit in hie shall be writable if the corresponding interrupt can ever become pending in hip.

RULE 4: For each writable bit in sie, the corresponding bit in hie shall be read-only zero.

REGISTER: hip
NUMBER: 0x644
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: UNKNOWN..UNKNOWN=UNDEFINED, 15..15=WPRI, 14..14=LCOFIP, 13..13=SGEIP, 12..12=WPRI, 11..11=VSEIP, 10..10=WPRI, 9..9=WPRI, 8..8=WPRI, 7..7=VSTIP, 6..6=WPRI, 5..5=WPRI, 4..4=WPRI, 3..3=VSSIP, 2..2=WPRI, 1..1=WPRI, 0..0=WPRI
EXTENSIONS: H, Smnpm, Ssdbltrp, Sstc, Svadu, Svpbmt, Zicbom, Zicboz, Zicfilp, Zicfiss
RULE 1: hip has an access type of HRW.
RULE 2: If the Sstc extension is implemented, the STCE bit in menvcfg is zero, and the H extension is implemented, then hip.VSTIP reverts to the behavior defined for a system without the Sstc extension.
RULE 3: For each writable bit in sie, the corresponding bit shall be read-only zero in hip.
RULE 4: Nonzero bits in sie and hip are always mutually exclusive.
RULE 5: Nonzero bits in sip and hip are always mutually exclusive.
RULE 6: An interrupt i will trap to HS-mode whenever (a) either the current operating mode is HS-mode and the SIE bit in sstatus is set, or the current operating mode has less privilege than HS-mode, (b) bit i is set in both hip and hie (or in both sip and sie), and (c) bit i is not set in hideleg.
RULE 7: If bit i in hip is writable, a pending interrupt i can be cleared by writing 0 to this bit.
RULE 8: If interrupt i can become pending in hip but bit i in hip is read-only, then either the interrupt can be cleared by clearing bit i of hvip, or the implementation must provide some other mechanism for clearing the pending interrupt.
RULE 9: hip.SGEIP is a read-only bit in hip that is 1 if and only if the bitwise logical-AND of CSRs hgeip and hgeie is nonzero in any bit.
RULE 10: hip.VSEIP is a read-only bit in hip that is the logical-OR of (i) bit VSEIP of hvip, (ii) the bit of hgeip selected by hstatus.VGEIN, and (iii) any other platform-specific external interrupt signal directed to VS-level.
RULE 11: hip.VSTIP is a read-only bit in hip that is the logical-OR of hvip.VSTIP and, when the Sstc extension is implemented, the timer interrupt signal resulting from vstimecmp.
RULE 12: The hip.VSTIP bit is cleared by writing vstimecmp with a greater value.
RULE 13: hip.VSSIP is a writable alias of the same bit in hvip.
RULE 14: If the STCE bit in henvcfg is 0, V=1, and an attempt is made to access stimecmp (vstimecmp), then the VSTIP field in hip reverts to its defined behavior as if the Sstc extension were not implemented.
RULE 15: When bit 10 of hideleg is one, hip.VSEIP is an alias of vsip.SEIP.
RULE 16: When bit 10 of hideleg is one, hie.VSEIE is an alias of vsie.SEIE.
RULE 17: When bit 6 of hideleg is one, hip.VSTIP is an alias of vsip.STIP.
RULE 18: When bit 6 of hideleg is one, hie.VSTIE is an alias of vsie.STIE.
RULE 19: When bit 2 of hideleg is one, hip.VSSIP is an alias of vsip.SSIP.
RULE 20: When bit 2 of hideleg is one, hie.VSSIE is an alias of vsie.SSIE.
RULE 21: The VSTIP bit in the hip register reflects the presence of a pending virtual supervisor timer interrupt.
RULE 22: The VSTIP bit in the hip register becomes set when the 64-bit truncated sum of time and htimedelta is greater than or equal to vstimecmp, treating the values as unsigned integers.
RULE 23: A change in the result of the comparison between (time + htimedelta) and vstimecmp must eventually be reflected in the VSTIP bit of the hip register, though the reflection need not occur immediately.
RULE 24: The VSTIP bit in the hip register remains set until vstimecmp becomes greater than the 64-bit truncated sum of time and htimedelta, typically as a result of writing vstimecmp.
RULE 25: For each bit position where the corresponding bit in mideleg is zero, the same bit in hip MUST be read-only zero.
RULE 26: The SGEIP bit in the mip CSR is an alias of the SGEIP bit in the hip CSR.
RULE 27: The VSEIP bit in the mip CSR is an alias of the VSEIP bit in the hip CSR.
RULE 28: The VSTIP bit in the mip CSR is an alias of the VSTIP bit in the hip CSR.
RULE 29: The VSSIP bit in the mip CSR is an alias of the VSSIP bit in the hip CSR.
RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing hip register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x644; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 31: In HS-mode, accessing hip register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x644; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 32: In U-mode, accessing hip register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x644; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 33: In M-mode, setting hip.WPRI (bit 15) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000; csrs 0x644, a0; csrr a1, 0x644; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8000].
RULE 34: In M-mode, setting hip.LCOFIP (bit 14) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x4000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4000; csrs 0x644, a0; csrr a1, 0x644; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x4000].
RULE 35: In M-mode, setting hip.SGEIP (bit 13) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2000; csrs 0x644, a0; csrr a1, 0x644; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2000].
