REGISTER: hpmcounter10
NUMBER: 0xc0a
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: Accessing hpmcounter10 when it is unimplemented may cause an illegal-instruction exception or may return a constant value.
RULE 2: If the event-selection configuration for hpmcounter10 is misconfigured, hpmcounter10 may return a constant value.
RULE 3: hpmcounter10 is a URO (unprivileged read-only) CSR.
RULE 4: The mhpmcounter10 CSR appears in the Machine Counter/Timers table, has machine read/write (MRW) privilege, and provides a machine performance-monitoring counter.
RULE 5: The mhpmevent10 CSR appears in the Machine Counter Setup table, has machine read/write (MRW) privilege, and selects the event counted by mhpmcounter10.
RULE 6: After a hart reset, hpmcounter10 contains an arbitrary value until software writes a defined value.
RULE 7: Any write to the hpmcounter10 CSR takes effect only after the executing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 8: The 64-bit WARL event selector CSR mhpmevent10 determines which events cause hpmcounter10 to increment.
RULE 9: A legal implementation may hard-wire hpmcounter10 to zero and make it read-only.
RULE 10: The mhpmevent10h CSR exists only if the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, and its presence can affect the high-half selection for hpmcounter10.
RULE 11: hpmcounter10 is a read-only shadow of mhpmcounter10.
RULE 12: If the HPM10 bit in mcounteren is clear, a read of hpmcounter10 while executing in S-mode or U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: If the HPM10 bit in mcounteren is set, access to hpmcounter10 is permitted in the next implemented lower-privilege mode (S-mode if the implementation provides S-mode, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 14: For an siselect value that selects counter 10, the sireg and sireg2 registers could be used to access mhpmcounter10.
RULE 15: When siselect holds the value 0x4A, the hpmcounter10 register can be read or written via sireg* if and only if mcounteren[10] = 1 and menvcfg.CDE = 1.
RULE 16: While executing in M-mode or S-mode with siselect = 0x4A, an illegal-instruction exception is raised for any attempt to access a sireg* if menvcfg.CDE = 0.
RULE 17: While executing in M-mode or S-mode with siselect = 0x4A, an illegal-instruction exception is raised for any attempt to access a sireg* if the counter selected by siselect is not delegated to S-mode, i.e., if mcounteren[10] = 0.
RULE 18: While executing in M-mode or S-mode with siselect = 0x4A, an illegal-instruction exception is raised for any attempt to access sireg4 or sireg5 when XLEN = 64.
RULE 19: While executing in M-mode or S-mode with siselect = 0x4A, an illegal-instruction exception is raised for any attempt to access sireg3 or sireg6.
RULE 20: If any extension on which the underlying state of hpmcounter10 depends is not implemented, an attempt from M-mode or S-mode to access hpmcounter10 through sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 21: If the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented, a virtual-instruction exception is raised for attempts from VS-mode or VU-mode to directly access vsiselect or any vsireg* that would affect hpmcounter10.
RULE 22: If the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented, a virtual-instruction exception is raised for attempts from VU-mode to access siselect or any sireg* that would affect hpmcounter10.
RULE 23: If the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented, while vsiselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F (including 0x4A for hpmcounter10), an illegal-instruction exception is raised for any attempt from M-mode or S-mode to access any vsireg* that would affect hpmcounter10.
RULE 24: If the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented, an attempt from VS-mode to access any sireg* (which maps to vsireg*) that would affect hpmcounter10 raises an illegal-instruction exception when menvcfg.CDE = 0.
RULE 25: If the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented, an attempt from VS-mode to access any sireg* (which maps to vsireg*) that would affect hpmcounter10 raises a virtual-instruction exception when menvcfg.CDE = 1.
RULE 26: If the HPM10 bit in scounteren is clear while executing in U-mode, an attempt to read hpmcounter10 causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 27: If the HPM10 bit in scounteren is set while executing in U-mode, access to hpmcounter10 is permitted and no illegal-instruction exception occurs.
RULE 28: If the HPM10 bit in scounteren is a read-only zero, reads of hpmcounter10 in U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 29: U-mode may access hpmcounter10 only when both the HPM10 bit in scounteren and the HPM10 bit in mcounteren are set.
RULE 30: The writability of the HPM10 bit in scounteren, which determines hpmcounter10 access, is not affected by the setting of the HPM10 bit in mcounteren.
RULE 31: In the mhpmevent register that corresponds to hpmcounter10, bit 63 named OF is the overflow status and interrupt disable bit that is set when the counter overflows.
RULE 32: In the mhpmevent register for hpmcounter10, bit 62 named MINH inhibits counting of events in M-mode when set.
RULE 33: In the mhpmevent register for hpmcounter10, bit 61 named SINH inhibits counting of events in S/HS-mode when set.
RULE 34: In the mhpmevent register for hpmcounter10, bit 60 named UINH inhibits counting of events in U-mode when set.
RULE 35: In the mhpmevent register for hpmcounter10, bit 59 named VSINH inhibits counting of events in VS-mode when set.
RULE 36: In the mhpmevent register for hpmcounter10, bit 58 named VUINH inhibits counting of events in VU-mode when set.
RULE 37: For each x INH bit in the mhpmevent register for hpmcounter10, if the associated privilege mode x is not implemented, the bit is read-only zero.
RULE 38: For hpmcounter10, each x INH bit, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in privilege mode x.
RULE 39: For hpmcounter10, when all five INH bits are zero, counting of events occurs in all privilege modes.
RULE 40: The OF bit for hpmcounter10 is set when the corresponding counter overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 41: Overflow of hpmcounter10 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter10 or mhpmevent10 registers, only from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 42: If hpmcounter10 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow-interrupt request is generated; if the OF bit is one, no interrupt request is generated.
RULE 43: The OF bit for hpmcounter10 also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for that counter.
RULE 44: The count-overflow-interrupt request generated by hpmcounter10 is treated as a standard local interrupt that corresponds to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 45: The mip and sip LCOFIP bits are the interrupt-pending bits for the count-overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter10, and the mie and sie LCOFIE bits are the interrupt-enable bits for that interrupt.
RULE 46: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter10 sets the associated OF bit.
RULE 47: When the OF bit for hpmcounter10 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 48: The mideleg register controls the delegation of the count-overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter10 to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 49: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for hpmcounter10 is done by clearing the OF bit in conjunction with initializing the counter to a starting value, because there are not separate overflow status and overflow interrupt enable bits.
RULE 50: Once hpmcounter10 has overflowed, it and its OF bit MUST be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 51: The overflow flag of hpmcounter10 is provided as a shadow copy in scountovf bit 10.
RULE 52: The read visibility of the overflow flag of hpmcounter10 follows the same mcounteren (or mcounteren and hcounteren) access rules that apply to the hpmcounter10 CSR itself.
RULE 53: In M-mode the overflow flag of hpmcounter10 is always readable via scountovf bit 10.
RULE 54: In S-mode the overflow flag of hpmcounter10 is readable via scountovf bit 10 only when mcounteren bit 10 is set, otherwise the read returns zero.
RULE 55: In VS-mode the overflow flag of hpmcounter10 is readable via scountovf bit 10 only when both mcounteren bit 10 and hcounteren bit 10 are set, otherwise the read returns zero.
RULE 56: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter10 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc0a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 57: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter10 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc0a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 58: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter10 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc0a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 59: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter10 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc0a, a0; csrr a1, 0xc0a; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 60: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter10 register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0xc0a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 61: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter10 register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc0a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 62: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter10 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xc0a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hpmcounter11
NUMBER: 0xc0b
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: Accessing an unimplemented hpmcounter11 may cause an illegal-instruction exception or may return a constant value.
RULE 2: If the configuration used to select the events counted by hpmcounter11 is misconfigured, hpmcounter11 may return a constant value.
RULE 3: hpmcounter11 has privilege URO (unprivileged read-only).
RULE 4: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter11 contains an arbitrary value and may be written with any given value.
RULE 5: A write to the mhpmcounter11 CSR takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 6: The mhpmevent11 CSR selects the event that causes mhpmcounter11 to increment.
RULE 7: Writing the value 0 to mhpmevent11 defines "no event" for mhpmcounter11.
RULE 8: A legal implementation may hard-wire mhpmcounter11 and its corresponding mhpmevent11 to read-only zero.
RULE 9: If the HPM 11 bit in mcounteren is clear, attempts to read hpmcounter11 while executing in S-mode or U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: If the HPM 11 bit in mcounteren is set, access to hpmcounter11 is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 11: hpmcounter11 is a read-only shadow of mhpmcounter11.
RULE 12: The setting of the mcountinhibit CSR does not affect the accessibility of hpmcounter11.
RULE 13: If the HPM 11 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, hpmcounter11 increments as usual.
RULE 14: If the HPM 11 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, hpmcounter11 does not increment.
RULE 15: If the mcountinhibit CSR is not implemented, hpmcounter11 increments as usual.
RULE 16: When the siselect value selects X = 11, the CSR aliases sireg and sireg2 give architectural access to the low-XLEN bits of the mhpmcounter11 register.
RULE 17: When the siselect value selects X = 11, the CSR aliases sireg4 and sireg5 give architectural access to the high-XLEN bits of the mhpmcounter11 register.
RULE 18: When mcounteren[11] = 1, menvcfg.CDE = 1, and siselect = 0x4B, a read or write to the generic sireg CSR accesses the hpmcounter11 register.
RULE 19: When mcounteren[11] = 1, menvcfg.CDE = 1, and siselect = 0x4B, a read or write to sireg4 accesses the high half of the hpmcounter11 register (alias hpmcounter11h).
RULE 20: If menvcfg.CDE = 0, any attempt in M-mode or S-mode to read or write hpmcounter11 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 21: If siselect = 0x41, any attempt in M-mode or S-mode to read or write hpmcounter11 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 22: If mcounteren[11] = 0, any attempt in M-mode or S-mode to read or write hpmcounter11 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 23: If XLEN = 64, an access in M-mode or S-mode to sireg4 (the hpmcounter11h alias) raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 24: If the standard HPM counter extensions on which hpmcounter11 depends are not implemented, any attempt in M-mode or S-mode to access hpmcounter11 through sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 25: If the hypervisor extension is implemented and code executing in VS-mode attempts to access hpmcounter11 through vsireg* while menvcfg.CDE = 0, an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 26: If the hypervisor extension is implemented and code executing in VS-mode attempts to access hpmcounter11 through vsireg* while menvcfg.CDE = 1, a virtual-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 27: If the HPM 11 bit in the scounteren register is clear, a read of the hpmcounter11 register while executing in U-mode MUST cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 28: If the HPM 11 bit in the scounteren register is implemented as a read-only zero, a read of the hpmcounter11 register in U-mode MUST cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 29: The OF bit in mhpmevent11 is set when hpmcounter11 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 30: Overflow of hpmcounter11 occurs when its unsigned value wraps around the implemented counter width.
RULE 31: After hpmcounter11 overflows, hpmcounter11 continues counting by wrapping and the sticky OF bit remains set, preserving all information.
RULE 32: If hpmcounter11 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow-interrupt request for hpmcounter11 is generated.
RULE 33: If hpmcounter11 overflows while its OF bit is one, no count-overflow-interrupt request for hpmcounter11 is generated.
RULE 34: When the OF bit associated with hpmcounter11 is one, count-overflow-interrupt requests for hpmcounter11 are disabled.
RULE 35: Writes to mhpmcounter11 or mhpmevent11 never cause overflow of hpmcounter11; overflow arises only from hardware increments of hpmcounter11.
RULE 36: When a count-overflow-interrupt request is generated for hpmcounter11, the OF bit in mhpmevent11 is set.
RULE 37: When the OF bit for hpmcounter11 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 38: The count-overflow-interrupt request for hpmcounter11 is treated as a standard local interrupt that corresponds to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 39: The mideleg register controls whether a pending count-overflow interrupt for hpmcounter11 is delegated to S-mode or taken in M-mode.
RULE 40: If supervisor mode is implemented, bit 11 of the scountovf register provides a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit in mhpmevent11 for hpmcounter11.
RULE 41: If the privilege mode associated with an INH bit in mhpmevent11 for hpmcounter11 is not implemented, that INH bit reads as zero and cannot be set.
RULE 42: When an INH bit in mhpmevent11 for hpmcounter11 is set for the current privilege mode, hpmcounter11 does not count events while executing in that mode.
RULE 43: If all INH bits in mhpmevent11 for hpmcounter11 are zero, hpmcounter11 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 44: Once hpmcounter11 has overflowed and its OF bit is set, software must write a new value to hpmcounter11 and clear the OF bit before another overflow interrupt for hpmcounter11 can be generated.
RULE 45: In S-mode or HS-mode, a read of hpmcounter11 is permitted only when the mcounteren bit 11 is set to 1; if mcounteren[11] is 0, the read is not permitted and the value returned is unspecified.
RULE 46: In VS-mode, a read of hpmcounter11 is permitted only when both the mcounteren bit 11 and the hcounteren bit 11 are set to 1; if either bit is 0, the read is not permitted and the value returned is unspecified.
RULE 47: If the HPM11 bit in hcounteren is clear and V=1 and the HPM11 bit in mcounteren is 1, then a read of hpmcounter11 causes a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 48: In VU-mode, a read of hpmcounter11 is not permitted unless the HPM11 bits in both hcounteren and scounteren are set.
RULE 49: If the HPM11 bit in hcounteren is read-only zero, then a read of hpmcounter11 while V=1 causes a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 50: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter11 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc0b; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 51: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter11 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc0b; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 52: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter11 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc0b; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 53: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter11 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc0b, a0; csrr a1, 0xc0b; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 54: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter11 register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc0b; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 55: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter11 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xc0b; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hpmcounter12
NUMBER: 0xc0c
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: If hpmcounter12 is unimplemented, accessing it may cause an illegal-instruction exception or may return a constant value.
RULE 2: If the event-selection configuration for hpmcounter12 is misconfigured, hpmcounter12 may return a constant value.
RULE 3: hpmcounter12 is an unprivileged CSR that has privilege level URO, meaning it is read-only.
RULE 4: The mhpmcounter12 CSR has Machine Read/Write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 5: The event selector register mhpmevent12 determines which events cause mhpmcounter12 to increment.
RULE 6: A legal implementation may hard-wire mhpmcounter12 to zero and make it read-only.
RULE 7: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter12 contains an arbitrary value.
RULE 8: A CSR write to mhpmcounter12 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 9: When the HPM12 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the hpmcounter12 register while executing in S-mode or U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: When the HPM12 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter12 register is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode.
RULE 11: The hpmcounter12 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter12 register.
RULE 12: In M or S privilege mode, if siselect selects hpmcounter12 (value 0x40-0x5F) and menvcfg.CDE = 0, any access to any sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: In M or S privilege mode, if siselect selects hpmcounter12, any access to sireg3 or sireg6 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 14: In M or S privilege mode, if siselect selects hpmcounter12 and XLEN = 64, any access to sireg4 or sireg5 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 15: In M or S privilege mode, if siselect selects hpmcounter12 and siselect = 0x41, any access to any sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 16: In M or S privilege mode, if siselect selects hpmcounter12 and the corresponding bit in mcounteren = 0 (the counter is not delegated to S-mode), any access to any sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 17: In M or S privilege mode, if any extension required for the underlying state of hpmcounter12 is not implemented, any access to that state through sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 18: When the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented, any attempt from VU-mode to access siselect or any sireg* that map to hpmcounter12 raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 19: When the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented and vsiselect selects hpmcounter12 (value 0x40-0x5F), any access to any vsireg* from M or S mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 20: When the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented and vsiselect selects hpmcounter12, any access from VS-mode to any vsireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception if menvcfg.CDE = 0.
RULE 21: When the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented and vsiselect selects hpmcounter12, any access from VS-mode to any vsireg* raises a virtual-instruction exception if menvcfg.CDE = 1.
RULE 22: If the HPM12 bit in scounteren is clear, a read of hpmcounter12 while executing in U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 23: If the HPM12 bit in scounteren is set, accesses to hpmcounter12 while executing in U-mode are permitted.
RULE 24: U-mode may only access hpmcounter12 when both the HPM12 bit in scounteren and the HPM12 bit in mcounteren are set.
RULE 25: If the HPM12 bit in scounteren is read-only zero, a read of hpmcounter12 while executing in U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 26: The OF bit in mhpmevent12 is set when the corresponding hpmcounter12 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 27: Overflow for hpmcounter12 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 28: After an overflow, hpmcounter12 wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit remains set.
RULE 29: Count overflow for hpmcounter12 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter12 or mhpmevent12 registers, only from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 30: If hpmcounter12 overflows while its associated OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 31: If the OF bit associated with hpmcounter12 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 32: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter12 sets its associated OF bit.
RULE 33: When the OF bit associated with hpmcounter12 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers.
RULE 34: The count-overflow-interrupt request generated by hpmcounter12 is treated as a standard local interrupt that corresponds to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 35: The LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers is the interrupt-pending bit for a count-overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter12.
RULE 36: The LCOFIE bit in the mie or sie registers is the interrupt-enable bit for a count-overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter12.
RULE 37: The mideleg register controls delegation of the count-overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter12 to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 38: If the associated privilege mode x is not implemented, the x INH bit in mhpmevent12 for hpmcounter12 is read-only zero.
RULE 39: When an x INH bit in mhpmevent12 for hpmcounter12 is set, counting of events for hpmcounter12 is inhibited while the processor is in privilege mode x.
RULE 40: When all x INH bits in mhpmevent12 for hpmcounter12 are zero, hpmcounter12 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 41: Read access to hpmcounter12 is controlled by mcounteren bit 12.
RULE 42: In VS-mode, read access to hpmcounter12 is also controlled by hcounteren bit 12.
RULE 43: scountovf bit 12 mirrors the OF bit in mhpmevent 12, which is the overflow indicator for the hardware performance counter associated with hpmcounter12.
RULE 44: If the HPM12 bit in hcounteren is clear, V=1, and the HPM12 bit in mcounteren is 1, then a read of hpmcounter12 causes a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 45: If the HPM12 bit in hcounteren is set and V=1, then access to hpmcounter12 is permitted provided no other architectural restriction applies.
RULE 46: In VU-mode, a read of hpmcounter12 is permitted only when both the HPM12 bits in hcounteren and scounteren are set; otherwise the read causes an exception.
RULE 47: Because hcounteren must be implemented, if its HPM12 bit is read-only zero then a read of hpmcounter12 while V=1 causes an exception.
RULE 48: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter12 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc0c; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 49: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter12 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc0c; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 50: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter12 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc0c; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 51: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter12 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc0c, a0; csrr a1, 0xc0c; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 52: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter12 register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0xc0c; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 53: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter12 register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc0c; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 54: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter12 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xc0c; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hpmcounter13
NUMBER: 0xc0d
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: hpmcounter13 is one of the additional unprivileged 64-bit hardware performance counters defined by the Zihpm extension.
RULE 2: hpmcounter13 is a 64-bit hardware performance counter when it is implemented.
RULE 3: Accessing hpmcounter13 when it is unimplemented may cause an illegal-instruction exception or may return a constant value.
RULE 4: In execution environments on RISC-V privileged platforms, access by lower-privileged modes to hpmcounter13 is controlled by privileged CSRs defined in the privileged architecture manual.
RULE 5: The hpmcounter13 CSR has MRW (machine-mode read/write) privilege.
RULE 6: The event counted by hpmcounter13 is selected by the mhpmevent13 CSR.
RULE 7: The mcounteren CSR controls whether hpmcounter13 is readable in lower privilege modes.
RULE 8: The mcountinhibit CSR can inhibit counting for hpmcounter13.
RULE 9: The counter mhpmcounter13 is incremented according to the value programmed in the corresponding event-selector CSR mhpmevent13.
RULE 10: The event-selector CSR mhpmevent13 is a 64-bit WARL register that controls which event causes mhpmcounter13 to increment.
RULE 11: Event value 0 in mhpmevent13 is defined to mean "no event".
RULE 12: A legal implementation may make both mhpmcounter13 and its corresponding event selector mhpmevent13 read-only zero, indicating the counter is not implemented.
RULE 13: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter13 has an arbitrary value.
RULE 14: Software can write a given value to mhpmcounter13.
RULE 15: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter13 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 16: The hpmcounter13 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter13 register.
RULE 17: If the HPM13 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read hpmcounter13 while executing in S-mode or U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 18: If the HPM13 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to hpmcounter13 is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode.
RULE 19: Reading or writing the mcounteren register does not affect the underlying hpmcounter13 counter, which continues to increment even when not accessible.
RULE 20: In harts with U-mode, the mcounteren register must be implemented and its field for hpmcounter13 is WARL and may be read-only zero, indicating that reads to hpmcounter13 will cause an illegal-instruction exception when executing in a less-privileged mode.
RULE 21: When the HPM13 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mhpmcounter13 register increments as usual.
RULE 22: When the HPM13 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mhpmcounter13 register does not increment.
RULE 23: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the HPM13 bit is treated as clear for the mhpmcounter13 register.
RULE 24: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the mhpmcounter13 register increments as usual.
RULE 25: When the siselect value selects counter 13, the CSR sireg or sireg2 could be used to access mhpmcounter13.
RULE 26: When the siselect value selects counter 13 and the counter is defined as 64 bits wide, the CSR sireg4 or sireg5 could be used to access the high-half CSR mhpmcounter13h.
RULE 27: If the HPM13 bit in the scounteren register is clear, a read of the hpmcounter13 register while executing in U-mode MUST cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 28: If the HPM13 bit in the scounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter13 register is permitted.
RULE 29: U-mode MAY only access the hpmcounter13 register when the HPM13 bit in both the scounteren register and the mcounteren register are set.
RULE 30: Any bit in scounteren, including the HPM13 bit that controls the hpmcounter13 register, MAY be read-only zero, and a zero value causes reads of the hpmcounter13 register in U-mode to raise an illegal-instruction exception, making that bit a WARL field.
RULE 31: The OF bit in the mhpmevent13 register is set when hpmcounter13 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 32: If hpmcounter13 overflows while its associated OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 33: If hpmcounter13 overflows while its associated OF bit is one, no interrupt request is generated.
RULE 34: The OF bit for hpmcounter13 also functions as a count-overflow-interrupt disable for hpmcounter13.
RULE 35: The count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by hpmcounter13 is treated as a standard local interrupt that corresponds to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 36: The mip and sip LCOFIP bits at position 13 are the interrupt-pending bits for the overflow interrupt of hpmcounter13, and the mie and sie LCOFIE bits at position 13 are the interrupt-enable bits for that interrupt.
RULE 37: Count overflow for hpmcounter13 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter13 or mhpmevent13 registers, only from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 38: If any INH bit (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in mhpmevent13 for hpmcounter13 is set, counting of events in the corresponding privilege mode is inhibited for hpmcounter13.
RULE 39: If all INH bits in mhpmevent13 for hpmcounter13 are zero, counting of events in all privilege modes is performed for hpmcounter13.
RULE 40: If a privilege mode is not implemented, the corresponding INH bit in mhpmevent13 for hpmcounter13 reads as zero.
RULE 41: When supervisor mode is implemented, the scountovf register bit that corresponds to hpmcounter13 provides a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit in mhpmevent13 for hpmcounter13.
RULE 42: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter13 sets the associated OF bit.
RULE 43: When the OF bit for hpmcounter13 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit at position 13 in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 44: The mideleg register controls the delegation of the overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter13 to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 45: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for hpmcounter13 is done by clearing its OF bit in conjunction with initializing hpmcounter13 to a starting value.
RULE 46: After hpmcounter13 has overflowed, both hpmcounter13 and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 47: Read access to hpmcounter13 is governed by the same mcounteren (or mcounteren and hcounteren) CSR bits that govern read access to scountovf bit 13.
RULE 48: In M-mode, hpmcounter13 is always readable.
RULE 49: In S-mode and HS-mode, hpmcounter13 reads as zero when mcounteren bit 13 is clear and reads its actual value when mcounteren bit 13 is set.
RULE 50: In VS-mode, hpmcounter13 reads as zero unless both mcounteren bit 13 and hcounteren bit 13 are set, in which case it reads its actual value.
RULE 51: If the HPM13 bit in the hcounteren register is clear, V=1, and the HPM13 bit in the mcounteren register is 1, then a read of the hpmcounter13 register causes a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 52: If the HPM13 bit in the hcounteren register is set and V=1, then access to the hpmcounter13 register is permitted unless another architectural rule explicitly prevents it.
RULE 53: In VU-mode, a read of the hpmcounter13 register is not permitted unless the HPM13 bit in both the hcounteren register and the scounteren register is set.
RULE 54: The HPM13 bit in the hcounteren register may be read-only zero, and when it is zero a read of the hpmcounter13 register will cause an exception when V=1.
RULE 55: The HPM13 bit in the hcounteren register is a WARL field that determines the behavior of reads to the hpmcounter13 register.
RULE 56: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter13 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc0d; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 57: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter13 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc0d; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 58: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter13 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc0d; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 59: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter13 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc0d, a0; csrr a1, 0xc0d; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 60: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter13 register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc0d; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 61: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter13 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xc0d; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hpmcounter14
NUMBER: 0xc0e
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zihpm
RULE 1: Accessing hpmcounter14 when it is unimplemented may cause an illegal-instruction exception or may return a constant value.
RULE 2: If the configuration used to select the events counted by hpmcounter14 is misconfigured, hpmcounter14 may return a constant value.
RULE 3: hpmcounter14 is a currently allocated unprivileged CSR that has privilege level URO.
RULE 4: The event selector mhpmevent14 controls which event causes mhpmcounter14 to increment.
RULE 5: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter14 may contain an arbitrary value.
RULE 6: Software may write any value to mhpmcounter14.
RULE 7: A write to the mhpmcounter14 CSR becomes visible only after the instruction that performed the write has otherwise completed.
RULE 8: When the HPM 14 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, a read of the hpmcounter14 register while executing in S-mode or U-mode MUST cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 9: When the HPM 14 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter14 register MUST be permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 10: The hpmcounter14 CSR is a read-only shadow of mhpmcounter14.
RULE 11: The HPM14 bit in the mcountinhibit register controls whether the mhpmcounter14 register increments.
RULE 12: When the HPM14 bit in mcountinhibit is clear, the mhpmcounter14 register increments as usual.
RULE 13: When the HPM14 bit in mcountinhibit is set, the mhpmcounter14 register does not increment.
RULE 14: The accessibility of the mhpmcounter14 register is not affected by the settings of the mcountinhibit register.
RULE 15: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as though the register were set to zero, causing the HPM14 bit to be treated as clear and the mhpmcounter14 register to increment as usual.
RULE 16: If menvcfg.CDE=0 while executing in M or S mode and siselect=0x4E, an illegal-instruction exception is raised on any attempt to access hpmcounter14.
RULE 17: If mcounteren[14]=0 while executing in M or S mode and siselect=0x4E, an illegal-instruction exception is raised on any attempt to access hpmcounter14.
RULE 18: If any extension required by the state underlying hpmcounter14 is not implemented, an attempt from M or S mode to access hpmcounter14 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 19: When the hypervisor extension is implemented, an attempt from VU-mode to access hpmcounter14 via sireg* raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 20: When the hypervisor extension is implemented and the current privilege mode is VS-mode, an attempt to access hpmcounter14 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception if menvcfg.CDE=0.
RULE 21: When the hypervisor extension is implemented and the current privilege mode is VS-mode, an attempt to access hpmcounter14 via sireg* raises a virtual-instruction exception if menvcfg.CDE=1.
RULE 22: When the hypervisor extension is implemented and vsiselect=0x4E, an attempt from M or S mode to access hpmcounter14 via vsireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 23: When the HPM14 bit in the scounteren CSR is clear, any attempt to read the hpmcounter14 register while executing in U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 24: When the HPM14 bit in the scounteren CSR is set, accesses to the hpmcounter14 register are permitted.
RULE 25: U-mode may access the hpmcounter14 register only if both the HPM14 bit in the scounteren CSR and the HPM14 bit in the mcounteren CSR are set.
RULE 26: The HPM14 bit in the scounteren CSR is a WARL field that may be implemented as a read-only zero, and when it is read-only zero reads of the hpmcounter14 register in U-mode must cause an exception.
RULE 27: The OF bit in mhpmevent14 is set when hpmcounter14 overflows and remains set until software writes it.
RULE 28: An overflow of hpmcounter14 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 29: When supervisor mode is implemented, the bit in scountovf that corresponds to mhpmevent14 reflects the OF status of hpmcounter14.
RULE 30: If hpmcounter14 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 31: If hpmcounter14 overflows while its OF bit is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 32: The OF bit in mhpmevent14 also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for hpmcounter14.
RULE 33: Writes to mhpmcounter14 or mhpmevent14 cannot cause an overflow of hpmcounter14.
RULE 34: Count overflow of hpmcounter14 can only result from hardware increments of the counter register, not from software writes.
RULE 35: A count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by hpmcounter14 is treated as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 36: The mip/sip LCOFIP bits are the interrupt-pending bits for the count-overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter14.
RULE 37: The mie/sie LCOFIE bits are the interrupt-enable bits for the count-overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter14.
RULE 38: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter14 sets the OF bit in mhpmevent14.
RULE 39: When the OF bit associated with hpmcounter14 is set, the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers will eventually be set.
RULE 40: The delegation of the count-overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter14 is controlled by the mideleg register.
RULE 41: After hpmcounter14 overflows, software must reinitialize both hpmcounter14 and the OF bit in mhpmevent14 to permit another overflow interrupt.
RULE 42: The MINH bit in mhpmevent14, when set, inhibits hpmcounter14 counting while the processor is in M-mode.
RULE 43: The SINH bit in mhpmevent14, when set, inhibits hpmcounter14 counting while the processor is in S/HS-mode.
RULE 44: The UINH bit in mhpmevent14, when set, inhibits hpmcounter14 counting while the processor is in U-mode.
RULE 45: The VSINH bit in mhpmevent14, when set, inhibits hpmcounter14 counting while the processor is in VS-mode.
RULE 46: The VUINH bit in mhpmevent14, when set, inhibits hpmcounter14 counting while the processor is in VU-mode.
RULE 47: If a privilege mode associated with an INH bit in mhpmevent14 is not implemented, that INH bit is read-only zero, leaving hpmcounter14 unaffected by that bit.
RULE 48: When all INH bits in mhpmevent14 are zero, hpmcounter14 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 49: Setting any of MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, or VUINH in mhpmevent14 prevents hpmcounter14 from counting events while the processor is in the corresponding privilege mode.
RULE 50: If the HPM14 bit in hcounteren is clear, V=1, and the HPM14 bit in mcounteren is 1, then a read of hpmcounter14 causes a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 51: In VU-mode, a read of hpmcounter14 is prohibited unless both the HPM14 bit in hcounteren and the HPM14 bit in scounteren are set.
RULE 52: The hcounteren register must be implemented, and its HPM14 bit may be read-only zero, which causes reads of hpmcounter14 to raise an exception when V=1.
RULE 53: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter14 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc0e; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 54: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter14 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc0e; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: hpmcounter15
NUMBER: 0xc0f
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: Accessing hpmcounter15 when it is unimplemented may cause an illegal-instruction exception or may return a constant value.
RULE 2: If the event-selection configuration for hpmcounter15 is mis-configured, hpmcounter15 may return a constant value.
RULE 3: hpmcounter15 has privilege URO, meaning it is unprivileged read-only.
RULE 4: After a hart reset, hpmcounter15 contains an arbitrary value.
RULE 5: Software may write a desired value to hpmcounter15.
RULE 6: Any CSR write to hpmcounter15 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 7: Implementations should provide hpmcounter15, but a legal implementation may make hpmcounter15 read-only zero.
RULE 8: A legal implementation may also make the corresponding event selector mhpmevent15 read-only zero, affecting hpmcounter15.
RULE 9: The event selector CSR mhpmevent15 directly determines which events cause hpmcounter15 to increment.
RULE 10: The high-half event selector CSR mhpmevent15h is provided only if the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, and it can affect which events increment hpmcounter15.
RULE 11: The hpmcounter15 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter15 register.
RULE 12: When the HPM15 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, any attempt to read the hpmcounter15 register while executing in S-mode or U-mode MUST cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: When the HPM15 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter15 register is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode.
RULE 14: The settings in the mcounteren register only control accessibility of the hpmcounter15 register and do not affect its underlying counter.
RULE 15: Reading or writing the mcounteren register does not affect the underlying counter of hpmcounter15, and the hpmcounter15 value continues to increment even when the register is not accessible.
RULE 16: The accessibility of hpmcounter15 is not affected by the settings of the mcountinhibit register.
RULE 17: If the HPM15 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, hpmcounter15 increments as usual.
RULE 18: If the HPM15 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, hpmcounter15 does not increment.
RULE 19: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as if the HPM15 bit were clear, and hpmcounter15 increments as usual.
RULE 20: When siselect = 0x4F, the hpmcounter15 register is accessed through the sireg indirect register provided that mcounteren[15] = 1 and menvcfg.CDE = 1.
RULE 21: When siselect = 0x4F, the sireg4 indirect register provides access to the high half of hpmcounter15 (hpmcounter15h).
RULE 22: In M-mode or S-mode, if menvcfg.CDE = 0, any attempt to read or write hpmcounter15 via sireg while siselect = 0x4F raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 23: In M-mode or S-mode, any attempt to access hpmcounter15 via the sireg3 or sireg6 indirect registers raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 24: In M-mode or S-mode on a 64-bit implementation (XLEN = 64), any attempt to access hpmcounter15 via the sireg4 or sireg5 indirect registers raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 25: In M-mode or S-mode, if mcounteren[15] = 0, any attempt to read or write hpmcounter15 via sireg while siselect = 0x4F raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 26: Access to hpmcounter15 via sireg is blocked for less-privileged modes when either mstateen0[60] = 0 or hstateen0[60] = 0, preventing the operation entirely.
RULE 27: If any architectural extension required for the underlying state of hpmcounter15 is not implemented, an attempt from M-mode or S-mode to access hpmcounter15 through sireg raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 28: When the H extension is implemented and vsiselect = 0x4F, any attempt from M-mode or S-mode to access hpmcounter15 via a vsireg indirect register raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 29: When the H extension is implemented, if a VS-mode program attempts to access hpmcounter15 via a virtual sireg (i.e., a vsireg) while menvcfg.CDE = 0, an illegal-instruction exception is raised; if menvcfg.CDE = 1, a virtual-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 30: When the HPM15 bit in the scounteren register is clear, a read of the hpmcounter15 register in U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 31: When the HPM15 bit in the scounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter15 register is permitted, subject to any additional conditions.
RULE 32: U-mode may read the hpmcounter15 register only when the HPM15 bits in both the scounteren and mcounteren registers are set.
RULE 33: The OF bit in the mhpmevent register paired with hpmcounter15 is set when hpmcounter15 overflows and remains set until software writes it.
RULE 34: Overflow of hpmcounter15 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits of hpmcounter15.
RULE 35: When hpmcounter15 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while its sticky OF bit remains set.
RULE 36: If a privilege mode x is not implemented, the corresponding x INH bit in the mhpmevent register paired with hpmcounter15 is read-only zero.
RULE 37: When an x INH bit in the mhpmevent register paired with hpmcounter15 is set, counting of events in privilege mode x is inhibited.
RULE 38: When all five x INH bits in the mhpmevent register paired with hpmcounter15 are zero, counting of events occurs in all privilege modes.
RULE 39: If supervisor mode is implemented, the scountovf register contains a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit that belongs to hpmcounter15.
RULE 40: If hpmcounter15 overflows while its associated OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 41: If the OF bit associated with hpmcounter15 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated, and the OF bit functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for hpmcounter15.
RULE 42: Count overflow for hpmcounter15 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter15 or its paired mhpmevent register, only from hardware increments of hpmcounter15.
RULE 43: Generation of a count overflow interrupt request by hpmcounter15 sets its associated OF bit.
RULE 44: When the OF bit associated with hpmcounter15 is set, it eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 45: The count overflow interrupt request generated by hpmcounter15 is treated as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 46: The LCOFIE bits in the mie and sie registers are the interrupt-enable bits for the count overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter15.
RULE 47: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for hpmcounter15 is done by clearing its OF bit in conjunction with initializing hpmcounter15 to a starting value.
RULE 48: After hpmcounter15 has overflowed, both hpmcounter15 and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 49: The overflow status of the event counted by hpmcounter15 is indicated by scountovf bit 15, which contains a shadow copy of the OF bit in mhpmevent15.
RULE 50: In M-mode, hpmcounter15 is always readable.
RULE 51: In S-mode, hpmcounter15 is readable only when mcounteren bit 15 is set; otherwise it reads as zero.
RULE 52: In VS-mode, hpmcounter15 is readable only when both mcounteren bit 15 and hcounteren bit 15 are set; otherwise it reads as zero.
RULE 53: When the HPM15 bit in the hcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the hpmcounter15 register while V=1 will cause a virtual-instruction exception if the HPM15 bit in mcounteren is 1.
RULE 54: When the HPM15 bit in the hcounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter15 register is permitted while V=1 unless prevented for some other reason.
RULE 55: In VU-mode, the hpmcounter15 register is not readable unless the HPM15 bit is set in both hcounteren and scounteren.
RULE 56: The hcounteren register must be implemented, and the HPM15 bit in it may be read-only zero, which causes reads to the hpmcounter15 register to raise an exception when V=1.
RULE 57: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter15 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc0f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 58: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter15 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc0f; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: hpmcounter16
NUMBER: 0xc10
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: Accessing an unimplemented hpmcounter16 may cause an illegal-instruction exception or may return a constant value.
RULE 2: If the configuration used to select the events counted by hpmcounter16 is misconfigured, the counter may return a constant value.
RULE 3: mhpmcounter16 together with mhpmevent16 forms a 64-bit WARL register that selects the event to be counted.
RULE 4: Implementations should provide mhpmcounter16, but may legally implement it as a read-only register hard-wired to zero.
RULE 5: A write to mhpmcounter16 becomes visible only after the instruction that performed the write has completed execution.
RULE 6: If the HPM16 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, any attempt to read the hpmcounter16 CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 7: If the HPM16 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter16 CSR is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode.
RULE 8: The hpmcounter16 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter16 register.
RULE 9: The value read from the hpmcounter16 CSR reflects the current value of the mhpmcounter16 register, which continues to increment regardless of the accessibility settings in the mcounteren register.
RULE 10: In harts that implement U-mode, the mcounteren register must be present and its HPM16 field may be a read-only zero, and when that field is zero reads to the hpmcounter16 CSR in S-mode or U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: When the privilege mode is M or S, siselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F that selects hpmcounter16, and the mcounteren bit for hpmcounter16 is 0, any attempt to access hpmcounter16 via any sireg* must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: When the privilege mode is M or S, siselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F that selects hpmcounter16, and menvcfg.CDE is 0, any attempt to access hpmcounter16 via any sireg* must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: When the privilege mode is M or S, siselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F that selects hpmcounter16, and XLEN is 64, any attempt to access the high-half part of hpmcounter16 via sireg4 or sireg5 must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 14: When the privilege mode is M or S and the architectural state of hpmcounter16 depends on an extension that is not implemented, any attempt to access hpmcounter16 through the corresponding sireg* must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 15: If the HPM16 bit in scounteren is clear, a read of hpmcounter16 while executing in U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 16: If the HPM16 bit in scounteren is set, a read of hpmcounter16 while executing in U-mode is permitted.
RULE 17: The implementation may make the HPM16 bit in scounteren read-only zero, and in that case a read of hpmcounter16 while executing in U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 18: U-mode may access hpmcounter16 only when both scounteren.HPM16 and mcounteren.HPM16 are set.
RULE 19: The OF bit for hpmcounter16 is set when hpmcounter16 overflows and remains set until software writes the OF bit.
RULE 20: After hpmcounter16 overflows, the counter value wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit for hpmcounter16 remains set, so no information is lost.
RULE 21: If hpmcounter16 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 22: If the OF bit for hpmcounter16 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 23: The OF bit for hpmcounter16 also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for hpmcounter16.
RULE 24: Count overflow of hpmcounter16 never results from writes to mhpmcounter16 or mhpmevent16 registers, only from hardware increments of hpmcounter16.
RULE 25: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter16 sets the OF bit associated with hpmcounter16.
RULE 26: When the OF bit for hpmcounter16 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 27: The count-overflow-interrupt request generated by hpmcounter16 is treated as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 28: The mip and sip LCOFIP bits are the interrupt-pending bits for the count-overflow-interrupt generated by hpmcounter16, and the mie and sie LCOFIE bits are the interrupt-enable bits for that interrupt.
RULE 29: The mideleg register controls whether the count-overflow-interrupt generated by hpmcounter16 is delegated to S-mode or remains in M-mode.
RULE 30: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for hpmcounter16 is done by clearing the OF bit for hpmcounter16 in conjunction with initializing hpmcounter16 to a starting value.
RULE 31: After hpmcounter16 has overflowed, hpmcounter16 and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated for hpmcounter16.
RULE 32: Each of the five x INH bits associated with hpmcounter16, when set, inhibits counting of events for hpmcounter16 while the processor is in privilege mode x.
RULE 33: If all five x INH bits associated with hpmcounter16 are zero, hpmcounter16 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 34: For each x INH bit associated with hpmcounter16, if privilege mode x is not implemented, that x INH bit is read-only zero.
RULE 35: The hpmcounter16 CSR is an hpmcounter CSR whose read access is mediated by the mcounteren CSR and, in VS-mode, also by the hcounteren CSR.
RULE 36: In M-mode, reads of the hpmcounter16 CSR are always permitted.
RULE 37: In S-mode, reads of the hpmcounter16 CSR are permitted only when bit 16 of the mcounteren CSR is set; otherwise reads return zero.
RULE 38: In VS-mode, reads of the hpmcounter16 CSR are permitted only when both bit 16 of the mcounteren CSR and bit 16 of the hcounteren CSR are set; otherwise reads return zero.
RULE 39: If the HPM16 bit in hcounteren is clear, V=1, and the HPM16 bit in mcounteren is 1, then a read of hpmcounter16 causes a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 40: In VU-mode, hpmcounter16 is not readable unless the HPM16 bits are set in both hcounteren and scounteren.
RULE 41: The hcounteren CSR must be implemented, and any of its bits, including the HPM16 bit, may be read-only zero, which causes reads to hpmcounter16 to raise an exception when V=1.
RULE 42: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter16 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc10; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 43: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter16 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc10; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 44: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter16 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc10; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 45: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter16 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc10, a0; csrr a1, 0xc10; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
