RULE 52: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter18 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc12; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 53: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter18 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc12, a0; csrr a1, 0xc12; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 54: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter18 register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc12; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 55: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter18 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xc12; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hpmcounter3
NUMBER: 0xc03
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: hpmcounter3 is an unprivileged 64-bit hardware performance counter defined by the Zihpm extension, which adds up to 29 additional counters named hpmcounter3-hpmcounter31.
RULE 2: Accessing an unimplemented hpmcounter3 may cause an illegal-instruction exception or may return a constant value.
RULE 3: If the configuration used to select the events counted by hpmcounter3 is misconfigured, hpmcounter3 may return a constant value.
RULE 4: The hpmcounter3 CSR resides at address 0xC03 and is accessed with URO privilege.
RULE 5: The hpmcounter3h CSR resides at address 0xC83 and is accessed with URO privilege.
RULE 6: The hpmcounter3 register is readable and writable in machine mode (MRW privilege).
RULE 7: In S-mode indirect CSR mapping, the entry with siselect = 0x43 maps sireg to the primary CSR hpmcounter3.
RULE 8: In the same entry, sireg4 maps to the high-word CSR hpmcounter3h, which is the high-word part of hpmcounter3.
RULE 9: No other fields in the siselect = 0x43 entry provide a mapping to hpmcounter3.
RULE 10: Any indirect CSR access in S-mode that uses siselect = 0x43 accesses hpmcounter3 as the primary CSR.
RULE 11: No other indirect-CSR entries map to hpmcounter3.
RULE 12: After a hart reset, the architectural value of mhpmcounter3 is arbitrary.
RULE 13: Software can write an explicit value to mhpmcounter3.
RULE 14: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter3 takes effect only after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 15: The event-selector CSR mhpmevent3, which is a 64-bit WARL register, determines which events cause mhpmcounter3 to increment.
RULE 16: Event code 0 is defined to mean "no event".
RULE 17: If mhpmevent3 is programmed to 0, mhpmcounter3 will not increment for any event.
RULE 18: A legal implementation may make mhpmcounter3 and its corresponding event selector read-only zero.
RULE 19: If the HPM3 bit in the mcounteren register is clear and the processor is executing in S-mode or U-mode, any attempt to read the hpmcounter3 register causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 20: If the HPM3 bit in the mcounteren register is set, reads of the hpmcounter3 register are permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode.
RULE 21: The hpmcounter3 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter3 register, and its reads return the current value of mhpmcounter3.
RULE 22: Writing to the hpmcounter3 CSR is not permitted because it is read-only.
RULE 23: The value of mhpmcounter3, and therefore the value observed through hpmcounter3, continues to increment regardless of the HPM3 bit setting in the mcounteren register.
RULE 24: A read of the hpmcounter3 register does not affect the underlying mhpmcounter3 counter.
RULE 25: An attempted write to the hpmcounter3 register does not affect the underlying mhpmcounter3 counter.
RULE 26: The counter-inhibit register mcountinhibit does not affect the accessibility of hpmcounter3.
RULE 27: When the HPM3 bit in mcountinhibit is clear, hpmcounter3 increments as usual.
RULE 28: When the HPM3 bit in mcountinhibit is set, hpmcounter3 does not increment.
RULE 29: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as though the register were set to zero, the HPM3 bit is treated as clear, and hpmcounter3 increments as usual.
RULE 30: hpmcounter3 may be accessed through sireg* only when mcounteren[3] = 1, menvcfg.CDE = 1, and siselect = 0x43.
RULE 31: When siselect = 0x43, the CSR sireg exposes the register hpmcounter3.
RULE 32: If menvcfg.CDE = 0, any access to hpmcounter3 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 33: If mcounteren[3] = 0, an access to hpmcounter3 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 34: If the extension indicated by the "2" marker for hpmcounter3 is not implemented, an access to hpmcounter3 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 35: Attempts to access hpmcounter3 via sireg3 or sireg6 do not raise an illegal-instruction exception because hpmcounter3 is accessed via sireg.
RULE 36: Attempts to access hpmcounter3 via sireg4 or sireg5 when XLEN = 64 do not raise an illegal-instruction exception because hpmcounter3 is accessed via sireg.
RULE 37: If the HPM3 bit in the scounteren CSR is clear, a U-mode read of hpmcounter3 MUST raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 38: If the HPM3 bit in the scounteren CSR is set, accesses to hpmcounter3 are permitted, subject to the additional requirement on the mcounteren CSR.
RULE 39: U-mode access to hpmcounter3 is allowed only when both the HPM3 bit in scounteren and the HPM3 bit in mcounteren are set.
RULE 40: The scounteren CSR MUST be implemented, and any of its bits that are read-only zero cause reads to the associated counter, including hpmcounter3, to raise an illegal-instruction exception when executing in U-mode.
RULE 41: The OF bit in mhpmevent3 is the overflow status and interrupt disable bit that is set when hpmcounter3 overflows.
RULE 42: The MINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events in M-mode for hpmcounter3.
RULE 43: The SINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events in S/HS-mode for hpmcounter3.
RULE 44: The UINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events in U-mode for hpmcounter3.
RULE 45: The VSINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events in VS-mode for hpmcounter3.
RULE 46: The VUINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events in VU-mode for hpmcounter3.
RULE 47: Bits 57-56 of mhpmevent3 are reserved (WPRI) and have no defined function for hpmcounter3.
RULE 48: If the M-mode privilege is not implemented, the MINH bit in mhpmevent3 reads as zero and is read-only for hpmcounter3.
RULE 49: If the S/HS-mode privilege is not implemented, the SINH bit in mhpmevent3 reads as zero and is read-only for hpmcounter3.
RULE 50: If the U-mode privilege is not implemented, the UINH bit in mhpmevent3 reads as zero and is read-only for hpmcounter3.
RULE 51: If the VS-mode privilege is not implemented, the VSINH bit in mhpmevent3 reads as zero and is read-only for hpmcounter3.
RULE 52: If the VU-mode privilege is not implemented, the VUINH bit in mhpmevent3 reads as zero and is read-only for hpmcounter3.
RULE 53: When all INH bits (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in mhpmevent3 are zero, hpmcounter3 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 54: The OF bit in mhpmevent3 is set when hpmcounter3 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 55: Overflow of hpmcounter3 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 56: After hpmcounter3 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit remains set, resulting in no loss of information.
RULE 57: If hpmcounter3 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 58: If the OF bit for hpmcounter3 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 59: The OF bit for hpmcounter3 also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable.
RULE 60: Count overflow for hpmcounter3 never results from writes to mhpmcounter3 or mhpmevent3, only from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 61: A count overflow interrupt request generated by hpmcounter3 is treated as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 62: The mip and sip LCOFIP bits are the interrupt-pending bits for the overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter3.
RULE 63: The mie and sie LCOFIE bits are the interrupt-enable bits for the overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter3.
RULE 64: Generation of a count overflow interrupt request by hpmcounter3 sets its associated OF bit.
RULE 65: When the OF bit for hpmcounter3 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 66: The mideleg register controls whether the overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter3 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 67: There are no separate overflow status and overflow interrupt enable bits for hpmcounter3; overflow interrupt generation is enabled by clearing the OF bit in conjunction with initializing the counter.
RULE 68: After hpmcounter3 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 69: scountovf bit 3 is the shadow copy of the overflow bit for hpmcounter3.
RULE 70: Read access to hpmcounter3 is subject to the same mcounteren (or mcounteren and hcounteren) CSR permissions that mediate access to the hpmcounter CSRs by S-mode (or VS-mode).
RULE 71: In M-mode, hpmcounter3 is always readable.
RULE 72: In S-mode (or HS-mode), hpmcounter3 is readable when mcounteren bit 3 is set, and otherwise reads as zero.
RULE 73: In VS-mode, hpmcounter3 is readable when both mcounteren bit 3 and hcounteren bit 3 are set, and otherwise reads as zero.
RULE 74: If the HPM3 bit in hcounteren is clear, V=1, and the HPM3 bit in mcounteren is set, then a read of hpmcounter3 causes a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 75: If the HPM3 bit in hcounteren is set, then accesses to hpmcounter3 are permitted when V=1 unless another architectural rule prevents the access.
RULE 76: In VU-mode, a read of hpmcounter3 is not permitted unless the HPM3 bits are set in both hcounteren and scounteren.
RULE 77: The HPM3 bit in hcounteren may be implemented as a read-only zero, and when it is zero any read of hpmcounter3 raises an exception when V=1.
RULE 78: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter3 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc03; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 79: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter3 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc03; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 80: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter3 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc03; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 81: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter3 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc03, a0; csrr a1, 0xc03; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 82: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter3 register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0xc03; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 83: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter3 register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc03; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 84: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter3 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xc03; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hpmcounter4
NUMBER: 0xc04
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: Accessing hpmcounter4 when it is unimplemented may cause an illegal-instruction exception or may return a constant value.
RULE 2: If the event-selection configuration for hpmcounter4 is misconfigured, hpmcounter4 may return a constant value.
RULE 3: The CSR located at address 0xC04 is named hpmcounter4, is accessed with URO privilege, and is defined as a performance-monitoring counter.
RULE 4: After a hart reset, the mhpmcounter4 register contains an arbitrary (undefined) value.
RULE 5: Software may write any value to mhpmcounter4, and the written value becomes the new contents of the register.
RULE 6: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter4 takes effect only after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 7: The 64-bit WARL event selector CSR mhpmevent4 determines which hardware event causes mhpmcounter4 to increment.
RULE 8: A conforming implementation may instead make mhpmcounter4 a read-only register that always returns zero.
RULE 9: The hpmcounter4 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter4 register.
RULE 10: When the HPM4 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the hpmcounter4 register while executing in S-mode or U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: If the HPM4 bit in the mcountinhibit CSR is clear, hpmcounter4 increments as usual.
RULE 12: If the HPM4 bit in the mcountinhibit CSR is set, hpmcounter4 does not increment.
RULE 13: If the mcountinhibit CSR is not implemented, the implementation behaves as if the register were zero, causing hpmcounter4 to increment as usual.
RULE 14: If the HPM 4 bit in scounteren is clear, any attempt by U-mode to read hpmcounter4 MUST cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 15: If the HPM 4 bit in scounteren is set, U-mode is permitted to access hpmcounter4.
RULE 16: The scounteren CSR MUST be implemented, and any of its bits, including the HPM 4 bit, MAY be read-only zero, which causes reads of hpmcounter4 from U-mode to raise an exception.
RULE 17: U-mode MAY access hpmcounter4 only if both scounteren.HPM 4 and mcounteren.HPM 4 are set.
RULE 18: In the mhpmevent4 register, bit 63 (the OF field) is the overflow status and interrupt disable bit that is set when hpmcounter4 overflows.
RULE 19: In the mhpmevent4 register, bit 62 (the MINH field) inhibits counting of events in M-mode for hpmcounter4 when set.
RULE 20: In the mhpmevent4 register, bit 61 (the SINH field) inhibits counting of events in S/HS-mode for hpmcounter4 when set.
RULE 21: In the mhpmevent4 register, bit 60 (the UINH field) inhibits counting of events in U-mode for hpmcounter4 when set.
RULE 22: In the mhpmevent4 register, bit 59 (the VSINH field) inhibits counting of events in VS-mode for hpmcounter4 when set.
RULE 23: In the mhpmevent4 register, bit 58 (the VUINH field) inhibits counting of events in VU-mode for hpmcounter4 when set.
RULE 24: In the mhpmevent4 register, bits 57-56 are reserved (WPRI) and have no defined effect on hpmcounter4.
RULE 25: If a privilege mode corresponding to an INH bit in mhpmevent4 is not implemented, the INH bit reads as zero and is read-only for hpmcounter4.
RULE 26: When any INH bit (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in mhpmevent4 is set, hpmcounter4 does not count events while the processor is executing in the corresponding privilege mode.
RULE 27: If all INH bits in mhpmevent4 are zero, hpmcounter4 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 28: The OF bit in mhpmevent4 is set when hpmcounter4 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 29: Overflow of hpmcounter4 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 30: After hpmcounter4 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit remains set, preserving information.
RULE 31: If hpmcounter4 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 32: If the OF bit of hpmcounter4 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated, and the OF bit also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for hpmcounter4.
RULE 33: Overflow of hpmcounter4 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter4 or mhpmevent4 registers, only from hardware increments.
RULE 34: The count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by hpmcounter4 is treated as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers, with the LCOFIP and LCOFIE bits serving as the pending and enable bits respectively.
RULE 35: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter4 sets its associated OF bit.
RULE 36: When the OF bit of hpmcounter4 is set, it eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers, though not necessarily immediately.
RULE 37: The mideleg register controls whether the count-overflow-interrupt generated by hpmcounter4 is delegated to S-mode or remains in M-mode.
RULE 38: Once hpmcounter4 has overflowed, it and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 39: The overflow flag for hpmcounter4 is the OF bit in mhpmevent4 and is shadow-copied into scountovf bit 4.
RULE 40: Read access to hpmcounter4 in S-mode is granted only when the corresponding bit for counter 4 in the mcounteren CSR is set.
RULE 41: Read access to hpmcounter4 in VS-mode is granted only when the corresponding bit for counter 4 in both the mcounteren and hcounteren CSRs are set.
RULE 42: If the HPM4 bit in hcounteren is clear and the HPM4 bit in mcounteren is 1, attempts to read the hpmcounter4 register while V=1 will cause a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 43: When the HPM4 bit in hcounteren is set, access to the hpmcounter4 register is permitted when V=1 unless some other reason prevents it.
RULE 44: In VU-mode, the hpmcounter4 register is not readable unless the HPM4 bit is set in both hcounteren and scounteren.
RULE 45: If the HPM4 bit in hcounteren is implemented as a read-only zero, reads of the hpmcounter4 register will cause an exception when V=1.
RULE 46: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter4 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc04; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 47: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter4 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc04; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 48: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter4 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc04; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 49: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter4 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc04, a0; csrr a1, 0xc04; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 50: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter4 register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc04; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 51: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter4 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xc04; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hpmcounter5
NUMBER: 0xc05
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: H, Smcntrpmf, Smcsrind, Smstateen, Sscofpmf, Sscsrind, Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: If hpmcounter5 is not implemented on a platform, an attempt to access it may raise an illegal-instruction exception or may return a constant value.
RULE 2: If the event-selection configuration for hpmcounter5 is misconfigured, reads of hpmcounter5 may return a constant value.
RULE 3: Event 0 is defined to mean "no event," and if mhpmevent5 is programmed with 0, hpmcounter5 will not count any events.
RULE 4: A conforming implementation may have hpmcounter5 read-only 0 together with mhpmevent5 read-only 0.
RULE 5: After a hart reset, hpmcounter5 contains an arbitrary value and may be written with a given value, with any CSR write taking effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 6: mhpmevent5h exists only when the Sscofpmf extension is present, and it supplies the high-half of the 64-bit event selector for hpmcounter5.
RULE 7: When the HPM5 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, a read of the hpmcounter5 CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 8: When the HPM5 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter5 CSR is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 9: The hpmcounter5 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter5 register.
RULE 10: The settings in the mcounteren register control only the accessibility of the hpmcounter5 CSR; reading or writing the hpmcounter5 CSR does not affect the underlying mhpmcounter5 counter, which continues to increment even when the hpmcounter5 CSR is not accessible.
RULE 11: The increment behavior of mhpmcounter5 is controlled by the HPM5 bit in the mcountinhibit register.
RULE 12: When the HPM5 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, mhpmcounter5 increments as usual.
RULE 13: When the HPM5 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, mhpmcounter5 does not increment.
RULE 14: The settings of the mcountinhibit register do not affect the accessibility of mhpmcounter5.
RULE 15: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as if the register were zero, treating the HPM5 bit as clear and causing mhpmcounter5 to increment as usual.
RULE 16: When mcounteren[5]=1, menvcfg.CDE=1, and siselect=0x45, the state of hpmcounter5 is accessible via sireg.
RULE 17: When siselect=0x45, any read or write of sireg accesses hpmcounter5.
RULE 18: In M-mode or S-mode, if siselect is in the range 0x40-0x5F and menvcfg.CDE=0, an attempt to access hpmcounter5 via sireg raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 19: In M-mode or S-mode, if siselect is in the range 0x40-0x5F and mcounteren[5]=0, an attempt to access hpmcounter5 via sireg raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 20: In M-mode or S-mode, if the extension indicated by superscript 2 for hpmcounter5 is not implemented, an attempt to access hpmcounter5 via sireg raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 21: When the Smstateen extension is implemented and mstateen0[60]=0, any attempt to access hpmcounter5 via sireg from a privilege mode less privileged than M-mode is prevented.
RULE 22: If mstateen0[60]=0 or hstateen0[60]=0, the illegal-instruction exception rules for hpmcounter5 do not apply because access to sireg (and thus hpmcounter5) is already blocked.
RULE 23: When the HPM5 bit in the scounteren register is clear, attempts to read the hpmcounter5 register while executing in U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 24: When the HPM5 bit in the scounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter5 register is permitted, subject to the condition on mcounteren described below.
RULE 25: U-mode may only access the hpmcounter5 register if both the HPM5 bit in the scounteren register and the HPM5 bit in the mcounteren register are set.
RULE 26: If the HPM5 bit in the scounteren register is read-only zero, reads of the hpmcounter5 register in U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 27: The OF bit in mhpmevent5 is set when hpmcounter5 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 28: If the MINH bit in mhpmevent5 is set, counting of events in hpmcounter5 is inhibited while the processor is in M-mode.
RULE 29: If the SINH bit in mhpmevent5 is set, counting of events in hpmcounter5 is inhibited while the processor is in S/HS-mode.
RULE 30: If the UINH bit in mhpmevent5 is set, counting of events in hpmcounter5 is inhibited while the processor is in U-mode.
RULE 31: If the VSINH bit in mhpmevent5 is set, counting of events in hpmcounter5 is inhibited while the processor is in VS-mode.
RULE 32: If the VUINH bit in mhpmevent5 is set, counting of events in hpmcounter5 is inhibited while the processor is in VU-mode.
RULE 33: When all five INH bits in mhpmevent5 are zero, hpmcounter5 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 34: For any privilege mode that is not implemented, the corresponding INH bit in mhpmevent5 reads as zero, so it does not inhibit counting for hpmcounter5.
RULE 35: Overflow of hpmcounter5 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits because hpmcounter5 values are unsigned.
RULE 36: After hpmcounter5 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit remains set, so no information is lost.
RULE 37: If hpmcounter5 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 38: If hpmcounter5 overflows while its OF bit is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 39: hpmcounter5 can overflow only as a result of hardware increments; writes to mhpmcounter5 or mhpmevent5 never cause overflow.
RULE 40: The count-overflow interrupt request generated by hpmcounter5 is mapped to bit 13 of the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 41: The LCOFIP bit in mip/sip is the interrupt-pending flag for the count-overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter5, and the LCOFIE bit in mie/sie is the corresponding interrupt-enable flag.
RULE 42: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt request by hpmcounter5 sets the OF bit in mhpmevent5.
RULE 43: When the OF bit for hpmcounter5 is set, it eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in mip/sip, though not necessarily immediately.
RULE 44: The mideleg register determines whether the count-overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter5 is delegated to S-mode or remains in M-mode.
RULE 45: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for hpmcounter5 is performed by clearing the OF bit together with initializing hpmcounter5 to a starting value.
RULE 46: After hpmcounter5 has overflowed, both hpmcounter5 and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 47: The overflow condition of hpmcounter5 is reflected in the OF bit of mhpmevent5, which is shadowed as scountovf bit 5.
RULE 48: In M-mode, scountovf bit 5, which indicates overflow of hpmcounter5, is always readable.
RULE 49: In S-mode (or HS-mode), scountovf bit 5, which indicates overflow of hpmcounter5, is readable only when mcounteren bit 5 is set, otherwise it reads as zero.
RULE 50: In VS-mode, scountovf bit 5, which indicates overflow of hpmcounter5, is readable only when both mcounteren bit 5 and hcounteren bit 5 are set, otherwise it reads as zero.
RULE 51: If the HPM5 bit in hcounteren is clear, V=1, and the HPM5 bit in mcounteren is 1, then a read of hpmcounter5 causes a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 52: If the HPM5 bit in hcounteren is set and V=1, then access to hpmcounter5 is permitted unless some other reason prevents it.
RULE 53: In VU-mode, hpmcounter5 is readable only if the HPM5 bit is set in both hcounteren and scounteren; otherwise it is not readable.
RULE 54: The hcounteren register must be implemented, and its HPM5 bit may be read-only zero, which causes reads of hpmcounter5 to raise an exception when V=1.

REGISTER: hpmcounter6
NUMBER: 0xc06
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: Accessing an unimplemented hpmcounter6 may cause an illegal-instruction exception or may return a constant value.
RULE 2: If the configuration that selects the events counted by hpmcounter6 is misconfigured, hpmcounter6 may return a constant value.
RULE 3: On RISC-V privileged platforms, privileged CSRs control access by lower-privileged modes to hpmcounter6.
RULE 4: After a hart reset, the mhpmcounter6 register holds an arbitrary value.
RULE 5: The mhpmcounter6 register can be written with a given value; any CSR write takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 6: The event selector CSR mhpmevent6 is a 64-bit WARL register that controls which event causes mhpmcounter6 to increment.
RULE 7: The mhpmevent6h CSR is provided only if the Sscofpmf extension is implemented; it selects events for mhpmcounter6.
RULE 8: A legal implementation can implement mhpmcounter6 as a read-only zero register.
RULE 9: The accessibility of hpmcounter6 is not affected by the settings in the mcountinhibit register.
RULE 10: The HPM 6 bit in mcountinhibit determines whether hpmcounter6 increments.
RULE 11: When the HPM 6 bit in mcountinhibit is clear (0), hpmcounter6 increments as usual.
RULE 12: When the HPM 6 bit in mcountinhibit is set (1), hpmcounter6 does not increment.
RULE 13: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as though it were zero, and hpmcounter6 increments normally.
RULE 14: hpmcounter6 can be read or written via sireg* when siselect = 0x46, mcounteren[6] = 1, and menvcfg.CDE = 1.
RULE 15: In M or S privilege mode, if menvcfg.CDE = 0, any access to hpmcounter6 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 16: In M or S privilege mode, any access to hpmcounter6 via sireg3 or sireg6 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 17: In M or S privilege mode on a 64-bit XLEN implementation, any access to hpmcounter6 via sireg4 or sireg5 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 18: In M or S privilege mode, if mcounteren[6] = 0, any access to hpmcounter6 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 19: If an extension required for the underlying state of hpmcounter6 is not implemented, any access to hpmcounter6 via sireg* in M or S mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 20: When the hypervisor extension is implemented and the current privilege mode is VS-mode or VU-mode, a direct access to the vsireg* that corresponds to hpmcounter6 raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 21: When the hypervisor extension is implemented and the current privilege mode is VU-mode, any access to the sireg* that corresponds to hpmcounter6 raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 22: When the hypervisor extension is implemented and vsiselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, any access to the vsireg* that corresponds to hpmcounter6 from M or S mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 23: When the hypervisor extension is implemented and the current privilege mode is VS-mode, an attempt to access hpmcounter6 via sireg* (interpreted as vsireg*) raises an illegal-instruction exception if menvcfg.CDE = 0, and raises a virtual-instruction exception if menvcfg.CDE = 1.
RULE 24: When the HPM6 bit in scounteren is clear, any attempt to read hpmcounter6 while executing in U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 25: When the HPM6 bit in scounteren is set, reading hpmcounter6 while executing in U-mode is permitted.
RULE 26: If the HPM6 bit in scounteren is read-only zero, reads of hpmcounter6 while executing in U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 27: U-mode may access hpmcounter6 only when both the HPM6 bit in scounteren and the HPM6 bit in mcounteren are set.
RULE 28: The OF bit in the mhpmevent register that corresponds to hpmcounter6 is set when hpmcounter6 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 29: Overflow for hpmcounter6 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 30: After an overflow, hpmcounter6 wraps around and continues counting while its sticky OF bit remains set, resulting in no loss of information.
RULE 31: For each privilege-mode INH bit (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in the mhpmevent register that corresponds to hpmcounter6, the bit is read-only zero if the associated privilege mode is not implemented.
RULE 32: When any of the five INH bits for hpmcounter6 are set, counting of events for hpmcounter6 is inhibited while the processor is in the corresponding privilege mode.
RULE 33: If all five INH bits for hpmcounter6 are zero, hpmcounter6 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 34: If supervisor mode is implemented, the scountovf register contains a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit for hpmcounter6.
RULE 35: If hpmcounter6 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 36: If the OF bit for hpmcounter6 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated, and the OF bit functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for hpmcounter6.
RULE 37: Count overflow for hpmcounter6 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter or mhpmevent registers; it occurs only from hardware increments of hpmcounter6.
RULE 38: A count overflow interrupt request generated by hpmcounter6 is treated as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 39: The pending status of a count overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter6 is indicated by the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip register, and the enable control is the LCOFIE bit in the mie or sie register.
RULE 40: Generation of a count overflow interrupt request by hpmcounter6 sets the OF bit associated with hpmcounter6.
RULE 41: When the OF bit for hpmcounter6 is set, the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip register is eventually set, though not necessarily immediately.
RULE 42: The mideleg register controls whether the count overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter6 is delegated to S-mode or remains in M-mode.
RULE 43: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for hpmcounter6 is performed by clearing its OF bit while initializing hpmcounter6 to a starting value.
RULE 44: After hpmcounter6 has overflowed, both hpmcounter6 and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 45: The scountovf CSR bit 6 is the shadow copy of the OF bit in mhpmevent 6, which is the event register associated with hpmcounter6.
RULE 46: Read access to hpmcounter6 is governed by the same mcounteren CSR (or the combination of mcounteren and hcounteren CSRs) that governs access to the hpmcounter CSRs for the corresponding privilege mode.
RULE 47: In S-mode (or HS-mode), a read of hpmcounter6 is permitted only when mcounteren bit 6 is set; otherwise the read is not permitted.
RULE 48: In VS-mode, a read of hpmcounter6 is permitted only when both mcounteren bit 6 and hcounteren bit 6 are set; otherwise the read is not permitted.
RULE 49: If the HPM6 bit in hcounteren is clear, V=1, and the HPM6 bit in mcounteren is 1, then a read of hpmcounter6 causes a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 50: In VU-mode, hpmcounter6 is not readable unless both the HPM6 bit in hcounteren and the HPM6 bit in scounteren are set.
RULE 51: The HPM6 bit in hcounteren is a WARL field, and if it is read-only zero then reads of hpmcounter6 when V=1 cause a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 52: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter6 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc06; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 53: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter6 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc06; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 54: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter6 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc06; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 55: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter6 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc06, a0; csrr a1, 0xc06; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 56: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter6 register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc06; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 57: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter6 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xc06; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hpmcounter7
NUMBER: 0xc07
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: hpmcounter7 is a 64-bit unprivileged hardware performance counter.
RULE 2: Accessing hpmcounter7 when it is unimplemented may cause an illegal-instruction exception or may return a constant value.
RULE 3: The CSR hpmcounter7 is an unprivileged read-only (URO) CSR.
RULE 4: The CSR named mhpmcounter7 is a Machine-mode read/write performance-monitoring counter.
RULE 5: The event selector for mhpmcounter7 is the CSR named mhpmevent7.
RULE 6: The CSR mhpmevent7 is a Machine-mode read/write performance-monitoring event selector associated with mhpmcounter7.
RULE 7: After a hart reset, the mhpmcounter7 register contains an arbitrary value.
RULE 8: The mhpmcounter7 register can be written with any value.
RULE 9: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter7 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 10: A legal implementation may make the mhpmcounter7 register read-only zero.
RULE 11: The high-half CSR mhpmcounter7h is provided only if the Sscofpmf extension is implemented.
RULE 12: The mhpmevent7 CSR is a 64-bit WARL register that selects the event that causes the mhpmcounter7 register to increment, with event 0 defined as meaning no event.
RULE 13: hpmcounter7 is a read-only shadow of mhpmcounter7.
RULE 14: If the HPM7 bit in the mcounteren CSR is clear, any attempt to read hpmcounter7 while executing in S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 15: If the HPM7 bit in the mcounteren CSR is set, access to hpmcounter7 is permitted in S-mode when S-mode is implemented.
RULE 16: If the HPM7 bit in the mcounteren CSR is set and S-mode is not implemented, access to hpmcounter7 is permitted in U-mode.
RULE 17: hpmcounter7 continues to increment even when access to it is denied.
RULE 18: In harts with U-mode, the HPM7 field of the mcounteren CSR is WARL and may be read-only zero.
RULE 19: If the HPM7 field of the mcounteren CSR is read-only zero, a read of hpmcounter7 while executing in S-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 20: If the HPM7 field of the mcounteren CSR is read-only zero, a read of hpmcounter7 while executing in U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 21: When the HPM7 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, hpmcounter7 increments as usual.
RULE 22: When the HPM7 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, hpmcounter7 does not increment.
RULE 23: The settings in mcountinhibit affect only the incrementing of hpmcounter7; they do not affect the accessibility of hpmcounter7.
RULE 24: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as if the HPM7 bit were clear, and therefore hpmcounter7 increments.
RULE 25: When mcounteren[7]=1, menvcfg.CDE=1, and siselect=0x47, the state of hpmcounter7 may be read or written via sireg*.
RULE 26: When siselect=0x47, sireg provides access to hpmcounter7.
RULE 27: When siselect=0x47, sireg4 provides access to hpmcounter7h, the high half of hpmcounter7.
RULE 28: When siselect=0x47, sireg2 provides access to hpmevent7, which selects events for hpmcounter7.
RULE 29: When siselect=0x47, sireg5 provides access to hpmevent7h, which selects events for hpmcounter7.
RULE 30: When menvcfg.CDE=0, any attempt in M or S mode to access a sireg* that maps to hpmcounter7 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 31: When siselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F and the accessed sireg* is sireg3 or sireg6, any attempt in M or S mode to access hpmcounter7 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 32: When XLEN=64 and the accessed sireg* is sireg4 or sireg5 that maps to hpmcounter7, any attempt in M or S mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 33: When siselect=0x41, any attempt in M or S mode to access a sireg* that maps to hpmcounter7 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 34: When the bit for hpmcounter7 in mcounteren is 0 (the counter is not delegated to S-mode), any attempt in M or S mode to access a sireg* that maps to hpmcounter7 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 35: If the implementation lacks any extension required for the state of hpmcounter7 or its associated hpmevent7/hpmcounter7h registers, an attempt from M or S mode to access that state through sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 36: When Sscofpmf is implemented, bit 62 of hpmevent7, which selects events for hpmcounter7, accessed via sireg2 or sireg5 is read-only 0.
RULE 37: When the H extension is implemented and vsiselect selects hpmcounter7 (vsiselect=0x47), any attempt in M or S mode to access the corresponding vsireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 38: When the H extension is implemented and vsiselect selects hpmcounter7, any attempt from VS-mode to access the corresponding vsireg* (via sireg*) raises an illegal-instruction exception if menvcfg.CDE=0, or raises a virtual-instruction exception if menvcfg.CDE=1.
RULE 39: When the HPM 7 bit in the scounteren CSR is clear, a read of the hpmcounter7 register while executing in U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 40: U-mode may only access the hpmcounter7 register if the HPM 7 bits in both the scounteren and mcounteren CSRs are set.
RULE 41: The HPM 7 bit in the scounteren CSR may be read-only zero, and if it is zero, reads of the hpmcounter7 register in U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 42: The setting of the HPM 7 bit in the mcounteren CSR does not affect the writability of the HPM 7 bit in the scounteren CSR, which controls access to the hpmcounter7 register.
RULE 43: The mhpmevent7 register that corresponds to hpmcounter7 contains bits 63-56, where bit 63 is OF, bits 62-58 are MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH respectively, and bits 57-56 are reserved.
RULE 44: Bits 57 and 56 of mhpmevent7 are reserved (WPRI) for hpmcounter7.
RULE 45: If the privilege mode associated with an INH bit in mhpmevent7 is not implemented, that INH bit reads as zero for hpmcounter7.
RULE 46: When the MINH bit in mhpmevent7 is set, hpmcounter7 does not count events while the processor is executing in machine mode.
RULE 47: When the SINH bit in mhpmevent7 is set, hpmcounter7 does not count events while the processor is executing in supervisor or hypervisor mode.
RULE 48: When the UINH bit in mhpmevent7 is set, hpmcounter7 does not count events while the processor is executing in user mode.
RULE 49: When the VSINH bit in mhpmevent7 is set, hpmcounter7 does not count events while the processor is executing in virtual-supervisor mode.
RULE 50: When the VUINH bit in mhpmevent7 is set, hpmcounter7 does not count events while the processor is executing in virtual-user mode.
RULE 51: If all five INH bits in mhpmevent7 are zero, hpmcounter7 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 52: The OF bit in mhpmevent7 is set by hardware when hpmcounter7 overflows and remains set until software writes the bit.
RULE 53: Overflow of hpmcounter7 is defined as unsigned overflow of its implemented counter bits, causing the counter to wrap around while the OF bit stays set.
RULE 54: If hpmcounter7 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 55: If hpmcounter7 overflows while its OF bit is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 56: The OF bit of hpmcounter7 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable.
RULE 57: Count overflow for hpmcounter7 can be caused only by hardware increments of the counter and never by software writes to mhpmcounter7 or mhpmevent7.
RULE 58: An overflow of hpmcounter7 generates a count-overflow-interrupt-request signal that maps to local interrupt bit 13, with pending status in the LCOFIP bits of mip and sip and enable control in the LCOFIE bits of mie and sie.
RULE 59: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter7 sets its OF bit.
RULE 60: When the OF bit of hpmcounter7 is set, the LCOFIP bit in mip or sip will eventually be set.
RULE 61: The mideleg register determines whether the overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter7 is delegated to supervisor mode or remains in machine mode.
RULE 62: To enable overflow interrupt generation for hpmcounter7, software must clear its OF bit while initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 63: After hpmcounter7 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 64: When the HPM7 bit in hcounteren is clear and the HPM7 bit in mcounteren is 1, attempts to read hpmcounter7 while V=1 cause a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 65: When the HPM7 bit in hcounteren is set, access to hpmcounter7 is permitted while V=1 unless prevented for some other reason.
RULE 66: In VU-mode, hpmcounter7 is not readable unless the HPM7 bits in both hcounteren and scounteren are set.
RULE 67: If the HPM7 bit in hcounteren is implemented as a read-only zero, attempts to read hpmcounter7 while V=1 cause a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 68: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter7 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc07; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 69: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter7 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc07; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 70: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter7 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc07; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 71: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter7 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc07, a0; csrr a1, 0xc07; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 72: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter7 register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc07; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 73: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter7 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xc07; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hpmcounter8
NUMBER: 0xc08
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: If hpmcounter8 is not implemented, an access to it may raise an illegal-instruction exception or may return a constant value.
RULE 2: If the event-selection configuration for hpmcounter8 is misconfigured, hpmcounter8 may return a constant value.
RULE 3: Reading hpmcounter8 does not involve a snapshot or atomic-read latch and may be subject to context-switch interference like other hpmcounters.
RULE 4: The architectural privilege of hpmcounter8 is URO (User-mode Read-Only).
RULE 5: The CSR hpmcounter8h, which provides access to the upper 32 bits of hpmcounter8, has privilege URO.
RULE 6: mhpmevent8 controls which event causes mhpmcounter8 to increment.
RULE 7: Event 0, which may be programmed into mhpmevent8, is defined to mean no event for mhpmcounter8.
RULE 8: A legal implementation may implement mhpmcounter8 as a read-only zero register, with mhpmevent8 also read-only zero.
RULE 9: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter8 contains an arbitrary value.
RULE 10: mhpmcounter8 may be written with a given value.
RULE 11: A CSR write to mhpmcounter8 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 12: If the HPM8 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the hpmcounter8 CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: If the HPM8 bit in the mcounteren register is set, reads of the hpmcounter8 CSR are permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode.
RULE 14: If the HPM8 field of the mcounteren register is read-only zero, any read of the hpmcounter8 CSR in a less-privileged mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 15: In harts that implement U-mode, the HPM8 field of the mcounteren register, which controls access to hpmcounter8, is a WARL field that may be read-only zero.
RULE 16: The hpmcounter8 register's increment behavior is controlled by the HPM 8 bit in the mcountinhibit register, while its accessibility is not affected.
RULE 17: When the HPM 8 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the hpmcounter8 register increments as usual.
RULE 18: When the HPM 8 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the hpmcounter8 register does not increment.
RULE 19: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as though the register were set to zero, treating the HPM 8 bit as clear and causing the hpmcounter8 register to increment as usual.
RULE 20: If the HPM8 bit in scounteren is clear, a read of the hpmcounter8 register while executing in U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 21: If the HPM8 bit in scounteren is set, a read of the hpmcounter8 register while executing in U-mode is permitted (subject to other conditions).
RULE 22: Because scounteren must be implemented, the HPM8 bit may be read-only zero, and in that case a read of the hpmcounter8 register in U-mode will cause an exception.
RULE 23: A U-mode read of the hpmcounter8 register is allowed only when both the HPM8 bit in scounteren and the HPM8 bit in mcounteren are set.
RULE 24: The OF bit in mhpmevent8 is set when hpmcounter8 overflows.
RULE 25: The OF bit in mhpmevent8 remains set until written by software.
RULE 26: hpmcounter8 values are unsigned, and overflow is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 27: If hpmcounter8 overflows while the associated OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 28: If the OF bit associated with hpmcounter8 is one, no interrupt request is generated.
RULE 29: The OF bit also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for hpmcounter8.
RULE 30: Count overflow never results from writes to the mhpmcounter8 or mhpmevent8 registers, only from hardware increments of hpmcounter8.
RULE 31: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter8 sets the associated OF bit.
RULE 32: When the OF bit for hpmcounter8 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers.
RULE 33: The mip/sip LCOFIP and mie/sie LCOFIE bits are, respectively, the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for the count overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter8.
RULE 34: The mideleg register controls delegation of the count overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter8 to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 35: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for hpmcounter8 is done by clearing the OF bit, typically together with initializing hpmcounter8 to a starting value.
RULE 36: Once hpmcounter8 has overflowed, hpmcounter8 and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 37: Each of the five x INH bits (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in mhpmevent8, when set, inhibits counting of events for hpmcounter8 while in the corresponding privilege mode.
RULE 38: If a particular privilege mode is not implemented, the corresponding x INH bit in mhpmevent8, which controls counting for hpmcounter8, is read-only zero.
RULE 39: All-zeroes for the INH bits in mhpmevent8 result in counting of events for hpmcounter8 in all privilege modes.
RULE 40: In S-mode, reads of hpmcounter8 return the counter value when mcounteren bit 8 is set, otherwise the read returns zero.
RULE 41: In VS-mode, reads of hpmcounter8 return the counter value only when both mcounteren bit 8 and hcounteren bit 8 are set, otherwise the read returns zero.
RULE 42: If the HPM8 bit in hcounteren is clear, V=1, and the HPM8 bit in mcounteren is 1, then a read of hpmcounter8 causes a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 43: In VU-mode, hpmcounter8 is readable only when the HPM8 bit is set in both hcounteren and scounteren.
RULE 44: If either the HPM8 bit in hcounteren or the HPM8 bit in scounteren is clear while in VU-mode, then hpmcounter8 is not readable.
RULE 45: The hcounteren register must be implemented, and if its HPM8 bit is read-only zero, then any read of hpmcounter8 while V=1 causes a virtual-instruction exception.

REGISTER: hpmcounter9
NUMBER: 0xc09
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Smcsrind, Sscsrind, Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: If hpmcounter9 is unimplemented, an access to it may cause an illegal-instruction exception or may return a constant value.
RULE 2: If the configuration that selects the events counted by hpmcounter9 is misconfigured, hpmcounter9 may return a constant value.
RULE 3: hpmcounter9 has privilege URO.
RULE 4: hpmcounter9 is readable at the unprivileged level.
RULE 5: hpmcounter9 is not writable.
RULE 6: mhpmcounter9 contains an arbitrary value after a hart reset and may be written with any value.
RULE 7: A write to mhpmcounter9 takes effect only after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 8: A legal implementation may implement mhpmcounter9 as a read-only zero register.
RULE 9: When the HPM9 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the hpmcounter9 register while executing in S-mode or U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: When the HPM9 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter9 register is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 11: The hpmcounter9 CSR is a read-only shadow of mhpmcounter9.
RULE 12: The settings in the mcounteren register only control accessibility of hpmcounter9 and do not affect the underlying counter value, which continues to increment even when not accessible.
RULE 13: The mhpmcounter9 register increments when the HPM9 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear.
RULE 14: The mhpmcounter9 register does not increment when the HPM9 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set.
RULE 15: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the mhpmcounter9 register increments as if the HPM9 bit were clear.
RULE 16: The accessibility of the mhpmcounter9 register is independent of the setting of the mcountinhibit register.
RULE 17: If mcounteren[9]=1 and menvcfg.CDE=1 and siselect=0x49, the CSR hpmcounter9 is accessed through sireg.
RULE 18: If mcounteren[9]=1 and menvcfg.CDE=1 and siselect=0x49 and XLEN=64, the CSR hpmcounter9h is accessed through sireg4.
RULE 19: In M or S mode, if menvcfg.CDE=0, an attempt to access hpmcounter9 via sireg with siselect=0x49 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 20: In M or S mode, if XLEN=64 and the access uses sireg4 to reach hpmcounter9h with siselect=0x49, the access raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 21: In M or S mode, if mcounteren[9]=0, an attempt to access hpmcounter9 via sireg with siselect=0x49 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 22: In M or S mode, if the implementation does not provide an extension required for the state of hpmcounter9 (or its associated hpmevent9 fields), an attempt to access hpmcounter9 via sireg raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 23: If the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented and the processor is in VS-mode, an attempt to access hpmcounter9 via sireg with siselect=0x49 raises an illegal-instruction exception when menvcfg.CDE=0.
RULE 24: If the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented and the processor is in VS-mode, an attempt to access hpmcounter9 via sireg with siselect=0x49 raises a virtual-instruction exception when menvcfg.CDE=1.
RULE 25: If the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented and the processor is in VU-mode, an attempt to access hpmcounter9 via sireg with siselect=0x49 raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 26: If the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented and the processor is in M or S mode, an attempt to access hpmcounter9 via vsireg* while vsiselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 27: If the HPM9 bit in the scounteren register is clear, any attempt to read the hpmcounter9 register while executing in U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 28: If the HPM9 bit in the scounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter9 register is permitted.
RULE 29: U-mode may only access the hpmcounter9 register when both the HPM9 bit in the scounteren register and the HPM9 bit in the mcounteren register are set.
RULE 30: If the HPM9 bit in the scounteren register is read-only zero, reads of the hpmcounter9 register in U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 31: The mhpmevent9 register contains an OF bit (bit 63) that is set when hpmcounter9 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 32: The OF bit in mhpmevent9 also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for hpmcounter9.
RULE 33: If hpmcounter9 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 34: If hpmcounter9 overflows while its OF bit is one, no interrupt request is generated.
RULE 35: Overflow for hpmcounter9 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 36: When hpmcounter9 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit remains set.
RULE 37: Writes to mhpmcounter9 or mhpmevent9 never cause overflow; overflow can occur only from hardware increments of hpmcounter9.
RULE 38: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter9 sets the associated OF bit.
RULE 39: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter9 eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers, though not necessarily immediately.
RULE 40: The mideleg register controls whether the overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter9 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 41: For each privilege mode x INH bit in mhpmevent9, if privilege mode x is not implemented, that INH bit is read-only zero.
RULE 42: For each privilege mode x INH bit in mhpmevent9, setting the INH bit inhibits counting of events for hpmcounter9 while executing in privilege mode x.
RULE 43: If all five x INH bits in mhpmevent9 are zero, hpmcounter9 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 44: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for hpmcounter9 is done by clearing its OF bit together with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 45: After hpmcounter9 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 46: The overflow flag associated with hpmcounter9 is the OF bit in mhpmevent9 and is mirrored as scountovf bit 9.
RULE 47: The readability of the overflow flag for hpmcounter9 follows the same mcounteren (and, where applicable, hcounteren) access controls that govern read access to the hpmcounter9 register itself.
RULE 48: In M-mode, the overflow flag for hpmcounter9 is always readable.
RULE 49: In S-mode (or HS-mode), the overflow flag for hpmcounter9 is readable only when mcounteren bit 9 is set, and reads as zero otherwise.
RULE 50: In VS-mode, the overflow flag for hpmcounter9 is readable only when both mcounteren bit 9 and hcounteren bit 9 are set, and reads as zero otherwise.
RULE 51: If the HPM9 bit in hcounteren is clear, V=1, and the HPM9 bit in mcounteren is set, then a read of hpmcounter9 MUST cause a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 52: If the HPM9 bit in hcounteren is set, then a read of hpmcounter9 while V=1 MUST be permitted unless some other architectural rule prevents the access.
RULE 53: In VU-mode, a read of hpmcounter9 MUST be denied unless the HPM9 bit is set in both hcounteren and scounteren.
RULE 54: The HPM9 bit in hcounteren MAY be hardwired to zero, and when it is zero a read of hpmcounter9 while V=1 MUST cause a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 55: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter9 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc09; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 56: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter9 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc09; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 57: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter9 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc09; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: hstateen0
NUMBER: 0x60c
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=SE0, 62..62=ENVCFG, 60..60=CSRIND, 59..59=AIA, 58..58=IMSIC, 57..57=CONTEXT, 54..54=CTR, 2..2=JVT, 1..1=FCSR, 0..0=C
EXTENSIONS: H, Sdtrig, Smcntrpmf, Smcsrind, Smctr, Smstateen, Ssaia, Sscofpmf, Sscsrind, Ssctr, Ssqosid, Ssstateen, Zcmt, Zdinx, Zfinx
RULE 1: If hstateen0 prevents access to a piece of state for a less-privileged mode, an instruction in that mode that attempts to read or write the protected state raises an illegal-instruction exception, or raises a virtual-instruction exception instead when executed in VS or VU mode and the conditions for a virtual-instruction exception are met.
RULE 2: Bits in the hstateen0 CSR that are defined to control state not implemented by a hart are read-only zeros for that hart.
RULE 3: All reserved bits in the hstateen0 CSR that have no defined meaning are read-only zeros.
RULE 4: If a bit in the mstateen0 CSR is zero, whether because it is a read-only zero or written zero, the corresponding bit in hstateen0 is a read-only zero.
RULE 5: If a bit in hstateen0 is zero, whether as a read-only zero or written zero, the corresponding bit in sstateen0 accessed in VS-mode is a read-only zero.
RULE 6: A bit in hstateen0 may be read-only one only if the corresponding bit in mstateen0 is also read-only one.
RULE 7: Bit 63 of mstateen0 is defined to control access to the hstateen0 CSR.
RULE 8: Bit 63 of hstateen0 controls access to the matching sstateen0 CSR.
RULE 9: Bit 63 of hstateen0 is always writable (not read-only).
RULE 10: The C bit in hstateen0 is a standard field of a standard CSR and therefore controls access to any and all custom state.
RULE 11: If software sets the C bit in hstateen0 but does not execute any custom instructions or access any custom state, the software must continue to execute as specified by all relevant RISC-V standards, otherwise the hardware is not standard-conforming.
RULE 12: When misa.F = 1, the FCSR bit in hstateen0 is read-only zero.
RULE 13: If misa.F = 0, the stateen CSRs are implemented, and the FCSR bit in hstateen0 is zero, then every floating-point instruction causes an illegal-instruction exception (or a virtual-instruction exception, if relevant).
RULE 14: The JVT bit in hstateen0 controls access to the jvt CSR provided by the Zcmt extension.
RULE 15: The SE0 bit in hstateen0 determines whether software can access the sstateen0 CSR.
RULE 16: The ENVCFG bit in hstateen0 determines access to the senvcfg CSRs.
RULE 17: The CSRIND bit in hstateen0 determines access to the siselect and sireg* CSRs (i.e., the vsiselect and vsireg* CSRs) provided by the Sscsrind extensions.
RULE 18: The IMSIC bit in hstateen0 governs access to the guest IMSIC state, including the vstopei CSR.
RULE 19: If the IMSIC bit in hstateen0 is zero, a virtual machine cannot access the hart's IMSIC, which is equivalent to hstatus.VGEIN = 0.
RULE 20: The AIA bit in hstateen0 determines access to all state introduced by the Ssaia extension that is not covered by the CSRIND or IMSIC bits of hstateen0.
RULE 21: The CONTEXT bit in hstateen0 governs access to the scontext CSR provided by the Sdtrig extension.
RULE 22: If machine-level software sets any writable bits of mstateen0 to a non-zero value, it MUST write zeros to hstateen0 (if hstateen0 exists).
RULE 23: When bit 63 of mstateen0 (or any mstateen CSR) is set, machine-level software MUST write zero to hstateen0.
RULE 24: A guest OS may access sstateen0 only when bit 63 of hstateen0 is set.
RULE 25: When bit 63 of hstateen0 is set, a hypervisor MUST include sstateen0 in the context it swaps for that guest OS.
RULE 26: When bit 63 of hstateen0 is set, a hypervisor MUST ensure that the writable bits of sstateen0 are initialized to zeros when the guest starts.
RULE 27: When bit 63 of hstateen0 is set, a hypervisor MUST emulate accesses to any other sstateen0 bits.
RULE 28: If a hypervisor does not support multiple contexts for less-privileged levels, it may write a value of all ones to hstateen0.
RULE 29: When hstateen0[60] = 0 and mstateen0[60] = 1, all attempts from VS-mode or VU-mode to access siselect or sireg* raise a virtual-instruction exception, not an illegal-instruction exception, regardless of the value of vsiselect or any other mstateen bit.
RULE 30: If the Smstateen extension is implemented and bit 60 of hstateen0 is zero, accesses to siselect and sireg (vsiselect and vsireg) from VS-mode are prohibited.
RULE 31: When the H extension is implemented and mstateen0.CTR = 1, the hstateen0.CTR bit determines whether VS-mode accesses to supervisor CTR state are permitted when V = 1.
RULE 32: The hstateen0.CTR bit is read-only zero when mstateen0.CTR = 0, and the register returns 0 and cannot be written.
RULE 33: If mstateen0.CTR = 1 and hstateen0.CTR = 0, VS-mode accesses to supervisor CTR state raise a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 34: If mstateen0.CTR = 1 and hstateen0.CTR = 0, execution of SCTRCLR in VS-mode raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 35: The hstateen0.CTR bit does not control access to the sctrdepth register.
RULE 36: VS-mode accesses to sctrdepth raise a virtual-instruction exception irrespective of the value of hstateen0.CTR.
RULE 37: If hstateen0.CTR = 0, qualified control transfers executed while V = 1 implicitly update entry registers and sctrstatus.
RULE 38: In M-mode, accessing hstateen0 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x60c; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 39: In S-mode, accessing hstateen0 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x60c; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: hstateen1
NUMBER: 0x60d
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=SE0
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The hstateen1 register resides at address 0x60E.
RULE 2: The hstateen1 register is accessed with hypervisor read/write (HRW) privilege.
RULE 3: The hstateen1h register resides at address 0x61E.
RULE 4: The hstateen1h register is accessed with hypervisor read/write (HRW) privilege.
RULE 5: Any bit that is zero in mstateen1 appears as a read-only-zero bit in hstateen1.
RULE 6: If a bit in hstateen1 is zero, the same bit is read-only zero in sstateen1 when the sstateen CSR is accessed in VS-mode.
RULE 7: A bit that is read-only one in hstateen1 must also be read-only one in mstateen1.
RULE 8: After reset, all writable bits of hstateen1 are initialized by hardware to zero.
RULE 9: If machine-level software writes a non-zero value to a writable bit of mstateen1, it must also write zero to the corresponding writable bit of hstateen1.
RULE 10: Bit 63 of hstateen1 determines whether lower-privilege software executing in VS/VU mode may access sstateen1.
RULE 11: Bit 63 of hstateen1 is always writable and is not read-only.
RULE 12: If hstateen1 disables access to a particular piece of state for VS/VU modes, any VS/VU instruction that attempts to read or write that state raises an illegal-instruction exception, or raises a virtual-instruction exception when the virtual-instruction exception conditions apply.
RULE 13: Any bit in hstateen1 that corresponds to unimplemented state or is reserved is a read-only-zero bit.
RULE 14: If machine-level software sets any writable mstateen bits to a nonzero value, then machine-level software MUST write zeros to hstateen1 if hstateen1 exists.
RULE 15: In the ordinary situation where machine-level software sets bit 63 of all mstateen CSRs, it writes zero to hstateen1.
RULE 16: A hypervisor MAY write the value all-ones to hstateen1 to maximize less-privileged access to all state.
RULE 17: In M-mode, accessing hstateen1 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x60d; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 18: In S-mode, accessing hstateen1 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x60d; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

RULE 20: In M-mode, setting hstateen1.SE0 (bit 63) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x60d, a0; csrr a1, 0x60d; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].

REGISTER: hstateen2
NUMBER: 0x60e
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=SE0
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The privilege for hstateen2 is HRW (hypervisor-mode read/write).
RULE 2: Every bit in hstateen2 controls less-privileged access to the corresponding extension state.
RULE 3: Any bit in hstateen2 that corresponds to state not implemented by the hart is read-only zero.
RULE 4: Any reserved bit in hstateen2 (a bit without a defined meaning) is read-only zero.
RULE 5: If a bit in mstateen2 is zero, then the corresponding bit in hstateen2 is read-only zero.
RULE 6: If a bit in hstateen2 is zero, then the corresponding bit in sstateen2 is read-only zero when accessed from VS-mode.
RULE 7: If a bit in hstateen2 is read-only one, then the same bit in mstateen2 must be read-only one.
RULE 8: After reset, all writable bits of hstateen2 are initialized to zero.
RULE 9: Bit 63 of hstateen2 controls access to sstateen2.
RULE 10: Bit 63 of hstateen2 is always writable.
