REGISTER: hstateen3
NUMBER: 0x60f
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=SE0
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The hstateen3 CSR must be accessed with hypervisor-read/write (HRW) privilege.
RULE 2: Any bit in hstateen3 that is defined to control state that a hart does not implement is read-only zero for that hart.
RULE 3: For every bit in the mstateen3 CSR that is zero, the same bit appears as read-only zero in hstateen3.
RULE 4: For every bit in hstateen3 that is zero, the same bit appears as read-only zero in the sstateen3 CSR when accessed in VS mode.
RULE 5: A bit in hstateen3 cannot be read-only one unless the same bit is read-only one in the matching mstateen3 CSR.
RULE 6: On reset, all bits of hstateen3 that correspond to writable mstateen bits are initialized to zeros.
RULE 7: Bit 63 of hstateen3 controls access to the matching sstateen3 CSR.
RULE 8: Bit 63 of hstateen3 is always writable and never read-only.
RULE 9: When hstateen3 prevents access to state for VS or VU mode, an attempt in that mode to execute an instruction that would read or write the protected state raises an illegal-instruction exception, or raises a virtual-instruction exception instead if the circumstances for a virtual-instruction exception apply.
RULE 10: If bit 63 of hstateen3 is set, then a guest OS is permitted to access the sstateen3 CSR and the hypervisor MUST include sstateen3 in the context it swaps for that guest OS.
RULE 11: In M-mode, accessing hstateen3 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x60f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 12: In S-mode, accessing hstateen3 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x60f; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 13: In U-mode, accessing hstateen3 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x60f; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 14: In M-mode, setting hstateen3.SE0 (bit 63) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x60f, a0; csrr a1, 0x60f; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 15: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hstateen3 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x60f, a0; csrr a1, 0x60f; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: hstatus
NUMBER: 0x600
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: 33..32=VSXL, 24..24=HUKTE, 22..22=VTSR, 21..21=VTW, 20..20=VTVM, 17..12=VGEIN, 9..9=HU, 8..8=SPVP, 7..7=SPV, 6..6=GVA, 5..5=VSBE
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The VTW bit is a bit in the hstatus register that can be set while executing in VS or VU mode.
RULE 2: If the VTW bit in hstatus is set while executing in VS or VU mode, the TW bit in mstatus is clear, and a WRS.NTO instruction does not complete within an implementation-specific bounded time limit, then the WRS.NTO instruction will cause a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 3: The hstatus register has HRW privilege, allowing it to be read and written in hypervisor mode.
RULE 4: Setting hstatus.VGEIN to 0 prevents a virtual machine from accessing the hart's IMSIC.
RULE 5: Setting hstatus.VGEIN to 0 has the same effect as clearing the IMSIC bit in hstateen0.
RULE 6: When hstatus.VTVM = 1, an attempt to execute SINVAL.VMA in VS-mode raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 7: SFENCE.W.INVAL and SFENCE.INVAL.IR are always permitted in S-mode and VS-mode regardless of the value of hstatus.VTVM (and regardless of mstatus.TVM).
RULE 8: When hstatus.VTVM = 1, SFENCE.W.INVAL and SFENCE.INVAL.IR instructions need not be trapped.
RULE 9: The hstatus CSR is provided to HS-mode.
RULE 10: The hstatus CSR is not provided to VS-mode.
RULE 11: The VSXL field of hstatus controls the effective XLEN for VS-mode (VSXLEN) and may differ from the XLEN for HS-mode (HSXLEN).
RULE 12: When HSXLEN = 64 the VSXL field in hstatus is a WARL field encoded identically to the MXL field of misa.
RULE 13: If HSXLEN is changed from 32 to a wider width and the VSXL field in hstatus is not restricted to a single value, the VSXL field acquires the value corresponding to the widest supported width not wider than the new HSXLEN.
RULE 14: The VTSR, VTW, and VTVM fields in hstatus are defined analogously to the mstatus fields TSR, TW, and TVM, but they affect execution only in VS-mode and cause virtual-instruction exceptions instead of illegal-instruction exceptions.
RULE 15: When the VTSR bit in hstatus is 1, an attempt in VS-mode to execute SRET raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 16: When the VTVM bit in hstatus is 1, an attempt in VS-mode to execute SFENCE.VMA or SINVAL.VMA or to access CSR satp raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 17: The VGEIN field in hstatus is a WLRL field that must be able to hold values from zero up to the maximum guest external interrupt number (GEILEN), inclusive.
RULE 18: When the HU bit in hstatus is 1, HLV, HLVX, and HSV can be executed in U-mode the same as in HS-mode.
RULE 19: When the HU bit in hstatus is 0, all hypervisor instructions cause an illegal-instruction exception in U-mode.
RULE 20: When the Ssnpm extension is implemented, the HUPMM field in hstatus enables or disables pointer masking for HLV.* and HSV.* instructions in U-mode according to Table 47 when their explicit memory access is performed as though in VU-mode.
RULE 21: When the Ssnpm extension is not implemented, the HUPMM field in hstatus is read-only zero.
RULE 22: The SPV bit in hstatus is written by the implementation whenever a trap is taken into HS-mode.
RULE 23: At trap entry into HS-mode, the SPV bit in hstatus is set to the value of the virtualization mode V at the time of the trap.
RULE 24: When an SRET instruction is executed while V = 0, the virtualization mode V is set to the value of the SPV bit in hstatus.
RULE 25: When V = 1 and a trap is taken into HS-mode, the SPVP bit in hstatus is set to the nominal privilege mode at the time of the trap, the same as sstatus.SPP.
RULE 26: If V = 0 before a trap, the SPVP bit in hstatus is left unchanged on trap entry.
RULE 27: The GVA field in hstatus is written by the implementation whenever a trap is taken into HS-mode.
RULE 28: For any trap that writes a guest virtual address to stval (including breakpoint, address-misaligned, access-fault, page-fault, or guest-page-fault traps), the GVA field in hstatus is set to 1.
RULE 29: For any other trap into HS-mode, the GVA field in hstatus is set to 0.
RULE 30: For breakpoint and memory-access traps that write a nonzero value to stval, the GVA field in hstatus is redundant with the SPV bit (both are set the same) except when the explicit memory access of an HLV, HLVX, or HSV instruction causes a fault; in that case SPV = 0 but GVA = 1.
RULE 31: The VSBE bit in hstatus is a WARL field that controls the endianness of explicit memory accesses made from VS-mode.
RULE 32: If VSBE in hstatus is 0, explicit load and store memory accesses made from VS-mode are little-endian, and if VSBE is 1 they are big-endian.
RULE 33: VSBE in hstatus also controls the endianness of all implicit accesses to VS-level memory-management data structures, such as page tables.
RULE 34: The hip.VSEIP bit is read-only and is defined as the logical-OR of three sources, one of which is the bit of hgeip selected by hstatus.VGEIN.
RULE 35: The value of hstatus.VGEIN determines which bit of the hgeip register is included in the logical-OR that defines the read-only hip.VSEIP bit.
RULE 36: The hstatus.VGEIN field selects the VS-level external interrupt signal from the hgeip register.
RULE 37: The enable bits in the hgeie register do not affect the VS-level external interrupt signal selected by hstatus.VGEIN.
RULE 38: When the effective privilege mode is U and hstatus.HU = 0, the hgatp register is not considered active for the address-translation algorithm.
RULE 39: When the effective privilege mode is not U, or when hstatus.HU ≠ 0, the hgatp register is considered active for the address-translation algorithm.
RULE 40: Implementations may make the UXL field a read-only copy of hstatus.VSXL, causing the value of UXL to be taken from hstatus.VSXL and forcing VU-mode XLEN to equal VSXLEN.
RULE 41: Implementations may make the UBE field a read-only copy of hstatus.VSBE, such that reads of UBE return the same value as hstatus.VSBE and writes to UBE have no effect.
RULE 42: When the effective privilege mode is U and the hstatus.HU field is 0, the vsatp register is not considered active for the address-translation algorithm.
RULE 43: Hypervisor virtual-machine load and store instructions are valid only when the current privilege mode is M-mode or HS-mode, or when the current privilege mode is U-mode and the hstatus.HU field equals 1.
RULE 44: When the hstatus.SPVP field is 0, the effective privilege mode of the explicit memory access performed by a hypervisor virtual-machine load or store instruction is VU.
RULE 45: When the hstatus.SPVP field is 1, the effective privilege mode of the explicit memory access performed by a hypervisor virtual-machine load or store instruction is VS.
RULE 46: When V=1, attempts to execute a hypervisor virtual-machine load or store instruction (HLV, HLVX, or HSV) cause a virtual-instruction exception, as defined in the hstatus architectural description.
RULE 47: When executing a hypervisor virtual-machine load or store instruction from U-mode while the hstatus.HU field is 0, an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 48: Executing an HFENCE.VVMA instruction must not trap because of the hstatus.VTVM field.
RULE 49: The effect of the MPRV bit does not apply to the virtual-machine load/store instructions HLV, HLVX, and HSV, which instead use the hstatus.SPVP field to determine the nominal privilege mode.
RULE 50: For the virtual-machine load/store instructions HLV, HLVX, and HSV, explicit loads and stores always act as though the virtualization mode V is 1, as defined by the architectural behavior of hstatus.
RULE 51: For the virtual-machine load/store instructions HLV, HLVX, and HSV, explicit loads and stores always use the nominal privilege mode specified by the hstatus.SPVP field, overriding any effect of MPRV.
RULE 52: In VS-mode, if an SRET instruction is attempted while hstatus.VTSR=1, a virtual-instruction exception must be raised.
RULE 53: In VS-mode, if an SFENCE.VMA instruction is attempted while hstatus.VTVM=1, a virtual-instruction exception must be raised.
RULE 54: In VS-mode, if a SINVAL.VMA instruction is attempted while hstatus.VTVM=1, a virtual-instruction exception must be raised.
RULE 55: In VS-mode, if satp is accessed while hstatus.VTVM=1, a virtual-instruction exception must be raised.
RULE 56: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the virtualization mode V field in hstatus is set to 0.
RULE 57: When a trap is taken into HS-mode and the previous privilege mode was U-mode, the SPV field in hstatus is set to 0.
RULE 58: When a trap is taken into HS-mode and the previous privilege mode was HS-mode, the SPV field in hstatus is set to 0.
RULE 59: When a trap is taken into HS-mode and the previous privilege mode was VU-mode, the SPV field in hstatus is set to 1.
RULE 60: When a trap is taken into HS-mode and the previous privilege mode was VS-mode, the SPV field in hstatus is set to 1.
RULE 61: If the virtualization mode V field in hstatus was 1 before a trap into HS-mode, the SPVP field in hstatus is set to the same value as sstatus.SPP.
RULE 62: If the virtualization mode V field in hstatus was 0 before a trap into HS-mode, the SPVP field in hstatus is left unchanged.
RULE 63: When a trap is taken into VS-mode, hstatus is not modified.
RULE 64: When a trap is taken into VS-mode, the virtualization mode V field in hstatus remains 1.
RULE 65: When SRET is executed in M-mode or HS-mode (V = 0), the new privilege mode is determined based on the values of hstatus.SPV and sstatus.SPP.
RULE 66: After the privilege-mode determination performed by SRET, the instruction sets hstatus.SPV to 0.
RULE 67: In M-mode, accessing hstatus register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x600; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 68: In HS-mode, accessing hstatus register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x600; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 69: In U-mode, accessing hstatus register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x600; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 70: In M-mode, setting hstatus.VSXL (bit 32) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x100000000; csrs 0x600, a0; csrr a1, 0x600; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 71: In M-mode, setting hstatus.HUKTE (bit 24) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1000000; csrs 0x600, a0; csrr a1, 0x600; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1000000].
RULE 72: In M-mode, setting hstatus.VTSR (bit 22) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x400000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x400000; csrs 0x600, a0; csrr a1, 0x600; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x400000].
RULE 73: In M-mode, setting hstatus.VTW (bit 21) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x200000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x200000; csrs 0x600, a0; csrr a1, 0x600; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x200000].

REGISTER: htimedelta
NUMBER: 0x605
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=DELTA
EXTENSIONS: H, Sstc
RULE 1: The privilege encoding for htimedelta is HRW, indicating that htimedelta is a hypervisor-read/write CSR.
RULE 2: The htimedelta CSR is provided to HS-mode and is not provided to VS-mode.
RULE 3: When software writes the vstimecmp CSR with a value that is less than or equal to the 64-bit truncation of the sum of the time CSR and the htimedelta register, the hip .VSTIP bit is set.
RULE 4: When software writes the vstimecmp CSR with a value greater than the 64-bit truncation of the sum of the time CSR and the htimedelta register, the hip .VSTIP bit is cleared.
RULE 5: The htimedelta CSR is a 64-bit read/write register that holds the delta between the time CSR value and the value returned in VS-mode or VU-mode.
RULE 6: Reading the time CSR in VS-mode or VU-mode returns the sum of the htimedelta register contents and the actual time CSR value.
RULE 7: When summing htimedelta and the time CSR, overflow is ignored, allowing large htimedelta values to represent negative time offsets.
RULE 8: The htimedelta CSR defines a single field spanning bits 63 down to 0.
RULE 9: When XLEN=64, the htimedeltah register does not exist.
RULE 10: If the time CSR is implemented, the htimedelta CSR must be implemented.
RULE 11: The virtual supervisor timer interrupt becomes pending (VSTIP bit set) whenever the unsigned 64-bit sum of the current time CSR and the htimedelta register, truncated to 64 bits, is greater than or equal to the vstimecmp CSR.
RULE 12: If the result of the unsigned comparison between (time + htimedelta) and vstimecmp changes, the VSTIP bit MUST eventually reflect the new result, though the reflection need not be immediate.
RULE 13: The virtual supervisor timer interrupt remains pending (VSTIP stays set) until the unsigned value of vstimecmp becomes greater than the unsigned 64-bit sum of time and htimedelta, typically after writing vstimecmp.
RULE 14: In M-mode, accessing htimedelta register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x605; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 15: In HS-mode, accessing htimedelta register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x605; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 16: In U-mode, accessing htimedelta register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x605; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 17: In M-mode, accessing htimedelta register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x605; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 18: In M-mode, accessing htimedelta register while Sstc extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sstc; csrr a0, 0x605; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hvip
NUMBER: 0x645
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..16=WPRI, 15..14=WPRI, 13..13=LCOFI, 12..10=WPRI, 9..9=VSEIP, 8..6=WPRI, 5..5=VSTIP, 4..2=WPRI, 1..1=VSSIP, 0..0=WPRI
EXTENSIONS: H, Smaia, Smcdeleg, Ssaia, Ssccfg, Sscofpmf, Sstc
RULE 1: The hvip register has HRW access, meaning it is both readable and writable.
RULE 2: If an implementation supports Smcdeleg or Ssccfg, Sscofpmf, Smaia or Ssaia, and the H extension, then the LCOFI bit (bit 13) in hvip is implemented and writable.
RULE 3: The implementation of hvip.LCOFI implies that the LCOFI bit (bit 13) in each of vsie and vsip is also implemented.
RULE 4: Bits of hvip that are not writable are read-only zeros.
RULE 5: The standard portion of hvip, bits 15:0, contains the VSEIP, VSTIP, and VSSIP bits, and these bits are writable.
RULE 6: Setting VSEIP = 1 in hvip asserts a VS-level external interrupt.
RULE 7: Setting VSTIP = 1 in hvip asserts a VS-level timer interrupt.
RULE 8: Setting VSSIP = 1 in hvip asserts a VS-level software interrupt.
RULE 9: The VSEIP bit of hvip is one of the inputs to the logical-OR that defines the read-only VSEIP field in hip.
RULE 10: The VSTIP bit of hvip is one of the inputs to the logical-OR that defines the read-only VSTIP field in hip.
RULE 11: The VSSIP bit in hip is an alias of the VSSIP bit in hvip, so writes to hvip.VSSIP are reflected in hip.VSSIP.
RULE 12: In M-mode, accessing hvip register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x645; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 13: In HS-mode, accessing hvip register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x645; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 14: In U-mode, accessing hvip register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x645; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: instret
NUMBER: 0xc02
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Smcdeleg, Smcntrpmf, Smcsrind, Smstateen, Ssccfg, Sscsrind, Zicntr, Zicsr
RULE 1: The instret register may be modified as a side effect of instruction execution.
RULE 2: When a CSR access instruction reads instret, it obtains the value that existed prior to the execution of that instruction.
RULE 3: When a CSR access instruction writes instret, the explicit write is performed instead of any side-effect update to instret.
RULE 4: The value written to instret by one instruction becomes the value read by the following instruction that accesses instret.
RULE 5: The INSTRET CSR is a 64-bit read-only register that counts the number of instructions retired by this hart from an arbitrary start point in the past.
RULE 6: For base ISAs with XLEN ≥ 64, the RDINSTRET pseudoinstruction reads the full 64 bits of the INSTRET counter.
RULE 7: The CSRRC, CSRRSI, and CSRRCI read-only instruction forms are also legal ways to read the INSTRET CSR.
RULE 8: Any read-only CSR instruction may be used to read the INSTRET CSR without modifying it.
RULE 9: Instructions that cause synchronous exceptions, including ECALL and EBREAK, are not considered to retire and therefore do not increment the INSTRET CSR.
RULE 10: The instret CSR is designated with privilege URO (user-read-only).
RULE 11: The instret CSR counts the number of instructions retired and provides the value returned by the RDINSTRET instruction.
RULE 12: The instreth CSR, which supplies the upper 32 bits of instret, is designated with privilege URO.
RULE 13: The machine instructions-retired counter register minstret is located at address 0xB02 and has machine-mode read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 14: The machine instret counter configuration register minstretcfg resides at address 0x322 and is accessible with machine-mode read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 15: For siselect 0x42, the indirect CSR field sireg selects the architectural register instret.
RULE 16: For siselect 0x42, the indirect CSR field sireg2 selects the architectural register instretcfg.
RULE 17: For siselect 0x42, the indirect CSR field sireg3 does not map to any architectural register, and therefore does not map to instret.
RULE 18: For siselect 0x42, the indirect CSR field sireg4 selects the architectural register instreth.
RULE 19: For siselect 0x42, the indirect CSR field sireg5 selects the architectural register instretcfgh.
RULE 20: For siselect 0x42, the indirect CSR field sireg6 does not map to any architectural register, and therefore does not map to instret.
RULE 21: If any of the CY, TM, IR, or any HPM n bits in the mcounteren register is clear, a read of the instret CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 22: When the IR bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the instret CSR is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if it is implemented, otherwise U-mode.
RULE 23: The instret CSR is a read-only shadow of the minstret CSR.
RULE 24: The settings in the mcounteren register control only the accessibility of the instret CSR and do not affect the underlying minstret counter, which continues to increment even when the CSR is not accessible.
RULE 25: In harts that implement U-mode, the IR field of mcounteren is WARL and may be read-only zero, indicating that a read of the instret CSR in a less-privileged mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 26: The settings of the mcountinhibit register control whether the minstret register increments but do not affect the accessibility of the minstret register.
RULE 27: If the IR bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the minstret register increments as usual.
RULE 28: If the IR bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the minstret register does not increment.
RULE 29: If any of the CY, IR, or HPM n bits in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the minstret register increments as usual.
RULE 30: If any of the CY, IR, or HPM n bits in the mcountinhibit register is set, the minstret register does not increment.
RULE 31: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as if the register were zero, so the minstret register increments as usual because the IR bit is treated as clear.
RULE 32: By default, the instret counter is not filtered by privilege mode.
RULE 33: If the MINH bit in minstretcfg is set, counting of events in M-mode is inhibited for the instret counters.
RULE 34: If the SINH bit in minstretcfg is set, counting of events in S/HS-mode is inhibited for the instret counters.
RULE 35: If the UINH bit in minstretcfg is set, counting of events in U-mode is inhibited for the instret counters.
RULE 36: If the VSINH bit in minstretcfg is set, counting of events in VS-mode is inhibited for the instret counters.
RULE 37: If the VUINH bit in minstretcfg is set, counting of events in VU-mode is inhibited for the instret counters.
RULE 38: When all INH bits (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in minstretcfg are zero, event counting is enabled in all privilege modes for the instret counters.
RULE 39: For each INH bit in positions 61:58 of minstretcfg, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, the bit reads as zero and does not affect instret counting.
RULE 40: The minstretcfg CSR, which configures the instret counters, may be accessible from Supervisor mode when the Smcdeleg or Ssccfg extensions are implemented.
RULE 41: Counting does not occur for instret while executing in an inhibited privilege mode.
RULE 42: Instructions that retire in a non-inhibited mode increment instret.
RULE 43: Instructions that retire in an inhibited mode do not increment instret.
RULE 44: Instructions that cause synchronous exceptions to a more privileged mode are not considered to retire and therefore do not increment instret.
RULE 45: xRET instructions retire and should increment instret only if the originating privilege mode is not inhibited.
RULE 46: When minstretcfg is configured to inhibit all modes except U-mode, a user-mode load should increment instret only once even if it takes a page fault or other exception.
RULE 47: In that scenario the faulting execution of the load will not increment instret because it does not retire.
RULE 48: In that scenario handler instructions execute in an inhibited mode and will not increment instret, including xRET which originates in an inhibited mode.
RULE 49: Only when the load is re-executed and retires will it increment instret.
RULE 50: When an instruction is emulated by software running in a privilege mode that is inhibited in minstretcfg, the emulation routine must emulate the instret increment.
RULE 51: When siselect equals 0x42, the CSR alias instret is provided via sireg.
RULE 52: When siselect equals 0x42, the CSR alias instreth is provided via sireg4.
RULE 53: When siselect equals 0x42, the CSR alias instretcfg is provided via sireg2.
RULE 54: When siselect equals 0x42, the CSR alias instretcfgh is provided via sireg5.
RULE 55: If mcounteren[2] = 1 and menvcfg.CDE = 1 and siselect = 0x42, the instret state may be accessed through the sireg* aliases.
RULE 56: If Smcntrpmf is implemented, bit 62 of the instretcfg register is read-only 0 when accessed via sireg4.
RULE 57: If Smcntrpmf is implemented, bit 62 of the instretcfgh register is read-only 0 when accessed via sireg5.
RULE 58: If mstateen0[60] = 0, access to the instret aliases via sireg* is prevented.
RULE 59: If hstateen0[60] = 0, access to the instret aliases via sireg* is prevented.
RULE 60: If menvcfg.CDE = 0, attempts to access instret via any sireg* raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 61: If XLEN = 64, attempts to access instretcfg via sireg4 raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 62: If XLEN = 64, attempts to access instretcfgh via sireg5 raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 63: If siselect = 0x42 and mcounteren[2] = 0, attempts to access instret via sireg* raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 64: If a required extension for the instret state is not implemented, an attempt from M or S mode to access instret via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 65: If the IR bit in scounteren is clear, a read of instret while executing in U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 66: If the IR bit in scounteren is set, a read of instret while executing in U-mode is permitted.
RULE 67: A U-mode read of instret is permitted only when both the IR bit in scounteren and the IR bit in mcounteren are set.
RULE 68: If either the IR bit in scounteren or the IR bit in mcounteren is clear, a U-mode read of instret must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 69: The IR bit in scounteren may be read-only zero, which makes the instret counter unavailable to U-mode.
RULE 70: If the IR bit in hcounteren is clear, the current privilege mode's V flag is 1, and the IR bit in mcounteren is 1, then any attempt to read the instret register will cause a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 71: If the IR bit in hcounteren is set and the current privilege mode's V flag is 1, then access to the instret register is permitted unless some other architectural rule prevents it.
RULE 72: In VU-mode, a read of the instret register is not permitted unless the IR bit is set in both hcounteren and scounteren.
RULE 73: If the IR bit in hcounteren is read-only zero, then any read of the instret register while V=1 will cause an exception.
RULE 74: In M-mode, accessing instret register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 75: In S-mode, accessing instret register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 76: In U-mode, accessing instret register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 77: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the instret register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc02, a0; csrr a1, 0xc02; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 78: In M-mode, accessing instret register while Smcdeleg extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smcdeleg; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 79: In M-mode, accessing instret register while Smcntrpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smcntrpmf; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 80: In M-mode, accessing instret register while Smcsrind extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smcsrind; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 81: In M-mode, accessing instret register while Smstateen extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smstateen; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 82: In M-mode, accessing instret register while Ssccfg extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssccfg; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 83: In M-mode, accessing instret register while Sscsrind extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscsrind; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 84: In M-mode, accessing instret register while Zicntr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicntr; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 85: In M-mode, accessing instret register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: marchid
NUMBER: 0xf12
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=Architecture
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: marchid is a machine-level read-only (MRO) CSR.
RULE 2: marchid is an MXLEN-bit read-only CSR that encodes the base microarchitecture of the hart.
RULE 3: marchid must be readable in any implementation.
RULE 4: marchid may return a value of 0 to indicate that the field is not implemented.
RULE 5: Open-source architecture IDs that may be placed in marchid are allocated globally by RISC-V International, are non-zero, and have a zero most-significant-bit.
RULE 6: Commercial architecture IDs that may be placed in marchid are allocated by each commercial vendor independently, must have the most-significant-bit set, and cannot contain zero in the remaining MXLEN-1 bits.
RULE 7: Commercial architecture IDs used in marchid must be disjoint from open-source architecture IDs by having the most-significant-bit set, to prevent collisions when a vendor uses both closed-source and open-source microarchitectures.
RULE 8: In M-mode, accessing marchid register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xf12; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 9: In S-mode, accessing marchid register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xf12; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 10: In U-mode, accessing marchid register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xf12; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 11: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the marchid register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xf12, a0; csrr a1, 0xf12; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: mcause
NUMBER: 0x342
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..63=INT, 62..0=CODE
EXTENSIONS: H, Smdbltrp, Smrnmi, Sscofpmf, Ssdbltrp, Zicfilp
RULE 1: The mcause CSR has machine-mode read/write privilege (MRW).
RULE 2: When a double-trap occurs, the Smrnmi extension is implemented, and mnstatus.NMIE is 1, the mncause register is written with the value that the unexpected trap would have written to the mcause register.
RULE 3: When a double-trap occurs and either the Smrnmi extension is not implemented or the Smrnmi extension is implemented with mnstatus.NMIE equal to 0, the mcause register is not updated as part of the architectural state.
RULE 4: When a trap is delegated to S-mode, the mcause register is not written.
RULE 5: The index of each bit position in the medeleg register is equal to the value returned in the mcause register.
RULE 6: If the bit in medeleg that corresponds to the value returned in the mcause register is set, a trap occurring in S-mode or U-mode is delegated to the S-mode trap handler.
RULE 7: The interrupt cause number i reported in the mcause CSR corresponds to bit i in the mip CSR.
RULE 8: The interrupt cause number i reported in the mcause CSR corresponds to bit i in the mie CSR.
RULE 9: mcause is an MXLEN-bit read-write register.
RULE 10: When a trap is taken into M-mode, mcause is written with a code indicating the event that caused the trap.
RULE 11: When a trap is not taken into M-mode, the implementation never writes mcause, although software may write it explicitly.
RULE 12: The Interrupt bit in mcause is set if the trap was caused by an interrupt.
RULE 13: The Exception Code field in mcause contains a code identifying the last exception or interrupt.
RULE 14: Load and load-reserved instructions generate load exceptions whose exception codes (such as 4-7, 13, 15, etc.) are recorded in mcause.
RULE 15: Store, store-conditional, and AMO instructions generate store/AMO exceptions whose exception codes (such as 6, 7, 15, etc.) are recorded in mcause.
RULE 16: If an instruction may raise multiple synchronous exceptions, the decreasing priority order defined in Table 17 determines which exception is taken and reported in mcause.
RULE 17: When a software-check exception is raised, mcause is written with Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 18.
RULE 18: When a hardware-error exception is raised, mcause is written with Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 19.
RULE 19: When virtual address translation determines a specific exception, the exception chosen according to Table 17 priority is the one reported in mcause.
RULE 20: Instruction address breakpoints are reported in mcause with Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 3.
RULE 21: Instruction address-misaligned exceptions are reported in mcause with Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 0 and have lower priority than other instruction-address exceptions.
RULE 22: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 0, the cause is Reserved.
RULE 23: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 1, the cause is a supervisor software interrupt.
RULE 24: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 2, the cause is Reserved.
RULE 25: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 3, the cause is a machine software interrupt.
RULE 26: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 4, the cause is Reserved.
RULE 27: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 5, the cause is a supervisor timer interrupt.
RULE 28: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 6, the cause is Reserved.
RULE 29: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 7, the cause is a machine timer interrupt.
RULE 30: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 8, the cause is Reserved.
RULE 31: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 9, the cause is a supervisor external interrupt.
RULE 32: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 10, the cause is Reserved.
RULE 33: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 11, the cause is a machine external interrupt.
RULE 34: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 12, the cause is Reserved.
RULE 35: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 13, the cause is a counter-overflow interrupt.
RULE 36: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code in the range 14-15, the cause is Reserved.
RULE 37: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code >= 16, the cause is designated for platform use.
RULE 38: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 0, the cause is an instruction address misaligned exception.
RULE 39: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 1, the cause is an instruction access fault.
RULE 40: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 2, the cause is an illegal instruction.
RULE 41: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 3, the cause is a breakpoint.
RULE 42: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 4, the cause is a load address misaligned exception.
RULE 43: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 5, the cause is a load access fault.
RULE 44: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 6, the cause is a store/AMO address misaligned exception.
RULE 45: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 7, the cause is a store/AMO access fault.
RULE 46: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 8, the cause is an environment call from U-mode.
RULE 47: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 9, the cause is an environment call from S-mode.
RULE 48: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 10, the cause is Reserved.
RULE 49: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 11, the cause is an environment call from M-mode.
RULE 50: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 12, the cause is an instruction page fault.
RULE 51: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 13, the cause is a load page fault.
RULE 52: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 14, the cause is Reserved.
RULE 53: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 15, the cause is a store/AMO page fault.
RULE 54: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 16, the cause is a double trap.
RULE 55: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 17, the cause is Reserved.
RULE 56: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 18, the cause is a software-check exception.
RULE 57: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 19, the cause is a hardware-error exception.
RULE 58: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code in the range 20-23, the cause is Reserved.
RULE 59: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code in the range 24-31, the cause is designated for custom use.
RULE 60: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code in the range 32-47, the cause is Reserved.
RULE 61: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code in the range 48-63, the cause is designated for custom use.
RULE 62: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code >= 64, the cause is Reserved.
RULE 63: Implementations that do not distinguish different reset conditions should return the value 0 in the mcause register after reset.
RULE 64: Implementations that distinguish different reset conditions should use the value 0 in the mcause register only to indicate the most complete reset.
RULE 65: When an NMI occurs, mcause is set to a value indicating the source of the NMI.
RULE 66: The high Interrupt bit of mcause should be set to indicate that this was an interrupt.
RULE 67: Exception Code 0 in mcause is reserved to mean "unknown cause".
RULE 68: When an unresumable non-maskable interrupt (UNMI) occurs and the NMI jumps to a handler in machine mode, the mcause CSR is overwritten with the new cause value.
RULE 69: If a UNMI occurs while the hart is executing machine-mode code in a trap handler, the prior value stored in mcause cannot be recovered.
RULE 70: When an unexpected trap occurs while the S-mode-disable-trap (SDT) bit is 1, the hart does not write the mcause register together with the other CSRs that would be written for a normal trap.
RULE 71: In the double-trap situation described, the hart later sets the mcause register to the fixed exception code 16, which is defined as the double-trap exception code.
RULE 72: In that same double-trap situation, after writing all other registers except mcause and mtval2, the value that would have been written to mcause by the unexpected trap is instead written to the mtval2 register.
RULE 73: In the mcause register the most-significant bit is 1 for interrupt causes and 0 for exception causes.
RULE 74: In the mcause register the remaining bits encode the numeric cause code as defined in the hypervisor-extension trap-cause table.
RULE 75: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 0, mcause reports a Reserved interrupt.
RULE 76: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 1, mcause reports a Supervisor software interrupt.
RULE 77: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 2, mcause reports a Virtual supervisor software interrupt.
RULE 78: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 3, mcause reports a Machine software interrupt.
RULE 79: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 4, mcause reports a Reserved interrupt.
RULE 80: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 5, mcause reports a Supervisor timer interrupt.
RULE 81: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 6, mcause reports a Virtual supervisor timer interrupt.
RULE 82: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 7, mcause reports a Machine timer interrupt.
RULE 83: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 8, mcause reports a Reserved interrupt.
RULE 84: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 9, mcause reports a Supervisor external interrupt.
RULE 85: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 10, mcause reports a Virtual supervisor external interrupt.
RULE 86: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 11, mcause reports a Machine external interrupt.
RULE 87: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 12, mcause reports a Supervisor guest external interrupt.
RULE 88: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 13, mcause reports a Counter-overflow interrupt.
RULE 89: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 14 or 15, mcause reports a Reserved interrupt.
RULE 90: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 16 or greater, mcause reports a platform-designated interrupt.
RULE 91: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 0, mcause reports an Instruction address misaligned exception.
RULE 92: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 1, mcause reports an Instruction access fault exception.
RULE 93: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 2, mcause reports an Illegal instruction exception.
RULE 94: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 3, mcause reports a Breakpoint exception.
RULE 95: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 4, mcause reports a Load address misaligned exception.
RULE 96: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 5, mcause reports a Load access fault exception.
RULE 97: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 6, mcause reports a Store/AMO address misaligned exception.
RULE 98: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 7, mcause reports a Store/AMO access fault exception.
RULE 99: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 8, mcause reports an Environment call from U-mode or VU-mode exception.
RULE 100: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 9, mcause reports an Environment call from HS-mode exception.
RULE 101: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 10, mcause reports an Environment call from VS-mode exception.
RULE 102: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 11, mcause reports an Environment call from M-mode exception.
RULE 103: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 12, mcause reports an Instruction page fault exception.
RULE 104: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 13, mcause reports a Load page fault exception.
RULE 105: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 14, mcause reports a Reserved exception.
RULE 106: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 15, mcause reports a Store/AMO page fault exception.
RULE 107: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 16, mcause reports a Double trap exception.
RULE 108: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 17, mcause reports a Reserved exception.
RULE 109: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 18, mcause reports a Software check exception.
RULE 110: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 19, mcause reports a Hardware error exception.
RULE 111: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 20, mcause reports an Instruction guest-page fault exception.
RULE 112: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 21, mcause reports a Load guest-page fault exception.
RULE 113: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 22, mcause reports a Virtual instruction exception.
RULE 114: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 23, mcause reports a Store/AMO guest-page fault exception.
RULE 115: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is in the range 24-31, mcause reports a custom-use exception.
RULE 116: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is in the range 32-47, mcause reports a Reserved exception.
RULE 117: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is in the range 48-63, mcause reports a custom-use exception.
RULE 118: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 64 or greater, mcause reports a Reserved exception.
RULE 119: An environment call from HS-mode sets mcause to the exception code 9.
RULE 120: An environment call from VS-mode sets mcause to the exception code 10.
RULE 121: When V=1 and the attempted instruction is HS-qualified but is prevented from executing because of insufficient privilege or because a supervisor or hypervisor CSR such as scounteren or hcounteren disables it, mcause is set to the virtual-instruction exception code 22.
RULE 122: In VS-mode, attempts to access a non-high-half counter CSR when the corresponding bit in hcounteren is 0 and the same bit in mcounteren is 1 cause mcause to be set to the virtual-instruction exception code 22.
RULE 123: In VU-mode, attempts to access a non-high-half counter CSR when either the corresponding bit in hcounteren or scounteren is 0 and the same bit in mcounteren is 1 cause mcause to be set to the virtual-instruction exception code 22.
RULE 124: In VS-mode or VU-mode, attempts to execute a hypervisor instruction (HLV, HLVX, HSV, or HFENCE) cause mcause to be set to the virtual-instruction exception code 22.
RULE 125: In VS-mode or VU-mode, attempts to access an implemented non-high-half hypervisor CSR or VS CSR when the same access would be allowed in HS-mode assuming mstatus.TVM=0 cause mcause to be set to the virtual-instruction exception code 22.
RULE 126: In VU-mode, attempts to access an implemented non-high-half supervisor CSR when the same access would be allowed in HS-mode assuming mstatus.TVM=0 cause mcause to be set to the virtual-instruction exception code 22.
RULE 127: In VS-mode, attempts to execute SRET when hstatus.VTSR=1 cause mcause to be set to the virtual-instruction exception code 22.
RULE 128: In VS-mode, attempts to execute an SFENCE.VMA or SINVAL.VMA instruction or to access satp when hstatus.VTVM=1 cause mcause to be set to the virtual-instruction exception code 22.
RULE 129: When an instruction can raise multiple synchronous exceptions, the exception with the highest priority according to the defined priority order is the one whose code is written into mcause.
RULE 130: An Instruction address breakpoint (exception code 3) has the highest priority among synchronous exceptions and therefore is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 131: During instruction address translation, the first encountered page fault (exception code 12), guest-page fault (exception code 20), or access fault (exception code 1) has priority over lower-priority exceptions and is reported in mcause.
RULE 132: An Instruction access fault with a physical address (exception code 1) has priority over illegal-instruction exceptions and is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 133: An Illegal instruction exception (exception code 2) has priority over virtual-instruction exceptions and is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 134: A Virtual instruction exception (exception code 22) has priority over instruction address misaligned exceptions and is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 135: An Instruction address misaligned exception (exception code 0) has priority over environment-call exceptions and is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 136: Environment call exceptions (exception codes 8, 9, 10, or 11) have priority over environment-break exceptions and are reported in mcause when they occur.
RULE 137: An Environment break exception (exception code 3) has priority over load/store/AMO address breakpoint exceptions and is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 138: A Load/store/AMO address breakpoint exception (exception code 3) has priority over optional load/store/AMO address-misaligned exceptions and is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 139: Optional load/store/AMO address-misaligned exceptions (exception codes 4 or 6) have priority over explicit memory-access page-fault or access-fault exceptions and are reported in mcause when they occur.
RULE 140: During address translation for an explicit memory access, the first encountered page fault (exception code 13), guest-page fault (exception code 15), or access fault (exception codes 21 or 23) has priority over load/store/AMO access-fault exceptions and is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 141: Load/store/AMO access-fault exceptions (exception codes 5 or 7) have priority over load/store/AMO address-misaligned exceptions when no higher-priority exception is present and are reported in mcause.
RULE 142: If no higher-priority exception applies, load/store/AMO address-misaligned exceptions (exception codes 4 or 6) are reported in mcause.
RULE 143: When a trap is taken into M-mode, the implementation writes the mcause CSR.
RULE 144: When a trap is taken into M-mode, the implementation writes the mcause CSR together with the mepc, mtval, mtval2, and mtinst CSRs.
RULE 145: In M-mode, accessing mcause register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x342; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 146: In S-mode, accessing mcause register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x342; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 147: In U-mode, accessing mcause register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x342; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 148: In M-mode, setting mcause.INT (bit 63) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x342, a0; csrr a1, 0x342; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000].
RULE 149: In M-mode, setting mcause.CODE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x342, a0; csrr a1, 0x342; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 150: In M-mode, accessing mcause register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x342; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 151: In M-mode, accessing mcause register while Smdbltrp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smdbltrp; csrr a0, 0x342; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 152: In M-mode, accessing mcause register while Smrnmi extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smrnmi; csrr a0, 0x342; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 153: In M-mode, accessing mcause register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0x342; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 154: In M-mode, accessing mcause register while Ssdbltrp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssdbltrp; csrr a0, 0x342; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 155: In M-mode, accessing mcause register while Zicfilp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicfilp; csrr a0, 0x342; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mconfigptr
NUMBER: 0xf15
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDRESS
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The mconfigptr CSR has privilege MRO (machine-read-only).
RULE 2: The mconfigptr register is an MXLEN-bit read-only CSR that holds the physical address of a configuration data structure.
RULE 3: If MXLEN is 8 × n, then the bits mconfigptr[log₂ n-1:0] MUST be zero.
RULE 4: The mconfigptr register MUST be implemented.
RULE 5: In M-mode, accessing mconfigptr register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xf15; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 6: In S-mode, accessing mconfigptr register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xf15; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 7: In U-mode, accessing mconfigptr register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xf15; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 8: In M-mode, setting mconfigptr.ADDRESS (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0xf15, a0; csrr a1, 0xf15; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 9: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the mconfigptr register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xf15, a0; csrr a1, 0xf15; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: mcontext
NUMBER: 0x7a8
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 13..0=HCONTEXT
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The mcontext CSR is defined with machine-mode read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: The mcontext CSR is a machine-mode register.
RULE 3: In M-mode, accessing mcontext register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x7a8; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 4: In S-mode, accessing mcontext register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x7a8; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 5: In U-mode, accessing mcontext register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x7a8; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 6: In M-mode, setting mcontext.HCONTEXT (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x7a8, a0; csrr a1, 0x7a8; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 7: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the mcontext register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x7a8, a0; csrr a1, 0x7a8; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: mcounteren
NUMBER: 0x306
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 32
FIELDS: 31..31=HPM31, 30..30=HPM30, 29..29=HPM29, 28..28=HPM28, 27..27=HPM27, 26..26=HPM26, 25..25=HPM25, 24..24=HPM24, 23..23=HPM23, 22..22=HPM22, 21..21=HPM21, 20..20=HPM20, 19..19=HPM19, 18..18=HPM18, 17..17=HPM17, 16..16=HPM16, 15..15=HPM15, 14..14=HPM14, 13..13=HPM13, 12..12=HPM12, 11..11=HPM11, 10..10=HPM10, 9..9=HPM9, 8..8=HPM8, 7..7=HPM7, 6..6=HPM6, 5..5=HPM5, 4..4=HPM4, 3..3=HPM3, 2..2=IR, 1..1=TM, 0..0=CY
EXTENSIONS: H, Smcdeleg, Smcntrpmf, Smcsrind, Smstateen, Ssccfg, Sscofpmf, Sscsrind
RULE 1: The mcounteren CSR has machine-mode read-write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: Reading or writing the mcounteren register does not affect the underlying counters, which continue to increment even when not accessible.
RULE 3: If any of the CY, TM, IR, or HPM n bits in the mcounteren register is clear, an attempt to read the corresponding counter register (cycle, time, instret, or hpmcountern) while executing in S-mode or U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 4: If any of the CY, TM, IR, or HPM n bits in the mcounteren register is set, access to the corresponding counter register is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented otherwise U-mode.
RULE 5: If the TM bit in the mcounteren register is clear, an attempt to access the stimecmp or vstimecmp register while executing in any mode less privileged than M must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 6: If the TM bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the stimecmp or vstimecmp register is permitted in S-mode if S-mode is implemented.
RULE 7: If the TM bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the vstimecmp register via the stimecmp address is permitted in VS-mode if VS-mode is implemented and the TM bit in hcounteren does not otherwise prevent it.
RULE 8: In harts that implement U-mode, the mcounteren register must be implemented and all of its fields are WARL and may be read-only zero.
RULE 9: In harts that implement U-mode, a zero value in an mcounteren field indicates that reads of the corresponding counter in a less-privileged mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: In harts that do not implement U-mode, the mcounteren register should not exist.
RULE 11: The mcounteren register permits M-mode to grant the next-lower privilege mode read access to selected hardware counters.
RULE 12: If the Smcdeleg or Ssccfg extensions are enabled (menvcfg.CDE = 1), then the mcounteren register additionally permits M-mode to delegate selected counters to S-mode.
RULE 13: A counter i is delegated when both mcounteren[i] = 1 and menvcfg.CDE = 1.
RULE 14: When a counter i is delegated (mcounteren[i] = 1 and menvcfg.CDE = 1) and siselect holds the value 0x40 + i, the register state associated with counter i may be read via sireg.
RULE 15: When a counter i is delegated (mcounteren[i] = 1 and menvcfg.CDE = 1) and siselect holds the value 0x40 + i, the register state associated with counter i may be written via sireg.
RULE 16: While executing in M-mode or S-mode and with siselect containing a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, any attempt to access a sireg when siselect = 0x41 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 17: While executing in M-mode or S-mode and with siselect containing a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, any attempt to access a sireg when the selected counter is not delegated to S-mode (the corresponding mcounteren bit = 0) raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 18: Setting a bit in mcounteren does not affect whether the corresponding bit in scounteren is writable.
RULE 19: U-mode may only access a counter if the corresponding bits in scounteren and mcounteren are both set.
RULE 20: Read access to a scountovf bit X in S-mode is governed by the same mcounteren CSR that mediates access to the hpmcounter CSRs for that privilege mode.
RULE 21: Read access to a scountovf bit X in VS-mode is governed by both the mcounteren CSR and the hcounteren CSR that mediate access to the hpmcounter CSRs for that privilege mode.
RULE 22: In M-mode, the mcounteren register does not restrict read access to a scountovf bit X, which is always readable.
RULE 23: In S-mode and HS-mode, a scountovf bit X is readable only when the corresponding bit X in the mcounteren register is set; otherwise the read returns zero.
RULE 24: In VS-mode, a scountovf bit X is readable only when both the corresponding bit X in the mcounteren register and the corresponding bit X in the hcounteren register are set; otherwise the read returns zero.
RULE 25: If the CY bit in hcounteren is clear, V=1, and the CY bit in mcounteren is 1, then a virtual-instruction exception occurs on an attempt to read the cycle register.
RULE 26: If the TM bit in hcounteren is clear, V=1, and the TM bit in mcounteren is 1, then a virtual-instruction exception occurs on an attempt to read the time register.
RULE 27: If the IR bit in hcounteren is clear, V=1, and the IR bit in mcounteren is 1, then a virtual-instruction exception occurs on an attempt to read the instret register.
RULE 28: If an HPM n bit in hcounteren is clear, V=1, and the same HPM n bit in mcounteren is 1, then a virtual-instruction exception occurs on an attempt to read the hpmcounter n register.
RULE 29: If the TM bit in hcounteren is clear, VS-mode is active, and the TM bit in mcounteren is set, then a virtual-instruction exception occurs on an attempt to access the vstimecmp register via stimecmp.
RULE 30: If the TM bit in hcounteren and the TM bit in mcounteren are both set, and the implementation provides the vstimecmp register, then access to vstimecmp in VS-mode is permitted.
RULE 31: In VS-mode, an attempt to access a non-high-half counter CSR when the corresponding bit in hcounteren is 0 and the same bit in mcounteren is 1 raises a virtual-instruction exception (exception code 22).
RULE 32: In VU-mode, an attempt to access a non-high-half counter CSR when the corresponding bit in either hcounteren or scounteren is 0 and the same bit in mcounteren is 1 raises a virtual-instruction exception (exception code 22).
RULE 33: In M-mode, accessing mcounteren register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x306; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 34: In S-mode, accessing mcounteren register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x306; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 35: In U-mode, accessing mcounteren register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x306; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 36: In M-mode, setting mcounteren.HPM18 (bit 18) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x40000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x40000; csrs 0x306, a0; csrr a1, 0x306; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x40000].

REGISTER: mcountinhibit
NUMBER: 0x320
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 32
FIELDS: 31..31=HPM31, 30..30=HPM30, 29..29=HPM29, 28..28=HPM28, 27..27=HPM27, 26..26=HPM26, 25..25=HPM25, 24..24=HPM24, 23..23=HPM23, 22..22=HPM22, 21..21=HPM21, 20..20=HPM20, 19..19=HPM19, 18..18=HPM18, 17..17=HPM17, 16..16=HPM16, 15..15=HPM15, 14..14=HPM14, 13..13=HPM13, 12..12=HPM12, 11..11=HPM11, 10..10=HPM10, 9..9=HPM9, 8..8=HPM8, 7..7=HPM7, 6..6=HPM6, 5..5=HPM5, 4..4=HPM4, 3..3=HPM3, 2..2=IR, 0..0=CY
EXTENSIONS: Smcdeleg, Ssccfg, Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The mcountinhibit CSR is a machine-level CSR.
RULE 2: The mcountinhibit CSR has read/write privilege, designated MRW.
RULE 3: Settings in the mcountinhibit register affect only whether the counters increment and do not affect the counters' accessibility.
RULE 4: When a CY, IR, or HPM n bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the corresponding mcycle, minstret, or mhpmcounter n register increments as usual.
RULE 5: When a CY, IR, or HPM n bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the corresponding counter does not increment.
RULE 6: If the mcycle CSR is shared between harts on the same core, the mcountinhibit.CY field is also shared between those harts and writes to mcountinhibit.CY are visible to those harts.
RULE 7: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as if the register were set to zero.
RULE 8: The mcountinhibit mechanism does not inhibit the mtime counter, which may be shared between multiple cores.
RULE 9: For any hardware counter that is delegated to supervisor mode, the corresponding bit in the mcountinhibit register can be read and written via the scountinhibit register.
RULE 10: For any hardware counter that is not delegated to supervisor mode, the corresponding bit in the scountinhibit register reads as zero, indicating that the associated mcountinhibit bit is not accessible through scountinhibit.
RULE 11: If the CDE field of the menvcfg CSR is zero, any attempt to access the scountinhibit register, which aliases mcountinhibit, causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: When supervisor counter delegation is enabled, any attempt to access the scountinhibit register from VS-mode or VU-mode, which maps to mcountinhibit, raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 13: In M-mode, accessing mcountinhibit register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x320; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 14: In S-mode, accessing mcountinhibit register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x320; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 15: In U-mode, accessing mcountinhibit register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x320; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 16: In M-mode, setting mcountinhibit.HPM18 (bit 18) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x40000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x40000; csrs 0x320, a0; csrr a1, 0x320; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x40000].

REGISTER: mcycle
NUMBER: 0xb00
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Smcdeleg, Ssccfg, Sscofpmf
RULE 1: Implicit reads of the mcycle CSR are ordered as device input.
RULE 2: For the purposes of the FENCE instruction, a read of the mcycle CSR is classified as device input (I).
RULE 3: For the purposes of the FENCE instruction, a write of the mcycle CSR is classified as device output (O).
RULE 4: An explicit read of the mcycle CSR returns the mcycle state before the execution of the instruction.
RULE 5: An explicit write to the mcycle CSR suppresses and overrides any implicit writes or modifications to the same CSR by the same instruction.
RULE 6: CSR accesses, including accesses to the mcycle CSR, are weakly ordered by default, and other harts or devices may observe mcycle CSR accesses in an order different from program order.
RULE 7: The mcycle CSR has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 8: The mcycle CSR counts the number of clock cycles executed by the processor core on which the hart is running.
RULE 9: After a hart reset, the mcycle register contains an arbitrary value.
RULE 10: The mcycle register can be written with a given value.
RULE 11: Any write to the mcycle CSR takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 12: The cycle CSR is a read-only shadow of mcycle.
RULE 13: Reading mcycle does not affect its underlying counter value.
RULE 14: Writing mcycle does not affect its underlying counter value.
RULE 15: The mcycle counter continues to increment even when it is not accessible.
RULE 16: If the CY bit in mcounteren is clear, a read of the cycle CSR executed in S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception, preventing read access to mcycle in those modes.
RULE 17: In harts that implement U-mode, each field of mcounteren is WARL and may be hardwired to zero, which causes reads of the corresponding counter - including reads of mcycle via the cycle CSR - to raise an illegal-instruction exception when executed in a less-privileged mode.
RULE 18: When the CY bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mcycle register increments as usual.
RULE 19: When the CY bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mcycle register does not increment.
RULE 20: The mcycle CSR may be shared between harts on the same core, and in that case the mcountinhibit.CY field is also shared so writes to mcountinhibit.CY are visible to those harts.
RULE 21: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as if the register were set to zero, causing the mcycle register to increment as usual.
RULE 22: The setting of the mcountinhibit register controls only the incrementing of the mcycle register and does not affect its accessibility.
RULE 23: If the MINH field (bit 62) of mcyclecfg is set, counting of events for mcycle in M-mode is inhibited.
RULE 24: If the SINH field (bit 61) of mcyclecfg is set, counting of events for mcycle in S/HS-mode is inhibited.
RULE 25: If the UINH field (bit 60) of mcyclecfg is set, counting of events for mcycle in U-mode is inhibited.
RULE 26: If the VSINH field (bit 59) of mcyclecfg is set, counting of events for mcycle in VS-mode is inhibited.
RULE 27: If the VUINH field (bit 58) of mcyclecfg is set, counting of events for mcycle in VU-mode is inhibited.
RULE 28: When all INH bits (bits 62-58) of mcyclecfg are zero, counting of events for mcycle is enabled in all privilege modes.
RULE 29: If a privilege mode corresponding to an INH bit (bits 61-58) of mcyclecfg is not implemented, that INH bit is read-only zero, thereby having no effect on mcycle counting.
RULE 30: If the Smcdeleg or Ssccfg extensions are implemented, supervisor-level code may access mcyclecfg, allowing it to influence mcycle counting behavior.
RULE 31: The mcycle register increments at the same rate as the elapsed cycle counter (CtrCycleCounter).
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing mcycle register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb00; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 33: In S-mode, accessing mcycle register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb00; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 34: In U-mode, accessing mcycle register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb00; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 35: In M-mode, accessing mcycle register while Smcdeleg extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smcdeleg; csrr a0, 0xb00; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 36: In M-mode, accessing mcycle register while Ssccfg extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssccfg; csrr a0, 0xb00; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 37: In M-mode, accessing mcycle register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0xb00; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: medeleg
NUMBER: 0x302
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 23..23=SGPF, 22..22=VI, 21..21=LGPF, 20..20=IGPF, 15..15=SPF, 13..13=LPF, 12..12=IPF, 11..11=EM, 10..10=EVS, 9..9=ES, 8..8=EU, 7..7=SAF, 6..6=SAM, 5..5=LAF, 4..4=LAM, 3..3=B, 2..2=II, 1..1=IAF, 0..0=IAM
EXTENSIONS: S
RULE 1: The medeleg CSR has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege, meaning it can be read and written in Machine mode.
RULE 2: medeleg is a 64-bit read/write register.
RULE 3: In harts that implement S-mode, medeleg must exist.
RULE 4: Setting a bit in medeleg delegates the corresponding trap, when occurring in S-mode or U-mode, to the S-mode trap handler.
RULE 5: In harts that do not implement S-mode, medeleg should not exist.
RULE 6: Implementations shall not have any bits of medeleg be read-only one; any synchronous trap that can be delegated must support not being delegated.
RULE 7: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, scause is written with the trap cause.
RULE 8: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, sepc is written with the virtual address of the instruction that took the trap.
RULE 9: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, stval is written with an exception-specific datum.
RULE 10: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, the SPP field of mstatus is written with the active privilege mode at the time of the trap.
RULE 11: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, the SPIE field of mstatus is written with the value of the SIE field at the time of the trap.
RULE 12: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, the SIE field of mstatus is cleared.
RULE 13: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, mcause is not written.
RULE 14: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, mepc is not written.
RULE 15: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, mtval is not written.
RULE 16: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, the MPP field of mstatus is not written.
RULE 17: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, the MPIE field of mstatus is not written.
RULE 18: medeleg has a bit position allocated for every synchronous exception, with the index of the bit equal to the value returned in the mcause register.
RULE 19: Setting bit 8 in medeleg allows user-mode environment calls to be delegated to a lower-privilege trap handler.
RULE 20: Bits in medeleg that correspond to exceptions that cannot occur in less privileged modes shall be read-only zero.
RULE 21: medeleg[11] is read-only zero.
RULE 22: medeleg[16] is read-only zero.
RULE 23: By default all traps at any privilege level are handled in M-mode, but the medeleg CSR can be used by M-mode to delegate selected traps to HS-mode.
RULE 24: A synchronous trap that has been delegated to HS-mode using medeleg is further delegated to VS-mode when V = 1 before the trap and the corresponding hedeleg bit is set.
RULE 25: Under the control of the CSR medeleg, guest-page-fault traps may be delegated from M-mode to HS-mode.
RULE 26: Guest-page-fault traps cannot be delegated to any privilege mode other than HS-mode via the CSR medeleg.
RULE 27: When a trap occurs in HS-mode or U-mode, the trap is taken in M-mode unless medeleg (or mideleg) delegates the trap, in which case the trap is taken in HS-mode.
RULE 28: When a trap occurs in VS-mode or VU-mode, the trap is taken in M-mode unless medeleg (or mideleg) delegates the trap, in which case the trap is taken in HS-mode unless hedeleg (or hideleg) further delegates the trap, in which case the trap is taken in VS-mode.
RULE 29: In M-mode, accessing medeleg register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x302; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 30: In S-mode, accessing medeleg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x302; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 31: In U-mode, accessing medeleg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x302; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
