RULE 47: In M-mode, setting medeleg.II (bit 2) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x4) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4; csrs 0x302, a0; csrr a1, 0x302; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x4].
RULE 48: In M-mode, setting medeleg.IAF (bit 1) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2; csrs 0x302, a0; csrr a1, 0x302; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2].
RULE 49: In M-mode, setting medeleg.IAM (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x302, a0; csrr a1, 0x302; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 50: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the medeleg register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x302, a0; csrr a1, 0x302; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 51: In M-mode, accessing medeleg register while S extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: S; csrr a0, 0x302; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: menvcfg
NUMBER: 0x30a
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=STCE, 62..62=PBMTE, 61..61=ADUE, 7..7=CBZE, 6..6=CBCFE, 5..4=CBIE, 3..3=SSE, 0..0=FIOM
EXTENSIONS: Svnapot, Svpbmt
RULE 1: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBIE field of menvcfg equals 00 then an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 2: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBIE field of menvcfg equals 01 then the instruction executes and performs a flush operation.
RULE 3: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBIE field of menvcfg is not 01 and is not 00 then the instruction executes and performs an invalidate operation.
RULE 4: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBCFE field of menvcfg is false then an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 5: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBCFE field of menvcfg is true then the instruction executes.
RULE 6: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBZE field of menvcfg is false then an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 7: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBZE field of menvcfg is true then the instruction executes.
RULE 8: The CBIE, CBCFE, and CBZE fields in menvcfg do not affect the read or write behavior of the same-named fields in senvcfg or henvcfg.
RULE 9: The menvcfg CSR is a machine-level CSR.
RULE 10: The menvcfg CSR has read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 11: The menvcfgh CSR, which supplies the upper 32 bits of menvcfg, is a machine-level CSR with read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 12: The menvcfg CSR is a 64-bit read/write register.
RULE 13: If the FIOM bit is set to one in menvcfg, FENCE instructions executed in modes less privileged than M are modified so the requirement to order accesses to device I/O also orders main memory accesses.
RULE 14: If FIOM=1 in menvcfg, for modes less privileged than M an atomic instruction that accesses a region ordered as device I/O and has its aq and/or rl bit set is ordered as though it accesses both device I/O and memory.
RULE 15: If S-mode is not supported or if satp.MODE is read-only zero, an implementation may make the FIOM bit read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 16: When FIOM=1 in menvcfg, setting the PI bit in a FENCE instruction implies predecessor device input and memory reads.
RULE 17: When FIOM=1 in menvcfg, setting the PO bit in a FENCE instruction implies predecessor device output and memory writes.
RULE 18: When FIOM=1 in menvcfg, setting the SI bit in a FENCE instruction implies successor device input and memory reads.
RULE 19: When FIOM=1 in menvcfg, setting the SO bit in a FENCE instruction implies successor device output and memory writes.
RULE 20: The PBMTE bit in menvcfg controls whether the Svpbmt extension is available for use in S-mode and G-stage address translation.
RULE 21: When PBMTE=1 in menvcfg, Svpbmt is available for S-mode and G-stage address translation.
RULE 22: When PBMTE=0 in menvcfg, the implementation behaves as though Svpbmt were not implemented.
RULE 23: If Svpbmt is not implemented, the PBMTE bit is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 24: For implementations with the hypervisor extension, henvcfg.PBMTE is read-only zero if menvcfg.PBMTE is zero.
RULE 25: After changing menvcfg.PBMTE, executing an SFENCE.VMA instruction with rs1=x0 and rs2=x0 suffices to synchronize address-translation caches with respect to the altered interpretation of page-table entries' PBMT fields.
RULE 26: The ADUE bit in menvcfg controls whether hardware updating of PTE A/D bits is enabled for S-mode and G-stage address translation when the Svadu extension is implemented.
RULE 27: When ADUE=1 in menvcfg, hardware updating of PTE A/D bits is enabled during S-mode address translation, and the implementation behaves as though Svade were not implemented for S-mode address translation.
RULE 28: When the hypervisor extension is implemented and ADUE=1 in menvcfg, hardware updating of PTE A/D bits is enabled during G-stage address translation, and the implementation behaves as though Svade were not implemented for G-stage address translation.
RULE 29: When ADUE=0 in menvcfg, the implementation behaves as though Svade is implemented for S-mode and G-stage address translation.
RULE 30: If Svadu is not implemented, the ADUE bit is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 31: For implementations with the hypervisor extension, henvcfg.ADUE is read-only zero if menvcfg.ADUE is zero.
RULE 32: After changing menvcfg.ADUE, executing an SFENCE.VMA instruction with rs1=x0 and rs2=x0 suffices to synchronize address-translation caches with respect to the altered interpretation of page-table entries' A/D bits.
RULE 33: When ADUE=0 in menvcfg, Svade is implemented, requiring page-fault exceptions to be raised when PTE A/D bits need to be set.
RULE 34: When CDE=1 in menvcfg, the Smcdeleg extension is enabled.
RULE 35: When CDE=0 in menvcfg, the Smcdeleg and Ssccfg extensions appear to be not implemented.
RULE 36: If the Smcdeleg extension is not implemented, the CDE bit is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 37: When the Sstc extension is not implemented, the STCE bit is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 38: The STCE bit in menvcfg enables stimecmp for S-mode when set to one.
RULE 39: When the Sstc extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, an attempt to access stimecmp in a mode other than M-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception, henvcfg.STCE is read-only zero, and STIP in mip and sip reverts to its defined behavior as if the extension were not implemented.
RULE 40: If the H extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, hip.VSTIP also reverts its defined behavior as if the extension were not implemented.
RULE 41: When the Zicboz extension is not implemented, the CBZE field is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 42: When CBZE=1 in menvcfg, it enables execution of the cache block zero instruction CBO.ZERO in modes less privileged than M.
RULE 43: When CBZE is not set to one in menvcfg, the CBO.ZERO instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception in modes less privileged than M.
RULE 44: When the Zicbom extension is not implemented, the CBCFE field is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 45: When CBCFE=1 in menvcfg, it enables execution of the cache block clean instruction CBO.CLEAN and the cache block flush instruction CBO.FLUSH in modes less privileged than M.
RULE 46: When CBCFE is not set to one in menvcfg, CBO.CLEAN and CBO.FLUSH raise illegal-instruction exceptions in modes less privileged than M.
RULE 47: When the Zicbom extension is not implemented, the CBIE field is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 48: When CBIE=00b in menvcfg, the instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception in modes less privileged than M.
RULE 49: Encoding 10b of the CBIE field in menvcfg is reserved.
RULE 50: When CBIE=01b in menvcfg and the instruction is enabled for execution in modes less privileged than M, the instruction is executed and performs a flush operation even if configured by a less privileged mode to perform a invalidate operation.
RULE 51: When CBIE=11b in menvcfg and the instruction is enabled for execution in modes less privileged than M, the instruction is executed and performs an invalidate operation unless configured by a less privileged mode to perform a flush operation.
RULE 52: The CBIE field in menvcfg is a WARL field.
RULE 53: When the Smnpm extension is not implemented, the PMM field is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 54: The PMM field in menvcfg is a WARL field.
RULE 55: The PMM field in menvcfg enables or disables pointer masking for the next-lower privilege mode according to Table 19.
RULE 56: When LPE=1 in menvcfg and S-mode is implemented, the Zicfilp extension is enabled in S-mode.
RULE 57: When LPE=1 in menvcfg and S-mode is not implemented, the Zicfilp extension is enabled in U-mode.
RULE 58: When LPE=0 in menvcfg, the Zicfilp extension is not enabled in S-mode.
RULE 59: When LPE=0 in menvcfg and S-mode is implemented, the hart does not update the ELP state, which remains NO_LP_EXPECTED.
RULE 60: When LPE=0 in menvcfg and S-mode is implemented, the LPAD instruction operates as a no-op.
RULE 61: When LPE=0 in menvcfg and S-mode is not implemented, the hart does not update the ELP state (remaining NO_LP_EXPECTED) and the LPAD instruction operates as a no-op in U-mode.
RULE 62: When SSE=1 in menvcfg, the Zicfiss extension is activated in S-mode.
RULE 63: When SSE=0 in menvcfg, 16-bit Zicfiss instructions revert to the behavior defined by Zcmop.
RULE 64: When SSE=0 in menvcfg, the pte.xwr=010b encoding in VS/S-stage page tables becomes reserved.
RULE 65: When SSE=0 in menvcfg, the SSAMOSWAP.W/D instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 66: When SSE=0 in menvcfg, the henvcfg.SSE and senvcfg.SSE fields are read-only zero.
RULE 67: When DTE=0 in menvcfg, the implementation behaves as though the Ssdbltrp extension is not implemented.
RULE 68: When XLEN=64, the menvcfgh register does not exist, providing no alias for menvcfg.
RULE 69: If U-mode is not supported, the menvcfg register does not exist.
RULE 70: If U-mode is not supported, the menvcfgh register does not exist, providing no alias for menvcfg.
RULE 71: If the current privilege mode is M or S and siselect is in the range 0x40-0x5F, then any attempt to access a sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception when menvcfg.CDE is 0.
RULE 72: If the current privilege mode is VS, vsiselect is in the range 0x40-0x5F, and menvcfg.CDE is 0, then any attempt to access a vsireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 73: If the current privilege mode is VS, vsiselect is in the range 0x40-0x5F, and menvcfg.CDE is 1, then any attempt to access a vsireg* raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 74: If menvcfg.CDE = 0, any attempt to access scountinhibit raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 75: For implementations that support Smcdeleg/Ssccfg, Sscofpmf, and the H extension, if menvcfg.CDE = 1 then an attempt to read scountovf from VS-mode raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 76: For implementations that support Smcdeleg/Ssccfg, Sscofpmf, and the H extension, if menvcfg.CDE = 1 then an attempt to read scountovf from VU-mode raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 77: When menvcfg.SSE is 1, the SSAMOSWAP.W/D instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception in U-mode.
RULE 78: When menvcfg.SSE is 1, the SSAMOSWAP.W/D instruction raises a virtual-instruction exception in VU-mode.
RULE 79: If the Svadu extension is implemented, the menvcfg.ADUE field is writable.
RULE 80: If menvcfg.SSE is 1, executing SSAMOSWAP.W or SSAMOSWAP.D must raise a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 81: When the PBMTE or ADUE bits in menvcfg are changed, an HFENCE.GVMA instruction with rs1 = x0 and rs2 = x0 suffices to synchronize with respect to the altered interpretation of G-stage and VS-stage PTEs' PBMT and A/D bit fields, respectively.
RULE 82: If S-mode is implemented and the current privilege mode is S or HS, the LPE field in the menvcfg register supplies the xLPE state.
RULE 83: If S-mode is not implemented and the current privilege mode is U, the LPE field in the menvcfg register supplies the xLPE state.
RULE 84: Attempts to access the ssp CSR may raise either an illegal-instruction exception or a virtual-instruction exception depending on the value of the menvcfg.SSE field (as well as the senvcfg.SSE and henvcfg.SSE fields).
RULE 85: If the current privilege mode is less than M and the menvcfg.SSE field is 0, an illegal-instruction exception is raised when accessing the ssp CSR.
RULE 86: In S-mode and HS-mode, the architectural xSSE setting is determined by the value of the menvcfg.SSE field.
RULE 87: In M-mode, the architectural xSSE setting is always 0 regardless of the value of the menvcfg.SSE field.
RULE 88: Updates to the menvcfg.SSE field that affect xSSE take effect immediately and do not require address-translation caches to be synchronized with SFENCE.VMA, HFENCE.GVMA, or HFENCE.VVMA instructions.
RULE 89: When menvcfg.SSE=0, the encoding R=0, W=1, X=0 remains reserved.
RULE 90: In M-mode, accessing menvcfg register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x30a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 91: In S-mode, accessing menvcfg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x30a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 92: In U-mode, accessing menvcfg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x30a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 93: In M-mode, setting menvcfg.STCE (bit 63) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x30a, a0; csrr a1, 0x30a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000].
RULE 94: In M-mode, setting menvcfg.PBMTE (bit 62) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4000000000000000; csrs 0x30a, a0; csrr a1, 0x30a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 95: In M-mode, setting menvcfg.CBZE (bit 7) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x80) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x80; csrs 0x30a, a0; csrr a1, 0x30a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x80].
RULE 96: In M-mode, setting menvcfg.CBCFE (bit 6) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x40) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x40; csrs 0x30a, a0; csrr a1, 0x30a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x40].
RULE 97: In M-mode, setting menvcfg.CBIE (bit 4) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x10) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x10; csrs 0x30a, a0; csrr a1, 0x30a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x10].
RULE 98: In M-mode, setting menvcfg.SSE (bit 3) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8; csrs 0x30a, a0; csrr a1, 0x30a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8].
RULE 99: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the menvcfg register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x30a, a0; csrr a1, 0x30a; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 100: In M-mode, accessing menvcfg register while Svnapot extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Svnapot; csrr a0, 0x30a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 101: In M-mode, accessing menvcfg register while Svpbmt extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Svpbmt; csrr a0, 0x30a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mepc
NUMBER: 0x341
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=PC
EXTENSIONS: Smdbltrp, Smrnmi
RULE 1: The mepc CSR resides at machine privilege level.
RULE 2: The mepc CSR has machine read/write (MRW) access permissions.
RULE 3: When the Smrnmi extension is implemented and mnstatus.NMIE = 1, an unexpected trap causes the mnepc register to be written with the same value that the trap would have written to the mepc register.
RULE 4: When a trap is delegated to S-mode by setting the corresponding bit in medeleg or mideleg so that the trap occurs in S-mode instead of M-mode, the mepc register is not written.
RULE 5: mepc is an MXLEN-bit read/write register.
RULE 6: The least-significant bit of mepc (mepc[0]) is always zero.
RULE 7: On implementations that support only IALIGN=32, both low bits of mepc (mepc[1] and mepc[0]) are always zero.
RULE 8: If an implementation permits IALIGN to be either 16 or 32, then when IALIGN=32, bit mepc[1] is masked on reads so that it appears to be zero.
RULE 9: The read masking of mepc[1] when IALIGN=32 also applies to the implicit read performed by the MRET instruction.
RULE 10: Although masked on reads when IALIGN=32, bit mepc[1] remains writable.
RULE 11: mepc is a WARL register that MUST be able to hold all valid virtual addresses.
RULE 12: When address translation is not in effect, the set of addresses that mepc must be able to represent includes all physical addresses that can be used as a valid program counter or effective address.
RULE 13: When a trap is taken into M-mode, mepc is written with the virtual address of the instruction that was interrupted or that caused the exception.
RULE 14: In all other circumstances, mepc is never written by the implementation, although software may explicitly write mepc.
RULE 15: For a breakpoint exception raised by C.EBREAK, the virtual address of the faulting instruction is already recorded in mepc.
RULE 16: When an instruction access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception occurs on a hart that supports variable-length instructions, mepc points to the beginning of the faulting instruction.
RULE 17: On an illegal-instruction exception, mepc points to the faulting instruction in memory.
RULE 18: When a non-maskable interrupt (NMI) occurs, the mepc register is written with the virtual address of the instruction that was interrupted.
RULE 19: When a non-maskable interrupt (UNMI) occurs, the hardware overwrites the current mepc register with the address of the NMI handler executing in machine mode.
RULE 20: If the hart was executing machine-mode code in a trap handler when a UNMI occurs, the previous value of mepc cannot be recovered.
RULE 21: When a trap is taken into M-mode, the implementation writes the CSR mepc.
RULE 22: The write to mepc occurs only when a trap is taken into M-mode (i.e., the trap is not delegated to a lower privilege mode).
RULE 23: mepc is written as part of the set of CSRs that are updated on trap entry.
RULE 24: During execution of the MRET instruction, the hardware sets the program counter (pc) to the value contained in the mepc register.
RULE 25: In M-mode, accessing mepc register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x341; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 26: In S-mode, accessing mepc register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x341; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 27: In U-mode, accessing mepc register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x341; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 28: In M-mode, setting mepc.PC (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x341, a0; csrr a1, 0x341; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 29: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the mepc register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x341, a0; csrr a1, 0x341; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing mepc register while Smdbltrp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smdbltrp; csrr a0, 0x341; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 31: In M-mode, accessing mepc register while Smrnmi extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smrnmi; csrr a0, 0x341; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhartid
NUMBER: 0xf14
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ID
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The mhartid CSR is defined to be accessed only at machine privilege level.
RULE 2: The mhartid CSR has machine read-only (MRO) access, meaning it can be read but not written by software.
RULE 3: The mhartid CSR is an MXLEN-bit read-only register that contains the integer ID of the hardware thread executing the code.
RULE 4: The mhartid register MUST be readable in any implementation.
RULE 5: One hart MUST have a hart ID of zero as read from mhartid.
RULE 6: Hart IDs read from mhartid MUST be unique within the execution environment.
RULE 7: In M-mode, accessing mhartid register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xf14; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 8: In S-mode, accessing mhartid register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xf14; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 9: In U-mode, accessing mhartid register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xf14; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 10: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the mhartid register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xf14, a0; csrr a1, 0xf14; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: mhpmcounter10
NUMBER: 0xb0a
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zihpm
RULE 1: mhpmcounter10 has MRW access, meaning it is a machine-privileged read/write register.
RULE 2: A conforming implementation may implement mhpmcounter10 as a read-only zero register.
RULE 3: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter10 contains an arbitrary (implementation-dependent) value.
RULE 4: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter10 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 5: The value programmed in the 64-bit WARL register mhpmevent10 directly determines which events cause mhpmcounter10 to increment.
RULE 6: When XLEN=64, a read of mhpmcounter10 accesses the full 64-bit value.
RULE 7: When XLEN=64, a write to mhpmcounter10 updates the full 64-bit value.
RULE 8: The HPM10 bit in the mcounteren register controls the accessibility of the mhpmcounter10 register to lower privilege modes.
RULE 9: If the HPM10 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, any attempt to read the mhpmcounter10 CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: If the HPM10 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the mhpmcounter10 CSR is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented otherwise U-mode.
RULE 11: The hpmcounter10 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter10 hardware counter.
RULE 12: The mhpmcounter10 hardware counter continues to increment regardless of the state of the HPM10 bit in the mcounteren register.
RULE 13: Reading or writing the mcounteren register does not affect the mhpmcounter10 counter, which continues to increment even when not accessible.
RULE 14: When the HPM10 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, mhpmcounter10 increments as usual.
RULE 15: When the HPM10 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, mhpmcounter10 does not increment.
RULE 16: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as though the register were set to zero, treating the HPM10 bit as clear and causing mhpmcounter10 to increment as usual.
RULE 17: The OF bit in the mhpmevent10 register is set when mhpmcounter10 overflows and remains set until software writes the OF bit.
RULE 18: An overflow of mhpmcounter10 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits, causing the counter to wrap around while the sticky OF bit stays set.
RULE 19: If mhpmcounter10 overflows while its associated OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 20: If the OF bit associated with mhpmcounter10 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 21: The OF bit associated with mhpmcounter10 also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable.
RULE 22: Count overflow of mhpmcounter10 never results from writes to mhpmcounter10 or mhpmevent10, only from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 23: If an INH bit for privilege mode x in mhpmevent10 is set, counting of events by mhpmcounter10 in privilege mode x is inhibited.
RULE 24: If privilege mode x is not implemented, the corresponding INH bit in mhpmevent10 reads as zero.
RULE 25: When all five INH bits in mhpmevent10 are zero, mhpmcounter10 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 26: If supervisor mode is implemented, the scountovf register provides a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit for mhpmevent10, reflecting the overflow status of mhpmcounter10.
RULE 27: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by mhpmcounter10 sets its associated OF bit.
RULE 28: When the OF bit for mhpmcounter10 is set, it eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers, though not necessarily immediately.
RULE 29: The LCOFIP bit in mip/sip serves as the interrupt-pending bit for the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter10, and the corresponding LCOFIE bit in mie/sie serves as the interrupt-enable bit.
RULE 30: The mideleg register determines whether the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter10 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 31: There are not separate overflow status and overflow interrupt enable bits for mhpmcounter10; the OF bit serves both purposes.
RULE 32: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmcounter10 is performed by clearing its OF bit while initializing mhpmcounter10 to a starting value.
RULE 33: After mhpmcounter10 has overflowed, both mhpmcounter10 and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 34: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter10 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb0a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 35: In S-mode, accessing mhpmcounter10 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb0a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 36: In U-mode, accessing mhpmcounter10 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb0a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 37: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter10 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xb0a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhpmcounter11
NUMBER: 0xb0b
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: mhpmcounter11 is a machine-level CSR that is readable and writable (MRW).
RULE 2: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter11 contains an arbitrary (undefined) value.
RULE 3: Writing a value to mhpmcounter11 updates the register after the executing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 4: The event selector CSR for mhpmcounter11 is mhpmevent11, which is a 64-bit WARL register.
RULE 5: Event 0 selected in mhpmevent11 (the selector for mhpmcounter11) is defined to mean no event, so mhpmcounter11 does not increment.
RULE 6: A legal implementation may make mhpmcounter11 and its corresponding event selector mhpmevent11 read-only zero.
RULE 7: The high-half event selector CSR mhpmevent11h for mhpmcounter11 is provided only if the Sscofpmf extension is implemented.
RULE 8: The mhpmcounter11 hardware performance-monitoring counter continues to increment even when it is not accessible.
RULE 9: The CSR hpmcounter11 is a read-only shadow of mhpmcounter11.
RULE 10: If the HPM11 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the mhpmcounter11 shadow hpmcounter11 while executing in S-mode or U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: If the HPM11 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the mhpmcounter11 shadow hpmcounter11 is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 12: In a hart that implements U-mode, the mcounteren register must be implemented and its HPM11 field is WARL and may be read-only zero, indicating that reads of the mhpmcounter11 shadow hpmcounter11 from less-privileged modes will raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: The OF bit in the corresponding mhpmevent11 register is set to 1 when mhpmcounter11 overflows and remains 1 until software writes it to 0.
RULE 14: Overflow of mhpmcounter11 is defined as an unsigned increment that wraps the implemented counter bits from their maximum value to zero.
RULE 15: After mhpmcounter11 overflows, the counter continues counting by wrapping around.
RULE 16: After mhpmcounter11 overflows, the OF bit remains set, preserving the overflow indication.
RULE 17: If mhpmcounter11 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 18: If mhpmcounter11 overflows while its OF bit is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 19: Setting the OF bit in mhpmevent11 disables further count-overflow interrupt requests from mhpmcounter11.
RULE 20: When mhpmcounter11 overflows and generates an interrupt, bit 13 (LCOFIP) in the appropriate local-interrupt pending register (mip for M-mode, sip for S-mode) is set.
RULE 21: After mhpmcounter11's OF bit becomes one, the LCOFIP bit will later be set, and software must clear LCOFIP before servicing the overflow interrupt.
RULE 22: The delegation of the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter11 to S-mode or M-mode is controlled by the appropriate bit(s) in the mideleg register.
RULE 23: Writing to mhpmcounter11 cannot cause an overflow; only hardware-performed increments can cause overflow.
RULE 24: If supervisor mode is implemented, bit 11 of the scountovf register provides a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit associated with mhpmcounter11.
RULE 25: If MINH in mhpmevent11 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter11 is inhibited while the processor is in M-mode.
RULE 26: If SINH in mhpmevent11 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter11 is inhibited while the processor is in S-mode or HS-mode.
RULE 27: If UINH in mhpmevent11 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter11 is inhibited while the processor is in U-mode.
RULE 28: If VSINH in mhpmevent11 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter11 is inhibited while the processor is in VS-mode.
RULE 29: If VUINH in mhpmevent11 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter11 is inhibited while the processor is in VU-mode.
RULE 30: For each INH bit, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, the INH bit in mhpmevent11 reads as zero and cannot inhibit counting for mhpmcounter11.
RULE 31: After mhpmcounter11 overflows, software must write a new starting value to mhpmcounter11 before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 32: After mhpmcounter11 overflows, software must clear the OF bit before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 33: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter11 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb0b; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 34: In S-mode, accessing mhpmcounter11 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb0b; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 35: In U-mode, accessing mhpmcounter11 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb0b; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 36: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter11 register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0xb0b; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

EXTENSIONS: Zihpm
RULE 1: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter12 contains an arbitrary value.

MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter16 contains an arbitrary value, and it can be written with a specified value.
RULE 2: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter16 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 3: All counters should be implemented, but a legal implementation may implement mhpmcounter16 as a read-only zero register together with its event selector mhpmevent16.
RULE 4: If mhpmevent16 is programmed with the value 0, which denotes "no event," then mhpmcounter16 does not increment for any event.
RULE 5: If the HPM16 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, a read of mhpmcounter16 in S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 6: If the HPM16 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to mhpmcounter16 is permitted in S-mode when S-mode is implemented, otherwise it is permitted in U-mode.
RULE 7: The hpmcounter16 CSR is a read-only shadow of the underlying mhpmcounter16 register.
RULE 8: The value of mhpmcounter16 continues to increment regardless of whether the HPM16 bit in mcounteren is clear or set, and accesses to mcounteren do not affect its count.
RULE 9: When the HPM16 field of mcounteren is a read-only zero WARL value, a read of mhpmcounter16 in a less-privileged mode (S-mode or U-mode) causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: The mhpmevent16 register contains bit 63 named OF, which is the overflow status and interrupt disable bit that is set when mhpmcounter16 overflows.
RULE 11: The mhpmevent16 register contains bit 62 named MINH, which when set inhibits counting of events for mhpmcounter16 while in M-mode.
RULE 12: The mhpmevent16 register contains bit 61 named SINH, which when set inhibits counting of events for mhpmcounter16 while in S/HS-mode.
RULE 13: The mhpmevent16 register contains bit 60 named UINH, which when set inhibits counting of events for mhpmcounter16 while in U-mode.
RULE 14: The mhpmevent16 register contains bit 59 named VSINH, which when set inhibits counting of events for mhpmcounter16 while in VS-mode.
RULE 15: The mhpmevent16 register contains bit 58 named VUINH, which when set inhibits counting of events for mhpmcounter16 while in VU-mode.
RULE 16: For each INH bit in mhpmevent16, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, the bit reads as zero for mhpmcounter16.
RULE 17: All INH bits cleared to zero in mhpmevent16 result in mhpmcounter16 counting events in all modes.
RULE 18: The OF bit in mhpmevent16 is set when mhpmcounter16 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 19: Overflow of mhpmcounter16 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 20: After mhpmcounter16 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit remains set.
RULE 21: When supervisor mode is implemented, scountovf bit 16 is a read-only shadow copy of mhpmevent16.OF for mhpmcounter16.
RULE 22: If mhpmcounter16 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 23: If mhpmcounter16's OF bit is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated for that overflow.
RULE 24: The OF bit in mhpmevent16 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for mhpmcounter16.
RULE 25: Writes to mhpmcounter16 never cause a count overflow; overflow only results from hardware increments of mhpmcounter16.
RULE 26: The count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by mhpmcounter16 is mapped to local interrupt bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 27: The mip (or sip) LCOFIP bit is the interrupt-pending bit for the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter16.
RULE 28: The mie (or sie) LCOFIE bit is the interrupt-enable bit for the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter16.
RULE 29: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by mhpmcounter16 sets the associated OF bit in mhpmevent16.
RULE 30: When the OF bit for mhpmcounter16 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers.
RULE 31: Software clears the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers before servicing the count overflow interrupt resulting from mhpmcounter16.
RULE 32: The mideleg register controls whether the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter16 is delegated to S-mode or remains in M-mode.
RULE 33: After mhpmcounter16 has overflowed, software must write a new value to mhpmcounter16 and clear mhpmevent16.OF before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 34: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter16 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb10; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 35: In S-mode, accessing mhpmcounter16 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb10; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 36: In U-mode, accessing mhpmcounter16 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb10; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 37: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter16 register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0xb10; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhpmcounter17
NUMBER: 0xb11
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zihpm
RULE 1: mhpmcounter17 is a machine-level CSR that provides read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: The event selector CSR mhpmevent17 is a 64-bit WARL register that controls which event causes mhpmcounter17 to increment.
RULE 3: Selecting event 0 in mhpmevent17 causes mhpmcounter17 not to increment.
RULE 4: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter17 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 5: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter17 contains an arbitrary value.
RULE 6: Software can write a given value to mhpmcounter17.
RULE 7: mhpmcounter17 continues to increment even when it is not accessible via the mcounteren register.
RULE 8: The hpmcounter17 CSR is a read-only shadow that returns the current value of mhpmcounter17.
RULE 9: When the HPM17 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read mhpmcounter17 from S-mode or U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: When the HPM17 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to mhpmcounter17 is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 11: In harts that implement U-mode, the HPM17 field of mcounteren may be WARL and read-only zero, indicating that reads of mhpmcounter17 from a less-privileged mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: In harts that implement U-mode, the mcounteren CSR MUST be implemented and all of its fields, including the HPM17 field, may be read-only zero, indicating that reads of mhpmcounter17 in less-privileged modes will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: The settings of the mcountinhibit CSR do not affect the accessibility of the mhpmcounter17 register.
RULE 14: If the HPM17 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mhpmcounter17 register increments as usual.
RULE 15: If the HPM17 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mhpmcounter17 register does not increment.
RULE 16: When the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as though the register were set to zero, so the HPM17 bit is considered clear and the mhpmcounter17 register increments as usual.
RULE 17: The OF bit (bit 63 of mhpmevent17) is an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when mhpmcounter17 overflows.
RULE 18: The OF bit for mhpmcounter17 is set when mhpmcounter17 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 19: Overflow of mhpmcounter17 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 20: After mhpmcounter17 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit remains set, resulting in no loss of information.
RULE 21: If mhpmcounter17 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 22: If mhpmcounter17 overflows while its OF bit is one, no count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 23: The OF bit for mhpmcounter17 functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for mhpmcounter17.
RULE 24: Count overflow of mhpmcounter17 never results from writes to mhpmcounter17 or mhpmevent17, only from hardware increments of mhpmcounter17.
RULE 25: The count-overflow-interrupt request generated by mhpmcounter17 is mapped to local interrupt bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers, where the corresponding pending bit is LCOFIP and the enable bit is LCOFIE.
RULE 26: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by mhpmcounter17 sets the OF bit for mhpmcounter17.
RULE 27: When the OF bit for mhpmcounter17 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 28: The LCOFIP bit associated with the count-overflow interrupt from mhpmcounter17 is cleared by software before servicing that interrupt.
RULE 29: The delegation of the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter17 to S-mode or M-mode is controlled by the mideleg register.
RULE 30: After mhpmcounter17 has overflowed, both mhpmcounter17 and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 31: If the MINH bit (bit 62 of mhpmevent17) is set, counting of events in M-mode for mhpmcounter17 is inhibited.
RULE 32: If the SINH bit (bit 61 of mhpmevent17) is set, counting of events in S/HS-mode for mhpmcounter17 is inhibited.
RULE 33: If the UINH bit (bit 60 of mhpmevent17) is set, counting of events in U-mode for mhpmcounter17 is inhibited.
RULE 34: If the VSINH bit (bit 59 of mhpmevent17) is set, counting of events in VS-mode for mhpmcounter17 is inhibited.
RULE 35: If the VUINH bit (bit 58 of mhpmevent17) is set, counting of events in VU-mode for mhpmcounter17 is inhibited.
RULE 36: For each INH bit associated with mhpmcounter17, if the corresponding privilege mode is not implemented, that INH bit is read-only zero.
RULE 37: When all INH bits for mhpmcounter17 are zero, counting of events for mhpmcounter17 is enabled in all privilege modes.
RULE 38: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter17 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb11; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 39: In S-mode, accessing mhpmcounter17 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb11; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 40: In U-mode, accessing mhpmcounter17 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb11; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 41: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter17 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xb11; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhpmcounter18
NUMBER: 0xb12
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: mhpmcounter18 is a machine-level CSR with read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter18 contains an arbitrary value.
RULE 3: After a hart reset, software may write a given value to mhpmcounter18.
RULE 4: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter18 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 5: If an implementation makes mhpmcounter18 read-only 0, then the corresponding event-selector CSR mhpmevent18 must also be read-only 0.
RULE 6: The 64-bit WARL event-selector CSR mhpmevent18 determines which event causes mhpmcounter18 to increment.
RULE 7: When mhpmevent18 is programmed with event 0, the selected event is defined as "no event" and mhpmcounter18 does not increment.
RULE 8: mhpmcounter18 increments when the event selected by mhpmevent18 occurs, as defined by the platform.
RULE 9: hpmcountern18 is a read-only shadow of mhpmcounter18.
RULE 10: If the HPM18 bit in mcounteren is clear, an attempt to read the mhpmcounter18 shadow CSR hpmcountern18 while executing in S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: If the HPM18 bit in mcounteren is set, access to the mhpmcounter18 shadow CSR hpmcountern18 is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented otherwise U-mode.
RULE 12: mhpmcounter18 continues to increment even when its shadow CSR hpmcountern18 is not accessible because of the mcounteren settings.
RULE 13: Reading or writing mhpmcounter18 does not affect the counter; the counter continues to increment independent of CSR accesses.
RULE 14: The settings in the mcountinhibit register do not affect the accessibility of the mhpmcounter18 register.
RULE 15: When the HPM18 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mhpmcounter18 register increments as usual.
RULE 16: When the HPM18 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mhpmcounter18 register does not increment.
RULE 17: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as though the HPM18 bit were clear, and therefore the mhpmcounter18 register increments as usual.
RULE 18: When the siselect CSR holds a value that is associated with counter 18, accesses to the sireg or sireg2 CSRs could be used to access mhpmcounter18.
RULE 19: The MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, and VUINH bits in the mhpmevent18 register each, when set, inhibit counting of events for mhpmcounter18 while the processor is in the corresponding privilege mode.
RULE 20: If a privilege mode is not implemented, the corresponding INH bit in mhpmevent18 reads as zero and therefore does not inhibit counting for mhpmcounter18.
RULE 21: When all INH bits in mhpmevent18 are zero, mhpmcounter18 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 22: The OF bit in mhpmevent18 is set when mhpmcounter18 overflows and remains set until software writes it.
RULE 23: Overflow of mhpmcounter18 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits of mhpmcounter18.
RULE 24: If mhpmcounter18 overflows while its OF bit in mhpmevent18 is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 25: If the OF bit for mhpmcounter18 is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated when mhpmcounter18 overflows.
RULE 26: The OF bit for mhpmcounter18 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for mhpmcounter18.
RULE 27: Count overflow for mhpmcounter18 never results from writes to mhpmcounter18 or mhpmevent18, only from hardware increments of mhpmcounter18.
RULE 28: When a count-overflow interrupt request is generated for mhpmcounter18, its OF bit in mhpmevent18 is set.
RULE 29: When the OF bit for mhpmcounter18 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 30: The mideleg register determines whether the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter18 is delegated to S-mode or remains in M-mode.
RULE 31: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmcounter18 is done by clearing its OF bit in mhpmevent18 and initializing mhpmcounter18 to a starting value.
RULE 32: Once mhpmcounter18 has overflowed, it and its OF bit MUST be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 33: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter18 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb12; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 34: In S-mode, accessing mhpmcounter18 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb12; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 35: In U-mode, accessing mhpmcounter18 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb12; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Zihpm
RULE 1: The mhpmcounter3 CSR has machine-level read/write (MRW) privilege.

RULE 3: a write to mhpmcounter3 takes effect only after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 4: a legal implementation may make mhpmcounter3 a read-only zero register together with its event selector also read-only zero.
RULE 5: the 64-bit WARL register mhpmevent3 controls which event causes mhpmcounter3 to increment.
RULE 6: The HPM 3 bit in the mcounteren register controls the accessibility of the mhpmcounter3 register through its read-only shadow CSR hpmcounter3.
RULE 7: If the HPM 3 bit in mcounteren is clear, any attempt to read the hpmcounter3 CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 8: If the HPM 3 bit in mcounteren is set, a read of the hpmcounter3 CSR is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented otherwise U-mode.
RULE 9: The hpmcounter3 CSR is a read-only shadow of mhpmcounter3, and reading hpmcounter3 returns the current value of mhpmcounter3.
RULE 10: Reading or writing the mcounteren register does not affect the value of mhpmcounter3.
RULE 11: The mhpmcounter3 counter continues to increment even when it is not accessible.
RULE 12: In harts that implement U-mode, the mcounteren register must be implemented and its HPM 3 field is WARL and may be read-only zero, which determines the accessibility of mhpmcounter3.
RULE 13: A zero value in the HPM 3 field of mcounteren indicates that reads to mhpmcounter3 will cause an illegal-instruction exception when executing in a less-privileged mode.

RULE 18: The overflow status (OF) bit associated with mhpmcounter3 is set when mhpmcounter3 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 19: Overflow of mhpmcounter3 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits of mhpmcounter3.
RULE 20: After mhpmcounter3 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while its OF bit remains set, resulting in no loss of information.
RULE 21: Overflow of mhpmcounter3 never results from writes to mhpmcounter3 or mhpmevent3, only from hardware increments of mhpmcounter3.

RULE 23: If the OF bit of mhpmcounter3 is one when an overflow occurs, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 24: The OF bit of mhpmcounter3 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for mhpmcounter3.
RULE 25: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt request by mhpmcounter3 sets the OF bit of mhpmcounter3.

RULE 28: The mip/sip LCOFIP bit and the mie/sie LCOFIE bit serve as the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits, respectively, for the count-overflow interrupt of mhpmcounter3.

RULE 33: If the UINH bit in mhpmevent3 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter3 in U-mode is inhibited.
RULE 34: If the VSINH bit in mhpmevent3 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter3 in VS-mode is inhibited.
RULE 35: If the VUINH bit in mhpmevent3 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter3 in VU-mode is inhibited.
RULE 36: When all five x-INH bits in mhpmevent3 are zero, counting of events for mhpmcounter3 occurs in all privilege modes.

RULE 42: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter3 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xb03; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhpmcounter4
NUMBER: 0xb04
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The privilege level for mhpmcounter4 is MRW (machine-read/write).
RULE 2: mhpmcounter4 is a WARL register.
RULE 3: mhpmcounter4 can be written with a given value.
RULE 4: A CSR write to mhpmcounter4 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 5: The event selector CSR mhpmevent4 is a 64-bit WARL register that controls which event causes mhpmcounter4 to increment.
RULE 6: When mhpmevent4 is set to 0, no event causes mhpmcounter4 to increment.
RULE 7: A legal implementation may make mhpmcounter4 and its corresponding event selector mhpmevent4 be read-only 0.
RULE 8: When the HPM4 bit in mcounteren is clear, a read of the hpmcounter4 CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 9: The hpmcounter4 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter4 register.
RULE 10: When the HPM4 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mhpmcounter4 register increments as usual.
RULE 11: When the HPM4 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mhpmcounter4 register does not increment.
RULE 12: The settings in the mcountinhibit register control only whether the mhpmcounter4 register increments and do not affect the accessibility of the mhpmcounter4 register.
RULE 13: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation must behave as though the HPM4 bit were zero, so the mhpmcounter4 register is not inhibited and increments as usual.
RULE 14: The OF bit in mhpmevent4 is set when mhpmcounter4 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 15: When the OF bit for mhpmcounter4 is set, the counter's overflow status is sticky and no further overflow-interrupt request will be generated until software clears the OF bit.
RULE 16: Overflow for mhpmcounter4 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 17: An unsigned wrap-around of the implemented bits of mhpmcounter4 is considered an overflow event.
RULE 18: After mhpmcounter4 overflows, it continues to count (wrapping) while its OF bit stays set.
RULE 19: If mhpmcounter4 overflows while the OF bit in mhpmevent4 is zero, a local count-overflow interrupt is raised.
RULE 20: When the OF bit for mhpmcounter4 is set, overflow of mhpmcounter4 does not generate a count-overflow interrupt.
RULE 21: Setting the OF bit in mhpmevent4 disables count-overflow interrupt generation for mhpmcounter4.
RULE 22: Writing to mhpmcounter4 or mhpmevent4 cannot cause an overflow condition for mhpmcounter4.
RULE 23: An overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter4 sets the LCOFIP (bit 13) pending bit in the appropriate mip or sip register.
RULE 24: After mhpmcounter4 overflows and its OF bit is set, the LCOFIP pending bit will eventually be set.
RULE 25: Whether the overflow interrupt from mhpmcounter4 is taken in S-mode or M-mode is determined by the mideleg register.
RULE 26: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmcounter4 is done by clearing its OF bit, typically together with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 27: After mhpmcounter4 overflows, both the counter value and its OF bit must be written to new values before a subsequent overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 28: When the MINH bit in mhpmevent4 is set, mhpmcounter4 does not count events while the processor is in M-mode.
RULE 29: When the SINH bit in mhpmevent4 is set, mhpmcounter4 does not count events while the processor is in S-mode or HS-mode.
RULE 30: When the UINH bit in mhpmevent4 is set, mhpmcounter4 does not count events while the processor is in U-mode.
RULE 31: When the VSINH bit in mhpmevent4 is set, mhpmcounter4 does not count events while the processor is in VS-mode.
RULE 32: When the VUINH bit in mhpmevent4 is set, mhpmcounter4 does not count events while the processor is in VU-mode.
RULE 33: For each INH bit in mhpmevent4 that affects mhpmcounter4, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, the bit is read-only zero.
RULE 34: mhpmcounter4 counts events in a privilege mode only if the corresponding INH bit in mhpmevent4 for that mode is cleared.
RULE 35: If all five INH bits in mhpmevent4 are zero, mhpmcounter4 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 36: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter4 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb04; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 37: In S-mode, accessing mhpmcounter4 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb04; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 38: In U-mode, accessing mhpmcounter4 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb04; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: mhpmcounter5
NUMBER: 0xb05
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zihpm
RULE 1: After a hart reset, the architectural value of mhpmcounter5 is undefined and software may write any value to it.
RULE 2: A CSR write to mhpmcounter5 becomes visible only after the executing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 3: The 64-bit WARL register mhpmevent5 selects the event that causes increments of mhpmcounter5.
RULE 4: When mhpmevent5 is set to 0, mhpmcounter5 does not count any events.
RULE 5: A legal implementation may make mhpmcounter5 a read-only register that always returns zero.
RULE 6: When the HPM 5 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, a read of the mhpmcounter5 register while executing in S-mode or U-mode MUST cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 7: When the HPM 5 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the mhpmcounter5 register is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 8: Reading the hpmcounter5 CSR reads the current value of the mhpmcounter5 register.
RULE 9: Reading or writing the mcounteren register does not affect the mhpmcounter5 counter, which continues to increment even when not accessible.
RULE 10: In harts that implement U-mode, the mcounteren register must be implemented and its fields may be read-only zero, causing a read of the mhpmcounter5 register in a less-privileged mode to cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: If the HPM5 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, mhpmcounter5 increments as usual.
RULE 12: If the HPM5 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, mhpmcounter5 does not increment.
RULE 13: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as if the register were zero, treating the HPM5 bit as clear and causing mhpmcounter5 to increment as usual.
RULE 14: For an siselect value associated with counter 5, sireg or sireg2 could be used to access mhpmcounter5.
RULE 15: For an siselect value associated with counter 5, sireg4 or sireg5 could be used to access mhpmcounter5h.
RULE 16: The OF bit in mhpmevent5 is set when mhpmcounter5 overflows.
RULE 17: The OF bit in mhpmevent5 remains set until it is written by software.
RULE 18: Overflow for mhpmcounter5 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 19: Count overflow for mhpmcounter5 never results from writes to mhpmcounter5 or mhpmevent5 registers, only from hardware increments.
RULE 20: If mhpmcounter5 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 21: If the OF bit for mhpmcounter5 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 22: The OF bit for mhpmcounter5 also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable.
RULE 23: The count-overflow-interrupt request generated by mhpmcounter5 is treated as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 24: The LCOFIP (interrupt-pending) and LCOFIE (interrupt-enable) bits in mip/sip and mie/sie respectively correspond to the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter5.
RULE 25: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by mhpmcounter5 sets its associated OF bit.
RULE 26: When the OF bit for mhpmcounter5 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 27: The mideleg register determines whether the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter5 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 28: If supervisor mode is implemented, the scountovf register contains a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit for mhpmcounter5.
RULE 29: If any INH bit in mhpmevent5 is set, counting of events in the corresponding privilege mode is inhibited for mhpmcounter5.
RULE 30: If all INH bits in mhpmevent5 are zero, counting of events in all privilege modes is enabled for mhpmcounter5.
RULE 31: For each INH bit in mhpmevent5, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, that bit is read-only zero for mhpmcounter5.
RULE 32: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmcounter5 is performed by clearing its OF bit together with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 33: After mhpmcounter5 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 34: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter5 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb05; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 35: In S-mode, accessing mhpmcounter5 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb05; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 36: In U-mode, accessing mhpmcounter5 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb05; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 37: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter5 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xb05; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhpmcounter6
NUMBER: 0xb06
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zihpm
RULE 1: Event 0 selected in mhpmevent6 is defined to mean that no event increments mhpmcounter6.
RULE 2: A legal implementation may make mhpmcounter6 read-only zero.
RULE 3: When the HPM6 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the hpmcounter6 CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception, and this restriction applies to accesses that would otherwise read the mhpmcounter6 register.
RULE 4: The hpmcounter6 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter6 register.
RULE 5: The mhpmcounter6 register continues to increment even when the HPM6 bit in the mcounteren register is cleared.
RULE 6: The settings in the mcountinhibit register control whether mhpmcounter6 increments, and they do not affect the accessibility of mhpmcounter6.
RULE 7: When the HPM 6 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, mhpmcounter6 increments as usual.
RULE 8: When the HPM 6 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, mhpmcounter6 does not increment.
RULE 9: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as though the HPM 6 bit were clear, so mhpmcounter6 increments as usual.
RULE 10: When mhpmcounter6 overflows, the OF bit in mhpmevent6 is set and remains set until written by software.
RULE 11: Overflow of mhpmcounter6 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits because mhpmcounter6 values are unsigned.
RULE 12: After mhpmcounter6 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit in mhpmevent6 remains set, resulting in no loss of information.
RULE 13: For each privilege mode x, if the privilege mode is not implemented, the corresponding x INH bit in mhpmevent6 for mhpmcounter6 is read-only zero.
RULE 14: When an x INH bit in mhpmevent6 for mhpmcounter6 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter6 is inhibited while executing in privilege mode x, and when all x INH bits are zero, mhpmcounter6 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 15: Writes to mhpmcounter6 or mhpmevent6 never cause a count overflow; count overflow for mhpmcounter6 occurs only from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 16: If mhpmcounter6 overflows while its associated OF bit in mhpmevent6 is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 17: If the OF bit associated with mhpmcounter6 in mhpmevent6 is one, a count overflow interrupt request is not generated.
RULE 18: A count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by mhpmcounter6 is treated as a standard local interrupt that corresponds to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 19: The LCOFIP bits in mip and sip are the interrupt-pending bits for the count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by mhpmcounter6.
RULE 20: The LCOFIE bits in mie and sie are the interrupt-enable bits for the count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by mhpmcounter6.
RULE 21: When mhpmcounter6 generates a count-overflow-interrupt request, its OF bit in mhpmevent6 is set.
RULE 22: After the OF bit for mhpmcounter6 in mhpmevent6 is set, the corresponding LCOFIP bit in mip or sip will eventually be set.
RULE 23: The LCOFIP bit for mhpmcounter6 is cleared by software before servicing the count overflow interrupt resulting from one or more overflows of mhpmcounter6.
RULE 24: The mideleg register controls whether the count-overflow-interrupt generated by mhpmcounter6 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 25: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter6 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb06; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 26: In S-mode, accessing mhpmcounter6 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb06; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 27: In U-mode, accessing mhpmcounter6 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb06; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter6 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xb06; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhpmcounter7
NUMBER: 0xb07
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zihpm
RULE 1: mhpmcounter7 is a machine-read/write (MRW) register.
RULE 2: mhpmcounter7h is a machine-read/write (MRW) register.
RULE 3: mhpmcounter7 is one of the hardware-performance monitor's additional 64-bit event counters (mhpmcounter3–mhpmcounter31) and is a 64-bit counter.
RULE 4: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter7 contains an arbitrary value.
RULE 5: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter7 may be written with any value.
RULE 6: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter7 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 7: mhpmevent7 is a 64-bit WARL register whose programmed value determines which event causes mhpmcounter7 to increment.
RULE 8: If mhpmevent7 = 0, mhpmcounter7 does not increment for any event.
RULE 9: A legal implementation may choose to make mhpmcounter7 read-only zero, in which case reads of mhpmcounter7 return 0 and writes have no effect.
RULE 10: If the HPM7 bit in mcounteren is clear, a read of hpmcounter7 (the read-only shadow of mhpmcounter7) while executing in S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: If the HPM7 bit in mcounteren is set, a read of hpmcounter7 (the read-only shadow of mhpmcounter7) is permitted in the next lower implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 12: The settings in mcounteren affect only accessibility and do not affect mhpmcounter7, which continues to increment regardless of the HPM7 bit state.
RULE 13: The increment behavior of mhpmcounter7 is controlled by the HPM7 bit in the mcountinhibit register.
RULE 14: The settings of the mcountinhibit register do not affect the accessibility of mhpmcounter7.
RULE 15: When the HPM7 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, mhpmcounter7 increments as usual.
RULE 16: When the HPM7 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, mhpmcounter7 does not increment.
RULE 17: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as though the register were set to zero, making the HPM7 bit effectively clear and causing mhpmcounter7 to increment as usual.
RULE 18: The OF bit in mhpmevent7 is set when mhpmcounter7 overflows and remains set until software writes to it.
RULE 19: An overflow of mhpmcounter7 occurs when its unsigned value wraps past the most-significant implemented counter bit.
RULE 20: After mhpmcounter7 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while its OF bit stays set.
RULE 21: If mhpmcounter7 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 22: If mhpmcounter7 overflows while its OF bit is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 23: Setting the OF bit in mhpmevent7 disables further count-overflow interrupt requests for mhpmcounter7.
RULE 24: mhpmcounter7 can overflow only as a result of hardware increments and never as a result of software writes to mhpmcounter7 or mhpmevent7.
RULE 25: An overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter7 sets the LCOFIP pending bit (bit 13) in mip and sip, and the corresponding LCOFIE enable bits in mie and sie control whether the interrupt is enabled.
RULE 26: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt by mhpmcounter7 sets its OF bit and eventually sets the LCOFIP pending bit in mip and sip.
RULE 27: The mideleg register determines whether the overflow interrupt from mhpmcounter7 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 28: There are no separate overflow status and overflow interrupt enable bits for mhpmcounter7; enabling overflow interrupt generation is performed by clearing the OF bit together with initializing the counter.
RULE 29: After mhpmcounter7 has overflowed, both the counter value and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 30: Setting any INH bit in mhpmevent7 (e.g., MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) inhibits counting of events for mhpmcounter7 while the processor is in the corresponding privilege mode, and if that privilege mode is not implemented the INH bit reads as zero.
RULE 31: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter7 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb07; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 32: In S-mode, accessing mhpmcounter7 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb07; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 33: In U-mode, accessing mhpmcounter7 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb07; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 34: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter7 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xb07; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhpmcounter8
NUMBER: 0xb08
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The CSR mhpmevent8 selects the event counted by mhpmcounter8.
RULE 2: The event that causes mhpmcounter8 to increment is selected by the corresponding event-selector CSR mhpmevent8.
RULE 3: If a legal implementation chooses to make the counter and its event selector read-only 0, then mhpmcounter8 reads as zero and cannot be written.
RULE 4: When XLEN = 64, reads of mhpmcounter8 access the full 64-bit register value.
RULE 5: When XLEN = 64, writes of mhpmcounter8 access the full 64-bit register value.
RULE 6: When the HPM 8 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, an attempt to read the hpmcounter8 CSR (the read-only shadow of mhpmcounter8) while executing in S-mode or U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.

RULE 8: The hpmcounter8 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter8 register.
RULE 9: When the HPM 8 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mhpmcounter8 register increments as usual.
RULE 10: When the HPM 8 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mhpmcounter8 register does not increment.
RULE 11: The setting of the mcountinhibit register does not affect the accessibility of the mhpmcounter8 register.

RULE 13: When the siselect value selects counter 8, the sireg and sireg2 registers can be used to access the mhpmcounter8 register and the corresponding mhpmevent8 register.
RULE 14: When the siselect value selects counter 8, the sireg4 and sireg5 registers can be used to access the high-half register mhpmcounter8h (the high half of mhpmcounter8) and the corresponding mhpmevent8h register.

RULE 16: When the OF bit in the mhpmcounter8 mhpmevent register is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 17: If mhpmcounter8 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 18: If the OF bit in the mhpmcounter8 mhpmevent register is one, no count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 19: The OF bit in the mhpmcounter8 mhpmevent register functions as a count-overflow-interrupt disable for mhpmcounter8.
RULE 20: The OF bit in the mhpmcounter8 mhpmevent register is set when mhpmcounter8 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 21: Overflow of mhpmcounter8 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits of mhpmcounter8.
RULE 22: After mhpmcounter8 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit remains set, resulting in no loss of information.
RULE 23: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by mhpmcounter8 sets its OF bit.
RULE 24: The LCOFIP bits in the mip and sip registers are the interrupt-pending bits and the LCOFIE bits in the mie and sie registers are the interrupt-enable bits for the mhpmcounter8 overflow interrupt.
RULE 25: The mhpmcounter8 overflow interrupt request is treated as a standard local interrupt that corresponds to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 26: The mideleg register controls delegation of the mhpmcounter8 overflow interrupt to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 27: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmcounter8 is done by clearing the OF bit together with initializing mhpmcounter8 to a starting value.
RULE 28: After mhpmcounter8 has overflowed, both mhpmcounter8 and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 29: Count overflow of mhpmcounter8 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter8 or its mhpmevent8 register, only from hardware increments of mhpmcounter8.
RULE 30: Each of the five x INH bits in the mhpmcounter8 mhpmevent register, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in privilege mode x.
RULE 31: If all five x INH bits in the mhpmcounter8 mhpmevent register are zero, counting of events occurs in all privilege modes.
RULE 32: If a privilege mode x is not implemented, the corresponding x INH bit in the mhpmcounter8 mhpmevent register is read-only zero.
RULE 33: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter8 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb08; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 34: In S-mode, accessing mhpmcounter8 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb08; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 35: In U-mode, accessing mhpmcounter8 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb08; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 36: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter8 register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0xb08; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhpmcounter9
NUMBER: 0xb09
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: mhpmcounter9 is a Machine-level CSR that is readable and writable by machine mode (privilege MRW).
RULE 2: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter9 contains an arbitrary value.

RULE 4: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter9 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.

RULE 11: mhpmcounter9 is a hardware performance-monitoring counter whose value can be observed through its read-only shadow CSR.

RULE 39: The mideleg register controls whether the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter9 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 40: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmcounter9 is performed by clearing its OF bit together with initializing mhpmcounter9 to a starting value.
