REGISTER: mhpmevent24
NUMBER: 0x338
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Zihpm
RULE 1: mhpmevent24 is a machine-read/write (MRW) CSR.
RULE 2: The mip .LCOFIP bit is a read-write field that reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request caused by any mhpmevent n . OF bit being set, including the mhpmevent24 OF bit.
RULE 3: If the mhpmevent24 OF bit is set, the implementation may set the mip .LCOFIP bit to indicate that a local-counter-overflow interrupt request has occurred.
RULE 4: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting the mhpmevent24 OF bit may cause the mip .LCOFIP bit to become set.
RULE 5: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mip .LCOFIP bit is a read-only zero and the setting of the mhpmevent24 OF bit does not cause any change to mip .LCOFIP.
RULE 6: Event code 0 in mhpmevent24 denotes "no event", meaning the associated counter will not be incremented for any event.
RULE 7: A legal implementation may implement mhpmevent24 as a read-only register that always returns 0.
RULE 8: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the mhpmevent24h CSR provides access to bits 63-32 of mhpmevent24, with reads returning those bits and writes affecting only bits 63-32.
RULE 9: When mcounteren[24] = 1 and menvcfg.CDE = 1, the state of mhpmevent24 can be accessed through sireg* with siselect = 0x58.
RULE 10: In M or S privilege mode, if siselect is in the range 0x40-0x5F and menvcfg.CDE = 0, an attempt to access mhpmevent24 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: In M or S privilege mode, if siselect = 0x41, an attempt to access mhpmevent24 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: In M or S privilege mode, if the counter selected by siselect is not delegated to S-mode (i.e., mcounteren[24] = 0 for mhpmevent24), an attempt to access mhpmevent24 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, bit 62 (MINH) of mhpmevent24 accessed through sireg* is read-only and always returns zero.
RULE 14: If any extension required for the underlying state of mhpmevent24 (such as Sscofpmf for the MINH bit) is not implemented, an attempt from M or S mode to access mhpmevent24 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 15: When the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented, an attempt from M or S mode to access mhpmevent24 via vsireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 16: When the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented and the current privilege mode is VS-mode, an attempt to access mhpmevent24 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception if menvcfg.CDE = 0, otherwise it raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 17: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting the OF bit in mhpmevent24 may cause sip.LCOFIP to become 1, indicating a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 18: The sip.LCOFIP field is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request generated by any mhpmevent<n>.OF bit being set, including mhpmevent24.OF.
RULE 19: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, setting the OF bit in mhpmevent24 does not affect sip.LCOFIP, which remains a read-only zero.
RULE 20: Because sip.LCOFIP is writable when the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, software can clear a pending interrupt generated by the mhpmevent24.OF bit by writing 0 to sip.LCOFIP.
RULE 21: The OF bit in mhpmevent24 is one of the mhpmevent<n>.OF bits whose setting can generate a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 22: The OF bit (bit 63) of mhpmevent24 indicates overflow status and disables the interrupt when set, and it is set when the associated hpmcounter overflows.
RULE 23: The MINH bit (bit 62) of mhpmevent24 inhibits counting of events while executing in M-mode when set.
RULE 24: The SINH bit (bit 61) of mhpmevent24 inhibits counting of events while executing in S/HS-mode when set.
RULE 25: The UINH bit (bit 60) of mhpmevent24 inhibits counting of events while executing in U-mode when set.
RULE 26: The VSINH bit (bit 59) of mhpmevent24 inhibits counting of events while executing in VS-mode when set.
RULE 27: The VUINH bit (bit 58) of mhpmevent24 inhibits counting of events while executing in VU-mode when set.
RULE 28: Bits 57-56 of mhpmevent24 are reserved (WPRI).
RULE 29: For each INH bit in mhpmevent24, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, the bit is read-only zero.
RULE 30: When any INH bit in mhpmevent24 is set, counting of events is inhibited while the processor is in the corresponding privilege mode.
RULE 31: If all INH bits in mhpmevent24 are zero, counting of events occurs in all privilege modes.
RULE 32: The OF bit of mhpmevent24 remains set until written by software.
RULE 33: Overflow of the counter paired with mhpmevent24 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 34: If an hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit of mhpmevent24 is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 35: If the OF bit of mhpmevent24 is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 36: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt request by the counter paired with mhpmevent24 sets the OF bit of mhpmevent24.
RULE 37: When the OF bit of mhpmevent24 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers.
RULE 38: The mideleg register controls whether the overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent24 is delegated to S-mode or remains in M-mode.
RULE 39: Writing mhpmevent24 does not cause a counter overflow; count overflow only results from hardware increments of the counter registers.
RULE 40: There are no separate overflow status and overflow interrupt enable bits for mhpmevent24; enabling overflow interrupt generation is performed by clearing the OF bit together with initializing the counter.
RULE 41: Once the counter paired with mhpmevent24 has overflowed, it and the OF bit MUST be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 42: The overflow (OF) bit of mhpmevent24 is mirrored in scountovf bit 24.
RULE 43: In M-mode, the overflow (OF) bit of mhpmevent24 is always readable via scountovf bit 24.
RULE 44: In S-mode or HS-mode, the overflow (OF) bit of mhpmevent24 is readable via scountovf bit 24 only when the corresponding mcounteren bit 24 is set; otherwise it reads as zero.
RULE 45: In VS-mode, the overflow (OF) bit of mhpmevent24 is readable via scountovf bit 24 only when both the corresponding mcounteren bit 24 and hcounteren bit 24 are set; otherwise it reads as zero.
RULE 46: In M-mode, accessing mhpmevent24 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x338; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

RULE 1: The privilege of mhpmevent25 is MRW, meaning it is a machine-mode CSR that can be read and written by privileged software.

RULE 3: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and the mhpmevent25 .OF bit is set, the mip.LCOFIP bit reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request caused by that set .OF bit.
RULE 4: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the mip.LCOFIP bit is read-write.
RULE 5: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the mie.LCOFIE bit is the interrupt-enable bit corresponding to the mip.LCOFIP bit.
RULE 6: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mhpmevent25 .OF bit (and all other mhpmevent n .OF bits) do not affect any architectural state.
RULE 7: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mhpmevent25 .OF bit does not affect any architectural state, and the mip.LCOFIP bit is a read-only zero.
RULE 8: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mhpmevent25 .OF bit does not affect any architectural state, and the mie.LCOFIE bit is a read-only zero.

RULE 10: A legal implementation may make mhpmevent25 read-only with the fixed value 0.
RULE 11: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and mhpmevent25 is accessed through the delegated alias registers (sireg*), event selector bit 62 (MINH) of mhpmevent25 is read-only 0 and cannot be written.

RULE 15: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the sip.LCOFIP bit is hard-wired to zero, and setting the mhpmevent25.OF bit does not affect sip.LCOFIP.
RULE 16: If a privilege mode corresponding to an INH bit (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, or VUINH) is not implemented, the respective INH bit in mhpmevent25 is read-only zero.
RULE 17: When any of the INH bits MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, or VUINH in mhpmevent25 is set, event counting is inhibited while the processor is in the corresponding privilege mode, and if all these INH bits are zero, events are counted in all privilege modes.
RULE 18: The OF bit in mhpmevent25 is set when its associated hpmcounter overflows and remains set until software writes to clear it.
RULE 19: Overflow for the OF bit in mhpmevent25 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented bits of the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 20: If the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent25 overflows while the mhpmevent25 OF bit is zero, a count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 21: If the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent25 overflows while the mhpmevent25 OF bit is one, no count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 22: Overflow of the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent25 never occurs as a result of writes to mhpmcounter25 or mhpmevent25 registers, and can only result from hardware increments of the counter.

RULE 25: When a count-overflow-interrupt request is generated by the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent25, the mhpmevent25 OF bit is set.
RULE 26: When the OF bit in mhpmevent25 becomes set, it eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers.
RULE 27: The delegation of the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent25 to supervisor mode or machine mode is controlled by the mideleg register.

RULE 29: After the counter associated with mhpmevent25 has overflowed, both the counter and the mhpmevent25 OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.

REGISTER: mhpmevent26
NUMBER: 0x33a
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The privilege level for mhpmevent26 is machine-read/write (MRW).
RULE 2: The privilege level for mhpmevent26h is machine-read/write (MRW).
RULE 3: mhpmevent26 is a 64-bit WARL register that belongs to the set of event selector CSRs mhpmevent3-mhpmevent31.
RULE 4: Event 0 in mhpmevent26 is defined to mean "no event."
RULE 5: The value written to mhpmevent26 selects the hardware event that causes the corresponding counter mhpmcounter26 to increment.
RULE 6: A legal implementation may implement mhpmevent26 as a read-only register that always returns 0.
RULE 7: Any write to mhpmevent26 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 8: If any extension required by the state accessed through mhpmevent26 is not implemented, then an access to that state via a system register (sireg) from M mode or S mode MUST raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 9: The mhpmevent26 register contains an OF bit that, when set, contributes to generating a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 10: When the mhpmevent26.OF bit is set, the sip.LCOFIP bit will indicate the resulting overflow interrupt request.
RULE 11: The mhpmevent26 register bits 63–56 are defined as OF, MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH, and two reserved WPRI bits.
RULE 12: The OF bit in mhpmevent26 is an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the associated counter overflows.
RULE 13: The MINH bit in mhpmevent26, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in M-mode.
RULE 14: The SINH bit in mhpmevent26, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in S-mode or HS-mode.
RULE 15: The UINH bit in mhpmevent26, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in U-mode.
RULE 16: The VSINH bit in mhpmevent26, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in VS-mode.
RULE 17: The VUINH bit in mhpmevent26, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in VU-mode.
RULE 18: The two WPRI bits in mhpmevent26 are reserved.
RULE 19: If a privilege mode corresponding to an INH bit in mhpmevent26 is not implemented, that INH bit reads as zero and is read-only.
RULE 20: When all five INH bits in mhpmevent26 are zero, counting of events occurs in all privilege modes; when any INH bit is set, counting is inhibited for its corresponding mode.
RULE 21: The OF bit in mhpmevent26 is set by hardware on unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits, remains set until written by software, and indicates that the counter has wrapped around without loss of information.
RULE 22: The OF bit in mhpmevent26 disables generation of a count-overflow interrupt request when it is set; if it is clear at the time of overflow, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 23: Writes to mhpmevent26 never cause a count overflow; count overflow can occur only from hardware increments of the associated counter.
RULE 24: A count-overflow interrupt generated due to overflow of the counter associated with mhpmevent26 is signaled via local interrupt bit 13 (LCOFIP/LCOFIE) in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 25: When a count-overflow interrupt request is generated by the counter associated with mhpmevent26, hardware sets the OF bit in mhpmevent26, which eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers, and software must clear the LCOFIP bit before servicing the interrupt; delegation of this interrupt is controlled by the mideleg register.
RULE 26: After the counter associated with mhpmevent26 has overflowed, software must reinitialize both the counter and the OF bit before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 27: The scountovf CSR bit 26 is a shadow copy of the OF bit in mhpmevent26.
RULE 28: In M-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent26 is always readable via the scountovf CSR.
RULE 29: In S-mode and HS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent26 is readable via the scountovf CSR when the corresponding mcounteren bit 26 is set, and otherwise reads as zero.
RULE 30: In VS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent26 is readable via the scountovf CSR when both the corresponding mcounteren bit 26 and hcounteren bit 26 are set, and otherwise reads as zero.
RULE 31: In M-mode, accessing mhpmevent26 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x33a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhpmevent27
NUMBER: 0x33b
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The CSR mhpmevent27 is accessible at Machine privilege level and has read/write permission (MRW).
RULE 2: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting the mhpmevent27.OF bit causes a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 3: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the mip.LCOFIP bit is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request generated by any mhpmeventn.OF bit being set, including mhpmevent27.OF.
RULE 4: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mip.LCOFIP bit is read-only zero regardless of the state of the mhpmevent27.OF bit.
RULE 5: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mie.LCOFIE bit is read-only zero regardless of the state of the mhpmevent27.OF bit.
RULE 6: mhpmevent27 is a 64-bit WARL register that controls which event causes the corresponding counter mhpmcounter27 to increment.
RULE 7: Event 0 is defined to mean "no event", therefore programming mhpmevent27 with the value 0 causes mhpmcounter27 to never increment for any event.
RULE 8: A write to mhpmevent27 takes effect only after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 9: When the siselect CSR holds the value 0x5B (0x40 + 27) in M-mode or S-mode, the low 32 bits of mhpmevent27 are accessed through sireg2.
RULE 10: When the siselect CSR holds the value 0x5B and the processor XLEN is 64, the high 32 bits of mhpmevent27 are accessed through sireg5.
RULE 11: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, bit 62 (MINH) of the selector field of mhpmevent27 must read as 0 and must be write-protected when mhpmevent27 is accessed via sireg2 or sireg5.
RULE 12: While executing in M-mode or S-mode with siselect = 0x5B, if the menvcfg.CDE bit is 0, any attempt to read or write mhpmevent27 via sireg2 or sireg5 must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: While executing in M-mode or S-mode with siselect = 0x5B, if mcounteren[27] is 0, any attempt to access mhpmevent27 via sireg2 or sireg5 must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 14: If the processor XLEN is 64, any attempt to access mhpmevent27 via sireg5 must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 15: If either mstateen0[60] is 0 or hstateen0[60] is 0, access to mhpmevent27 through sireg is prevented regardless of other conditions.
RULE 16: If any extension required for the underlying state of mhpmevent27 (such as Smstateen or Sscofpmf) is not implemented, an M-mode or S-mode access to mhpmevent27 via sireg2 or sireg5 must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 17: The implementation of the H extension does not cause illegal-instruction exceptions for M-mode or S-mode accesses to mhpmevent27 via sireg.
RULE 18: The implementation of the H extension prevents VS-mode from using the indirect mapping (siselect = 0x5B) to access mhpmevent27 via vsireg.
RULE 19: The OF field of mhpmevent27 is an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the counter overflows.
RULE 20: If the MINH bit of mhpmevent27 is set, counting of events in M-mode is inhibited.
RULE 21: If the SINH bit of mhpmevent27 is set, counting of events in S/HS-mode is inhibited.
RULE 22: If the UINH bit of mhpmevent27 is set, counting of events in U-mode is inhibited.
RULE 23: If the VSINH bit of mhpmevent27 is set, counting of events in VS-mode is inhibited.
RULE 24: If the VUINH bit of mhpmevent27 is set, counting of events in VU-mode is inhibited.
RULE 25: For each x INH bit in mhpmevent27, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, the bit is read-only zero.
RULE 26: When any of the five x INH bits in mhpmevent27 are set, counting of events is inhibited while executing in the corresponding privilege mode.
RULE 27: When all five x INH bits in mhpmevent27 are zero, counting of events occurs in all privilege modes.
RULE 28: The OF bit of mhpmevent27 is set when the corresponding hpmcounter overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 29: Overflow for mhpmevent27 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits because hpmcounter values are unsigned.
RULE 30: When the OF bit of mhpmevent27 is set, the counter continues to wrap around and count while the sticky OF bit remains set, so overflow does not lose information.
RULE 31: If an hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent27 overflows while the OF bit is zero, a count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 32: If the OF bit of mhpmevent27 is one, no count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 33: The OF bit of mhpmevent27 also functions as a count-overflow-interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 34: Count overflow for mhpmevent27 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter or mhpmevent registers, only from hardware increments of counter registers.
RULE 35: The count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent27 is treated as a standard local interrupt that corresponds to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 36: The mip and sip LCOFIP bits and the mie and sie LCOFIE bits are respectively the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for the count-overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent27.
RULE 37: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent27 sets the OF bit of mhpmevent27.
RULE 38: When the OF bit of mhpmevent27 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 39: The mideleg register controls the delegation of the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent27 to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 40: Once the counter associated with mhpmevent27 has overflowed, it and the OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 41: In M-mode, reads of the scountovf shadow of mhpmevent27's OF bit (bit 27) are always permitted.
RULE 42: In S-mode or HS-mode, reads of the scountovf shadow of mhpmevent27's OF bit (bit 27) are permitted only when mcounteren bit 27 is set, and otherwise return zero.
RULE 43: In VS-mode, reads of the scountovf shadow of mhpmevent27's OF bit (bit 27) are permitted only when both mcounteren bit 27 and hcounteren bit 27 are set, and otherwise return zero.

REGISTER: mhpmevent28
NUMBER: 0x33c
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Zihpm
RULE 1: Writing the value 0 to mhpmevent28 selects "no event" for mhpmcounter28.
RULE 2: A conforming implementation may make mhpmevent28 read-only and hard-wired to 0.
RULE 3: mhpmevent28 is a 64-bit WARL register, so any value written must be a legal value for the implementation and a read may return a different value than written.
RULE 4: Any write to mhpmevent28 takes effect only after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 5: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, bit 62 (MINH) of mhpmevent28 accessed via the hpmevent28 alias through sireg* is read-only 0.
RULE 6: If menvcfg.CDE = 0, any access to mhpmevent28 via its hpmevent28 alias through sireg* in M-mode or S-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 7: If XLEN = 64, any access to mhpmevent28 via its hpmevent28 alias through sireg4 or sireg5 in M-mode or S-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 8: If siselect selects counter 28 (i.e., siselect value in the range 0x40-0x5F that maps to mhpmevent28), any access to mhpmevent28 via its hpmevent28 alias through sireg* in M-mode or S-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 9: If the bit in mcounteren that delegates mhpmevent28 to S-mode is 0, any access to mhpmevent28 via its hpmevent28 alias through sireg* in M-mode or S-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: If any extension required for the state of mhpmevent28 is not implemented, any attempt from M-mode or S-mode to access mhpmevent28 via its hpmevent28 alias through sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: If the H extension is implemented, any attempt from VS-mode or VU-mode to access mhpmevent28 via its hpmevent28 alias through sireg* raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 12: The mhpmevent28.OF bit is one of the mhpmevent n .OF bits whose setting causes the sip.LCOFIP bit to be set.
RULE 13: When the mhpmevent28.OF bit is set, the sip.LCOFIP bit is set.
RULE 14: Bit 63 of mhpmevent28 is the OF field, which indicates overflow status and serves as an interrupt-disable bit that is set when the counter overflows.
RULE 15: Bit 62 of mhpmevent28 is the MINH field; if set, counting of events in M-mode is inhibited.
RULE 16: Bit 61 of mhpmevent28 is the SINH field; if set, counting of events in S/HS-mode is inhibited.
RULE 17: Bit 60 of mhpmevent28 is the UINH field; if set, counting of events in U-mode is inhibited.
RULE 18: Bit 59 of mhpmevent28 is the VSINH field; if set, counting of events in VS-mode is inhibited.
RULE 19: Bit 58 of mhpmevent28 is the VUINH field; if set, counting of events in VU-mode is inhibited.
RULE 20: Bits 57 and 56 of mhpmevent28 are reserved (WPRI).
RULE 21: If the privilege mode associated with an INH bit in mhpmevent28 is not implemented, that INH bit reads as zero and is read-only.
RULE 22: When an INH bit in mhpmevent28 is set, it inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in the corresponding privilege mode.
RULE 23: If all five INH bits (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in mhpmevent28 are zero, counting of events occurs in all modes.
RULE 24: The OF bit in mhpmevent28 is set when the associated hpmcounter overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 25: Overflow for the OF bit in mhpmevent28 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits of the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 26: After an overflow, the counter associated with mhpmevent28 wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit remains set.
RULE 27: If an hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit of mhpmevent28 is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 28: If the OF bit of mhpmevent28 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 29: The OF bit of mhpmevent28 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 30: Writes to mhpmevent28 do not cause overflow because count overflow never results from writes to the mhpmcounter n or mhpmevent n registers, only from hardware increments.
RULE 31: The count-overflow-interrupt-request signal generated by the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent28 is treated as a standard local interrupt that corresponds to bit 13 in the mip/mie/sip/sie registers.
RULE 32: The LCOFIP bit in mip/sip is the interrupt-pending bit for the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent28.
RULE 33: The LCOFIE bit in mie/sie is the interrupt-enable bit for the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent28.
RULE 34: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent28 sets the OF bit of mhpmevent28.
RULE 35: When the OF bit of mhpmevent28 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip/sip registers.
RULE 36: Software clears the LCOFIP bit before servicing the count overflow interrupt resulting from one or more count overflows associated with mhpmevent28.
RULE 37: The mideleg register controls the delegation of the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent28 to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 38: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmevent28 is done by clearing the OF bit in conjunction with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 39: Once the counter associated with mhpmevent28 has overflowed, it and the OF bit MUST be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 40: The scountovf CSR contains a shadow copy of the overflow (OF) bit for mhpmevent28 in its bit 28.
RULE 41: Read access to the overflow shadow bit for mhpmevent28 (scountovf bit 28) is governed by the same mcounteren (or mcounteren and hcounteren) CSR permissions that control access to hpmcounter CSRs.
RULE 42: In M-mode, the overflow shadow bit for mhpmevent28 (scountovf bit 28) is always readable.
RULE 43: In S-mode or HS-mode, the overflow shadow bit for mhpmevent28 (scountovf bit 28) is readable only when mcounteren bit 28 is set, otherwise it reads as zero.
RULE 44: In VS-mode, the overflow shadow bit for mhpmevent28 (scountovf bit 28) is readable only when both mcounteren bit 28 and hcounteren bit 28 are set, otherwise it reads as zero.
RULE 45: In M-mode, accessing mhpmevent28 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x33c; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 46: In S-mode, accessing mhpmevent28 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x33c; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 47: In U-mode, accessing mhpmevent28 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x33c; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 48: In M-mode, setting mhpmevent28.OF (bit 63) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x33c, a0; csrr a1, 0x33c; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000].
RULE 49: In M-mode, setting mhpmevent28.MINH (bit 62) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x4000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4000000000000000; csrs 0x33c, a0; csrr a1, 0x33c; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x4000000000000000].

EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: mhpmevent29 is a machine-level CSR with read/write access (privilege MRW).

RULE 5: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, then setting the mhpmevent29 .OF bit does not cause any change to the mie .LCOFIE bit because that bit is a read-only zero.

RULE 13: If the implementation does not include the extension(s) that define the state of mhpmevent29, any M-mode or S-mode sireg* access to mhpmevent29 raises an illegal-instruction exception.

RULE 15: If hpmcounter29 overflows while the OF bit in mhpmevent29 is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 16: If the OF bit in mhpmevent29 is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated for an overflow of hpmcounter29.
RULE 17: When a count-overflow interrupt request is generated for hpmcounter29, the OF bit in mhpmevent29 is set.
RULE 18: After the OF bit in mhpmevent29 is set by a count-overflow interrupt request, the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers is eventually set but not necessarily immediately.
RULE 19: The mideleg register controls delegation of the overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter29, which is the interrupt associated with the OF bit in mhpmevent29.

RULE 22: After hpmcounter29 has overflowed, both the counter and the OF bit in mhpmevent29 MUST be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.

RULE 24: The SINH bit in mhpmevent29, when set, inhibits counting of events for hpmcounter29 in supervisor/hypervisor mode.

RULE 27: The VUINH bit in mhpmevent29, when set, inhibits counting of events for hpmcounter29 in virtual-user mode.

REGISTER: mhpmevent3
NUMBER: 0x323
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The mhpmevent3 register is accessible with machine read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: The LCOFIP bit in the mip register is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request resulting from the OF bit of mhpmevent3 being set.
RULE 3: If the OF bit of mhpmevent3 is set, the LCOFIP bit in the mip register becomes set to indicate a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 4: The LCOFIE bit in the mie register controls whether an interrupt request indicated by the LCOFIP bit, which may be caused by the OF bit of mhpmevent3, can trap.
RULE 5: mhpmevent3 is a 64-bit WARL register that selects the event that causes its corresponding performance counter to increment.
RULE 6: Setting mhpmevent3 to the value 0 selects the defined "no event".
RULE 7: A legal implementation is permitted to make mhpmevent3 a read-only register that always returns zero.
RULE 8: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and the mhpmevent3 register is accessed through the sireg* CSRs (siselect = 0x43, sireg2), event selector bit 62 (MINH) reads as 0 and cannot be written.
RULE 9: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting the .OF bit of mhpmevent3 may cause the sip.LCOFIP bit to become set, reflecting a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 10: The .OF bit of mhpmevent3 reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request when it is set.

RULE 15: The VSINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in VS-mode.
RULE 16: The VUINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in VU-mode.
RULE 17: The two WPRI bits in mhpmevent3 are reserved.
RULE 18: For each INH bit in mhpmevent3, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, the bit is read-only zero.
RULE 19: If all INH bits in mhpmevent3 are zero, counting of events is enabled in all privilege modes.
RULE 20: Overflow of the associated hpmcounter is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 21: After overflow, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the OF bit in mhpmevent3 remains set.
RULE 22: If supervisor mode is implemented, the scountovf register contains a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit of mhpmevent3.
RULE 23: If the associated hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit of mhpmevent3 is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 24: If the OF bit of mhpmevent3 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 25: The OF bit of mhpmevent3 functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 26: Writes to mhpmevent3 never cause a count overflow; count overflow can only result from hardware increments of the associated hpmcounter.

EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: When the .OF bit of mhpmevent30 is set, the LCOFIP bit in the mip register becomes set.
RULE 2: The LCOFIP bit in the mip register is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request generated by any mhpmevent n .OF bit being set, including the .OF bit of mhpmevent30.
RULE 3: When mhpmevent30 is programmed with the value 0, it selects no event.
RULE 4: A legal implementation may make mhpmevent30 read-only 0.
RULE 5: Any write to the mhpmevent30 CSR takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 6: An illegal-instruction exception may be raised when an indirect access to mhpmevent30 is attempted via mireg* while miselect holds a non-implemented value.
RULE 7: An indirect access to mhpmevent30 via a mireg i may result in accessing the register state, accessing a read-only zero state, or raising an illegal-instruction exception, depending on the defining extension.
RULE 8: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and mhpmevent30 is accessed through a sireg* CSR, bit 62 (MINH) of mhpmevent30 reads as 0 and is read-only.
RULE 9: If the privilege mode is M or S, siselect is in the range 0x40-0x5F, and an attempt is made to access mhpmevent30 via any sireg* CSR while menvcfg.CDE = 0, then an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 10: If the privilege mode is M or S, siselect is in the range 0x40-0x5F, and an attempt is made to access mhpmevent30 via sireg4 or sireg5 while XLEN = 64, then an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 11: If the privilege mode is M or S and siselect = 0x41, then an attempt to access mhpmevent30 via a sireg* CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: If the privilege mode is M or S, siselect is in the range 0x40-0x5F, and the counter selected by siselect is not delegated to S-mode (the corresponding bit in mcounteren = 0), then an attempt to access mhpmevent30 via a sireg* CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: If any extension required for the state accessed by mhpmevent30 is not implemented, then an attempt in M or S mode to access mhpmevent30 via a sireg* CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 14: The OF bit in mhpmevent30 indicates overflow status and disables the overflow interrupt when set.
RULE 15: The MINH bit in mhpmevent30, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in M-mode.
RULE 16: The SINH bit in mhpmevent30, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in S/HS-mode.
RULE 17: The UINH bit in mhpmevent30, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in U-mode.
RULE 18: The VSINH bit in mhpmevent30, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in VS-mode.
RULE 19: The VUINH bit in mhpmevent30, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in VU-mode.
RULE 20: The WPRI bits in mhpmevent30 are reserved.
RULE 21: If a privilege mode associated with an INH bit in mhpmevent30 is not implemented, that INH bit is read-only zero.
RULE 22: When any INH bit in mhpmevent30 is set, counting of events is inhibited while the processor is in the corresponding privilege mode, and if all INH bits are zero, counting occurs in all modes.
RULE 23: The OF bit in mhpmevent30 is set when the corresponding hpmcounter overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 24: If the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent30 overflows while the OF bit in mhpmevent30 is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 25: If the OF bit in mhpmevent30 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 26: The OF bit in mhpmevent30 also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 27: Count overflow for the counter linked to mhpmevent30 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter or mhpmevent registers, only from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 28: The count overflow interrupt request generated by the OF bit of mhpmevent30 is treated as a standard local interrupt mapped to bit 13 of the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 29: The LCOFIP bits in mip and sip are the interrupt-pending bits, and the LCOFIE bits in mie and sie are the interrupt-enable bits for the overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent30.
RULE 30: Generation of a count overflow interrupt request by the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent30 sets the OF bit in mhpmevent30.
RULE 31: When the OF bit in mhpmevent30 is set, the LCOFIP bit in mip and sip is eventually set, though not necessarily immediately.
RULE 32: The delegation of the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent30 to S-mode or M-mode is controlled by the mideleg register.
RULE 33: After the counter linked to mhpmevent30 overflows, both the counter and the OF bit in mhpmevent30 must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 34: The overflow (OF) bit of mhpmevent30 is mirrored in scountovf bit 30.
RULE 35: In M-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent30 (accessed via scountovf bit 30) is always readable.
RULE 36: In S-mode and HS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent30 (accessed via scountovf bit 30) is readable only when mcounteren bit 30 is set, otherwise it reads as zero.
RULE 37: In VS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent30 (accessed via scountovf bit 30) is readable only when both mcounteren bit 30 and hcounteren bit 30 are set, otherwise it reads as zero.
RULE 38: In M-mode, accessing mhpmevent30 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x33e; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 39: In S-mode, accessing mhpmevent30 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x33e; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 40: In U-mode, accessing mhpmevent30 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x33e; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 41: In M-mode, setting mhpmevent30.OF (bit 63) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x33e, a0; csrr a1, 0x33e; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000].
RULE 42: In M-mode, setting mhpmevent30.MINH (bit 62) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x4000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4000000000000000; csrs 0x33e, a0; csrr a1, 0x33e; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x4000000000000000].
RULE 43: In M-mode, setting mhpmevent30.SINH (bit 61) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2000000000000000; csrs 0x33e, a0; csrr a1, 0x33e; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2000000000000000].
RULE 44: In M-mode, setting mhpmevent30.UINH (bit 60) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1000000000000000; csrs 0x33e, a0; csrr a1, 0x33e; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1000000000000000].
RULE 45: In M-mode, setting mhpmevent30.VSINH (bit 59) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x800000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x800000000000000; csrs 0x33e, a0; csrr a1, 0x33e; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x800000000000000].
RULE 46: In M-mode, setting mhpmevent30.VUINH (bit 58) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x400000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x400000000000000; csrs 0x33e, a0; csrr a1, 0x33e; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x400000000000000].
RULE 47: In M-mode, accessing mhpmevent30 register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0x33e; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhpmevent31
NUMBER: 0x33f
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The mhpmevent31 CSR is accessible with machine-read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and the mhpmevent31.OF bit is set, the LCOFIP bit in the mip register reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 3: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the LCOFIE bit in the mie register is the interrupt-enable for the local-counter-overflow interrupt that can be generated by setting mhpmevent31.OF.
RULE 4: The local-counter-overflow interrupt is pending only if the LCOFIP bit in mip reflects the occurrence of setting mhpmevent31.OF and the LCOFIE bit in mie is set.
RULE 5: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mip.LCOFIP and mie.LCOFIE bits are read-only zeros, so they never reflect a change caused by mhpmevent31.OF.
RULE 6: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, setting the mhpmevent31.OF bit does not cause any architectural effect and no local-counter-overflow interrupt is generated.
RULE 7: mhpmevent31 is a 64-bit WARL register that controls which event causes the corresponding counter to increment.
RULE 8: Event 0 is defined to mean "no event" for mhpmevent31.
RULE 9: A legal implementation may make mhpmevent31 read-only 0.
RULE 10: The mhpmevent31 register can be accessed indirectly via the sireg2 CSR when the siselect field is set to 0x5F.
RULE 11: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, bit 62 (MINH) of mhpmevent31 is read-only and reads as 0 when the register is accessed through any sireg*.
RULE 12: In privilege mode M or S with siselect in the range 0x40-0x5F, an attempt to access mhpmevent31 via sireg2 raises an illegal-instruction exception when menvcfg.CDE is 0.
RULE 13: In privilege mode M or S with siselect in the range 0x40-0x5F, an attempt to access mhpmevent31 via sireg2 raises an illegal-instruction exception when mcounteren[31] is 0 (the counter is not delegated to S-mode).
RULE 14: Illegal-instruction exceptions for accesses to mhpmevent31 through sireg2 are defined only when both mstateen0[60] and hstateen0[60] are non-zero.
RULE 15: If any architectural extension required for the state of mhpmevent31 is not implemented, an attempt from M or S mode to access mhpmevent31 via sireg2 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 16: The .OF bit of mhpmevent31 is one of the mhpmevent n .OF bits whose setting can generate a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 17: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting the .OF bit in mhpmevent31 contributes to the condition that any mhpmevent n .OF bit is set, thereby generating a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 18: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, a local-counter-overflow interrupt request generated by the .OF bit in mhpmevent31 causes the sip.LCOFIP bit to be set, and sip.LCOFIP is a read-write bit.
RULE 19: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, sip.LCOFIP is a read-only zero, so setting the .OF bit in mhpmevent31 does not affect sip.LCOFIP.
RULE 20: The sip.LCOFIP bit reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request that results from any mhpmevent n .OF bit being set, including the .OF bit of mhpmevent31.
RULE 21: If a privilege mode corresponding to an x INH bit in mhpmevent31 is not implemented, that x INH bit is read-only zero.
RULE 22: When set, each of the five x INH bits in mhpmevent31 inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in the corresponding privilege mode x.
RULE 23: When all five x INH bits in mhpmevent31 are zero, events are counted in all privilege modes.
RULE 24: The OF bit in mhpmevent31 is set when the associated hpmcounter overflows and remains set until it is written by software.
RULE 25: If an hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit in mhpmevent31 is zero, a count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 26: If the OF bit in mhpmevent31 is one, no count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 27: The OF bit in mhpmevent31 also functions as a count-overflow-interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 28: Count overflow for the counter linked to mhpmevent31 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter n or mhpmevent n registers, only from hardware increments of the counter registers.
RULE 29: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by the hpmcounter sets the OF bit in mhpmevent31.
RULE 30: When the OF bit in mhpmevent31 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers.
RULE 31: Enabling overflow interrupt generation is accomplished by clearing the OF bit in mhpmevent31 together with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 32: Once the counter associated with mhpmevent31 has overflowed, both the counter and the OF bit in mhpmevent31 must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 33: The scountovf CSR contains a shadow copy of the OF (overflow) bit of mhpmevent31.
RULE 34: Bit 31 of the scountovf CSR corresponds to the OF bit of mhpmevent31.
RULE 35: In M-mode, accessing mhpmevent31 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x33f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 36: In S-mode, accessing mhpmevent31 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x33f; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 37: In U-mode, accessing mhpmevent31 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x33f; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 38: In M-mode, setting mhpmevent31.OF (bit 63) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x33f, a0; csrr a1, 0x33f; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000].
RULE 39: In M-mode, setting mhpmevent31.MINH (bit 62) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x4000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4000000000000000; csrs 0x33f, a0; csrr a1, 0x33f; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x4000000000000000].
RULE 40: In M-mode, setting mhpmevent31.SINH (bit 61) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2000000000000000; csrs 0x33f, a0; csrr a1, 0x33f; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2000000000000000].
RULE 41: In M-mode, setting mhpmevent31.UINH (bit 60) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1000000000000000; csrs 0x33f, a0; csrr a1, 0x33f; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1000000000000000].
RULE 42: In M-mode, setting mhpmevent31.VSINH (bit 59) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x800000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x800000000000000; csrs 0x33f, a0; csrr a1, 0x33f; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x800000000000000].

RULE 44: In M-mode, accessing mhpmevent31 register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0x33f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhpmevent4
NUMBER: 0x324
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Zihpm
RULE 1: The mhpmevent4 CSR is accessed with machine-mode read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: mhpmevent4 is a 64-bit WARL CSR that selects which event causes the corresponding counter mhpmcounter4 to increment.
RULE 3: An event value of 0 in mhpmevent4 is defined to mean "no event".
RULE 4: An implementation may make mhpmevent4 read-only zero.
RULE 5: If the mhpmevent4.OF bit is set, the sip.LCOFIP bit reflects the resulting local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 6: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the sip.LCOFIP bit is a read-only zero irrespective of the mhpmevent4.OF bit.
RULE 7: The OF bit in mhpmevent4 is an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the associated hpmcounter overflows.
RULE 8: The OF bit in mhpmevent4 remains set until it is written by software.
RULE 9: When the MINH bit in mhpmevent4 is 1, counting of events is inhibited while the core is in M-mode.
RULE 10: When the SINH bit in mhpmevent4 is 1, counting of events is inhibited while the core is in S-mode or HS-mode.
RULE 11: When the UINH bit in mhpmevent4 is 1, counting of events is inhibited while the core is in U-mode.
RULE 12: When the VSINH bit in mhpmevent4 is 1, counting of events is inhibited while the core is in VS-mode.
RULE 13: When the VUINH bit in mhpmevent4 is 1, counting of events is inhibited while the core is in VU-mode.
RULE 14: If a privilege mode corresponding to an INH bit in mhpmevent4 is not implemented, that INH bit reads as zero and is read-only.
RULE 15: Setting any INH bit in mhpmevent4 inhibits counting of events while the core is in the associated privilege mode, and all INH bits cleared to zero permits counting in all modes.
RULE 16: Overflow of the associated hpmcounter is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits, which causes the OF bit in mhpmevent4 to be set.
RULE 17: An hpmcounter overflow generates a count-overflow interrupt request for mhpmevent4 only when the OF bit in mhpmevent4 is zero at the moment of overflow.
RULE 18: When the OF bit in mhpmevent4 is one, further count-overflow interrupt requests for the associated counter are disabled.
RULE 19: Writing to mhpmevent4 cannot cause a counter overflow; only hardware increments of the linked hpmcounter can set the OF bit.
RULE 20: A count-overflow interrupt generated by the counter associated with mhpmevent4 raises a standard local interrupt that sets bit 13 in the appropriate interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable CSRs (mip, mie, sip, or sie).
RULE 21: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt request by the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent4 sets the OF bit in mhpmevent4.
RULE 22: After the OF bit in mhpmevent4 becomes one, the local-count-overflow-interrupt-pending (LCOFIP) bit in mip or sip will be set eventually, but not necessarily immediately.
RULE 23: The delegation of the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent4's counter to S-mode or M-mode is controlled by the mideleg CSR.
RULE 24: After the counter associated with mhpmevent4 has overflowed, the counter and the OF bit MUST be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 25: Writing to the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent4 does not cause a count overflow; overflow occurs only from hardware increments of that counter.
RULE 26: The scountovf CSR contains a shadow copy of the OF bit of mhpmevent4 in its bit position 4.
RULE 27: Any change to the OF bit of mhpmevent4 is reflected as a corresponding change in scountovf bit 4.
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing mhpmevent4 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x324; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 29: In S-mode, accessing mhpmevent4 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x324; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 30: In U-mode, accessing mhpmevent4 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x324; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 31: In M-mode, setting mhpmevent4.OF (bit 63) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x324, a0; csrr a1, 0x324; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000].

RULE 34: In M-mode, setting mhpmevent4.UINH (bit 60) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1000000000000000; csrs 0x324, a0; csrr a1, 0x324; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1000000000000000].

REGISTER: mhpmevent5
NUMBER: 0x325
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The privilege of mhpmevent5 is MRW (machine-read/write).
RULE 2: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the .OF bit of mhpmevent5 can cause a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 3: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, mip.LCOFIP is a read-write register that reflects the occurrence of a local counter-overflow interrupt request resulting from any mhpmevent n .OF bits being set, including mhpmevent5 .OF.
RULE 4: When mhpmevent5 .OF is set, mip.LCOFIP will be set, reflecting the interrupt request.
RULE 5: The interrupt request caused by mhpmevent5 .OF can be enabled or disabled via mie.LCOFIE.
RULE 6: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mhpmevent5 .OF bit has no effect because mip.LCOFIP is a read-only zero.
RULE 7: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mhpmevent5 .OF bit has no effect because mie.LCOFIE is a read-only zero.
RULE 8: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, setting mhpmevent5 .OF does not change mip.LCOFIP, which remains zero.
RULE 9: mhpmevent5 controls which event causes the corresponding counter mhpmcounter5 to increment.
RULE 10: Event code 0 in mhpmevent5 is defined to mean "no event".
RULE 11: A legal implementation makes mhpmevent5 read-only and always returns 0.
RULE 12: When mhpmevent5h is present, reads of mhpmevent5h return bits 63-32 of the mhpmevent5 register.
RULE 13: When mhpmevent5h is present, writes to mhpmevent5h change only bits 63-32 of the mhpmevent5 register.
RULE 14: When the siselect register holds the value allocated to counter 5, the sireg2 CSR may be used to access the CSR mhpmevent5.
RULE 15: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the MINH event selector bit (bit 62) of the mhpmevent5 register is read-only zero when the register is accessed through any sireg* alias.
RULE 16: When XLEN equals 64, and the processor is in machine or supervisor mode with siselect holding a value between 0x40 and 0x5F, any attempt to access sireg5 raises an illegal-instruction exception, thereby preventing indirect access to the high half of the mhpmevent5 state.
RULE 17: The sip.LCOFIP bit reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request that results from any mhpmevent n .OF bit being set, including mhpmevent5.OF.
RULE 18: If mhpmevent5.OF is set, it may cause sip.LCOFIP to become 1.
RULE 19: The OF field in mhpmevent5 is an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the associated counter overflows.
RULE 20: The MINH field in mhpmevent5, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in M-mode.
RULE 21: The SINH field in mhpmevent5, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in S/HS-mode.
RULE 22: The UINH field in mhpmevent5, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in U-mode.
RULE 23: The VSINH field in mhpmevent5, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in VS-mode.
RULE 24: The VUINH field in mhpmevent5, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in VU-mode.
RULE 25: The two WPRI fields in mhpmevent5 are reserved.
RULE 26: For each INH bit in mhpmevent5, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, the bit is read-only zero.
RULE 27: When any INH bit in mhpmevent5 is set, counting of events for that register is inhibited while the processor executes in the corresponding privilege mode.
RULE 28: If all INH bits in mhpmevent5 are zero, events are counted in all privilege modes.
RULE 29: The OF bit in mhpmevent5 is set by hardware when the corresponding hpmcounter overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 30: Overflow of the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent5 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 31: After an overflow, the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent5 wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit in mhpmevent5 remains set, preserving information.
RULE 32: When supervisor mode is implemented, the scountovf register provides a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit from mhpmevent5.
RULE 33: If the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent5 overflows while the OF bit in mhpmevent5 is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 34: If the OF bit in mhpmevent5 is one, a count overflow interrupt request is not generated.
RULE 35: The OF bit in mhpmevent5 also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for its associated hpmcounter.
RULE 36: Count overflow for mhpmevent5 can only result from hardware increments of its hpmcounter and never from writes to mhpmcounter5 or mhpmevent5.
RULE 37: The count-overflow-interrupt-request signal generated by mhpmevent5 is mapped to bit 13 of the mip, mie, sip, and sie CSRs.
RULE 38: The LCOFIP bit in mip/sip and the LCOFIE bit in mie/sie are the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits, respectively, for the count overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent5.
RULE 39: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent5 sets the OF bit in mhpmevent5.
RULE 40: When the OF bit in mhpmevent5 becomes set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip CSR.
RULE 41: Delegation of the count overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent5 to S-mode or M-mode is controlled by the mideleg register.
RULE 42: Once the counter linked to mhpmevent5 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 43: The OF bit of mhpmevent5 is mirrored as bit 5 of the read-only scountovf CSR.
RULE 44: In M-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent5 (accessed via its scountovf shadow) is always readable.
RULE 45: In S-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent5 (accessed via its scountovf shadow) is readable only if mcounteren bit 5 is set, otherwise a read returns zero.
RULE 46: In VS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent5 (accessed via its scountovf shadow) is readable only if both mcounteren bit 5 and hcounteren bit 5 are set, otherwise a read returns zero.
RULE 47: In M-mode, accessing mhpmevent5 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x325; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 48: In S-mode, accessing mhpmevent5 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x325; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

RULE 28: If the OF bit in mhpmevent6 is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 29: The OF bit in mhpmevent6 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.

EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The CSR mhpmevent7 is accessible with MRW privilege.
RULE 2: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting the mhpmevent7 .OF bit may be reflected as a local-counter-overflow interrupt request in the mip.LCOFIP bit because LCOFIP is read-write and reflects overflow events from any mhpmevent n .OF bits.
RULE 3: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mip.LCOFIP bit (and the mie.LCOFIE bit) are read-only zeros, and setting the mhpmevent7 .OF bit does not cause any interrupt request to be reflected in LCOFIP.
RULE 4: mhpmevent7 is a 64-bit WARL register that selects the event which causes mhpmcounter7 to increment.
RULE 5: Event value 0 in mhpmevent7 is defined to mean "no event", so writing the value 0 to mhpmevent7 selects no event for mhpmcounter7.
RULE 6: A conforming implementation may make mhpmevent7 a read-only register that always returns 0.
RULE 7: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, a separate CSR named mhpmevent7h exists to access the high half of mhpmevent7.
RULE 8: When mhpmevent7h exists, a read of mhpmevent7h returns bits 63-32 of mhpmevent7.
RULE 9: When mhpmevent7h exists, a write to mhpmevent7h modifies only bits 63-32 of mhpmevent7.
RULE 10: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the CSR mhpmevent7h does not exist.
RULE 11: If Sscofpmf is implemented, event selector bit 62 of mhpmevent7 is read-only 0 when accessed through sireg*.
RULE 12: Bit 63 of mhpmevent7 is named OF and indicates overflow status and also disables the overflow interrupt when set.
RULE 13: Bit 62 of mhpmevent7 is named MINH and, if set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in M-mode.
RULE 14: Bit 61 of mhpmevent7 is named SINH and, if set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in S/HS-mode.
RULE 15: Bit 60 of mhpmevent7 is named UINH and, if set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in U-mode.
RULE 16: Bit 59 of mhpmevent7 is named VSINH and, if set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in VS-mode.
RULE 17: Bit 58 of mhpmevent7 is named VUINH and, if set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in VU-mode.
RULE 18: For each INH bit in mhpmevent7, if the corresponding privilege mode is not implemented, the bit is read-only zero.
RULE 19: In mhpmevent7, each INH bit, when set, inhibits counting of events in its associated privilege mode, and if all INH bits are zero, events are counted in all modes.
RULE 20: In mhpmevent7, the OF bit is set when the associated hpmcounter overflows and remains set until software writes to clear it.
RULE 21: In mhpmevent7, the OF bit becomes set when an unsigned overflow occurs in the implemented counter bits of the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 22: After the OF bit of mhpmevent7 is set, the counter continues to wrap around and count while the OF bit remains sticky, ensuring no loss of information.
RULE 23: In mhpmevent7, a count overflow interrupt request is generated only if the associated hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit is zero; if the OF bit is one, no interrupt request is generated.
RULE 24: In mhpmevent7, the OF bit functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 25: In mhpmevent7, count overflow never results from writes to the mhpmcounter or mhpmevent registers, only from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 26: The overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent7 is delivered as a standard local interrupt mapped to bit 13 of the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers, with LCOFIP as the pending bit and LCOFIE as the enable bit.
RULE 27: Generation of a count overflow interrupt request by the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent7 sets the OF bit, which eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip register.
RULE 28: The LCOFIP bit is cleared by software before servicing the count overflow interrupt that resulted from an overflow indicated by mhpmevent7.

RULE 30: Once mhpmevent7's OF bit is set, the counter and the OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated because there are no separate overflow status and interrupt enable bits.

REGISTER: mhpmevent8
NUMBER: 0x328
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: Setting the .OF bit of mhpmevent8 can cause mip.LCOFIP to reflect the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 2: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the .OF bit of mhpmevent8 contributes to the condition that makes the read-write mip.LCOFIP pending bit reflect a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 3: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, setting the .OF bit of mhpmevent8 does not affect mip.LCOFIP or mie.LCOFIE, which remain read-only zeros.
RULE 4: mhpmevent8 is a 64-bit WARL CSR.
RULE 5: mhpmevent8 controls which event causes mhpmcounter8 to increment.
RULE 6: Event 0 for mhpmevent8 is defined to mean "no event."
RULE 7: A legal implementation may make mhpmevent8 read-only 0.
RULE 8: A write to the mhpmevent8 CSR takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 9: The mhpmevent8h CSR is provided only if the Sscofpmf extension is implemented.
RULE 10: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and mhpmevent8 is accessed via a sireg* register, bit 62 (MINH) is read-only and reads as zero.
RULE 11: If the processor is in M-mode or S-mode, siselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, and the menvcfg.CDE field is zero, then any access to mhpmevent8 via a sireg* register raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: If the processor is in M-mode or S-mode and siselect equals 0x41, then any access to mhpmevent8 via a sireg* register raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: If the processor is in M-mode or S-mode, siselect is in the range 0x40-0x5F, and the corresponding bit in mcounteren for the selected counter is zero, then any access to mhpmevent8 via a sireg* register raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 14: If any architectural extension required by the mhpmevent8 counter is not implemented, then an attempt from M-mode or S-mode to access mhpmevent8 via a sireg* register raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 15: When the Smstateen extension is implemented and bit 60 of the mstateen0 CSR is zero, privileged modes less privileged than M-mode cannot access mhpmevent8 through a sireg* register.
RULE 16: When the `.OF` bit in mhpmevent8 is set, the sip.LCOFIP bit MUST be set to indicate that a local-counter-overflow interrupt request has occurred.
RULE 17: The sip.LCOFIP bit is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request resulting from the `.OF` bit in mhpmevent8 being set.
RULE 18: The OF field of mhpmevent8 is the overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the associated counter overflows.
RULE 19: The MINH field of mhpmevent8, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in M-mode.
RULE 20: The SINH field of mhpmevent8, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in S/HS-mode.
RULE 21: The UINH field of mhpmevent8, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in U-mode.
RULE 22: The VSINH field of mhpmevent8, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in VS-mode.
RULE 23: The VUINH field of mhpmevent8, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in VU-mode.
RULE 24: For each x INH bit in mhpmevent8, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, the bit reads as zero and is read-only.
RULE 25: Each x INH bit in mhpmevent8, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in privilege mode x.
RULE 26: When the MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, and VUINH bits in mhpmevent8 are all zero, counting of events occurs in all privilege modes.
RULE 27: The OF bit in mhpmevent8 is set when the corresponding hpmcounter overflows and remains set until software writes it to zero.
RULE 28: The OF bit in mhpmevent8 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 29: If an hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit of mhpmevent8 is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 30: If the OF bit of mhpmevent8 is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 31: Count overflow never results from writes to the mhpmcounter n or mhpmevent n registers, only from hardware increments of counter registers, and this applies to mhpmevent8.
RULE 32: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt request by an hpmcounter sets the associated OF bit of mhpmevent8.
RULE 33: When the OF bit of mhpmevent8 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers.
RULE 34: The mideleg register determines whether the count-overflow interrupt originating from the OF bit of mhpmevent8 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 35: Enabling overflow-interrupt generation is accomplished by clearing the OF bit of mhpmevent8, typically together with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 36: Once a counter has overflowed, both the counter and the OF bit of mhpmevent8 MUST be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 37: In M-mode, the shadow copy of the OF bit of mhpmevent8 located in scountovf bit 8 is always readable.
RULE 38: In S-mode and HS-mode, the shadow copy of the OF bit of mhpmevent8 located in scountovf bit 8 is readable only when mcounteren bit 8 is set, and otherwise reads as zero.
RULE 39: In VS-mode, the shadow copy of the OF bit of mhpmevent8 located in scountovf bit 8 is readable only when both mcounteren bit 8 and hcounteren bit 8 are set, and otherwise reads as zero.
RULE 40: In M-mode, accessing mhpmevent8 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x328; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhpmevent9
NUMBER: 0x329
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the mip.LCOFIP bit is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request resulting from any mhpmevent n .OF bit being set, including the .OF bit in mhpmevent9.
RULE 2: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting the .OF bit in mhpmevent9 can cause the mip.LCOFIP bit to become 1.
RULE 3: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mip.LCOFIP bit is a read-only zero regardless of the state of mhpmevent9.OF.
RULE 4: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mie.LCOFIE bit is a read-only zero regardless of the state of mhpmevent9.OF.
RULE 5: Writing the value 0 to mhpmevent9 selects no event for counter 9.
RULE 6: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, reading mhpmevent9h returns bits 63-32 of the 64-bit mhpmevent9 value.
RULE 7: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, writing mhpmevent9h modifies only bits 63-32 of the 64-bit mhpmevent9 value.
RULE 8: The high-half CSR mhpmevent9h is provided only on implementations that include the Sscofpmf extension.
RULE 9: The state of mhpmevent9 can be accessed partially via hpmevent9 when hpmevent9 is read or written through the indirect CSR mapping (sireg*).
RULE 10: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, bit 62 of mhpmevent9 is read-only and reads as 0 when accessed through sireg*.
RULE 11: Indirect access to mhpmevent9 via sireg* is permitted only when siselect = 0x49, mcounteren[9] = 1, and menvcfg.CDE = 1.
RULE 12: An illegal-instruction exception is raised on indirect access to mhpmevent9 via sireg* if menvcfg.CDE = 0, regardless of siselect.
RULE 13: An illegal-instruction exception is raised on indirect access to mhpmevent9 via sireg* if siselect = 0x49 but mcounteren[9] = 0.
RULE 14: Accessing mhpmevent9 via sireg* when siselect is not equal to 0x49 results in no indirect access to mhpmevent9 (the access would target a different register).
RULE 15: If any extension on which the underlying state of mhpmevent9 depends is not implemented, an attempt from M or S mode to access mhpmevent9 through sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 16: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, attempts to write the MINH bit (bit 62) of mhpmevent9 via sireg* are ignored and the bit continues to read as 0.
RULE 17: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and the OF bit of mhpmevent9 is set, sip.LCOFIP becomes 1 (pending).
RULE 18: The OF bit of mhpmevent9 is one of the mhpmevent n .OF bits whose setting can generate a local-counter-overflow interrupt request that is reflected in sip.LCOFIP when the Sscofpmf extension is implemented.
RULE 19: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, setting the OF bit of mhpmevent9 does not affect sip.LCOFIP.
RULE 20: A local-counter-overflow interrupt can trap to S-mode only if the OF bit of mhpmevent9 has been set (producing a pending sip.LCOFIP), the sie.LCOFIE bit is set, and either the current privilege mode is S with the SIE bit in sstatus set or the current privilege mode has less privilege than S-mode.
RULE 21: The OF bit in mhpmevent9 is an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the associated counter overflows.
RULE 22: The MINH bit in mhpmevent9, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in machine mode.
RULE 23: The SINH bit in mhpmevent9, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in supervisor or hypervisor mode.
RULE 24: The UINH bit in mhpmevent9, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in user mode.
RULE 25: The VSINH bit in mhpmevent9, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in virtual-supervisor mode.
RULE 26: The VUINH bit in mhpmevent9, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in virtual-user mode.
RULE 27: The WPRI bits in mhpmevent9 are reserved and are read-only.
RULE 28: For each INH bit in mhpmevent9, if the corresponding privilege mode is not implemented, the bit is read-only zero.
RULE 29: Each INH bit in mhpmevent9, when set, inhibits counting of events in its associated privilege mode.
RULE 30: If all INH bits in mhpmevent9 are zero, counting of events is enabled in all privilege modes.
RULE 31: The OF bit in mhpmevent9 is set by hardware when the corresponding hpmcounter overflows and remains set until software writes a zero to it.
RULE 32: The OF bit in mhpmevent9 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 33: Overflow for the purpose of setting the OF bit in mhpmevent9 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 34: If the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent9 overflows while the OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 35: If the OF bit in mhpmevent9 is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated when the associated counter overflows.
RULE 36: The count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by overflow of the counter associated with mhpmevent9 is treated as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 37: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent9 sets the OF bit in mhpmevent9.
RULE 38: When the OF bit in mhpmevent9 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 39: Count overflow never results from writes to the mhpmcounter n or mhpmevent n registers, so writes to mhpmevent9 cannot cause its OF bit to be set.
RULE 40: Once the counter associated with mhpmevent9 has overflowed, both the counter and the OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 41: The overflow (OF) bit of mhpmevent9 is mirrored as bit 9 of the read-only scountovf CSR.
RULE 42: In M-mode, the shadow copy of the OF bit of mhpmevent9 (scountovf bit 9) is always readable.
RULE 43: In S-mode and HS-mode, the shadow copy of the OF bit of mhpmevent9 (scountovf bit 9) is readable only when the corresponding mcounteren bit 9 is set; otherwise it reads as zero.
RULE 44: In VS-mode, the shadow copy of the OF bit of mhpmevent9 (scountovf bit 9) is readable only when both the corresponding mcounteren bit 9 and hcounteren bit 9 are set; otherwise it reads as zero.
RULE 45: In M-mode, accessing mhpmevent9 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x329; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 46: In S-mode, accessing mhpmevent9 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x329; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
