REGISTER: pmpaddr26
NUMBER: 0x3ca
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr26[G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 while a read of the register returns 0.
RULE 2: CSRRS and CSRRC may modify any bit in pmpaddr26 that reads as a value different from its underlying value even when the corresponding bit in rs1 is zero.
RULE 3: Executing CSRRC or CSRRS to modify a different bit causes a read of pmpaddr26[G-1] to return 0 and subsequently writes back 0, updating the underlying value of pmpaddr26[G-1] to 0.
RULE 4: For RV64, pmpaddr26 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 5: pmpaddr26 is a WARL (write-any-value-read-legal) register because not all physical address bits may be implemented.
RULE 6: On RV64, pmpaddr26 is limited to bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address because the RV64 PMP address registers impose the same limit as the Sv39 and Sv48 virtual-memory schemes.
RULE 7: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 is 0, then the PMP entry is disabled and matches no addresses.
RULE 8: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 selects NA4, then pmpaddr26 encodes a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 9: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 selects NAPOT and the least-significant bit of pmpaddr26 is 0, then the entry matches an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 10: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 selects NAPOT and the two least-significant bits of pmpaddr26 are 01, then the entry matches a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 11: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 selects NAPOT and the three least-significant bits of pmpaddr26 are 011, then the entry matches a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 selects NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr26 have the pattern yy01 followed by all ones, then the entry matches a 2 XLEN-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 selects NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr26 have the pattern y011 followed by all ones, then the entry matches a 2 XLEN+1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 selects NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr26 have the pattern 0111 followed by all ones, then the entry matches a 2 XLEN+2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 15: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 selects NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr26 are all ones, then the entry matches a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 16: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 is TOR, then the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr25 ≤ y < pmpaddr26, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg25.
RULE 17: If pmpaddr25 ≥ pmpaddr26 and the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 is TOR, then the entry matches no addresses.
RULE 18: When G ≥ 2 and the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 has its high bit set (mode NAPOT), then bits pmpaddr26[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 19: When G ≥ 1 and the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 has its high bit clear (mode OFF or TOR), then bits pmpaddr26[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 20: The low-order G bits of pmpaddr26 do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 21: Changing the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT does not alter the stored value of bit pmpaddr26[G-1]; the stored bit remains unchanged.
RULE 22: When the L bit of PMP entry 26 is set, any write to the pmpaddr26 register is ignored.
RULE 23: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr26 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3ca; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 24: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr26 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3ca; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 25: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr26 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3ca; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 26: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr26.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3ca, a0; csrr a1, 0x3ca; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 27: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr26 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3ca; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr27
NUMBER: 0x3cb
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction modifies a bit in pmpaddr27 that is different from the G-1 bit, and the underlying hardware value of pmpaddr27[G-1] is 1 while the read value of pmpaddr27[G-1] is 0, then the instruction reads 0 from pmpaddr27[G-1] and writes 0 back, updating the underlying hardware value of pmpaddr27[G-1] to 0.
RULE 2: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction modifies any bit of pmpaddr27 other than the G-1 bit, a mismatch between the underlying hardware value and the read value of pmpaddr27[G-1] can cause the read value (0) to be written back, thereby updating the underlying hardware value of pmpaddr27[G-1] to match the read value.
RULE 3: pmpaddr27 is a Machine-level CSR with read/write privilege (MRW).
RULE 4: In RV64 implementations, pmpaddr27 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 5: Because the pmpaddr registers are WARL, pmpaddr27 MAY be read-only zero.
RULE 6: Because all PMP CSR fields are WARL, pmpaddr27 MAY be read-only zero.
RULE 7: PMP CSRs are only accessible to M-mode, therefore pmpaddr27 is only accessible to M-mode.
RULE 8: When pmpcfg27.A = NAPOT, the pattern of the low-order bits of pmpaddr27 encodes the size of the matched NAPOT region exactly as specified in the NAPOT range encoding table.
RULE 9: When pmpcfg27.A = TOR, pmpaddr27 provides the top address of the range while pmpaddr26 provides the bottom address.
RULE 10: When pmpcfg27.A = TOR, the PMP entry 27 matches any address y such that pmpaddr26 ≤ y < pmpaddr27, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg26.
RULE 11: If pmpcfg27.A = TOR and pmpaddr26 ≥ pmpaddr27, then PMP entry 27 matches no addresses.
RULE 12: When the implementation granularity G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg27.A[1] = 1 (NAPOT mode), reads of pmpaddr27 return all ones in bits G-2 down to 0.
RULE 13: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg27.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), reads of pmpaddr27 return all zeros in bits G-1 down to 0.
RULE 14: The low bits of pmpaddr27 masked by granularity (bits G-1 down to 0) are ignored by the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 15: The physical bit pmpaddr27[G-1] retains its original stored value when pmpcfg27.A is changed between NAPOT and OFF/TOR modes, even though the read value of pmpaddr27 may change.
RULE 16: If PMP entry 27 is locked, writes to pmpaddr27 are ignored.
RULE 17: The L bit for entry 27 indicates that the PMP entry is locked, and therefore writes to pmpaddr27 are ignored.
RULE 18: Setting the L bit for entry 27 locks the PMP entry even when the A field is set to OFF, and consequently writes to pmpaddr27 are ignored.
RULE 19: For the PMP rule that uses pmpaddr27 to be a valid protected physical memory region, the field pmpcfg27.A must not be OFF.
RULE 20: If pmpcfg27.A is TOR, then the value in pmpaddr26 must be strictly less than the value in pmpaddr27.
RULE 21: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr27 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3cb; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 22: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr27 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3cb; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 23: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr27 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3cb; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 24: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr27.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3cb, a0; csrr a1, 0x3cb; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 25: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr27 register while P extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: P; csrr a0, 0x3cb; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 26: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr27 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3cb; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr28
NUMBER: 0x3cc
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: A CSRRW instruction that targets pmpaddr28 reads the old value of pmpaddr28, zero-extends it to XLEN bits, writes it to integer register rd, and writes the initial value in rs1 to pmpaddr28.
RULE 2: If a CSRRW instruction targeting pmpaddr28 has rd = x0, the instruction shall not read pmpaddr28 and shall not cause any of the side effects that might occur on a CSR read.
RULE 3: A CSRRW instruction targeting pmpaddr28 with rs1 = x0 will attempt to write zero to pmpaddr28.
RULE 4: A CSRRS instruction that targets pmpaddr28 reads the value of pmpaddr28, zero-extends it to XLEN bits, writes it to integer register rd, and treats the initial value in rs1 as a bit mask that sets corresponding writable bits in pmpaddr28.
RULE 5: A CSRRC instruction that targets pmpaddr28 reads the value of pmpaddr28, zero-extends it to XLEN bits, writes it to integer register rd, and treats the initial value in rs1 as a bit mask that clears corresponding writable bits in pmpaddr28.
RULE 6: When executing CSRRS or CSRRC on pmpaddr28, any bits that read as a different value from their underlying value may be modified even if the corresponding bit is not set in rs1.
RULE 7: If pmpaddr28[G-1] has an underlying value of 1 but reads as 0, executing CSRRC or CSRRS on pmpaddr28 to modify a different bit will cause 0 to be read from pmpaddr28[G-1] and then written back, updating the underlying value to 0.
RULE 8: For CSRRS and CSRRC instructions targeting pmpaddr28, if rs1 = x0, the instruction will not write to pmpaddr28 at all, shall not cause any of the side effects that might otherwise occur on a CSR write, and shall not raise illegal-instruction exceptions on accesses to read-only pmpaddr28.
RULE 9: CSRRS and CSRRC instructions targeting pmpaddr28 always read pmpaddr28 and cause any read side effects regardless of the values of rs1 and rd.
RULE 10: If rs1 specifies a register other than x0 and that register holds a zero value, a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targeting pmpaddr28 will not trigger any per-field side effects but will trigger any side effects caused by writing to the entire pmpaddr28.
RULE 11: The CSRRWI, CSRRSI, and CSRRCI immediate-form instructions targeting pmpaddr28 behave as their register-operand counterparts, using a zero-extended 5-bit immediate instead of rs1.
RULE 12: If a CSRRSI or CSRRCI instruction targeting pmpaddr28 has an immediate field uimm[4:0] equal to zero, the instruction will not write to pmpaddr28, shall not cause any of the side effects that might otherwise occur on a CSR write, and shall not raise illegal-instruction exceptions on accesses to read-only pmpaddr28.
RULE 13: For a CSRRW instruction targeting pmpaddr28 with rd = x0, the instruction does not read pmpaddr28 and writes to pmpaddr28.
RULE 14: For a CSRRW instruction targeting pmpaddr28 with rd != x0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and writes to pmpaddr28.
RULE 15: For CSRRS or CSRRC instructions targeting pmpaddr28 with rs1 = x0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and does not write to pmpaddr28.
RULE 16: For CSRRS or CSRRC instructions targeting pmpaddr28 with rs1 != x0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and writes to pmpaddr28.
RULE 17: For a CSRRWI instruction targeting pmpaddr28 with rd = x0, the instruction does not read pmpaddr28 and writes to pmpaddr28.
RULE 18: For a CSRRWI instruction targeting pmpaddr28 with rd != x0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and writes to pmpaddr28.
RULE 19: For CSRRSI or CSRRCI instructions targeting pmpaddr28 with uimm = 0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and does not write to pmpaddr28.
RULE 20: For CSRRSI or CSRRCI instructions targeting pmpaddr28 with uimm != 0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and writes to pmpaddr28.
RULE 21: No standard CSR, including pmpaddr28, has side effects on field writes.
RULE 22: pmpaddr28 is not among the CSRs that are automatically modified as side effects of instruction execution, so no automatic update side effect applies to pmpaddr28.
RULE 23: pmpaddr28 is a WARL field.
RULE 24: Software may write any value to pmpaddr28.
RULE 25: The hardware may modify the value written to pmpaddr28.
RULE 26: pmpaddr28 may read as zero if the implementation provides a read-only zero value.
RULE 27: pmpaddr28 is accessible only in machine mode.
RULE 28: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is 0, the entry is disabled and matches no addresses.
RULE 29: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is 1, the entry uses TOR mode with pmpaddr28 serving as the top of the address range.
RULE 30: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is 2, the entry uses NA4 mode and pmpaddr28 encodes a 4-byte range.
RULE 31: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is 3, the entry uses NAPOT mode and pmpaddr28 encodes a naturally aligned power-of-two range.
RULE 32: If the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is set to TOR, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr27 ≤ y < pmpaddr28, irrespective of the value of the preceding configuration register.
RULE 33: If pmpaddr27 ≥ pmpaddr28 and the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is TOR, then the entry matches no addresses.
RULE 34: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NA4, the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 encode a 4-byte range as defined by the NA4 encoding.
RULE 35: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern yyyy…yyy0, the entry matches an 8-byte range.
RULE 36: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern yyyy…yy01, the entry matches a 16-byte range.
RULE 37: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern yyyy…y011, the entry matches a 32-byte range.
RULE 38: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern yy01…1111, the entry matches a range of size 2 × XLEN bytes.
RULE 39: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern y011…1111, the entry matches a range of size 2 × XLEN + 1 bytes.
RULE 40: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern 0111…1111, the entry matches a range of size 2 × XLEN + 2 bytes.
RULE 41: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern 1111…1111, the entry matches a range of size 2 × XLEN + 3 bytes.
RULE 42: When the PMP granularity G is greater than or equal to 1, the NA4 mode must not be selected for the entry whose address register is pmpaddr28.
RULE 43: When G ≥ 2 and the high bit of the A field (A[1]) for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is set, bits pmpaddr28[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 44: When G ≥ 1 and the high bit of the A field (A[1]) for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is clear, bits pmpaddr28[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 45: Bits pmpaddr28[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic for the entry that contains pmpaddr28.
RULE 46: Changing the high bit of the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 changes the value read from pmpaddr28 but does not alter the underlying stored value, and pmpaddr28[G-1] retains its original value when the configuration is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 47: Writes to pmpaddr28 are ignored when PMP entry 28 is locked.
RULE 48: The L bit of PMP entry 28 indicates that the entry is locked, causing writes to the configuration register and associated address registers, including pmpaddr28, to be ignored.
RULE 49: When pmpaddr28 is locked, it remains locked until the hart is reset.
RULE 50: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr28 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3cc; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 51: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr28 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3cc; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 52: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr28 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3cc; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 53: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr28.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3cc, a0; csrr a1, 0x3cc; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 54: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr28 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3cc; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr29
NUMBER: 0x3cd
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: When the CSR pmpaddr29 is read, bit G-1 may have an underlying stored value of 1 but be observed as 0.
RULE 2: Executing a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction on pmpaddr29 with a mask that modifies a bit other than G-1 will cause the read of pmpaddr29[G-1] to return 0.
RULE 3: Executing a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction on pmpaddr29 with a mask that modifies a bit other than G-1 will cause the read value 0 to be written back to pmpaddr29[G-1], updating the underlying stored value of pmpaddr29[G-1] to 0.
RULE 4: When a CSRRS, CSRRC, or their immediate variants are executed on pmpaddr29 and a bit's read-back value differs from its underlying stored value, that bit may be modified by the instruction even if the corresponding bit is not set in the rs1/uimm mask.
RULE 5: For RV64, pmpaddr29 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 6: pmpaddr29 is a WARL field because not all physical address bits may be implemented.
RULE 7: pmpaddr29 may be read-only zero as all PMP CSR fields are WARL and may be read-only zero.
RULE 8: Reads or writes of pmpaddr29 are only permitted when the processor is executing in M-mode.
RULE 9: If the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 has its A field set to NA4, then the value stored in pmpaddr29 is of the form yyyy…yyyy and pmpaddr29 matches a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 10: If the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 is set to NAPOT and the value stored in pmpaddr29 ends with a single zero (…0), then pmpaddr29 matches an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 11: If the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 is set to NAPOT and the value stored in pmpaddr29 ends with the bit pattern …01, then pmpaddr29 matches a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: If the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 is set to NAPOT and the value stored in pmpaddr29 ends with the bit pattern …011, then pmpaddr29 matches a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: If the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 is set to NAPOT and the value stored in pmpaddr29 consists entirely of ones, then pmpaddr29 matches a 2XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range, and the encoding pattern continues as described in Table 24 for intermediate sizes.
RULE 14: If the A field of the PMP configuration register for entry 29 is set to TOR, then pmpaddr29 defines the top of the address range and the preceding address register pmpaddr28 defines the bottom of the address range.
RULE 15: If the A field of the PMP configuration register for entry 29 is set to TOR, then entry 29 matches any address y such that pmpaddr28 ≤ y < pmpaddr29, irrespective of the value of the configuration register for entry 28.
RULE 16: If pmpaddr28 ≥ pmpaddr29 and the A field of the PMP configuration register for entry 29 is TOR, then entry 29 matches no addresses.
RULE 17: When the PMP granularity G satisfies G ≥ 2 and bit 1 of the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 is set (indicating NAPOT mode), then bits pmpaddr29[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 18: When the PMP granularity G satisfies G ≥ 1 and bit 1 of the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 is clear (indicating OFF or TOR mode), then bits pmpaddr29[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 19: Bits pmpaddr29[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic for entry 29.
RULE 20: Although changing bit 1 of the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 alters the value read from pmpaddr29, it does not modify the underlying stored bits, and specifically bit pmpaddr29[G-1] retains its original stored value when the A field is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 21: Software may determine the PMP granularity by writing zero to pmp0cfg, writing all ones to pmpaddr29, and then reading back pmpaddr29; the index G of the least-significant set bit in the read value indicates that the granularity is 2^G + 2 bytes.
RULE 22: If the L bit of PMP entry 29 is set, writes to pmpaddr29 are ignored.
RULE 23: Once the L bit of PMP entry 29 has been set, the lock on pmpaddr29 persists until a hart reset occurs.
RULE 24: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 29 locks the entry and causes writes to pmpaddr29 to be ignored regardless of the value of the A field in pmp29 cfg.

WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: M, Smepmp
RULE 1: The G-1 bit of the pmpaddr3 CSR may have an underlying value of 1 while a read of pmpaddr3 returns 0 for that bit.

RULE 13: The bit pmpaddr3[G-1] retains its original stored value when pmpcfg3.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.

REGISTER: pmpaddr35
NUMBER: 0x3d3
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr35 has machine read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: On an RV64 hart, pmpaddr35 encodes bits 55-2 of the 56-bit physical address used for PMP entry 35.
RULE 3: The fields of pmpaddr35 are WARL and may be read-only zero.
RULE 4: pmpaddr35 may contain unimplemented bits and is therefore WARL.
RULE 5: When a PMP entry's configuration (A field) selects the preceding-address mode, pmpaddr35 can be used as the address register for PMP entry 36, directly affecting the region defined for that entry.
RULE 6: The address-matching mode of the pmpaddr35 register is defined by the A field of pmpcfg35, where the encodings are OFF = 0, TOR = 1, NA4 = 2, and NAPOT = 3.
RULE 7: When pmpcfg35.A equals TOR, pmpaddr35 supplies the upper bound of the address range so that any address y satisfying pmpaddr34 ≤ y < pmpaddr35 is matched (the value of pmpcfg34 is irrelevant).
RULE 8: When pmpcfg35.A equals TOR and pmpaddr34 is greater than or equal to pmpaddr35, the pmpaddr35 entry matches no addresses.
RULE 9: When pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT, the low-order bits of pmpaddr35 encode the size of the range according to the pattern definitions in Table 24.
RULE 10: If pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT and pmpaddr35 matches the pattern `yyyy…yyyy`, the entry defines a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 11: If pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT and pmpaddr35 matches the pattern `yyyy…yyy0`, the entry defines an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: If pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT and pmpaddr35 matches the pattern `yyyy…yy01`, the entry defines a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: If pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT and pmpaddr35 matches the pattern `yyyy…y011`, the entry defines a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: If pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT and pmpaddr35 matches the pattern `yy01…1111`, the entry defines a 2 XLEN-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 15: If pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT and pmpaddr35 matches the pattern `y011…1111`, the entry defines a 2 XLEN+1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 16: If pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT and pmpaddr35 matches the pattern `0111…1111`, the entry defines a 2 XLEN+2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 17: If pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT and pmpaddr35 matches the pattern `1111…1111`, the entry defines a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range.

RULE 19: When the PMP granularity G is at least 1 and pmpcfg35.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), reads of bits pmpaddr35[G-1:0] return all zeros.
RULE 20: Bits pmpaddr35[G-1:0] are ignored by the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 21: Changing pmpcfg35.A[1] may modify the value read from pmpaddr35 while the underlying stored bits remain unchanged.
RULE 22: The stored bit pmpaddr35[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg35.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 23: If the PMP granularity G is at least 1, the NA4 mode is not selectable for entry 35, so pmpaddr35 cannot be used with a pmpcfg35.A encoding of NA4.
RULE 24: If PMP entry 35 is locked, writes to pmpaddr35 are ignored.
RULE 25: When the L bit in pmp35cfg is set, writes to pmpaddr35 are ignored.

REGISTER: pmpaddr37
NUMBER: 0x3d5
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr37 may have an underlying value of 1 but read as 0.
RULE 2: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction modifies a bit other than the top-most PMP address bit of pmpaddr37, the hardware must read the current read value of pmpaddr37[G-1] (which may be 0 even if the underlying value is 1), must write that read value back, and must update the underlying value of that bit to match the read value.
RULE 3: CSRRS and CSRRC always read pmpaddr37 and cause any read side effects defined for pmpaddr37 regardless of the rs1 and rd fields.
RULE 4: CSRRS or CSRRC with rs1 = x0 must not write to pmpaddr37 and shall not cause any write side effects on pmpaddr37.
RULE 5: CSRRS or CSRRC with rs1 ≠ x0 must write to pmpaddr37 and must trigger side effects for any fields whose corresponding bits are set in rs1.
RULE 6: CSRRS or CSRRC with rs1 ≠ x0 and with the source register containing zero must not trigger per-field side effects on pmpaddr37 but must trigger any side effects associated with writing the entire CSR.
RULE 7: For any CSRRS or CSRRC targeting pmpaddr37, the CSR is always read and it is written only when rs1 ≠ x0.
RULE 8: CSRRSI or CSRRCI with uimm[4:0] = 0 shall not write to pmpaddr37 and shall not cause any write side effects on pmpaddr37.
RULE 9: CSRRSI or CSRRCI with uimm[4:0] ≠ 0 must read and write pmpaddr37 and must follow the same per-field side-effect rules as CSRRS or CSRRC.
RULE 10: A CSRRW targeting pmpaddr37 with rs1 = x0 must write the value 0 into pmpaddr37.
RULE 11: The architectural privilege level for pmpaddr37 is MRW (Machine-Read/Write).
RULE 12: Reads or writes to the register pmpaddr37 MUST be performed only when the hart is executing in M-mode.
RULE 13: Each field of the register pmpaddr37 is a WARL (Write-Any-Read-Legal) field and the register MAY read back as zero regardless of the value written.
RULE 14: When executing on an RV64 hart, the value written to the register pmpaddr37 supplies bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address for PMP entry 37.
RULE 15: Physical-address bits that are not implemented on a particular implementation affect the legal values that can be written to the register pmpaddr37, and writes of illegal values MAY be silently masked or cause the register to read back a different legal value.
RULE 16: With pmpcfg37.A = 2 (NA4), the low-order bits of pmpaddr37 are all ones and represent a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 17: With pmpcfg37.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr37 ending in 0, the encoded region size is 8 bytes.
RULE 18: With pmpcfg37.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr37 ending in 01, the encoded region size is 16 bytes.
RULE 19: With pmpcfg37.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr37 ending in 011, the encoded region size is 32 bytes.
RULE 20: With pmpcfg37.A = 3 (NAPOT) and all low-order bits of pmpaddr37 set to 1, the encoded region size is 2^{XLEN}+3 bytes.
RULE 21: When pmpcfg37.A = TOR, pmpaddr37 serves as the top bound of the address range and the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr36 ≤ y < pmpaddr37, regardless of the value of pmpcfg36.
RULE 22: If pmpaddr36 ≥ pmpaddr37 and pmpcfg37.A = TOR, then PMP entry 37 matches no addresses.
RULE 23: If G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg37.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), then bits pmpaddr37[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 24: If G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg37.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), then bits pmpaddr37[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 25: Bits pmpaddr37[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 26: Changing pmpcfg37.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr37 but does not alter the underlying stored value, and pmpaddr37[G-1] retains its original value when the mode is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and back to NAPOT.
RULE 27: If the L bit in pmpcfg37 is set, writes to pmpaddr37 are ignored.
RULE 28: The lock of PMP entry 37, which governs pmpaddr37, remains in effect until the hart is reset.
RULE 29: The architectural rule that a locked PMP entry causes writes to its pmpaddr register to be ignored applies to entry 37, so the L bit in pmpcfg37 directly causes the write-ignore behavior for pmpaddr37.
RULE 30: A PMP rule that includes pmpaddr37 is valid only when pmpcfg37.A is not OFF.
RULE 31: If pmpcfg37.A TOR, then a PMP rule that includes pmpaddr37 is valid only when pmpaddr36 is less than pmpaddr37.
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr37 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3d5; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 33: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr37 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3d5; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

RULE 1: The register pmpaddr38 may have an underlying bit value that differs from the value read, such that pmpaddr38[G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 but be read as 0.

REGISTER: pmpaddr4
NUMBER: 0x3b4
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr4[G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 but be read as 0.
RULE 2: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction accesses pmpaddr4, any bits whose read value differs from their underlying value may be modified by the instruction even if the corresponding bit is not set in rs1.
RULE 3: Executing a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction that modifies a bit other than G-1 of pmpaddr4 will cause a read of 0 from pmpaddr4[G-1] and will write back 0, updating the underlying value of pmpaddr4[G-1] to 0.
RULE 4: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its source register rs1 is x0, the instruction shall not write to pmpaddr4 and shall not cause any side effects that would occur on a CSR write, nor shall it raise an illegal-instruction exception on a read-only pmpaddr4.
RULE 5: A CSRRS or CSRRC instruction that targets pmpaddr4 shall always read pmpaddr4 and shall cause any read side effects regardless of the values of rs1 and rd.
RULE 6: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction accesses pmpaddr4 with rs1 specifying a register other than x0 that contains the value zero, the instruction will not action any per-field side effects but will action any side effects caused by writing the entire pmpaddr4.
RULE 7: A CSRRW instruction that accesses pmpaddr4 with rs1 equal to x0 will attempt to write zero to pmpaddr4.
RULE 8: When a CSRRW instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its destination register rd is x0, the instruction shall not read pmpaddr4 but shall write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 9: When a CSRRW instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its destination register rd is not x0, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 10: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its source register rs1 is x0, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall not write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 11: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its source register rs1 is not x0, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 12: When a CSRRWI instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its destination register rd is x0, the instruction shall not read pmpaddr4 but shall write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 13: When a CSRRWI instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its destination register rd is not x0, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 14: When a CSRRSI or CSRRCI instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its immediate rs1 (uimm) is zero, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall not write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 15: When a CSRRSI or CSRRCI instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its immediate rs1 (uimm) is non-zero, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 16: When pmpaddr4 is written by a CSRRW or CSRRWI instruction, side effects for all fields of pmpaddr4 shall be enacted.
RULE 17: When pmpaddr4 is written by a CSRRS, CSRRC, CSRRSI, or CSRRCI instruction, side effects shall be enacted only for those fields of pmpaddr4 whose corresponding bits are set in the rs1 register or uimm argument.
RULE 18: pmpaddr4 is a WARL register.
RULE 19: Any field of pmpaddr4 may be read-only zero.
RULE 20: pmpaddr4 can be accessed only while the hart is in M-mode.
RULE 21: When pmpcfg4.A = NAPOT, bits pmpaddr4 encode the NAPOT range size as follows: pattern …yyy0 selects an 8-byte range, …yy01 selects a 16-byte range, …y011 selects a 32-byte range, …yy01…1111 selects a 2 XLEN-byte range, …y011…1111 selects a 2 XLEN+1-byte range, 0111…1111 selects a 2 XLEN+2-byte range, and 1111…1111 selects a 2 XLEN+3-byte range.
RULE 22: When pmpcfg4.A = NA4, the value of pmpaddr4 is ignored and the entry defines a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 23: When pmpcfg4.A = TOR, pmpaddr4 defines the top address of the TOR range and the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr3 ≤ y < pmpaddr4, irrespective of pmpcfg3.
RULE 24: If pmpaddr3 ≥ pmpaddr4 and pmpcfg4.A = TOR, then PMP entry 4 matches no addresses.
RULE 25: When the granularity G is at least 2 and pmpcfg4.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr4[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 26: When the granularity G is at least 1 and pmpcfg4.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr4[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 27: Bits pmpaddr4[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 28: Changing pmpcfg4.A[1] alters the read-value of pmpaddr4 but does not change the underlying stored value, and pmpaddr4[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg4.A changes from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 29: When the granularity G is at least 1, the NA4 mode is not selectable, so pmpaddr4 cannot be used with pmpcfg4.A = 2 (NA4) in such implementations.
RULE 30: If PMP entry 4 is locked, any write to the address register pmpaddr4 has no effect and is ignored.
RULE 31: If PMP entry 4 is locked and its configuration register pmp4 cfg specifies address-matching mode TOR, any write to the preceding address register pmpaddr4-1 is ignored.
RULE 32: Setting the L bit in pmp4 cfg locks PMP entry 4 regardless of the value of pmp4 cfg.A (including OFF), causing subsequent writes to pmpaddr4 to be ignored.
RULE 33: When the L bit in pmp4 cfg is set, the R, W, and X permission checks associated with entry 4 are enforced for M-mode accesses that match pmpaddr4 as well as for S- and U-mode accesses.
RULE 34: When the L bit in pmp4 cfg is clear, M-mode accesses that match entry 4 as defined by pmpaddr4 succeed irrespective of the R, W, and X permission bits, while S- and U-mode accesses that match pmpaddr4 are still subject to those permission checks.
RULE 35: pmpaddr3 MUST be less than pmpaddr4 when the address-matching mode field A of pmpcfg4 is TOR.
RULE 36: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr4 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3b4; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 37: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr4 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3b4; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 38: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr4 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3b4; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 39: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr4.ADDR (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3b4, a0; csrr a1, 0x3b4; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 40: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr4 register while P extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: P; csrr a0, 0x3b4; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 41: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr4 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3b4; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr40
NUMBER: 0x3d8
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: The most-significant bit (bit G-1) of the pmpaddr40 CSR may have an underlying stored value of 1 while reads of that bit return 0.

RULE 6: The actual bits that pmpaddr40 can hold depend on the implementation's supported physical-address width because not all physical address bits may be implemented.
RULE 7: PMP CSRs are only accessible to M-mode, therefore pmpaddr40 can be read or written only when the hart is in M-mode.
RULE 8: When the granularity G is at least 2 and pmpcfg40.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr40[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 9: When the granularity G is at least 1 and pmpcfg40.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr40[G-1:0] read as all zeros.

RULE 12: The bit pmpaddr40[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg40.A changes from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 13: If the A field of PMP entry 40 is TOR, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr39 <= y < pmpaddr40, irrespective of pmpcfg39.
RULE 14: If pmpaddr39 >= pmpaddr40 and pmpcfg40.A = TOR, then PMP entry 40 matches no addresses.
RULE 15: If PMP entry 40 is locked, writes to pmpaddr40 are ignored.
RULE 16: Setting the L bit in pmp40 cfg locks PMP entry 40, and as a result writes to pmpaddr40 are ignored.
RULE 17: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr40 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3d8; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 18: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr40 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3d8; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

RULE 6: pmpaddr42 can be accessed only while executing in M-mode.

RULE 4: In RV64 implementations, pmpaddr45 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 5: pmpaddr45 is a WARL field and may read as zero.
RULE 6: pmpaddr45 is WARL with respect to any unimplemented physical-address bits.
RULE 7: If pmpcfg45.A = 0 then pmpaddr45 operates in OFF mode, defining a null region that is disabled and matches no addresses.
RULE 8: If pmpcfg45.A = 1 then pmpaddr45 operates in TOR mode, acting as the top of an address range whose bottom is defined by pmpaddr44.
RULE 9: If pmpcfg45.A = 2 then pmpaddr45 operates in NA4 mode, defining a naturally aligned four-byte region.
RULE 10: If pmpcfg45.A = 3 then pmpaddr45 operates in NAPOT mode, defining a naturally aligned power-of-two region of size at least eight bytes.
RULE 11: When pmpcfg45.A = 2 (NA4) the low-order bits of pmpaddr45 encode a 4-byte NAPOT range, with the most-significant bits (the "y" bits) unchanged.

RULE 20: If pmpcfg45.A = TOR and pmpaddr44 ≥ pmpaddr45 then PMP entry 45 matches no addresses.

RULE 22: When the granularity G is at least 1 and pmpcfg45.A[1] is clear (indicating OFF or TOR mode), the bits pmpaddr45[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 23: Bits pmpaddr45[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic for PMP entry 45.

RULE 26: Changing pmpcfg50.A between NAPOT and TOR or OFF does not modify the stored value of pmpaddr50[G-1]; the bit remains unchanged.
RULE 27: If PMP entry 50 is locked, writes to pmpaddr50 are ignored.
RULE 28: If PMP entry 50 is locked, writes to pmpcfg50 are ignored, and the lock also causes writes to pmpaddr50 to be ignored.
RULE 29: If PMP entry 50 is locked and pmpcfg50.A is set to TOR, writes to pmpaddr49 are ignored, and the lock likewise prevents writes to pmpaddr50.
RULE 30: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 50 locks the entry even when the A field is OFF, causing the lock behavior that applies to pmpaddr50.
RULE 31: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr50 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3e2; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 32: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr50 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3e2; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: pmpaddr51
NUMBER: 0x3e3
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P
RULE 1: When CSRRS or CSRRC accesses pmpaddr51, any bit that reads as a value different from its underlying value may be modified by the instruction even if the corresponding bit in rs1 is zero.
RULE 2: The pmpaddr51[G-1] field may have an underlying value of 1 while a read of that field returns 0.
RULE 3: Executing CSRRC or CSRRS on pmpaddr51 to modify a bit other than pmpaddr51[G-1] causes a 0 to be read from pmpaddr51[G-1] and then written back, updating the underlying value of pmpaddr51[G-1] to 0.
RULE 4: The privilege level for pmpaddr51 is MRW, meaning machine-read/write access.
RULE 5: pmpaddr51 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address when the implementation is RV64.
RULE 6: pmpaddr51 is a WARL register because not all physical address bits may be implemented.
RULE 7: pmpaddr51 is accessible only in M-mode.
RULE 8: The A field of pmpcfg51 encodes the address-matching mode of pmpaddr51, where OFF = 0, TOR = 1, NA4 = 2, and NAPOT = 3.
RULE 9: When pmpcfg51.A is NA4 or NAPOT, the low-order bits of pmpaddr51 encode the size of the address range according to the pattern defined in Table 24.
RULE 10: When pmpcfg51.A is TOR, pmpaddr51 provides the top address of the PMP entry's address range.
RULE 11: When pmpcfg51.A is TOR, the PMP entry matches any address y satisfying pmpaddr50 ≤ y < pmpaddr51, independent of pmpcfg50.
RULE 12: If pmpcfg51.A is TOR and pmpaddr50 is greater than or equal to pmpaddr51, then the PMP entry matches no addresses.
RULE 13: When the PMP granularity G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg51.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), the bits pmpaddr51[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 14: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg51.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), the bits pmpaddr51[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 15: Bits pmpaddr51[G-1:0] are ignored by the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 16: Changing pmpcfg51.A[1] modifies the value read from pmpaddr51 but does not alter the underlying stored value of pmpaddr51.
RULE 17: The bit pmpaddr51[G-1] retains its original stored value when pmpcfg51.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 18: If PMP entry 51 is locked, writes to pmpaddr51 are ignored.
RULE 19: The L bit of PMP entry 51 indicates that the entry is locked, and therefore writes to pmpaddr51 are ignored.
RULE 20: Setting the L bit for PMP entry 51 locks the entry and causes writes to pmpaddr51 to be ignored even when the A field is set to OFF.

RULE 22: For the PMP entry that uses pmpaddr51, the associated pmpcfg[51].A field MUST NOT be OFF for the entry to encode a valid protected physical memory region.
RULE 23: If the associated pmpcfg[51].A field is TOR then pmpaddr50 MUST be less than pmpaddr51.

REGISTER: pmpaddr53
NUMBER: 0x3e5
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr53[G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 while a read of that bit returns 0.
RULE 2: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction accesses pmpaddr53, any bit that reads as a value different from its underlying value may be modified even if the corresponding bit in rs1 is zero.
RULE 3: Executing a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction on pmpaddr53 to modify a bit other than G-1 will cause a read of pmpaddr53[G-1] that returns 0 and will subsequently write back 0, updating its underlying value to 0.
RULE 4: Any CSRRS or CSRRC instruction that targets pmpaddr53 always reads pmpaddr53 and triggers any read-side effects regardless of the values of rs1 and rd.
RULE 5: For a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targeting pmpaddr53, if rs1 equals x0 the instruction reads pmpaddr53 but does not write it.
RULE 6: For a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targeting pmpaddr53, if rs1 is not x0 the instruction reads pmpaddr53 and writes it, subject to the per-field side-effect rules.
RULE 7: The privilege of pmpaddr53 is MRW, allowing read and write access only in machine mode.
RULE 8: pmpaddr53 is a WARL register.
RULE 9: pmpaddr53 may contain any value that is legal for the implementation.
RULE 10: Reads of pmpaddr53 may return zero even if written with a non-zero value.
RULE 11: pmpaddr53 can be read only when the hart is executing in M-mode.
RULE 12: pmpaddr53 can be written only when the hart is executing in M-mode.
RULE 13: When a PMP setting that additionally uses the preceding address register applies to PMP entry 53, the behavior of pmpaddr53 can be directly affected by the value in pmpaddr52.
RULE 14: If the A field of PMP entry 53 is 0 (OFF), the entry is disabled and matches no addresses, and the value stored in pmpaddr53 is irrelevant for matching.
RULE 15: If the A field of PMP entry 53 is set to TOR, pmpaddr53 forms the top of the address range for entry 53.
RULE 16: In TOR mode, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr52 <= y < pmpaddr53, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg52.
RULE 17: If pmpaddr52 >= pmpaddr53 and pmpcfg53.A = TOR, then PMP entry 53 matches no addresses.
RULE 18: If the A field of PMP entry 53 is NA4, the entire contents of pmpaddr53 are used as a 4-byte NAPOT range aligned to a four-byte boundary, and the low-order bits are not interpreted for size.
RULE 19: If the A field of PMP entry 53 is NAPOT, the low-order bits of pmpaddr53 encode the size of the region according to the specified patterns.
RULE 20: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 are all 1, the NAPOT region size is 4 bytes.
RULE 21: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 end with 0, the NAPOT region size is 8 bytes.
RULE 22: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 end with 01, the NAPOT region size is 16 bytes.
RULE 23: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 end with 011, the NAPOT region size is 32 bytes.
RULE 24: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 match the pattern ...yy01...1111, the NAPOT region size is 2*XLEN bytes.
RULE 25: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 match the pattern ...y011...1111, the NAPOT region size is 2*XLEN+1 bytes.
RULE 26: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 match the pattern ...0111...1111, the NAPOT region size is 2*XLEN+2 bytes.
RULE 27: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 match the pattern ...1111...1111, the NAPOT region size is 2*XLEN+3 bytes.
RULE 28: If G >= 2 and pmpcfg53.A[1] is set (entry 53 is in NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr53[G-2:0] read as all ones regardless of their stored values.
RULE 29: If G >= 1 and pmpcfg53.A[1] is clear (entry 53 is OFF or TOR), bits pmpaddr53[G-1:0] read as all zeros and these bits do not affect TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 30: Changing pmpcfg53.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr53 but does not change the underlying value stored in the register.
RULE 31: Bit pmpaddr53[G-1] retains its original stored value when pmpcfg53.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 32: If PMP entry 53 is locked, any write to the address register pmpaddr53 is ignored.
RULE 33: When the L bit of PMP entry 53 is set, writes to the address register pmpaddr53 are ignored.
RULE 34: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 53 locks the entry and causes writes to pmpaddr53 to be ignored even if the A field of pmpcfg53 is OFF.
RULE 35: A locked PMP entry 53, and therefore its address register pmpaddr53, remains locked and write-ignored until the hart is reset.
RULE 36: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr53 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3e5; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 37: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr53 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3e5; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: pmpaddr54

WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr54 has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege.

RULE 14: If the low-order bits of pmpaddr54 match the pattern yy01…1111, then the NAPOT range size encoded by pmpaddr54 is 2 XLEN bytes.

RULE 16: If the low-order bits of pmpaddr54 match the pattern 0111…1111, then the NAPOT range size encoded by pmpaddr54 is 2 XLEN+2 bytes.
RULE 17: If the low-order bits of pmpaddr54 match the pattern 1111…1111, then the NAPOT range size encoded by pmpaddr54 is 2 XLEN+3 bytes.

RULE 19: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg54.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr54[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 20: Bits pmpaddr54[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 21: Changing pmpcfg54.A[1] (switching between NAPOT and TOR/OFF) affects the value read from pmpaddr54 but does not affect the underlying stored value, and pmpaddr54[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg54.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF then back to NAPOT.

REGISTER: pmpaddr56
NUMBER: 0x3e8
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction modifies any bit of pmpaddr56 other than bit G-1 while the stored value of pmpaddr56[G-1] is 1 and a read of pmpaddr56 returns 0, the instruction will cause 0 to be read from pmpaddr56[G-1] and then written back, updating the stored value of pmpaddr56[G-1] to 0.
RULE 2: pmpaddr56 has privilege level Machine.
RULE 3: pmpaddr56 has access type MRW, meaning it is machine-read/write.
RULE 4: On RV64 harts, pmpaddr56 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 5: pmpaddr56 is a WARL register and may be read-only zero.
RULE 6: A write to pmpaddr56 may be masked to the subset of physical address bits that are implemented.
RULE 7: When PMP entry 56 is configured in TOR address-matching mode, pmpaddr56 may serve as the upper bound address while pmpaddr55 supplies the lower bound.
RULE 8: If pmpcfg56.A = 0, pmpaddr56 defines a null region (disabled).
RULE 9: If pmpcfg56.A = 1, pmpaddr56 defines the top of a TOR address range.
RULE 10: If pmpcfg56.A = 2, pmpaddr56 defines a naturally aligned four-byte (NA4) region.
RULE 11: If pmpcfg56.A = 3, pmpaddr56 defines a naturally aligned power-of-two region of size at least eight bytes (NAPOT).
RULE 12: If pmpcfg56.A = TOR, the address range matched by pmpaddr56 includes all addresses y such that pmpaddr55 ≤ y < pmpaddr56, irrespective of pmpcfg55.A.
RULE 13: If pmpcfg56.A = TOR and pmpaddr55 ≥ pmpaddr56, the entry matches no addresses.
RULE 14: If pmpcfg56.A = NAPOT and the least-significant bits of pmpaddr56 are all ones (pattern yyyy…yyyy), the matched region is a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 15: If pmpcfg56.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr56 ends with …0 (pattern yyyy…yyy0), the matched region is an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 16: If pmpcfg56.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr56 ends with …01 (pattern yyyy…yy01), the matched region is a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 17: If pmpcfg56.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr56 ends with …011 (pattern yyyy…y011), the matched region is a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 18: If pmpcfg56.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr56 matches the pattern yy01…1111, the matched region size is 2 XLEN-byte.
RULE 19: If pmpcfg56.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr56 matches the pattern y011…1111, the matched region size is 2 XLEN+1-byte.
RULE 20: If pmpcfg56.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr56 matches the pattern 0111…1111, the matched region size is 2 XLEN+2-byte.
RULE 21: If pmpcfg56.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr56 matches the pattern 1111…1111, the matched region size is 2 XLEN+3-byte.
RULE 22: If G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg56.A[1] is set, bits pmpaddr56[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 23: If G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg56.A[1] is clear, bits pmpaddr56[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 24: Bits pmpaddr56[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 25: Changing pmpcfg56.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr56 but does not change the underlying stored value; specifically, pmpaddr56[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg56.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 26: If the L bit of PMP entry 56 is set, the PMP entry is locked even when pmpcfg56.A is set to OFF, and this lock status applies to pmpaddr56.
RULE 27: When PMP entry 56 is locked, any write to pmpaddr56 is ignored.
RULE 28: A locked PMP entry 56, including its pmpaddr56 register, remains locked until the hart is reset.
RULE 29: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr56 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3e8; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 30: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr56 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3e8; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

RULE 1: pmpaddr57 may have an underlying stored value of 1 for the bit pmpaddr57[G-1] while reads of that bit return 0.

RULE 22: If PMP entry 60 is locked, writes to pmpaddr60 are ignored.
RULE 23: The L bit of PMP entry 60 indicates that writes to pmpaddr60 are ignored.
RULE 24: Once PMP entry 60 is locked, it remains locked until the hart is reset, so pmpaddr60 stays locked.
RULE 25: Setting the L bit locks PMP entry 60 (and thus pmpaddr60) even when the A field is set to OFF.
RULE 26: When the L bit of PMP entry 60 is set, the R/W/X permissions associated with pmpaddr60 are enforced for all privilege modes.
RULE 27: When the L bit of PMP entry 60 is clear, any M-mode access matching pmpaddr60 will succeed and the R/W/X permissions apply only to S and U modes.
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr60 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3ec; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 29: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr60 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3ec; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

RULE 1: The pmpaddr61 register [G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 while a read returns 0.

REGISTER: pmpaddr62
NUMBER: 0x3ee
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr62 is a CSR whose underlying value may differ from the value read, for example the underlying value may be 1 while the CSR reads 0.
RULE 2: Any bits of pmpaddr62 that read as a different value from their underlying value may be modified by CSRRS or CSRRC instructions even if the corresponding bit is not set in rs1.

RULE 8: pmpaddr62 exists only in implementations that provide 64 PMP entries and is absent in implementations that provide 0 or 16 PMP entries.

RULE 10: If the L bit of PMP entry 62 is set, any write to pmpaddr62 MUST be ignored.

REGISTER: pmpaddr63
NUMBER: 0x3ef
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction modifies any bit of pmpaddr63 other than bit G-1, the instruction shall read pmpaddr63, and if bit G-1 reads as a value different from its underlying stored value, the instruction shall write back that read value for bit G-1, thereby updating the underlying value of bit G-1 to the read value.
RULE 2: Bit G-1 of pmpaddr63 may be stored as 1 but read as 0.
RULE 3: Any CSRRS or CSRRC instruction that targets pmpaddr63 shall read pmpaddr63 and shall cause any read side effects associated with pmpaddr63 regardless of the values in rs1 or rd.
RULE 4: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction with rs1 = x0 targets pmpaddr63, the instruction shall not write to pmpaddr63, shall not cause any write-side effects on pmpaddr63, and shall not raise an illegal-instruction exception for a read-only access to pmpaddr63.
RULE 5: For pmpaddr63, a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction with rs1 not equal to x0 shall both read pmpaddr63 and write pmpaddr63.
RULE 6: For pmpaddr63, a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction with rs1 = x0 shall read pmpaddr63 and shall not write pmpaddr63.
RULE 7: The pmpaddr63 CSR has privilege MRW (machine-read/write).
RULE 8: In RV64 systems, pmpaddr63 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 9: pmpaddr63 is a WARL field and may be read-only zero.
RULE 10: pmpaddr63 may be accessed (read or written) only while executing in M-mode.
RULE 11: If pmpcfg63.A = OFF, pmpaddr63 defines a null (disabled) region.
RULE 12: If pmpcfg63.A = TOR, pmpaddr63 forms the top address of the range, with pmpaddr62 as the bottom address.

RULE 14: If pmpcfg63.A = TOR and the entry is the first PMP entry, then zero is used as the lower bound and the entry matches any address y < pmpaddr63.
RULE 15: If pmpaddr62 ≥ pmpaddr63 and pmpcfg63.A = TOR, then the entry using pmpaddr63 matches no addresses.
RULE 16: pmpaddr63 MUST NOT be used to represent the address 2^XLEN+2 as the top of a TOR range, and therefore a TOR entry using pmpaddr63 cannot grant access to the uppermost word of memory.
RULE 17: If pmpcfg63.A = NA4, pmpaddr63 specifies a 4-byte NAPOT range.

RULE 19: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 end with 01, then pmpaddr63 encodes a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 20: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 end with 011, then pmpaddr63 encodes a 32-byte NAPOT range.

RULE 22: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 match the pattern y011…1111, then pmpaddr63 encodes a 2 XLEN+1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 23: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 match the pattern 0111…1111, then pmpaddr63 encodes a 2 XLEN+2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 24: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 match the pattern 1111…1111, then pmpaddr63 encodes a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 25: When G ≥ 1, pmpaddr63 MUST NOT be used in NA4 mode.
RULE 26: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg63.A[1] = 1 (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr63[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 27: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg63.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr63[G-1:0] read as all zeros.

RULE 31: Once the L bit of PMP entry 63 is set, the lock remains in effect until a hart reset, causing writes to pmpaddr63 to continue to be ignored.
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr63 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3ef; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

RULE 15: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr9 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3b9; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

RULE 17: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr9 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3b9; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 18: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr9.ADDR (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3b9, a0; csrr a1, 0x3b9; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].

RULE 20: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr9 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3b9; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpcfg0
NUMBER: 0x3a0
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 7..0=pmp0cfg, 15..8=pmp1cfg, 23..16=pmp2cfg, 31..24=pmp3cfg, 39..32=pmp4cfg, 47..40=pmp5cfg, 55..48=pmp6cfg, 63..56=pmp7cfg
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp, Smmpm, Zicfilp, Zkr
RULE 1: The pmpcfg0 CSR has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: When mseccfg.RLB is 0 and pmpcfg0.L is 1 in any rule or entry, including disabled entries, mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and any further modifications to mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.
RULE 3: When mseccfg.MML is set, a pmpcfg0.L bit set marks the rule as M-mode-only and a pmpcfg0.L bit clear marks the rule as S/U-mode-only.
RULE 4: When mseccfg.MML is set, the encoding pmpcfg0.RW=01 is no longer reserved but encodes a Shared-Region.
RULE 5: When mseccfg.MML is set, the encoding pmpcfg0.LRWX=1111 encodes a Shared-Region.
RULE 6: A Shared-Region rule is enforced on all modes and, if pmpcfg0.L is clear, the rule is not executable, M-mode has read/write access, and S/U-mode has read access when pmpcfg0.X is clear or read/write access when pmpcfg0.X is set.
RULE 7: A Shared-Region rule is enforced on all modes and, if pmpcfg0.L is set, the rule is not writable, both M-mode and S/U-mode have execute access, and M-mode also has read access when pmpcfg0.X is set.
RULE 8: A Shared-Region rule with pmpcfg0.LRWX=1111 allows sharing data between M-mode and S/U-mode where both modes have only read-only access.
RULE 9: An M-mode-only rule, identified by pmpcfg0.L set when mseccfg.MML is set, is enforced on Machine mode, denied in Supervisor and User modes, and remains locked so that any further modifications to its configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 10: A locked Shared-Region rule, identified by pmpcfg0.L set, also remains locked so that further modifications to its configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 11: When mseccfg.MML is set, attempts to write pmpcfg0 with executable privileges that would create an M-mode-only rule or a locked Shared-Region rule are ignored, leaving pmpcfg0 unchanged.
RULE 12: When mseccfg.MML is set, the restriction on writing executable pmpcfg0 entries can be temporarily lifted by setting mseccfg.RLB.
RULE 13: Executing code with Machine mode privileges is permitted only from memory regions covered by a matching M-mode-only rule or a locked Shared-Region rule with executable privileges as encoded in pmpcfg0; execution from a region without such a rule or covered only by a matching S/U-mode-only rule is denied.
RULE 14: When mseccfg.MML is not set, the combination pmpcfg0.RW=01 remains reserved for future standard use.
RULE 15: In RV64 implementations, any odd-numbered PMP configuration CSR other than pmpcfg0 (e.g., pmpcfg1, pmpcfg3, …, pmpcfg15) is illegal.
RULE 16: Any read or write of pmpcfg0 MUST be performed in M-mode; accesses from lower privilege modes are NOT permitted.
RULE 17: Each field within pmpcfg0 (R, W, X, A, L) is a WARL field and may read back as zero even if a different value was written.
RULE 18: In pmpcfg0, the R, W, and X bits, when set, indicate that the PMP entry permits read, write, and instruction execution, respectively.
RULE 19: In pmpcfg0, when any of the R, W, or X bits is clear, the corresponding access type is denied.
RULE 20: In pmpcfg0, the R, W, and X bits together form a collective WARL field for which the combination R = 0 and W = 1 is reserved.
RULE 21: If the X bit in pmpcfg0 for a PMP entry is clear, attempting to fetch an instruction from the corresponding region raises an instruction access-fault exception.
RULE 22: If the R bit in pmpcfg0 for a PMP entry is clear, attempting to execute a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction that accesses a physical address within the region raises a load access-fault exception.
RULE 23: If the W bit in pmpcfg0 for a PMP entry is clear, attempting to execute a store, store-conditional, AMO, or cache-block zero instruction that accesses a physical address within the region raises a store access-fault exception.
RULE 24: In pmpcfg0, an A field value of 0 (OFF) encodes a null region that is disabled.
RULE 25: In pmpcfg0, an A field value of 1 (TOR) encodes the top-of-range address-matching mode.
RULE 26: In pmpcfg0, an A field value of 2 (NA4) encodes the naturally aligned four-byte region mode.
RULE 27: In pmpcfg0, an A field value of 3 (NAPOT) encodes the naturally aligned power-of-two region mode of size at least eight bytes.
RULE 28: If the A field of pmpcfg0 is set to TOR, the lower bound of the range is zero and the entry matches any address y such that y < pmpaddr0.
RULE 29: When the A field of pmpcfg0 is set to TOR, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr(i-1) ≤ y < pmpaddr0, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg(i-1).
RULE 30: If pmpaddr(i-1) ≥ pmpaddr0 and the A field of pmpcfg0 is TOR, then the entry matches no addresses.
RULE 31: When the PMP granularity G is greater than or equal to 1, the NA4 mode (A = 2) is not selectable in pmpcfg0.
RULE 32: When G ≥ 2 and bit 1 of the A field in pmpcfg0 is set (indicating NAPOT mode), the bits pmpaddr0[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 33: When G ≥ 1 and bit 1 of the A field in pmpcfg0 is clear (indicating OFF or TOR mode), the bits pmpaddr0[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 34: Bits pmpaddr0[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic of pmpcfg0.
RULE 35: Changing bit 1 of the A field in pmpcfg0 changes the value read from pmpaddr0 but does not change the underlying stored bits of pmpaddr0; specifically, pmpaddr0[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg0.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 36: Software can discover the PMP granularity by writing zero to pmpcfg0, writing all ones to pmpaddr0, reading back pmpaddr0, and interpreting the index of the least-significant set bit G as a granularity of 2 G + 2 bytes.
RULE 37: If pmpcfg0.A is NA4 and the pattern of pmpaddr0 is all ones, the matched region is a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 38: If pmpcfg0.A is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr0 end with 0 (pattern yyyy…yyy0), the matched region is an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 39: If pmpcfg0.A is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr0 end with 01 (pattern yyyy…yy01), the matched region is a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 40: If pmpcfg0.A is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr0 end with 011 (pattern yyyy…y011), the matched region is a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 41: If pmpcfg0.A is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr0 follow the pattern yy01…1111, the matched region size is 2 × XLEN bytes.
RULE 42: If pmpcfg0.A is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr0 follow the pattern y011…1111, the matched region size is 2 × XLEN + 1 bytes.
RULE 43: If pmpcfg0.A is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr0 follow the pattern 0111…1111, the matched region size is 2 × XLEN + 2 bytes.
RULE 44: If pmpcfg0.A is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr0 follow the pattern 1111…1111, the matched region size is 2 × XLEN + 3 bytes.
RULE 45: A PMP rule defined by pmpcfg0 is valid only when pmpcfg0.A is not OFF.
RULE 46: If pmpcfg0.A is TOR, then pmpaddr[i-1] must be less than pmpaddr0.
RULE 47: When pmpcfg0.L equals 1, the PMP entry defined by pmpcfg0 and pmpaddr0 is locked.
RULE 48: When a PMP rule defined by pmpcfg0 matches an address range, the permissions encoded in pmpcfg0 are ignored and all accesses to that range are allowed.
RULE 49: When a PMP rule defined by pmpcfg0 matches an address range, only the access types specified by pmpcfg0 are allowed and any disallowed access causes an access-fault exception.
RULE 50: When a PMP rule defined by pmpcfg0 matches an address range and is denied, all accesses to that range are prohibited and any attempted access causes an access-fault exception.
RULE 51: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception indicating an inaccessible region.
RULE 52: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception indicating an inaccessible region.
RULE 53: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception.
RULE 54: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses are treated as an Execute-only region.
RULE 55: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses constitute a shared data region with read/write permission, while S/U-Mode accesses are read-only.
RULE 56: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses are read-only in the shared data region described for pmpcfg0.
RULE 57: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses are a shared data region with read/write permission for both M-Mode and S/U-Mode.
RULE 58: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses are a shared data region with read/write permission for both M-Mode and S/U-Mode.
RULE 59: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception.
RULE 60: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses are treated as a read-only region.
RULE 61: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception.
RULE 62: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses are a read/execute region.
RULE 63: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception.
RULE 64: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses are a read/write region.

RULE 67: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception for a locked inaccessible region*.
RULE 68: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception for a locked inaccessible region*.

RULE 74: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses are a locked shared code region that executes only on S/U-Mode and provides read/execute permission on M-Mode*.

RULE 76: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception.
RULE 77: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses are a locked read/execute region*.
RULE 78: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception.
RULE 79: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses are a locked read/write region*.
RULE 80: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception.
RULE 81: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses are a locked shared data region that is read-only for both M-Mode and S/U-Mode*.

REGISTER: pmpcfg10
NUMBER: 0x3aa
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 7..0=pmp40cfg, 15..8=pmp41cfg, 23..16=pmp42cfg, 31..24=pmp43cfg, 39..32=pmp44cfg, 47..40=pmp45cfg, 55..48=pmp46cfg, 63..56=pmp47cfg
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: If mseccfg.RLB=0 and pmpcfg10.L=1, then mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and any further modifications to mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.
RULE 2: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.L=1 (M-mode-only rule), then the rule is enforced in Machine mode and denied in Supervisor and User modes.
RULE 3: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.L=1 (M-mode-only rule), then the rule remains locked so that any further modifications to its associated configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 4: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.L=0 (S/U-mode-only rule), then the rule is enforced in Supervisor and User modes and denied in Machine mode.
RULE 5: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.RW=01 defines a Shared-Region and pmpcfg10.L=0, then the region is not executable.
RULE 6: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.RW=01 defines a Shared-Region and pmpcfg10.L=0, then Machine mode has read/write access to the region.
RULE 7: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.RW=01 defines a Shared-Region and pmpcfg10.L=0 and pmpcfg10.X=0, then Supervisor and User modes have read-only access to the region.
RULE 8: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.RW=01 defines a Shared-Region and pmpcfg10.L=0 and pmpcfg10.X=1, then Supervisor and User modes have read/write access to the region.
RULE 9: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.RW=01 defines a Shared-Region and pmpcfg10.L=1, then the region is not writable.
RULE 10: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.RW=01 defines a Shared-Region and pmpcfg10.L=1, then both Machine mode and Supervisor/User modes have execute access to the region.
RULE 11: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.RW=01 defines a Shared-Region and pmpcfg10.L=1 and pmpcfg10.X=1, then Machine mode also has read access to the region.
RULE 12: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.RW=01 defines a Shared-Region and pmpcfg10.L=1, then the rule remains locked so that any further modifications to its associated configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 13: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.LRWX=1111, then both Machine mode and Supervisor/User modes have read-only access to the region.
RULE 14: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.LRWX=1111, then the rule remains locked so that any further modifications to its associated configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 15: If a pmpcfg10 write attempts to add a rule with executable privileges that would be M-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region, then the write is ignored and pmpcfg10 remains unchanged.
RULE 16: Execution of code with Machine mode privileges is permitted only from regions that have an M-mode-only rule or a locked Shared-Region rule with executable privileges as encoded in pmpcfg10; execution from regions without such a matching rule or with a matching S/U-mode-only rule is denied.
RULE 17: If mseccfg.MML is not set, then pmpcfg10.RW=01 remains reserved for future standard use.
RULE 18: Every field within pmpcfg10 is a WARL field and may read as zero regardless of the implemented value.
RULE 19: Only M-mode may read or write pmpcfg10; attempts from U, S, or HS modes are not permitted.
RULE 20: In pmpcfg10 the R bit, when set, permits read accesses to the PMP entries it configures, and when clear, read accesses are denied.
RULE 21: In pmpcfg10 the W bit, when set, permits write accesses to the PMP entries it configures, and when clear, write accesses are denied.
RULE 22: In pmpcfg10 the X bit, when set, permits instruction-fetch (execute) accesses to the PMP entries it configures, and when clear, execute accesses are denied.
RULE 23: The R, W, and X fields of pmpcfg10 together form a WARL field for which the combination R=0 and W=1 is reserved and must not be used.
RULE 24: If the X bit in pmpcfg10 does not permit execute permission for a PMP region, an instruction fetch from that region raises an instruction access-fault exception.
RULE 25: If the R bit in pmpcfg10 does not permit read permission for a PMP region, a load that accesses an address in that region raises a load access-fault exception.
RULE 26: If the W bit in pmpcfg10 does not permit write permission for a PMP region, a store that accesses an address in that region raises a store access-fault exception.
RULE 27: If pmpcfg10.A = 0, then the PMP entry is disabled and matches no addresses.
RULE 28: If pmpcfg10.A = 1 (TOR), then the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr9 ≤ y < pmpaddr10, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg9.
RULE 29: If pmpcfg10.A = 1 and pmpaddr9 ≥ pmpaddr10, then the entry matches no addresses.
RULE 30: If G ≥ 1, then the NA4 encoding (value 2) is not selectable for pmpcfg10.A.
RULE 31: If G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg10.A[1] = 1 (indicating NAPOT mode), then bits pmpaddr10[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 32: If G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg10.A[1] = 0 (indicating OFF or TOR mode), then bits pmpaddr10[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 33: The bits pmpaddr10[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic for pmpcfg10.
RULE 34: Changing pmpcfg10.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr10 but does not modify the underlying stored bits of pmpaddr10, and the stored bit pmpaddr10[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg10.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 35: If the L bit in pmpcfg10 is set, then the PMP Entry formed with pmpaddr10 is a Locked entry.
RULE 36: A PMP Rule that uses pmpcfg10 is considered valid only when the address-matching field pmpcfg10.A is not equal to OFF.
RULE 37: When the address-matching field pmpcfg10.A is set to TOR, the address ordering requirement pmpaddr9 < pmpaddr10 must be satisfied for the PMP Rule to be valid.
RULE 38: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg10 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3aa; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 39: In S-mode, accessing pmpcfg10 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3aa; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
