REGISTER: pmpcfg12
NUMBER: 0x3ac
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 7..0=pmp48cfg, 15..8=pmp49cfg, 23..16=pmp50cfg, 31..24=pmp51cfg, 39..32=pmp52cfg, 47..40=pmp53cfg, 55..48=pmp54cfg, 63..56=pmp55cfg
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: If the MSECCFG.MML bit is set, then a pmpcfg12 entry whose L bit is 1 causes the corresponding PMP rule to be interpreted as Machine-mode-only.
RULE 2: If the MSECCFG.MML bit is set, then a pmpcfg12 entry whose L bit is 0 causes the corresponding PMP rule to be interpreted as Supervisor/User-mode-only.
RULE 3: When the MSECCFG.MML bit is set, a pmpcfg12 encoding with the RW field equal to 01 and the LRWX field equal to 1111 denotes a Shared-Region rule.
RULE 4: When the MSECCFG.MML bit is clear, a pmpcfg12 entry with the RW field equal to 01 is reserved for future standard use.
RULE 5: When the MSECCFG.MML bit is set, a write to pmpcfg12 that would create a rule with executable privileges and that is either Machine-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region must be ignored, leaving the entire pmpcfg register, including pmpcfg12, unchanged.
RULE 6: If the MSECCFG.MML bit is set and the MSECCFG.RLB bit is set, then writes to pmpcfg12 that would create a rule with executable privileges and that is either Machine-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region are permitted and are not ignored.
RULE 7: When the MSECCFG.MML bit is set, Machine-mode execution is permitted only from memory regions whose pmpcfg12 entries define a matching Machine-mode-only rule or a locked Shared-Region rule with executable privileges; execution from regions without such a matching rule or with a matching Supervisor/User-mode-only rule is denied.
RULE 8: If MSECCFG.RLB is 0 and any pmpcfg12 entry has its L bit set to 1, then MSECCFG.RLB remains 0 and any further writes to MSECCFG.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.
RULE 9: All PMP CSR fields are WARL and may be read-only zero, and this applies to every field contained in pmpcfg12.
RULE 10: pmpcfg12 can be read or written only when the processor is executing in M-mode.
RULE 11: In pmpcfg12, the R, W, and X bits, when set, indicate that the PMP entry permits read, write, and instruction execution, respectively.
RULE 12: In pmpcfg12, a clear R, W, or X bit denies the corresponding read, write, or execute access type.
RULE 13: The R, W, and X fields in pmpcfg12 constitute a collective WARL field that reserves any combination where R = 0 and W = 1.
RULE 14: If an entry in pmpcfg12 has X = 0, an instruction fetch from the corresponding region must raise an instruction access-fault exception.
RULE 15: If an entry in pmpcfg12 has R = 0, a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction accessing that region must raise a load access-fault exception.
RULE 16: If an entry in pmpcfg12 has W = 0, a store, store-conditional, AMO, or cache-block zero instruction accessing that region must raise a store access-fault exception.
RULE 17: pmpcfg12.A = 0 selects the OFF null region (disabled).
RULE 18: pmpcfg12.A = 1 selects the TOR top-of-range address-matching mode.
RULE 19: pmpcfg12.A = 2 selects the NA4 naturally aligned four-byte region mode.
RULE 20: pmpcfg12.A = 3 selects the NAPOT naturally aligned power-of-two region mode of size at least eight bytes.
RULE 21: When pmpcfg12.A encodes NA4, a pmpaddr12 pattern of all ones (yyyy…yyyy) defines a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 22: When pmpcfg12.A encodes NAPOT and pmpaddr12 ends with a zero (yyyy…yyy0), the region size is 8 bytes.
RULE 23: When pmpcfg12.A encodes NAPOT and pmpaddr12 ends with the bits 01 (yyyy…yy01), the region size is 16 bytes.
RULE 24: When pmpcfg12.A encodes NAPOT and pmpaddr12 ends with the bits 011 (yyyy…y011), the region size is 32 bytes.
RULE 25: When pmpcfg12.A encodes NAPOT and pmpaddr12 matches the pattern yy01…1111, the region size is 2 × XLEN bytes.
RULE 26: When pmpcfg12.A encodes NAPOT and pmpaddr12 matches the pattern y011…1111, the region size is 2 × XLEN + 1 bytes.
RULE 27: When pmpcfg12.A encodes NAPOT and pmpaddr12 matches the pattern 0111…1111, the region size is 2 × XLEN + 2 bytes.
RULE 28: When pmpcfg12.A encodes NAPOT and pmpaddr12 matches the pattern 1111…1111, the region size is 2 × XLEN + 3 bytes.
RULE 29: pmpcfg12.A MUST NOT be set to 2 when the PMP granularity G is greater than or equal to 1.
RULE 30: If G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg12.A[1] = 1 (NAPOT mode), then reads of pmpaddr12 return ones in bits [G-2:0].
RULE 31: If G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg12.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), then reads of pmpaddr12 return zeros in bits [G-1:0].
RULE 32: The bits pmpaddr12[G-1:0] do not affect address matching when pmpcfg12.A selects TOR.
RULE 33: Writing pmpcfg12.A[1] to change between NAPOT and OFF/TOR does not modify the stored value of pmpaddr12[G-1]; only the masked read value changes.
RULE 34: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg12 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3ac; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 35: In S-mode, accessing pmpcfg12 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3ac; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 36: In U-mode, accessing pmpcfg12 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3ac; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 37: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg12.pmp48cfg (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3ac, a0; csrr a1, 0x3ac; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 38: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg12.pmp49cfg (bit 8) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x100; csrs 0x3ac, a0; csrr a1, 0x3ac; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 39: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg12.pmp50cfg (bit 16) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x10000; csrs 0x3ac, a0; csrr a1, 0x3ac; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 40: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg12.pmp51cfg (bit 24) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1000000; csrs 0x3ac, a0; csrr a1, 0x3ac; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpcfg14
NUMBER: 0x3ae
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 7..0=pmp56cfg, 15..8=pmp57cfg, 23..16=pmp58cfg, 31..24=pmp59cfg, 39..32=pmp60cfg, 47..40=pmp61cfg, 55..48=pmp62cfg, 63..56=pmp63cfg
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpcfg14 has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: When mseccfg.MML is set, the pmpcfg14.L field marks a rule as M-mode-only if the bit is 1 and as S/U-mode-only if the bit is 0.
RULE 3: When mseccfg.MML is set, a pmpcfg14.RW value of 01 encodes a Shared-Region rule.
RULE 4: When mseccfg.MML is set, a pmpcfg14.LRWX value of 1111 encodes a Shared-Region rule.
RULE 5: A write to pmpcfg14 that attempts to add a rule with executable privileges which is either M-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region is ignored and leaves pmpcfg14 unchanged.
RULE 6: The restriction on adding executable-privilege M-mode-only or locked Shared-Region rules to pmpcfg14 is temporarily lifted when mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 7: Executing code with Machine-mode privileges is permitted only from memory regions that have a matching pmpcfg14 entry that is M-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region with executable privileges.
RULE 8: Executing code with Machine-mode privileges from a memory region that lacks a matching pmpcfg14 entry or that matches a pmpcfg14 entry that is S/U-mode-only is denied.
RULE 9: When mseccfg.MML is not set, a pmpcfg14.RW value of 01 remains reserved for future standard use.
RULE 10: When mseccfg.RLB is 1, locked PMP rules, including those defined in pmpcfg14, may be removed or modified.
RULE 11: When mseccfg.RLB is 0 and any pmpcfg14.L bit is 1 (including in disabled entries), mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and any further attempts to modify mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.
RULE 12: All fields within pmpcfg14 are WARL and may be read-only zero.
RULE 13: pmpcfg14 is accessible only in M-mode.
RULE 14: Each 8-bit configuration field in pmpcfg14 contains an R bit that, when set, indicates the PMP entry permits read accesses and, when clear, denies read accesses.
RULE 15: Each 8-bit configuration field in pmpcfg14 contains a W bit that, when set, indicates the PMP entry permits write accesses and, when clear, denies write accesses.
RULE 16: Each 8-bit configuration field in pmpcfg14 contains an X bit that, when set, indicates the PMP entry permits instruction execution and, when clear, denies execution.
RULE 17: In pmpcfg14, the combination of R = 0 and W = 1 in a configuration field is reserved.
RULE 18: If an instruction fetch accesses a physical address within a PMP region whose configuration in pmpcfg14 has the X bit clear, an instruction access-fault exception is raised.
RULE 19: If a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction accesses a physical address within a PMP region whose configuration in pmpcfg14 has the R bit clear, a load access-fault exception is raised.
RULE 20: If a store, store-conditional, AMO, or cache-block zero instruction accesses a physical address within a PMP region whose configuration in pmpcfg14 has the W bit clear, a store access-fault exception is raised.
RULE 21: In pmpcfg14, A=0 selects the OFF mode which disables the entry and causes it to match no addresses.
RULE 22: In pmpcfg14, A=1 selects the TOR mode, causing pmpaddr14 to serve as the top of the address range and pmpaddr13 to serve as the bottom of the address range.
RULE 23: When pmpcfg14.A = TOR, the entry matches any address y that satisfies pmpaddr13 ≤ y < pmpaddr14 regardless of the value of pmpcfg13.
RULE 24: If pmpaddr13 ≥ pmpaddr14 and pmpcfg14.A = TOR, then entry 14 matches no addresses.
RULE 25: In pmpcfg14, A=2 selects the NA4 mode, causing the entry to match a naturally aligned four-byte region.
RULE 26: In pmpcfg14, A=3 selects the NAPOT mode, and the low-order bits of pmpaddr14 encode the size of the matched region according to the NAPOT pattern table.
RULE 27: When the granularity G is greater than or equal to 1, pmpcfg14.A must not be 2, so the NA4 mode is not selectable.
RULE 28: When G ≥ 2 and the high bit of pmpcfg14.A (pmpcfg14.A[1]) is set, bits pmpaddr14[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 29: When G ≥ 1 and the high bit of pmpcfg14.A (pmpcfg14.A[1]) is clear, bits pmpaddr14[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 30: Bits pmpaddr14[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic of pmpcfg14.
RULE 31: Changing pmpcfg14.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr14 but does not modify the underlying stored value of pmpaddr14.
RULE 32: When pmpcfg14.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT, the bit pmpaddr14[G-1] retains its original stored value.
RULE 33: The granularity G, obtained by writing zero to pmp0cfg, writing all ones to pmpaddr0, and reading back pmpaddr0, directly governs the granularity constraints that apply to pmpcfg14.
RULE 34: When pmpcfg14.L=0, R=0, W=0, X=0 and mseccfg.MML=1, the region is inaccessible and causes an Access Exception in both MMode and S/U Mode.
RULE 35: When pmpcfg14.L=0, R=0, W=0, X=1 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode generates an Access Exception while S/U Mode treats the region as execute-only.
RULE 36: When pmpcfg14.L=0, R=0, W=1, X=0 and mseccfg.MML=1, both MMode and S/U Mode see a shared data region with read/write permission in MMode and read-only permission in S/U Mode.
RULE 37: When pmpcfg14.L=0, R=0, W=1, X=1 and mseccfg.MML=1, both MMode and S/U Mode see a shared data region with read/write permission for both modes.
RULE 38: When pmpcfg14.L=0, R=1, W=0, X=0 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode generates an Access Exception while S/U Mode sees a read-only region.
RULE 39: When pmpcfg14.L=0, R=1, W=0, X=1 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode generates an Access Exception while S/U Mode sees a read/execute region.
RULE 40: When pmpcfg14.L=0, R=1, W=1, X=0 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode generates an Access Exception while S/U Mode sees a read/write region.
RULE 41: When pmpcfg14.L=0, R=1, W=1, X=1 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode generates an Access Exception while S/U Mode sees a read/write/execute region.
RULE 42: When pmpcfg14.L=1, R=0, W=0, X=0 and mseccfg.MML=1, both MMode and S/U Mode treat the region as a locked inaccessible region* and cause an Access Exception.
RULE 43: When pmpcfg14.L=1, R=0, W=0, X=1 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode sees a locked execute-only region* while S/U Mode generates an Access Exception.
RULE 44: When pmpcfg14.L=1, R=0, W=1, X=0 and mseccfg.MML=1, both MMode and S/U Mode see a locked shared code region that is execute-only for both modes*.
RULE 45: When pmpcfg14.L=1, R=0, W=1, X=1 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode sees a locked shared code region that is read/execute*, while S/U Mode sees the same region as execute-only*.
RULE 46: When pmpcfg14.L=1, R=1, W=0, X=0 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode sees a locked read-only region* while S/U Mode generates an Access Exception.
RULE 47: When pmpcfg14.L=1, R=1, W=0, X=1 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode sees a locked read/execute region* while S/U Mode generates an Access Exception.
RULE 48: When pmpcfg14.L=1, R=1, W=1, X=0 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode sees a locked read/write region* while S/U Mode generates an Access Exception.
RULE 49: When pmpcfg14.L=1, R=1, W=1, X=1 and mseccfg.MML=1, both MMode and S/U Mode see a locked shared data region that is read-only for both modes*.
RULE 50: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg14 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3ae; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 51: In S-mode, accessing pmpcfg14 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3ae; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 52: In U-mode, accessing pmpcfg14 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3ae; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 53: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg14.pmp56cfg (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3ae, a0; csrr a1, 0x3ae; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpcfg2
NUMBER: 0x3a2
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 7..0=pmp8cfg, 15..8=pmp9cfg, 23..16=pmp10cfg, 31..24=pmp11cfg, 39..32=pmp12cfg, 47..40=pmp13cfg, 55..48=pmp14cfg, 63..56=pmp15cfg
EXTENSIONS: H, Smepmp, Smmpm, Zicfilp, Zkr
RULE 1: The pmpcfg2 CSR is accessible in machine mode with read/write privileges (MRW).
RULE 2: When mseccfg.RLB is 0 and a pmpcfg2 entry has its L bit set, then mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and any further writes to mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.
RULE 3: When mseccfg.MML is set, the L bit in each pmpcfg2 entry indicates an M-mode-only rule if the bit is 1 and a S/U-mode-only rule if the bit is 0.
RULE 4: When mseccfg.MML is set, a pmpcfg2 entry with the RW field equal to 01 or with the LRWX field equal to 1111 encodes a Shared-Region rule.
RULE 5: When mseccfg.MML is set and a pmpcfg2 entry is an M-mode-only rule (L=1), the rule is enforced in Machine mode, denied in Supervisor and User modes, and remains locked against further configuration or address-register modifications until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 6: When mseccfg.MML is set and a pmpcfg2 entry is a S/U-mode-only rule (L=0), the rule is enforced in Supervisor and User modes and denied in Machine mode.
RULE 7: When mseccfg.MML is set and a pmpcfg2 entry encodes a Shared-Region with L=0, the rule is non-executable, grants M-mode read/write access, and grants S/U-mode read access unless the X bit is set, in which case it grants S/U-mode read/write access.
RULE 8: When mseccfg.MML is set and a pmpcfg2 entry encodes a Shared-Region with L=1, the rule provides execute access to both Machine and S/U modes, is not writable, grants M-mode read access if the X bit is set, and remains locked against further configuration or address-register modifications until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 9: When mseccfg.MML is set and a pmpcfg2 entry encodes a Shared-Region with LRWX=1111, the rule provides read-only access to both Machine and S/U modes and remains locked against further configuration or address-register modifications until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 10: When a pmpcfg2 write attempts to create a rule that grants executable privileges to an M-mode-only rule or to a locked Shared-Region, the write is ignored and the pmpcfg2 entry remains unchanged unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 11: Execution of Machine-mode code from a memory region is permitted only if the corresponding pmpcfg2 entry is an M-mode-only rule or a locked Shared-Region rule that includes executable privileges; otherwise execution is denied.
RULE 12: When mseccfg.MML is clear, a pmpcfg2 entry with the RW field equal to 01 is reserved for future standard use.
RULE 13: In RV64, the CSR pmpcfg2 is legal while the odd-numbered configuration registers such as pmpcfg1 are illegal.
RULE 14: RV64 harts use the CSR pmpcfg2, instead of pmpcfg1, to hold the configurations for PMP entries 8 through 15.
RULE 15: All fields within the CSR pmpcfg2 are WARL (Write-Any-Read-Legal) and may be read-only zero.
RULE 16: The CSR pmpcfg2 is accessible only in M-mode.
RULE 17: In each 8-bit field of pmpcfg2, setting the R bit indicates that the corresponding PMP entry permits read accesses, setting the W bit indicates write permission, and setting the X bit indicates instruction execution permission.
RULE 18: If any of the R, W, or X bits in a given 8-bit field of pmpcfg2 is clear, the corresponding access type (read, write, or execute) is denied for that PMP entry.
RULE 19: The R, W, and X bits together constitute a collective WARL field in each 8-bit subfield of pmpcfg2, and the combination where R=0 and W=1 is reserved.
RULE 20: If the X bit in the relevant pmpcfg2 field denies execute permission for a PMP region, an instruction fetch from that region raises an instruction access-fault exception.
RULE 21: If the R bit in the relevant pmpcfg2 field denies read permission for a PMP region, executing a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction that accesses a physical address in that region raises a load access-fault exception.
RULE 22: If the W bit in the relevant pmpcfg2 field denies write permission for a PMP region, executing a store, store-conditional, AMO, or cache-block zero instruction that accesses a physical address in that region raises a store access-fault exception.
RULE 23: In pmpcfg2, A = 0 selects the OFF mode, which disables the entry and matches no addresses.
RULE 24: In pmpcfg2, A = 1 selects the TOR mode, which defines a top-of-range address region.
RULE 25: In pmpcfg2, A = 2 selects the NA4 mode, which defines a naturally aligned four-byte region.
RULE 26: In pmpcfg2, A = 3 selects the NAPOT mode, which defines a naturally aligned power-of-two region of at least eight bytes.
RULE 27: When pmpcfg2 entry i is in TOR mode, the associated address register forms the top of the address range and the preceding PMP address register forms the bottom of the address range.
RULE 28: If pmpcfg2 entry i has A = TOR, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr(i-1) ≤ y < pmpaddr(i), irrespective of the value of pmpcfg(i-1).
RULE 29: If pmpcfg2 entry 0 has A = TOR, the lower bound is zero, so the entry matches any address y < pmpaddr0.
RULE 30: If pmpaddr(i-1) ≥ pmpaddr(i) and pmpcfg2 entry i has A = TOR, then entry i matches no addresses.
RULE 31: In NAPOT mode (A = 3) of pmpcfg2, the low-order bits of the associated address register encode the region size.
RULE 32: In NA4 mode (A = 2) of pmpcfg2, the associated address register defines a naturally aligned four-byte region.
RULE 33: When the PMP granularity G is greater than or equal to 1, the NA4 mode is not selectable in pmpcfg2.
RULE 34: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg2's A[1] bit is set (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr[i][G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 35: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg2's A[1] bit is clear (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr[i][G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 36: Bits pmpaddr[i][G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic for entries configured via pmpcfg2.
RULE 37: Changing pmpcfg2's A[1] bit alters the value read from the corresponding pmpaddr register but does not alter the underlying stored value of that register.
RULE 38: The bit pmpaddr[i][G-1] retains its original stored value when pmpcfg2's A field is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 39: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg2 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3a2; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 40: In S-mode, accessing pmpcfg2 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3a2; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 41: In U-mode, accessing pmpcfg2 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3a2; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 42: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg2.pmp8cfg (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3a2, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a2; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].

RULE 45: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg2.pmp11cfg (bit 24) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1000000; csrs 0x3a2, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a2; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1000000].

REGISTER: pmpcfg4
NUMBER: 0x3a4
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 7..0=pmp16cfg, 15..8=pmp17cfg, 23..16=pmp18cfg, 31..24=pmp19cfg, 39..32=pmp20cfg, 47..40=pmp21cfg, 55..48=pmp22cfg, 63..56=pmp23cfg
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: When mseccfg.RLB is 0 and pmpcfg4.L is 1, mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and any further modifications to mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.
RULE 2: When mseccfg.MML is set, pmpcfg4.L marks a rule as M-mode-only when set and as S/U-mode-only when unset.
RULE 3: When mseccfg.MML is set, the encoding pmpcfg4.RW=01 and the encoding pmpcfg4.LRWX=1111 denote a Shared-Region.
RULE 4: An M-mode-only rule defined by pmpcfg4 is enforced in Machine mode and denied in Supervisor and User modes.
RULE 5: An M-mode-only rule defined by pmpcfg4 remains locked so that any further modifications to its associated configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 6: An S/U-mode-only rule defined by pmpcfg4 is enforced in Supervisor and User modes and denied in Machine mode.
RULE 7: A Shared-Region rule defined by pmpcfg4 where pmpcfg4.L is not set is not executable, grants Machine mode read/write access, and grants Supervisor/User mode read access if pmpcfg4.X is not set or read/write access if pmpcfg4.X is set.
RULE 8: A Shared-Region rule defined by pmpcfg4 where pmpcfg4.L is set is not writable, grants execute access to both Machine and Supervisor/User modes, and grants Machine mode read access if pmpcfg4.X is set; the rule remains locked so that any further modifications to its associated configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 9: A Shared-Region rule defined by pmpcfg4 with encoding pmpcfg4.LRWX=1111 provides read-only access to both Machine and Supervisor/User modes and remains locked so that any further modifications to its associated configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 10: Writes to pmpcfg4 that would create a rule with executable privileges and that is either M-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region are ignored, leaving pmpcfg4 unchanged; this restriction can be temporarily lifted by setting mseccfg.RLB.
RULE 11: Execution of code with Machine mode privileges is permitted only from regions for which pmpcfg4 defines a matching M-mode-only rule or a locked Shared-Region rule with executable privileges, and is denied from regions without such a matching rule or with a matching S/U-mode-only rule.
RULE 12: If mseccfg.MML is not set, the encoding pmpcfg4.RW=01 remains reserved for future standard use.
RULE 13: Reads and writes to pmpcfg4 are permitted only when the hart is executing in M-mode.
RULE 14: Each field inside pmpcfg4 is a WARL field and may read as zero regardless of the value written.
RULE 15: Each 8-bit configuration entry stored in pmpcfg4 contains an R bit that, when set, indicates the PMP entry permits read accesses.
RULE 16: Each 8-bit configuration entry stored in pmpcfg4 contains a W bit that, when set, indicates the PMP entry permits write accesses.
RULE 17: Each 8-bit configuration entry stored in pmpcfg4 contains an X bit that, when set, indicates the PMP entry permits instruction-execute accesses.
RULE 18: The R, W, and X bits of each entry in pmpcfg4 together form a collective WARL field.
RULE 19: The combination of R=0 and W=1 in the R, W, X collective WARL field of any entry in pmpcfg4 is reserved.
RULE 20: If pmpcfg4.A = 0, then entry 4 matches no addresses.
RULE 21: If pmpcfg4.A = TOR, then entry 4 matches any address y such that pmpaddr3 ≤ y < pmpaddr4, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg3.
RULE 22: If pmpaddr3 ≥ pmpaddr4 and pmpcfg4.A = TOR, then entry 4 matches no addresses.
RULE 23: If the PMP granularity G ≥ 1, then pmpcfg4 cannot select the NA4 mode (A = 2).
RULE 24: If G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg4.A[1] = 1 (NAPOT mode), then bits pmpaddr4[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 25: If G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg4.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), then bits pmpaddr4[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 26: When pmpcfg4.A = TOR, bits pmpaddr4[G-1:0] do not influence the TOR address-matching logic for entry 4.
RULE 27: Modifying pmpcfg4.A[1] may change the value read from pmpaddr4, but the physical bit pmpaddr4[G-1] remains unchanged when pmpcfg4.A is toggled between NAPOT and TOR/OFF and later restored to NAPOT.
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg4 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3a4; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 29: In S-mode, accessing pmpcfg4 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3a4; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 30: In U-mode, accessing pmpcfg4 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3a4; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: pmpcfg6

FIELDS: 7..0=pmp24cfg, 15..8=pmp25cfg, 23..16=pmp26cfg, 31..24=pmp27cfg, 39..32=pmp28cfg, 47..40=pmp29cfg, 55..48=pmp30cfg, 63..56=pmp31cfg
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpcfg6 can be accessed only when the processor is executing in M-mode.
RULE 2: All fields of pmpcfg6 are WARL and may be read-only zero.
RULE 3: When the R bit in pmpcfg6 is set, the corresponding PMP entry permits read accesses; when the R bit is clear, read accesses are denied.
RULE 4: When the W bit in pmpcfg6 is set, the corresponding PMP entry permits write accesses; when the W bit is clear, write accesses are denied.
RULE 5: When the X bit in pmpcfg6 is set, the corresponding PMP entry permits instruction fetches; when the X bit is clear, instruction fetches are denied.
RULE 6: The R, W, and X fields of pmpcfg6 together form a collective WARL field for which the combination of R=0 and W=1 is reserved.
RULE 7: When pmpcfg6.A = 0, the entry is OFF (null region, disabled).
RULE 8: When pmpcfg6.A = 0, this PMP entry is disabled and matches no addresses.
RULE 9: If pmpcfg6.A = 1, the associated address register forms the top of the address range and the preceding PMP address register forms the bottom of the address range.
RULE 10: If pmpcfg6.A = 1 for entry i, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr(i-1) ≤ y < pmpaddr(i), irrespective of the value of pmpcfg(i-1).
RULE 11: If pmpcfg6.A = 1 for entry 0, zero is used for the lower bound and the entry matches any address y < pmpaddr0.
RULE 12: If pmpcfg6.A = 1 and pmpaddr(i-1) ≥ pmpaddr(i), then entry i matches no addresses.

RULE 19: When pmpcfg6.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the pmpaddr pattern matches y011…1111, the entry matches a 2 × XLEN + 1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 20: When pmpcfg6.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the pmpaddr pattern matches 0111…1111, the entry matches a 2 × XLEN + 2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 21: When pmpcfg6.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the pmpaddr pattern matches 1111…1111, the entry matches a 2 × XLEN + 3-byte NAPOT range.

NUMBER: 0x3a8
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 7..0=pmp32cfg, 15..8=pmp33cfg, 23..16=pmp34cfg, 31..24=pmp35cfg, 39..32=pmp36cfg, 47..40=pmp37cfg, 55..48=pmp38cfg, 63..56=pmp39cfg

RULE 1: If mseccfg.RLB is 0 and pmpcfg8.L is 1 in any rule or entry (including disabled entries), then mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and any further writes to mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.

RULE 3: If mseccfg.MML is 1, then the encoding pmpcfg8.LRWX = 1111 is interpreted as a Shared-Region.

RULE 5: If mseccfg.MML is 1 and pmpcfg8.L is 1, then the rule remains locked so that further modifications to its configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is 1.
RULE 6: If mseccfg.MML is 1 and pmpcfg8.L is 0, then the rule is enforced in Supervisor and User modes and denied in Machine mode.
RULE 7: If mseccfg.MML is 1, pmpcfg8.L is 0, and the rule is a Shared-Region, then the rule is not executable.
RULE 8: If mseccfg.MML is 1, pmpcfg8.L is 0, and the rule is a Shared-Region, then Machine mode has read/write access to the region.
RULE 9: If mseccfg.MML is 1, pmpcfg8.L is 0, and the rule is a Shared-Region, then Supervisor and User modes have read access if pmpcfg8.X is 0, or read/write access if pmpcfg8.X is 1.
RULE 10: If mseccfg.MML is 1, pmpcfg8.L is 1, and the rule is a Shared-Region, then the rule is not writable.
RULE 11: If mseccfg.MML is 1, pmpcfg8.L is 1, and the rule is a Shared-Region, then both Machine mode and Supervisor/User modes have execute access to the region.
RULE 12: If mseccfg.MML is 1, pmpcfg8.L is 1, and the rule is a Shared-Region, then Machine mode also has read access if pmpcfg8.X is 1.
RULE 13: If mseccfg.MML is 1, pmpcfg8.L is 1, and the rule is a Shared-Region, then the rule remains locked so that further modifications to its configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is 1.
RULE 14: If mseccfg.MML is 1 and pmpcfg8.LRWX = 1111, then both Machine mode and Supervisor/User modes have read-only access to the region.
RULE 15: If mseccfg.MML is 1 and pmpcfg8.LRWX = 1111, then the rule remains locked so that further modifications to its configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is 1.
RULE 16: If a write to pmpcfg8 attempts to set executable privileges for a rule that would be M-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region while mseccfg.RLB is 0, then the write is ignored and pmpcfg8 remains unchanged.
RULE 17: Execution in Machine mode is permitted only from a region that matches a pmpcfg8 rule that is M-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region with executable privileges.
RULE 18: Execution in Machine mode is denied if the region does not match any pmpcfg8 rule or matches a pmpcfg8 rule that is S/U-mode-only.
RULE 19: If mseccfg.MML is 0, then the encoding pmpcfg8.RW = 01 is reserved for future standard use.
RULE 20: pmpcfg8 must be accessed only in M-mode.
RULE 21: All fields within pmpcfg8 are WARL and may be read-only zero.
RULE 22: Within pmpcfg8, an R bit set permits reads and a cleared R bit denies reads.
RULE 23: Within pmpcfg8, a W bit set permits writes and a cleared W bit denies writes.
RULE 24: Within pmpcfg8, an X bit set permits instruction execution and a cleared X bit denies execution.
RULE 25: The combination R = 0 and W = 1 within any subfield of pmpcfg8 is reserved.
RULE 26: If the X bit supplied by pmpcfg8 for a PMP entry is clear, an attempt to fetch an instruction from that region raises an instruction access-fault exception.
RULE 27: If the R bit supplied by pmpcfg8 for a PMP entry is clear, an attempt to execute a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction that accesses that region raises a load access-fault exception.
RULE 28: If the W bit supplied by pmpcfg8 for a PMP entry is clear, an attempt to execute a store, store-conditional, AMO, or cache-block zero instruction that accesses that region raises a store access-fault exception.
RULE 29: In pmpcfg8, the A field value 0 selects the OFF mode, which disables the PMP entry and matches no addresses.
RULE 30: In pmpcfg8, the A field value 1 selects the TOR mode, where pmpaddr8 forms the top of the address range and pmpaddr7 forms the bottom.
RULE 31: In pmpcfg8 TOR mode, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr7 ≤ y < pmpaddr8 irrespective of the value of pmpcfg7.
RULE 32: In pmpcfg8 TOR mode, if pmpaddr7 ≥ pmpaddr8 then the PMP entry matches no addresses.
RULE 33: In pmpcfg8, the A field value 2 selects the NA4 mode, which matches a naturally aligned four-byte region.
RULE 34: In pmpcfg8, the A field value 3 selects the NAPOT mode, where the size of the matched region is encoded in the low-order bits of pmpaddr8.
RULE 35: In pmpcfg8 NAPOT mode, the low-order bits of pmpaddr8 encode the region size according to Table 24, ranging from an 8-byte region up to a 2 XLEN+3-byte power-of-two region.
RULE 36: When PMP granularity G ≥ 1, the NA4 mode is not selectable and therefore pmpcfg8 A cannot be set to 2.
RULE 37: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg8 A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr8[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 38: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg8 A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr8[G-1:0] read as all zeros, and these bits do not affect TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 39: Changing pmpcfg8 A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr8 but does not modify the underlying stored value, and pmpaddr8[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg8 A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF and back to NAPOT.
RULE 40: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg8 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3a8; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 41: In S-mode, accessing pmpcfg8 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3a8; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 42: In U-mode, accessing pmpcfg8 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3a8; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 43: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg8.pmp32cfg (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3a8, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a8; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 44: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg8.pmp33cfg (bit 8) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x100; csrs 0x3a8, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a8; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 45: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg8.pmp34cfg (bit 16) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x10000; csrs 0x3a8, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a8; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 46: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg8.pmp35cfg (bit 24) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1000000; csrs 0x3a8, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a8; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 47: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg8.pmp36cfg (bit 32) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x100000000; csrs 0x3a8, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a8; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 48: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg8.pmp37cfg (bit 40) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x10000000000; csrs 0x3a8, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a8; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 49: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg8.pmp38cfg (bit 48) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1000000000000; csrs 0x3a8, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a8; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 50: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg8.pmp39cfg (bit 56) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x100000000000000; csrs 0x3a8, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a8; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 51: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg8 register while P extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: P; csrr a0, 0x3a8; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 52: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg8 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3a8; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: satp
NUMBER: 0x180
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: 63..60=MODE, 59..44=ASID, 43..0=PPN
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The satp CSR is accessible with supervisor read/write (SRW) privileges.
RULE 2: All S-mode instruction fetches implicitly read the satp CSR.
RULE 3: Unless otherwise specified, the value returned by an implicit read of the satp CSR is the same value that would be returned by an explicit read of the CSR using a CSR-access instruction in a sufficient privilege mode.
RULE 4: The SUM bit in satp is read-only 0 if S-mode is not supported.
RULE 5: The SUM bit in satp is read-only 0 if the satp MODE field is read-only 0.
RULE 6: When TVM=1, any attempt to read or write the satp CSR while executing in S-mode MUST raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 7: When TVM=0, reads and writes of the satp CSR are permitted while executing in S-mode.
RULE 8: When S-mode is not supported, the TVM field of satp is read-only and has the value 0.
RULE 9: If S-mode is not supported, or if satp.MODE is read-only zero (always Bare), the implementation may make FIOM read-only zero.
RULE 10: The PBMTE bit controls whether the Svpbmt extension is available for S-mode and G-stage address translation for page tables pointed to by satp or hgatp.
RULE 11: When PBMTE=1, Svpbmt is available for S-mode and G-stage address translation using the page tables referenced by satp.
RULE 12: When PBMTE=0, the implementation behaves as though Svpbmt were not implemented for translations that would use satp.
RULE 13: If Svpbmt is not implemented, PBMTE is read-only zero irrespective of any satp configuration.
RULE 14: For implementations with the hypervisor extension, henvcfg.PBMTE is read-only zero if menvcfg.PBMTE is zero, and this condition does not depend on satp.
RULE 15: After changing menvcfg.PBMTE, executing an SFENCE.VMA with rs1=x0 and rs2=x0 suffices to synchronize address-translation caches for translations that use the page tables identified by satp.
RULE 16: When ADUE=1, hardware updating of PTE A/D bits is enabled during S-mode address translation that uses the page table whose physical address is held in satp, and the implementation behaves as though Svade were not implemented for S-mode address translation.
RULE 17: When the hypervisor extension is implemented and ADUE=1, hardware updating of PTE A/D bits is enabled during G-stage address translation, the implementation behaves as though Svade were not implemented for G-stage address translation, and satp may still hold the S-mode page-table base address.
RULE 18: When ADUE=0, the implementation behaves as though Svade were implemented for S-mode and G-stage address translation that use the page tables referenced by satp.
RULE 19: If Svadu is not implemented, ADUE is read-only zero regardless of any satp setting.
RULE 20: For implementations with the hypervisor extension, henvcfg.ADUE is read-only zero if menvcfg.ADUE is zero, independent of satp.
RULE 21: After changing menvcfg.ADUE, executing an SFENCE.VMA with rs1=x0 and rs2=x0 suffices to synchronize address-translation caches for translations that use the page tables identified by satp.
RULE 22: The Svade extension requires page-fault exceptions be raised when PTE A/D bits need be set for translations using the page table referenced by satp, hence Svade is implemented when ADUE=0.
RULE 23: Upon reset, if the hypervisor extension is implemented, the satp-derived hgatp.MODE field is reset to 0.
RULE 24: Upon reset, if the hypervisor extension is implemented, the satp-derived vsatp.MODE field is reset to 0.
RULE 25: When satp.MODE is 0, the SUM field must be read-only and return 0.
RULE 26: If satp.MODE is read-only zero (always Bare), the implementation may make the FIOM bit in the senvcfg CSR read-only zero.
RULE 27: When MODE=Bare, supervisor virtual addresses are equal to supervisor physical addresses and there is no additional memory protection beyond the physical memory protection scheme described in Section 3.7.
RULE 28: Implementations are not required to support all satp MODE settings and if satp is written with an unsupported MODE the entire write has no effect; no fields in satp are modified.
RULE 29: The number of implemented ASID bits, termed ASIDLEN, may be determined by writing one to every bit position in the ASID field of satp and then reading back satp to see which bit positions hold a one.
RULE 30: The least-significant bits of the satp ASID field are implemented first, so if ASIDLEN > 0 then ASID[ASIDLEN-1:0] of satp is writable.
RULE 31: The maximal value of ASIDLEN, termed ASIDMAX, is 9 for Sv32 or 16 for Sv39, Sv48, and Sv57.
RULE 32: For SXLEN=64, satp MODE encoding value 0 denotes Bare, values 1-7 are reserved for standard use, value 8 denotes Sv39, value 9 denotes Sv48, value 10 denotes Sv57, value 11 denotes Sv64 (reserved for page-based 64-bit virtual addressing), values 12-13 are reserved for standard use, and values 14-15 are designated for custom use.
RULE 33: Implementations must only raise exceptions for implicit accesses generated as a result of instruction execution that are caused by the current satp translation, and must not raise exceptions for implicit accesses performed speculatively.
RULE 34: Changing satp.MODE from Bare to other modes and vice versa takes effect immediately without requiring execution of an SFENCE.VMA instruction.
RULE 35: Changes to satp.ASID take effect immediately.
RULE 36: The immediate effect of changing satp.MODE or satp.ASID applies even when the virtual-address width for that translation differs from the width currently specified by satp.MODE.
RULE 37: Implementations that make satp.MODE read-only zero (always Bare) might raise an illegal-instruction exception when an SFENCE.VMA instruction is executed.
RULE 38: If any PTE along the traversal path had its G bit set, rs2 must be x0; otherwise rs2 should be set to the ASID that will be placed in satp.ASID for the translation being modified.
RULE 39: The physical page number of the root page table is stored in the satp register.
RULE 40: When the hstatus.VTVM field is 1, an attempt in VS-mode to access the satp CSR raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 41: A write to satp with an unsupported MODE value is ignored.
RULE 42: The vsatp register is a VSXLEN-bit read/write register that serves as the VS-mode version of the supervisor register satp.
RULE 43: When the V bit in mstatus is 1, any instruction that reads or modifies satp accesses vsatp instead of the physical satp register.
RULE 44: When V=1, a write to satp containing a MODE field value that is not supported is ignored and no write to vsatp takes effect.
RULE 45: When V=0, a write to satp containing a MODE field value that is not supported is ignored.
RULE 46: When V=1, execution is in VS-mode or VU-mode, and an instruction accesses the satp register while hstatus.VTVM=1, a virtual-instruction exception with exception code 22 is raised.
RULE 47: When a virtual-instruction exception is raised due to an access to satp under the specified conditions, the mtval or stval register is written with the same value as for an illegal-instruction trap.
RULE 48: If satp.MODE (or vsatp.MODE when V=1) is set to Bare and the effective privilege mode is less than M, any execution of a shadow-stack instruction must raise a store/AMO access-fault exception.
RULE 49: If satp.MODE (or vsatp.MODE when V=1) is set to Bare, the effective privilege mode is M, and a memory access is performed by an SSAMOSWAP.W or SSAMOSWAP.D instruction, the access must raise a store/AMO access-fault exception.
RULE 50: When the ignore transformation is applied to a physical address, including guest-physical addresses, and the active satp register's MODE field is Bare, the transformation replaces the upper PMLEN bits with 0.
RULE 51: The ignore transformation does not replace the upper PMLEN bits when the active satp register's MODE field is not Bare.
RULE 52: The condition that the ignore transformation replaces the upper PMLEN bits with 0 applies both when executing in M-mode and when executing in any other privilege mode with the active satp register's MODE field set to Bare.
RULE 53: In M-mode, accessing satp register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x180; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 54: In S-mode, accessing satp register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x180; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 55: In U-mode, accessing satp register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x180; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 56: In M-mode, setting satp.MODE (bit 60) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1000000000000000; csrs 0x180, a0; csrr a1, 0x180; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 57: In M-mode, setting satp.ASID (bit 44) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x100000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x100000000000; csrs 0x180, a0; csrr a1, 0x180; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x100000000000].
RULE 58: In M-mode, setting satp.PPN (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x180, a0; csrr a1, 0x180; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 59: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the satp register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x180, a0; csrr a1, 0x180; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: scause
NUMBER: 0x142
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: 63..63=INT, 62..0=CODE
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Ssdbltrp, Sstc
RULE 1: The privilege level for accessing scause is supervisor mode.
RULE 2: The access type for scause is supervisor read/write (SRW).
RULE 3: When a trap is delegated to S-mode, the scause register is written with the trap cause.
RULE 4: The interrupt cause number i reported in the scause register corresponds to bit i in both the sip and sie registers.
RULE 5: scause is an SXLEN-bit read-write CSR.
RULE 6: When a trap is taken into S-mode, the implementation writes scause with a code indicating the event that caused the trap.
RULE 7: When a trap is not taken into S-mode, the implementation never writes scause, although software may write it explicitly.
RULE 8: The Interrupt bit of scause is set to 1 if the trap was caused by an interrupt.
RULE 9: The Exception Code field of scause contains a code that identifies the last exception or interrupt.
RULE 10: The Exception Code field of scause is required to implement bits 4-0, thereby supporting values 0 through 31.
RULE 11: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 1 and the Exception Code field of scause is 0, the scause value is reserved.
RULE 12: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 1 and the Exception Code field of scause is 1, the scause value indicates a supervisor software interrupt.
RULE 13: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 1 and the Exception Code field of scause is any value from 2 to 4, the scause value is reserved.
RULE 14: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 1 and the Exception Code field of scause is 5, the scause value indicates a supervisor timer interrupt.
RULE 15: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 1 and the Exception Code field of scause is any value from 6 to 8, the scause value is reserved.
RULE 16: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 1 and the Exception Code field of scause is 9, the scause value indicates a supervisor external interrupt.
RULE 17: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 1 and the Exception Code field of scause is any value from 10 to 12, the scause value is reserved.
RULE 18: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 1 and the Exception Code field of scause is 13, the scause value indicates a counter-overflow interrupt.
RULE 19: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 1 and the Exception Code field of scause is any value from 14 to 15, the scause value is reserved.
RULE 20: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 1 and the Exception Code field of scause is any value greater than or equal to 16, the scause value is designated for platform use.
RULE 21: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 0, the scause value indicates an instruction address misaligned exception.
RULE 22: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 1, the scause value indicates an instruction access fault.
RULE 23: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 2, the scause value indicates an illegal instruction.
RULE 24: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 3, the scause value indicates a breakpoint.
RULE 25: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 4, the scause value indicates a load address misaligned exception.
RULE 26: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 5, the scause value indicates a load access fault.
RULE 27: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 6, the scause value indicates a store/AMO address misaligned exception.
RULE 28: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 7, the scause value indicates a store/AMO access fault.
RULE 29: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 8, the scause value indicates an environment call from U-mode.
RULE 30: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 9, the scause value indicates an environment call from S-mode.
RULE 31: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is any value from 10 to 11, the scause value is reserved.
RULE 32: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 12, the scause value indicates an instruction page fault.
RULE 33: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 13, the scause value indicates a load page fault.
RULE 34: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 14, the scause value is reserved.
RULE 35: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 15, the scause value indicates a store/AMO page fault.
RULE 36: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is any value from 16 to 17, the scause value is reserved.
RULE 37: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 18, the scause value indicates a software check.
RULE 38: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 19, the scause value indicates a hardware error.
RULE 39: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is any value from 20 to 23, the scause value is reserved.
RULE 40: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is any value from 24 to 31, the scause value is designated for custom use.
RULE 41: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is any value from 32 to 47, the scause value is reserved.
RULE 42: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is any value from 48 to 63, the scause value is designated for custom use.
RULE 43: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is any value greater than or equal to 64, the scause value is reserved.
RULE 44: The scause register is a supervisor register.
RULE 45: When the virtualization mode bit V is 1, any instruction that normally reads or modifies scause actually accesses vscause instead.
RULE 46: When the virtualization mode bit V is 0, accesses to scause operate on the real scause register.
RULE 47: The most-significant bit of scause (bit VSXLEN-1) is the Interrupt flag.
RULE 48: Bits VSXLEN-2 down to 0 of scause hold the Exception Code, which is a WLRL field.
RULE 49: When the most-significant interrupt bit of scause is 1, the exception-code field values 0-15 and ≥16 are defined as: 0 reserved, 1 supervisor software interrupt, 2 virtual supervisor software interrupt, 3 machine software interrupt, 4 reserved, 5 supervisor timer interrupt, 6 virtual supervisor timer interrupt, 7 machine timer interrupt, 8 reserved, 9 supervisor external interrupt, 10 virtual supervisor external interrupt, 11 machine external interrupt, 12 supervisor guest external interrupt, 13 counter-overflow interrupt, 14-15 reserved, and codes ≥16 are designated for platform use.
RULE 50: When the interrupt bit of scause is 0, the exception-code field values are defined as: 0 instruction address misaligned, 1 instruction access fault, 2 illegal instruction, 3 breakpoint, 4 load address misaligned, 5 load access fault, 6 store/AMO address misaligned, 7 store/AMO access fault, 8 environment call from U-mode or VU-mode, 9 environment call from HS-mode, 10 environment call from VS-mode, 11 environment call from M-mode, 12 instruction page fault, 13 load page fault, 14 reserved, 15 store/AMO page fault, 16 double trap, 17 reserved, 18 software check, 19 hardware error, 20 instruction guest-page fault, 21 load guest-page fault, 22 virtual instruction, 23 store/AMO guest-page fault, 24-31 designated for custom use, 32-47 reserved, 48-63 designated for custom use, and codes ≥64 reserved.
RULE 51: An environment-call from HS-mode causes scause to contain exception code 9, and an environment-call from VS-mode causes scause to contain exception code 10.
RULE 52: When the V bit in hstatus is 1 and the attempted instruction is HS-qualified but is prevented from executing because of insufficient privilege or because a supervisor or hypervisor CSR such as scounteren or hcounteren disables it, scause is set to the virtual-instruction exception code 22 instead of the illegal-instruction code 2.
RULE 53: In VS-mode, attempting to access a non-high-half counter CSR while the corresponding bit in hcounteren is 0 and the same bit in mcounteren is 1 causes scause to contain exception code 22.
RULE 54: In VU-mode, attempting to access a non-high-half counter CSR while either hcounteren or scounteren has the corresponding bit 0 and mcounteren has the corresponding bit 1 causes scause to contain exception code 22.
RULE 55: In VS-mode or VU-mode, attempting to execute a hypervisor instruction (HLV, HLVX, HSV, or HFENCE) causes scause to contain exception code 22.
RULE 56: In VS-mode or VU-mode, attempting to access an implemented non-high-half hypervisor CSR or VS CSR in a way that would be allowed in HS-mode assuming mstatus.TVM=0 causes scause to contain exception code 22.
RULE 57: In VU-mode, attempting to access an implemented non-high-half supervisor CSR in a way that would be allowed in HS-mode assuming mstatus.TVM=0 causes scause to contain exception code 22.
RULE 58: In VS-mode, attempting to execute SRET when hstatus.VTSR=1 causes scause to contain exception code 22.
RULE 59: In VS-mode, attempting to execute an SFENCE.VMA or SINVAL.VMA instruction or to access satp when hstatus.VTVM=1 causes scause to contain exception code 22.
RULE 60: When scause reports a virtual-instruction exception (code 22), the mtval or stval register is written with the same faulting instruction value as for an illegal-instruction trap.
RULE 61: If an instruction can raise multiple synchronous exceptions, the exception with the highest priority according to Table 51 is the one whose code is placed in scause.
RULE 62: When an instruction is prevented from executing because the FS or VS field in sstatus or vsstatus is zero, scause is set to the illegal-instruction exception code 2 rather than to the virtual-instruction exception code 22.
RULE 63: The TSR and TVM fields in mstatus are ignored when determining which exception code is placed in scause for VS-mode traps.
RULE 64: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the implementation writes the scause CSR together with the sepc, stval, htval, and htinst CSRs.
RULE 65: In M-mode, accessing scause register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x142; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 66: In S-mode, accessing scause register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x142; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 67: In U-mode, accessing scause register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x142; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 68: In M-mode, setting scause.INT (bit 63) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x142, a0; csrr a1, 0x142; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000].

REGISTER: scounteren
NUMBER: 0x106
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: 32
FIELDS: 31..31=HPM31, 30..30=HPM30, 29..29=HPM29, 28..28=HPM28, 27..27=HPM27, 26..26=HPM26, 25..25=HPM25, 24..24=HPM24, 23..23=HPM23, 22..22=HPM22, 21..21=HPM21, 20..20=HPM20, 19..19=HPM19, 18..18=HPM18, 17..17=HPM17, 16..16=HPM16, 15..15=HPM15, 14..14=HPM14, 13..13=HPM13, 12..12=HPM12, 11..11=HPM11, 10..10=HPM10, 9..9=HPM9, 8..8=HPM8, 7..7=HPM7, 6..6=HPM6, 5..5=HPM5, 4..4=HPM4, 3..3=HPM3, 2..2=IR, 1..1=TM, 0..0=CY
EXTENSIONS: S
RULE 1: The scounteren register is accessible with supervisor read/write privilege (SRW).
RULE 2: When a CY, TM, IR, or HPM n bit in the scounteren register is clear, attempts to read the corresponding cycle, time, instret, or hpmcountern register while executing in U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 3: When a CY, TM, IR, or HPM n bit in the scounteren register is set, access to the corresponding counter register is permitted.
RULE 4: Any bit in the scounteren register may be read-only zero, indicating that reads to the corresponding counter will cause an exception when executing in U-mode.
RULE 5: The bits of the scounteren register are effectively WARL fields.
RULE 6: The setting of a bit in mcounteren does not affect whether the corresponding bit in scounteren is writable.
RULE 7: U-mode may only access a counter if the corresponding bits in scounteren and mcounteren are both set.
RULE 8: When the virtual-instruction mode bit V is 1, scounteren continues to have its usual function and accessibility, with VS-mode and VU-mode substituting for HS-mode and U-mode.
RULE 9: In VU-mode, a counter must not be readable unless the applicable enable bits are set in both hcounteren and scounteren.
RULE 10: When V=1 and an HS-qualified instruction is disabled by scounteren, a virtual-instruction exception (code 22) is raised instead of an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: In VU-mode, accessing a non-high-half counter CSR causes a virtual-instruction exception when the corresponding scounteren bit is 0 and the same bit in mcounteren is 1.
RULE 12: In M-mode, accessing scounteren register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x106; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 13: In S-mode, accessing scounteren register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x106; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 14: In U-mode, accessing scounteren register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x106; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 15: In M-mode, setting scounteren.HPM18 (bit 18) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x40000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x40000; csrs 0x106, a0; csrr a1, 0x106; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x40000].

REGISTER: scountinhibit
NUMBER: 0x120
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: 63..32=WPRI, 31..3=HPM3_HPM31, 2..2=IR, 1..1=TM, 0..0=CY
EXTENSIONS: Smcdeleg, Ssccfg
RULE 1: The scountinhibit CSR has privilege encoding SRW, meaning it is Supervisor Read/Write.
RULE 2: For counters delegated to S-mode, the corresponding mcountinhibit bits are accessible via scountinhibit.
RULE 3: For counters not delegated to S-mode, the corresponding bits in scountinhibit read as zero and are read-only.
RULE 4: If menvcfg.CDE is zero, any attempt to access scountinhibit raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 5: If Supervisor Counter Delegation is enabled, any attempt to access scountinhibit from VS-mode or VU-mode raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 6: In M-mode, setting scountinhibit.WPRI (bit 32) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x100000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x100000000; csrs 0x120, a0; csrr a1, 0x120; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x100000000].
