REGISTER: seed
NUMBER: 0x015
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: XLEN
FIELDS: 31..30=OPST, 29..24=WPRI, 23..16=custom, 15..0=entropy, UNKNOWN..UNKNOWN=UNKNOWN
EXTENSIONS: Zkr
RULE 1: seed bits 29:24 are reserved for future use by the RISC-V specification.
RULE 2: seed bits 15:0 form the entropy field that provides 16 bits of randomness only when OPST=ES16.
RULE 3: Attempted access to seed using a read-only CSR-access instruction (CSRRS or CSRRC with rs1=x0, or CSRRSI or CSRRCI with uimm=0) raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 4: The write value supplied to seed (in rs1 or uimm) must be ignored by implementations.
RULE 5: Seed is also access-controlled by execution mode, and attempted read or write of seed outside M mode raises an illegal-instruction exception unless access is explicitly granted.
RULE 6: When OPST in seed is not ES16, the entropy field of seed must be set to 0.
RULE 7: Polling (reading) seed must also have the side effect of clearing the entropy contents of seed and changing the OPST field of seed to WAIT unless entropy is immediately available for ES16.
RULE 8: A BIST alarm in seed must be latched until seed is polled at least once.
RULE 9: The value 0x8000ABCD is a valid ES16 status encoding for seed, with 0xABCD representing the entropy bits.
RULE 10: The value 0xFFFFFFFF is an invalid DEAD encoding for seed and contains no entropy value.
RULE 11: Implementations may implement mseccfg such that the [s,u]seed fields are read-only constant values of 0.
RULE 12: Software may discover whether access to the seed CSR can be enabled in U and S modes by writing a 1 to the [s,u]seed fields and reading back the result.
RULE 13: A read of the seed CSR flushes the secret entropy bits.
RULE 14: When the OPST bits of the seed CSR are 11 (DEAD), they indicate that feature discovery has failed and the entropy source is not available.
RULE 15: When the OPST bits of the seed CSR are 00 (BIST), they indicate that feature discovery has failed and the entropy source is not available.
RULE 16: A read of the seed CSR returns a 16-bit value.
RULE 17: When the mnoise register's NOISE_TEST bit (mnoise[31]) is set to 1, the seed CSR must not return any data via the ES16 interface.
RULE 18: When NOISE_TEST is asserted (value 1), the seed CSR cannot transition to the WAIT or ES16 states, and consequently the seed CSR produces no entropy output.
RULE 19: The seed CSR has URW access, meaning it is unprivileged and both readable and writable.
RULE 20: When USEED = 0, any access to the seed CSR in U-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 21: When USEED = 1, read-write access to the seed CSR from U-mode is allowed.
RULE 22: When USEED = 1, all non-read-write accesses to the seed CSR from U-mode raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 23: If Zkr or U-mode is not implemented, the seed CSR's USEED field is read-only zero.
RULE 24: When SSEED = 0, any access to the seed CSR from S-mode or HS-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 25: When SSEED = 1, read-write access to the seed CSR from S-mode or HS-mode is allowed.
RULE 26: When SSEED = 1, all non-read-write accesses to the seed CSR from S-mode or HS-mode raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 27: If Zkr or S-mode is not implemented, the seed CSR's SSEED field is read-only zero.
RULE 28: When the H extension is implemented, access to the seed CSR from an HS-qualified instruction in VS mode raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 29: When the H extension is implemented, access to the seed CSR from an HS-qualified instruction in VU mode raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 30: When the H extension is implemented, all other types of access to the seed CSR raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 31: The seed CSR is always available in machine mode as a normal read-write CSR.
RULE 32: An attempted read of the seed CSR without a preceding write raises an illegal-instruction exception regardless of privilege mode and access-control bits.
RULE 33: When operating in U-mode and USEED = 0, any access to the seed CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 34: When operating in U-mode and USEED = 1, the seed CSR is accessible as normal and no exception is raised for read-write accesses.
RULE 35: When operating in S-mode or HS-mode and SSEED = 0, any access to the seed CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 36: When operating in S-mode or HS-mode and SSEED = 1, the seed CSR is accessible as normal and no exception is raised for read-write accesses.
RULE 37: When operating in VS-mode or VU-mode and SSEED = 0, any access to the seed CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 38: When operating in VS-mode or VU-mode and SSEED = 1, a read-write access to the seed CSR raises a virtual-instruction exception while all other accesses raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 39: In M-mode, reading seed register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x015; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 40: In S-mode, reading seed register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x015; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 41: In U-mode, reading seed register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x015; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: senvcfg
NUMBER: 0x10a
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 7..7=CBZE, 6..6=CBCFE, 5..4=CBIE, 8..8=UKTE, 3..3=SSE, 0..0=FIOM
EXTENSIONS: Ssnpm, Zicbom, Zicboz, Zicfilp, Zicfiss
RULE 1: If priv_mode == U and senvcfg.CBIE == 00, a CBO.INVAL instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 2: If priv_mode == VU and (senvcfg.CBIE == 00 or henvcfg.CBIE == 00), a CBO.INVAL instruction raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 3: If priv_mode == U and senvcfg.CBIE == 01, a CBO.INVAL instruction executes and performs a flush operation.
RULE 4: If priv_mode == U and senvcfg.CBIE is neither 00 nor 01, a CBO.INVAL instruction executes and performs an invalidate operation.
RULE 5: If priv_mode == U and senvcfg.CBCFE is false, a CBO.CLEAN or CBO.FLUSH instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 6: If priv_mode == VU and not (henvcfg.CBCFE and senvcfg.CBCFE), a CBO.CLEAN or CBO.FLUSH instruction raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 7: If (priv_mode == U and senvcfg.CBCFE is true) or (priv_mode == VU and henvcfg.CBCFE and senvcfg.CBCFE are both true), a CBO.CLEAN or CBO.FLUSH instruction executes and performs the clean or flush operation.
RULE 8: If priv_mode == U and senvcfg.CBZE is false, a CBO.ZERO instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 9: If priv_mode == VU and not (henvcfg.CBZE and senvcfg.CBZE), a CBO.ZERO instruction raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 10: If (priv_mode == U and senvcfg.CBZE is true) or (priv_mode == VU and henvcfg.CBZE and senvcfg.CBZE are both true), a CBO.ZERO instruction executes and performs the zero operation.
RULE 11: The CBIE, CBCFE, and CBZE fields in each xenvcfg register, including those in senvcfg, do not affect the read and write behavior of the same fields in the other xenvcfg registers.
RULE 12: If privilege_mode is U and senvcfg.SSE is 0, an illegal-instruction exception is raised for the SSAMOSWAP.W/D instruction.
RULE 13: If privilege_mode is VU and senvcfg.SSE is 0, a virtual-instruction exception is raised for the SSAMOSWAP.W/D instruction.
RULE 14: senvcfg has SRW privilege, allowing Supervisor-mode reads and writes.
RULE 15: When menvcfg.SSE is 0, the senvcfg.SSE field is read-only and always returns zero.
RULE 16: The value of the ENVCFG bit in the mstateen0 CSR determines whether software can access the senvcfg CSR.
RULE 17: The value of the ENVCFG bit in the hstateen0 CSR determines whether software can access the senvcfg CSR.
RULE 18: The senvcfg CSR is an SXLEN-bit read/write register that controls certain characteristics of the U-mode execution environment.
RULE 19: If FIOM is set to 1 in senvcfg, FENCE instructions executed in U-mode are modified so that ordering device I/O also orders main memory accesses.
RULE 20: If FIOM is 1 in senvcfg, a FENCE instruction with the PI bit set in U-mode implies predecessor ordering of device input and memory reads (PR implied).
RULE 21: If FIOM is 1 in senvcfg, a FENCE instruction with the PO bit set in U-mode implies predecessor ordering of device output and memory writes (PW implied).
RULE 22: If FIOM is 1 in senvcfg, a FENCE instruction with the SI bit set in U-mode implies successor ordering of device input and memory reads (SR implied).
RULE 23: If FIOM is 1 in senvcfg, a FENCE instruction with the SO bit set in U-mode implies successor ordering of device output and memory writes (SW implied).
RULE 24: If FIOM is 1 in senvcfg and an atomic instruction in U-mode accesses a region ordered as device I/O and has its aq and/or rl bit set, then that instruction is ordered as though it accesses both device I/O and memory.
RULE 25: Execution of CBO.ZERO in U-mode is enabled only if execution of the instruction is enabled for use in S-mode and CBZE is set to 1 in senvcfg; otherwise an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 26: When the Zicboz extension is not implemented, CBZE is read-only zero in senvcfg.
RULE 27: Execution of CBO.CLEAN and CBO.FLUSH instructions in U-mode is enabled only if execution of these instructions is enabled for use in S-mode and CBCFE is set to 1 in senvcfg; otherwise an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 28: When the Zicbom extension is not implemented, CBCFE is read-only zero in senvcfg.
RULE 29: Execution of CBO.INVAL in U-mode is enabled only if execution of the instruction is enabled for use in S-mode and CBIE is 01b or 11b in senvcfg; otherwise an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 30: The encoding 10b of CBIE is reserved in senvcfg.
RULE 31: When the Zicbom extension is not implemented, CBIE is read-only zero in senvcfg.
RULE 32: If CBO.INVAL is enabled in S-mode to perform a flush operation, then when the instruction is enabled in U-mode it performs a flush operation even if CBIE is 11b in senvcfg.
RULE 33: If CBIE is 01b in senvcfg, then CBO.INVAL in U-mode is executed and performs a flush operation.
RULE 34: If CBIE is 11b in senvcfg, then CBO.INVAL in U-mode is executed and performs an invalidate operation.
RULE 35: If the Ssnpm extension is implemented, the PMM field in senvcfg enables or disables pointer masking for the next-lower privilege mode (U/VU) according to Table 39.
RULE 36: If the Ssnpm extension is not implemented, PMM is read-only zero in senvcfg.
RULE 37: If PMM is 00 in senvcfg, pointer masking is disabled (PMLEN = 0).
RULE 38: The PMM encoding 01b is reserved in senvcfg.
RULE 39: If PMM is 10 in senvcfg, pointer masking is enabled with PMLEN = XLEN-57 (PMLEN = 7 on RV64).
RULE 40: If PMM is 11 in senvcfg, pointer masking is enabled with PMLEN = XLEN-48 (PMLEN = 16 on RV64).
RULE 41: When the LPE field is set to 1 in senvcfg, the Zicfilp extension is enabled in VU/U-mode.
RULE 42: When the LPE field is 0 in senvcfg, the Zicfilp extension is not enabled in VU/U-mode.
RULE 43: If LPE is 0 in senvcfg, the hart does not update the ELP state; it remains as NO_LP_EXPECTED.
RULE 44: If LPE is 0 in senvcfg, the LPAD instruction operates as a no-op.
RULE 45: When the SSE field is set to 1 in senvcfg, the Zicfiss extension is activated in VU/U-mode.
RULE 46: When the SSE field is 0 in senvcfg, the Zicfiss extension remains inactive in VU/U-mode.
RULE 47: If SSE is 0 in senvcfg, 16-bit Zicfiss instructions revert to their behavior as defined by Zcmop.
RULE 48: The senvcfg register retains its normal function and accessibility even when the V bit is set to 1.
RULE 49: When V=1, accesses to the senvcfg register in VS-mode and VU-mode are treated as accesses that would occur in HS-mode and U-mode, respectively.
RULE 50: In HS and M modes, the senvcfg.PMM field enables or disables pointer masking for HLV.*, HLVX, and HSV instructions when their explicit memory accesses are performed as though in VU-mode.
RULE 51: If senvcfg.SSE is 1, then the Zicfiss extension is activated in VS-mode.
RULE 52: If senvcfg.SSE is 0, then the Zicfiss extension remains inactive in VS-mode.
RULE 53: If senvcfg.SSE is 0 and V=1, then 16-bit Zicfiss instructions revert to the behavior defined by Zcmop.
RULE 54: If senvcfg.SSE is 0 and V=1, then the pte.xwr=010b encoding in VS-stage page tables is reserved.
RULE 55: If senvcfg.SSE is 0, then reads of senvcfg.SSE return zero and the field is read-only.
RULE 56: If senvcfg.SSE is 0 and menvcfg.SSE is 1, then execution of SSAMOSWAP.W or SSAMOSWAP.D raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 57: When virtualization is active in VS or VU mode and vsatp.MODE is Bare, the two extra bits of a guest physical address may be subject to pointer masking, and this depends on hgatp.MODE and the senvcfg.PMM field (or henvcfg.PMM for VU/VS mode).
RULE 58: If vsatp.MODE is not Bare, the pointer-masking issue that may involve senvcfg.PMM does not apply.
RULE 59: When the processor is in U-mode and senvcfg.SSE is 0, an illegal-instruction exception is raised on any access to the ssp CSR.
RULE 60: When the processor is in VU-mode and either henvcfg.SSE is 0 or senvcfg.SSE is 0, a virtual-instruction exception is raised on any access to the ssp CSR.
RULE 61: When S-mode is implemented, the value of the senvcfg.SSE field determines the xSSE status for the U and VU privilege modes.
RULE 62: For privilege mode U or VU with S-mode implemented, the xSSE value is equal to the value of senvcfg.SSE.
RULE 63: The xSSE value derived from senvcfg.SSE for U or VU privilege modes decides whether backward-edge control-flow integrity using shadow stacks provided by the Zicfiss extension is enabled at that privilege mode.
RULE 64: In M-mode, accessing senvcfg register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x10a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 65: In S-mode, accessing senvcfg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x10a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 66: In U-mode, accessing senvcfg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x10a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 67: In M-mode, setting senvcfg.CBZE (bit 7) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x80) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x80; csrs 0x10a, a0; csrr a1, 0x10a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x80].
RULE 68: In M-mode, setting senvcfg.CBCFE (bit 6) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x40) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x40; csrs 0x10a, a0; csrr a1, 0x10a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x40].
RULE 69: In M-mode, setting senvcfg.CBIE (bit 4) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x10) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x10; csrs 0x10a, a0; csrr a1, 0x10a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x10].
RULE 70: In M-mode, setting senvcfg.UKTE (bit 8) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x100) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x100; csrs 0x10a, a0; csrr a1, 0x10a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x100].
RULE 71: In M-mode, setting senvcfg.SSE (bit 3) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8; csrs 0x10a, a0; csrr a1, 0x10a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8].
RULE 72: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the senvcfg register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x10a, a0; csrr a1, 0x10a; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 73: In M-mode, accessing senvcfg register while Ssnpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssnpm; csrr a0, 0x10a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 74: In M-mode, accessing senvcfg register while Zicbom extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicbom; csrr a0, 0x10a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 75: In M-mode, accessing senvcfg register while Zicboz extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicboz; csrr a0, 0x10a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 76: In M-mode, accessing senvcfg register while Zicfilp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicfilp; csrr a0, 0x10a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 77: In M-mode, accessing senvcfg register while Zicfiss extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicfiss; csrr a0, 0x10a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: sepc
NUMBER: 0x141
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=PC
EXTENSIONS: H, S, Ssdbltrp
RULE 1: The sepc CSR has Supervisor Read/Write (SRW) privilege.
RULE 2: When a trap is delegated to S-mode, the sepc register is written with the virtual address of the instruction that took the trap.
RULE 3: Setting a bit in medeleg or mideleg delegates the corresponding trap that occurs in S-mode or U-mode to the S-mode trap handler, and as a result the sepc register is written with the virtual address of the instruction that took the trap.
RULE 4: When a double-trap exception is delivered to M-mode because the S-mode-disable-trap (SDT) bit is already 1, the hart writes the sepc register with the same information that the unexpected trap would have written if it had been taken into M-mode.
RULE 5: sepc is an SXLEN-bit read/write CSR.
RULE 6: The low bit sepc[0] is always zero.
RULE 7: In implementations that support only IALIGN = 32, both low bits sepc[1:0] are always zero.
RULE 8: Whenever IALIGN = 32, reads of sepc mask bit sepc[1] so that it appears to be zero.
RULE 9: The implicit read of sepc performed by the SRET instruction also masks bit sepc[1] when IALIGN = 32.
RULE 10: Even when IALIGN = 32 masks sepc[1] on reads, software may still write to bit sepc[1].
RULE 11: sepc is a WARL register that must be able to hold all valid virtual addresses.
RULE 12: When a trap is taken into S-mode, the implementation writes sepc with the virtual address of the interrupted or faulting instruction.
RULE 13: Apart from trap handling, the implementation never writes sepc; it may only be written explicitly by software.
RULE 14: If stval is written with a nonzero value during an instruction access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception on a hart that supports variable-length instructions, then sepc points to the beginning of the faulting instruction.
RULE 15: When an illegal-instruction exception occurs and the stval register is used to return the faulting instruction bits, then sepc points to the faulting instruction in memory.
RULE 16: When the V bit is 1, any instruction that reads sepc actually reads vsepc instead.
RULE 17: When the V bit is 1, any instruction that writes sepc actually writes to vsepc instead.
RULE 18: When the V bit is 0, vsepc does not directly affect the behavior of the machine.
RULE 19: When the V bit is 0, accesses to sepc operate according to sepc's defined behavior without redirection to vsepc.
RULE 20: The set of values that sepc can hold defines the set of values that the WARL register vsepc must be able to hold.
RULE 21: When a trap is taken into HS-mode after any delegation by medeleg or mideleg and after the virtualization mode V is cleared to 0, the implementation MUST write the CSR sepc (together with the CSRs scause, stval, htval, and htinst).
RULE 22: The architectural effect of taking a trap into HS-mode is that the value of the sepc register is updated as part of the trap entry sequence.
RULE 23: When the SRET instruction is executed in M-mode or HS-mode with V=0, the processor sets the program counter to the value contained in sepc after the new privilege mode has been determined.
RULE 24: In M-mode, accessing sepc register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x141; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 25: In S-mode, accessing sepc register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x141; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 26: In U-mode, accessing sepc register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x141; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 27: In M-mode, setting sepc.PC (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x141, a0; csrr a1, 0x141; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 28: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the sepc register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x141, a0; csrr a1, 0x141; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 29: In M-mode, accessing sepc register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x141; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing sepc register while S extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: S; csrr a0, 0x141; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 31: In M-mode, accessing sepc register while Ssdbltrp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssdbltrp; csrr a0, 0x141; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: sie
NUMBER: 0x104
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: 1..1=SSIE, 5..5=STIE, 9..9=SEIE, 13..13=LCOFIE
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Sstc
RULE 1: The sie register is a supervisor-level CSR.
RULE 2: The sie register is readable and writable in supervisor mode (SRW).
RULE 3: If an interrupt is delegated to S-mode by setting the corresponding bit in the mideleg register, then that interrupt can be masked using the sie register.
RULE 4: If the corresponding bit in the mideleg register is not set, then the corresponding bits in the sie register are read-only zero.
RULE 5: The supervisor can disable individual interrupt sources using the sie CSR.
RULE 6: When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, SPIE is set to the value of SIE.
RULE 7: When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, SIE is set to 0.
RULE 8: When an SRET instruction is executed, SIE is set to the value of SPIE.
RULE 9: When an SRET instruction is executed, SPIE is set to 1.
RULE 10: Reading SIE in sstatus mirrors reading SIE in mstatus.
RULE 11: Writing SIE in sstatus mirrors writing SIE in mstatus.
RULE 12: sie is an SXLEN-bit read/write register that contains interrupt-enable bits.
RULE 13: Interrupt cause number i corresponds with bit i in both sip and sie.
RULE 14: An interrupt i will trap to S-mode only if the corresponding sie bit i is set.
RULE 15: A write to sie causes the interrupt-trap conditions to be evaluated immediately.
RULE 16: A bit in sie must be writable if the corresponding interrupt can ever become pending.
RULE 17: Bits of sie that are not writable are read-only zero.
RULE 18: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the sie.LCOFIE bit is a read-only zero.
RULE 19: If a standard interrupt type (SEI, STI, SSI, or LCOFI) is not implemented, the corresponding sie bit is a read-only zero.
RULE 20: All bits in sie are WARL (Write-Any-Read-Legal) fields.
RULE 21: Implemented sie bits can be discovered by writing one to every bit location in sie and reading back to identify bits that retain a one.
RULE 22: Reading a sie bit reads the corresponding mie bit, and writing a writable sie bit writes the corresponding mie bit.
RULE 23: Bit 13 of the sie register is assigned to the count-overflow interrupt.
RULE 24: In the sie register, the LCOFIE bit is the interrupt-enable bit for the count-overflow interrupt.
RULE 25: The interrupt-enable bits for the count-overflow interrupt include the sie LCOFIE bit.
RULE 26: Whether the count-overflow interrupt is enabled by the sie LCOFIE bit depends on the delegation setting in the mideleg register.
RULE 27: For each writable bit in sie, the corresponding bit in both hip and hie shall be read-only zero.
RULE 28: The nonzero bits in sie and hie are always mutually exclusive, and the nonzero bits in sip and hip are always mutually exclusive.
RULE 29: An interrupt i traps to HS-mode if (1) the current operating mode is HS-mode and the SIE bit in the sstatus register is set, or the current operating mode has less privilege than HS-mode; (2) bit i is set in both sip and sie, or in both hip and hie; and (3) bit i is not set in hideleg.
RULE 30: vsie is a VSXLEN-bit read/write register that is the VS-mode version of the supervisor CSR sie.
RULE 31: When hideleg[13] is one, vsie.LCOFIE is an alias of sie.LCOFIE.
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing sie register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x104; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 33: In S-mode, accessing sie register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x104; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 34: In U-mode, accessing sie register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x104; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 35: In M-mode, setting sie.SSIE (bit 1) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2; csrs 0x104, a0; csrr a1, 0x104; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2].
RULE 36: In M-mode, setting sie.STIE (bit 5) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x20) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x20; csrs 0x104, a0; csrr a1, 0x104; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x20].
RULE 37: In M-mode, setting sie.SEIE (bit 9) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x200) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x200; csrs 0x104, a0; csrr a1, 0x104; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x200].
RULE 38: In M-mode, setting sie.LCOFIE (bit 13) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2000; csrs 0x104, a0; csrr a1, 0x104; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2000].
RULE 39: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the sie register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x104, a0; csrr a1, 0x104; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 40: In M-mode, accessing sie register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0x104; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 41: In M-mode, accessing sie register while Sstc extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sstc; csrr a0, 0x104; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: sip
NUMBER: 0x144
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 1..1=SSIP, 5..5=STIP, 9..9=SEIP, 13..13=LCOFIP
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Sstc
RULE 1: Implicit reads of the sip CSR are ordered as device input.
RULE 2: The sip register is accessible with Supervisor-read/write privilege (SRW).
RULE 3: The sip register provides a restricted view of the mip register for supervisor level.
RULE 4: If an interrupt is delegated to S-mode by setting a bit in the mideleg register, then that bit becomes visible in the sip register.
RULE 5: If an interrupt is delegated to S-mode by setting a bit in the mideleg register, then that bit is maskable using the sie register.
RULE 6: If the corresponding bit is not set in the mideleg register, then the corresponding bits in the sip register and the sie register are read-only zero.
RULE 7: When the Sstc extension is implemented and the STCE bit in menvcfg is zero, the STIP field in the sip CSR reverts to its defined behavior as if the Sstc extension were not implemented.
RULE 8: The sip register can be interrogated to determine the presence of any interrupt in supervisor mode.
RULE 9: sip.LCOFIP is a field of the sip register that can be cleared by software.
RULE 10: When sip.LCOFIP is cleared before the LCOFI trap is raised, some or all CTR history may be overwritten while handling the LCOFI.
RULE 11: An interrupt i traps to S-mode if the current privilege mode is S and the SIE bit in sstatus is set, or if the current privilege mode has less privilege than S-mode, and bit i is set in both sip and sie.
RULE 12: Each individual bit in sip may be writable or read-only; when a bit i in sip is writable, a pending interrupt i can be cleared by writing 0 to that bit; if bit i in sip is read-only while interrupt i can become pending, the implementation must provide some other mechanism for clearing the pending interrupt.
RULE 13: If implemented, the SEIP bit in sip is read-only and is set and cleared by the execution environment, typically through a platform-specific interrupt controller.
RULE 14: If implemented, the STIP bit in sip is read-only; when the Sstc extension is not implemented, STIP is set and cleared by the execution environment; when the Sstc extension is implemented, STIP reflects the timer interrupt signal from stimecmp, being set by writing stimecmp with a value less than or equal to time and cleared by writing stimecmp with a value greater than time.
RULE 15: If implemented, the SSIP bit in sip is writable and may also be set to 1 by a platform-specific interrupt controller.
RULE 16: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the LCOFIP bit in sip is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request resulting from any mhpmevent n.OF bit being set; if the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, sip.LCOFIP is a read-only zero.
RULE 17: A standard interrupt type (SEI, STI, SSI, or LCOFI) may not be implemented, and if it is not implemented the corresponding pending bit in sip is a read-only zero.
RULE 18: Reading any implemented field of sip or writing any writable field of sip causes a read or write of the homonymous field of mip.
RULE 19: The STIP bit in the sip register becomes pending whenever the unsigned integer value of time is greater than or equal to stimecmp.
RULE 20: When the result of the comparison time ≥ stimecmp changes, the STIP bit in the sip register is guaranteed to eventually reflect the new comparison result, though the update need not be immediate.
RULE 21: The STIP bit in the sip register remains set while stimecmp is less than or equal to time.
RULE 22: The STIP bit in the sip register may remain set briefly after stimecmp is written to a value greater than time, which can cause a spurious timer interrupt.
RULE 23: In the sip register, the new count overflow interrupt will be treated as a standard local interrupt.
RULE 24: The new count overflow interrupt is assigned to bit 13 in the sip register.
RULE 25: The count-overflow-interrupt-request signal is treated as a standard local interrupt that corresponds to bit 13 of the sip register.
RULE 26: Bit 13 of the sip register, named LCOFIP, functions as the interrupt-pending bit for the count-overflow interrupt.
RULE 27: When an OF bit is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the sip register.
RULE 28: The LCOFIP bit in the sip register is cleared by software before servicing the count-overflow interrupt.
RULE 29: hip and hie are HSXLEN-bit read/write registers that supplement HS-level's sip.
RULE 30: Nonzero bits in sip and hip are always mutually exclusive.
RULE 31: An interrupt i traps to HS-mode when bit i is set in both sip and sie, provided that either the current mode is HS-mode with the SIE bit in sstatus set or the current mode has less privilege than HS-mode, and bit i is not set in hideleg.
RULE 32: Active bits of hip must not be placed in HS-level's sip.
RULE 33: When V=1, an instruction that reads the sip register accesses the vsip register instead.
RULE 34: When V=1, an instruction that writes the sip register accesses the vsip register instead.
RULE 35: If the Shlcofideleg extension is implemented and hideleg bit 13 is one, the sip.LCOFIP field is aliased to the vsip.LCOFIP field.
RULE 36: In M-mode, accessing sip register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x144; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 37: In S-mode, accessing sip register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x144; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 38: In U-mode, accessing sip register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x144; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 39: In M-mode, setting sip.SSIP (bit 1) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2; csrs 0x144, a0; csrr a1, 0x144; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2].
RULE 40: In M-mode, setting sip.STIP (bit 5) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x20; csrs 0x144, a0; csrr a1, 0x144; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 41: In M-mode, setting sip.SEIP (bit 9) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x200; csrs 0x144, a0; csrr a1, 0x144; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 42: In M-mode, setting sip.LCOFIP (bit 13) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2000; csrs 0x144, a0; csrr a1, 0x144; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2000].
RULE 43: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the sip register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x144, a0; csrr a1, 0x144; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 44: In M-mode, accessing sip register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0x144; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 45: In M-mode, accessing sip register while Sstc extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sstc; csrr a0, 0x144; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: siselect
NUMBER: 0x150
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: H, Smcntrpmf, Smctr, Smstateen, Ssaia, Sscofpmf, Sscsrind, Ssctr, Ssstateen
RULE 1: The siselect CSR has supervisor-read/write (SRW) privilege, meaning it is accessible only in supervisor mode for both reads and writes.
RULE 2: When siselect holds a value listed in Table 9, the indirect CSR mechanism accesses the CSR(s) named in the sireg, sireg2, sireg3, sireg4, sireg5, and sireg6 columns of that row.
RULE 3: When siselect contains the value 0x30, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = iprio0 and all other indirect-CSR slots (sireg2-sireg6) are none.
RULE 4: When siselect contains the value 0x3F, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = iprio15 and all other indirect-CSR slots (sireg2-sireg6) are none.
RULE 5: When siselect contains the value 0x40, the indirect CSRs accessed are sireg = cycle, sireg2 = cyclecfg, sireg4 = cycleh, sireg5 = cyclecfgh, while sireg3 and sireg6 are none.
RULE 6: When siselect contains the value 0x41, all indirect-CSR slots (sireg-sireg6) are none.
RULE 7: When siselect contains the value 0x42, the indirect CSRs accessed are sireg = instret, sireg2 = instretcfg, sireg4 = instreth, sireg5 = instretcfgh, while sireg3 and sireg6 are none.
RULE 8: When siselect contains the value 0x43, the indirect CSRs accessed are sireg = hpmcounter3, sireg2 = hpmevent3, sireg4 = hpmcounter3h, sireg5 = hpmevent3h, while sireg3 and sireg6 are none.
RULE 9: When siselect contains any value between 0x44 and 0x4F inclusive, the mapping of indirect CSRs is defined analogously by the corresponding table rows.
RULE 10: When siselect contains the value 0x5F, the indirect CSRs accessed are sireg = hpmcounter31, sireg2 = hpmevent31, sireg4 = hpmcounter31h, sireg5 = hpmevent31h, while sireg3 and sireg6 are none.
RULE 11: When siselect contains the value 0x70, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = eidelivery and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 12: When siselect contains the value 0x71, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = 0 and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 13: When siselect contains the value 0x72, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = eithreshold and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 14: When siselect contains the value 0x73, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = 0 and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 15: When siselect contains the value 0x7F, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = 0 and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 16: When siselect contains the value 0x80, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = eip0 and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 17: When siselect contains the value 0xBF, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = eip63 and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 18: When siselect contains the value 0xC0, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = eie0 and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 19: When siselect contains the value 0xFF, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = eie63 and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 20: When siselect contains the value 0x200, the indirect CSRs accessed are sireg = ctrsource0, sireg2 = ctrtarget0, sireg3 = ctrdata0, and sireg4-sireg6 are 0.
RULE 21: When siselect contains the value 0x2FF, the indirect CSRs accessed are sireg = ctrsource255, sireg2 = ctrtarget255, sireg3 = ctrdata255, and sireg4-sireg6 are 0.
RULE 22: If a hypervisor is oblivious to the AIA extension, it will not swap the siselect CSR on context switches, allowing siselect to be used as a covert channel between multiple guest OSes.
RULE 23: The CSRIND bit in mstateen0 controls access to the siselect CSR provided by the Sscsrind extensions.
RULE 24: The CSRIND bit in hstateen0 controls access to the siselect CSR provided by the Sscsrind extensions.
RULE 25: For an siselect value associated with counter X, the sireg and sireg2 registers can be used to access the mhpmcounterX and mhpmeventX CSRs.
RULE 26: For an siselect value associated with counter X, the sireg4 and sireg5 registers can be used to access the mhpmcounterXh and mhpmeventXh CSRs.
RULE 27: siselect will support the value range 0 .. 0xFFF at a minimum.
RULE 28: Ordinarily, when siselect holds a standard-defined and implemented value, each sireg_i will either access register state, access a read-only zero state, or raise an illegal-instruction exception unless execution is occurring in a virtual machine.
RULE 29: Implementations SHOULD give siselect the same number of bits as vsiselect.
RULE 30: A virtual-instruction exception MUST be raised when a direct access to siselect occurs while execution is in VU-mode.
RULE 31: The siselect CSR is always XLEN bits wide (the current XLEN) and is not VSXLEN.
RULE 32: When the Smstateen extension and Smcsrind are implemented, bit 60 of the state-enable CSR mstateen0 controls access to the siselect CSR.
RULE 33: If mstateen0[60] = 0 and an attempt to access siselect is made from a privilege mode less privileged than M-mode, the attempt results in an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 34: If an attempt to access siselect is made while executing in M-mode, the state-enable CSRs do not affect accessibility and the access is allowed.
RULE 35: If mstateen0[60] = 1, a virtual-instruction exception is raised for all attempts from VU-mode to access siselect or any CSR accessed indirectly through siselect, regardless of any other mstateen bits.
RULE 36: If the hypervisor extension is implemented, bit 60 of the hypervisor CSR hstateen0 controls access to siselect and any CSR accessed indirectly through siselect.
RULE 37: When hstateen0[60] = 0 and mstateen0[60] = 1, all attempts from VS-mode or VU-mode to access siselect or any CSR accessed indirectly through siselect raise a virtual-instruction exception, not an illegal-instruction exception, regardless of the value of vsiselect or any other mstateen bit.
RULE 38: siselect index values from 0x40 to 0x5F are reserved for delegated counter access.
RULE 39: When a counter i is delegated (mcounteren[i]=1 and menvcfg.CDE=1), siselect holds the value 0x40+i to access the counter's state via sireg*.
RULE 40: If the Smstateen extension is implemented and mstateen0[60]=0, any access to siselect from a privilege mode less privileged than M-mode must be prohibited.
RULE 41: If the Smstateen extension is implemented and hstateen0[60]=0, any access to siselect from VS-mode must be prohibited.
RULE 42: When siselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F and menvcfg.CDE=0, any M-mode or S-mode attempt to access sireg* must raise an illegal-instruction exception, provided access is not blocked by the mstateen0[60] or hstateen0[60] conditions.
RULE 43: When siselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, any M-mode or S-mode attempt to access sireg3 or sireg6 must raise an illegal-instruction exception, provided access is not blocked by the mstateen0[60] or hstateen0[60] conditions.
RULE 44: When siselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F and XLEN=64, any M-mode or S-mode attempt to access sireg4 or sireg5 must raise an illegal-instruction exception, provided access is not blocked by the mstateen0[60] or hstateen0[60] conditions.
RULE 45: When siselect equals 0x41, any M-mode or S-mode attempt to access sireg* must raise an illegal-instruction exception, provided access is not blocked by the mstateen0[60] or hstateen0[60] conditions.
RULE 46: When siselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F and the corresponding mcounteren bit for the selected counter is 0, any M-mode or S-mode attempt to access sireg* must raise an illegal-instruction exception, provided access is not blocked by the mstateen0[60] or hstateen0[60] conditions.
RULE 47: When siselect equals 0x41, the accessed register is the memory-mapped mtime register, which is not a performance-monitoring counter and therefore any access must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 48: For any siselect value defined in Table 25, if an extension required for the underlying counter state is not implemented, then any M-mode or S-mode attempt to access the associated sireg* must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 49: If the H extension is implemented, any attempt from VS-mode or VU-mode to directly access siselect must raise a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 50: When siselect is set to 0x200, the logical entry 0 accessed via sireg* always corresponds to the physical buffer entry immediately preceding the WRPTR entry.
RULE 51: For any siselect value that selects a logical entry X where X < depth, the physical buffer entry Y accessed via sireg* is computed as Y = (WRPTR – X – 1) mod depth, with depth defined as 2^(DEPTH+4).
RULE 52: When siselect selects a logical entry whose index is ≥ depth, reads of that entry return zero and the entry is read-only, so it cannot be written.
RULE 53: When siselect holds a value within 0x200-0x2FF, reads of sireg access the CTR logical entry field ctrsource.
RULE 54: When siselect holds a value within 0x200-0x2FF, reads of sireg2 access the CTR logical entry field ctrtarget.
RULE 55: When siselect holds a value within 0x200-0x2FF, reads of sireg3 access the CTR logical entry field ctrdata.
RULE 56: When siselect holds a value within 0x200-0x2FF, reads of sireg4, sireg5, and sireg6 return zero and these registers are read-only.
RULE 57: If mstateen0.CTR = 0 and the current privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, any attempt to access a sireg* register while siselect holds a value in the range 0x200 to 0x2FF raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 58: In M-mode, accessing siselect register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x150; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 59: In S-mode, accessing siselect register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x150; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 60: In U-mode, accessing siselect register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x150; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 61: In M-mode, setting siselect.VALUE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x150, a0; csrr a1, 0x150; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 62: In M-mode, accessing siselect register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x150; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 63: In M-mode, accessing siselect register while Smcntrpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smcntrpmf; csrr a0, 0x150; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 64: In M-mode, accessing siselect register while Smctr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smctr; csrr a0, 0x150; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 65: In M-mode, accessing siselect register while Smstateen extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smstateen; csrr a0, 0x150; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 66: In M-mode, accessing siselect register while Ssaia extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssaia; csrr a0, 0x150; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 67: In M-mode, accessing siselect register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0x150; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 68: In M-mode, accessing siselect register while Sscsrind extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscsrind; csrr a0, 0x150; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 69: In M-mode, accessing siselect register while Ssctr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssctr; csrr a0, 0x150; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 70: In M-mode, accessing siselect register while Ssstateen extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssstateen; csrr a0, 0x150; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: sscratch
NUMBER: 0x140
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=SCRATCH
EXTENSIONS: S
RULE 1: The sscratch CSR is a supervisor-level CSR that permits both read and write operations.
RULE 2: The sscratch CSR is an SXLEN-bit read/write register that is dedicated for use by the supervisor.
RULE 3: When the V bit equals 1, any instruction that would normally read sscratch actually accesses vsscratch instead.
RULE 4: When the V bit equals 1, any instruction that would normally modify sscratch actually accesses vsscratch instead.
RULE 5: When V=1, the contents of sscratch are not read.
RULE 6: When V=1, the contents of sscratch are not written.
RULE 7: In M-mode, accessing sscratch register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x140; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 8: In S-mode, accessing sscratch register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x140; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 9: In U-mode, accessing sscratch register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x140; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 10: In M-mode, accessing sscratch register while S extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: S; csrr a0, 0x140; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: ssp
NUMBER: 0x011
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: XLEN
FIELDS: 63..3=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: Zaamo, Zcmop, Zicfiss, Zicsr, Zimop
RULE 1: Reading the ssp register yields its current contents.
RULE 2: The SSRDP instruction reads the current contents of the ssp register and writes that value to a general-purpose register.
RULE 3: The ssp CSR is an unprivileged read-write (URW) CSR.
RULE 4: The ssp CSR reads and writes the XLEN low-order bits of the shadow stack pointer ssp.
RULE 5: Bits 1:0 of ssp are read-only zero.
RULE 6: If the UXLEN or SXLEN may never be 32, then bit 2 of ssp is read-only zero.
RULE 7: A shadow-stack push operation is defined as a decrement of the ssp register by XLEN/8 followed by a store of the link-register value to memory at the new top of the shadow stack.
RULE 8: In the architectural definition of SSPUSH, the store writes the source register to memory at address ssp-XLEN/8 and then the ssp register is set to ssp-XLEN/8.
RULE 9: The base address for the store performed by SSPUSH and C.SSPUSH is implicitly the current value of the ssp register.
RULE 10: The access width of the store performed by SSPUSH and C.SSPUSH is implicitly XLEN bits.
RULE 11: SSPUSH and C.SSPUSH decrement the ssp register by XLEN/8 only when the condition xSSE == 1 holds.
RULE 12: The ssp register is decremented by SSPUSH and C.SSPUSH only if the store to the shadow stack completes successfully.
RULE 13: A shadow stack pop operation reads an XLEN-wide value from the memory address held in ssp and then increments ssp by XLEN/8 bytes.
RULE 14: The SSPOPCHK and C.SSPOPCHK instructions perform a load identical to existing load instructions except that the base address is implicitly ssp and the access width is implicitly XLEN.
RULE 15: The pseudo-code for SSPOPCHK/C.SSPOPCHK specifies that, after a successful operation, ssp is updated as ssp = ssp + (XLEN/8).
RULE 16: Only the architectural registers x1 and x5 may be used as the source register for SSPOPCHK/C.SSPOPCHK; using any other source register raises a software-check exception and ssp is not incremented.
RULE 17: If the value loaded from the address referenced by ssp does not equal the value in rs1, a software-check exception with cause = 18 is raised and xtval is set to "shadow stack fault (code=3)", and ssp is not incremented.
RULE 18: ssp is incremented by SSPOPCHK and C.SSPOPCHK only when the load from the shadow stack completes without error and no software-check exception is raised.
RULE 19: The increment applied to ssp by SSPOPCHK and C.SSPOPCHK is exactly XLEN divided by 8 bytes.
RULE 20: The SSRDP instruction moves the contents of ssp to a destination register, subject to the xSSE condition.
RULE 21: If xSSE == 1, SSRDP writes the current value of ssp to the destination register.
RULE 22: If xSSE != 1, SSRDP does not read ssp and instead writes 0 to the destination register.
RULE 23: When the Zicfiss extension is not active, SSRDP does not read ssp and instead writes 0 to the destination register.
RULE 24: The csrw ssp instruction writes the supplied value to the ssp register.
RULE 25: When the instruction csrrw ra, ssp, ra is executed, the CSR ssp is written with the original value of register ra.
RULE 26: When the instruction csrrw ra, ssp, ra is executed, register ra is written with the previous value of the CSR ssp.
RULE 27: The ssp register is accessible with URW privilege, meaning it can be read and written by unprivileged software.
RULE 28: Attempts to access the ssp CSR may result in either an illegal-instruction exception or a virtual-instruction exception, contingent upon the state of the relevant x envcfg.SSE fields.
RULE 29: If the current privilege mode is less than M and menvcfg.SSE is 0, accessing the ssp CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 30: If the current privilege mode is U-mode and senvcfg.SSE is 0, accessing the ssp CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 31: If the current privilege mode is VS-mode and henvcfg.SSE is 0, accessing the ssp CSR raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 32: If the current privilege mode is VU-mode and either henvcfg.SSE is 0 or senvcfg.SSE is 0, accessing the ssp CSR raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 33: If none of the preceding conditions apply, access to the ssp CSR is allowed.
RULE 34: If the virtual address in ssp is not XLEN-aligned, then the SSPUSH instruction causes a store/AMO access-fault exception.
RULE 35: If the virtual address in ssp is not XLEN-aligned, then the C.SSPUSH instruction causes a store/AMO access-fault exception.
RULE 36: If the virtual address in ssp is not XLEN-aligned, then the SSPOPCHK instruction causes a store/AMO access-fault exception.
RULE 37: If the virtual address in ssp is not XLEN-aligned, then the C.SSPOPCHK instruction causes a store/AMO access-fault exception.
RULE 38: If the memory referenced by ssp is not idempotent, then the SSPUSH instruction causes a store/AMO access-fault exception.
RULE 39: If the memory referenced by ssp is not idempotent, then the C.SSPUSH instruction causes a store/AMO access-fault exception.
RULE 40: If the memory referenced by ssp is not idempotent, then the SSPOPCHK instruction causes a store/AMO access-fault exception.
RULE 41: If the memory referenced by ssp is not idempotent, then the C.SSPOPCHK instruction causes a store/AMO access-fault exception.
RULE 42: If the memory referenced by ssp is not idempotent, then the SSAMOSWAP.W/D instruction causes a store/AMO access-fault exception.
RULE 43: In M-mode, accessing ssp register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x011; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 44: In S-mode, accessing ssp register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x011; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 45: In U-mode, accessing ssp register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x011; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 46: In M-mode, setting ssp.VALUE (bit 3) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8; csrs 0x011, a0; csrr a1, 0x011; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8].
RULE 47: In M-mode, accessing ssp register while Zaamo extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zaamo; csrr a0, 0x011; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 48: In M-mode, accessing ssp register while Zcmop extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zcmop; csrr a0, 0x011; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 49: In M-mode, accessing ssp register while Zicfiss extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicfiss; csrr a0, 0x011; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 50: In M-mode, accessing ssp register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0x011; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 51: In M-mode, accessing ssp register while Zimop extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zimop; csrr a0, 0x011; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: sstateen0
NUMBER: 0x10c
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 2..2=JVT, 1..1=FCSR, 0..0=C
EXTENSIONS: F, Sdtrig, Ssaia, Sscsrind, Ssqosid, Zcmt, Zdinx, Zfinx
RULE 1: sstateen0 does not have a high-half CSR and its upper 32 bits are defined to be zero.
RULE 2: If a bit in mstateen0 is zero, whether read-only zero or writable zero, the corresponding bit in sstateen0 is read-only zero.
RULE 3: Each standard-defined bit of sstateen0 is WARL and may be either read-only zero or read-only one, subject to the specified conditions.
RULE 4: Any bit in sstateen0 that would control state not implemented by a hart is read-only zero for that hart.
RULE 5: All reserved bits in sstateen0 that have no defined meaning are read-only zero.
RULE 6: A bit in sstateen0 cannot be read-only one unless the corresponding bit in mstateen0 is read-only one and, when the hypervisor extension is implemented, the corresponding bit in hstateen0 is also read-only one.
RULE 7: Bit 63 of mstateen0 may be read-only zero only when the hypervisor extension is not implemented and all bits of sstateen0 are read-only zero.
RULE 8: If sstateen0 prevents access to a state for a less-privileged mode, any instruction in that mode that attempts to read or write the protected state must raise an illegal-instruction exception, or a virtual-instruction exception instead when executing in VS or VU mode and the conditions for a virtual-instruction exception are met.
RULE 9: The C bit of sstateen0 controls access to any and all custom state.
RULE 10: The FCSR bit of sstateen0 controls access to fcsr when floating-point instructions operate on x registers instead of f registers as defined by the Zfinx and related extensions.
RULE 11: When misa.F = 1, the FCSR bit of sstateen0 is read-only zero.
RULE 12: When stateen CSRs are implemented and misa.F = 0, if the FCSR bit of sstateen0 is zero then all floating-point instructions cause an illegal-instruction exception (or a virtual-instruction exception, if relevant) as though they all access fcsr.
RULE 13: The JVT bit of sstateen0 controls access to the jvt CSR provided by the Zcmt extension.
RULE 14: The SE0 bit in mstateen0 controls access to the sstateen0 CSRs.
RULE 15: The SE0 bit in hstateen0 controls access to the sstateen0 CSR.
RULE 16: In M-mode, accessing sstateen0 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x10c; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 17: In S-mode, accessing sstateen0 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x10c; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 18: In U-mode, accessing sstateen0 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x10c; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 19: In M-mode, setting sstateen0.JVT (bit 2) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4; csrs 0x10c, a0; csrr a1, 0x10c; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 20: In M-mode, setting sstateen0.FCSR (bit 1) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2; csrs 0x10c, a0; csrr a1, 0x10c; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 21: In M-mode, setting sstateen0.C (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x10c, a0; csrr a1, 0x10c; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 22: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the sstateen0 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x10c, a0; csrr a1, 0x10c; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 23: In M-mode, accessing sstateen0 register while F extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: F; csrr a0, 0x10c; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: sstateen1
NUMBER: 0x10d
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=DATA
EXTENSIONS: Smctr, Smstateen, Ssctr, Ssstateen
RULE 1: sstateen1 has privilege (access type) SRW, indicating Supervisor Read/Write access.
RULE 2: The upper 32 bits of the CSR sstateen1 are always zeros.
RULE 3: Each bit of the supervisor-level CSR sstateen1 controls user-level (U-mode or VU-mode) access to the corresponding extension's state.
RULE 4: The CSR sstateen1 controls access to state at all less-privileged levels but does not control access at the supervisor level itself.
RULE 5: When sstateen1 prevents access to state by a less-privileged mode, an instruction in that mode that reads or writes the protected state raises an illegal-instruction exception, or raises a virtual-instruction exception instead if the execution is in VS or VU mode and the conditions for a virtual-instruction exception apply.
RULE 6: Any bit of sstateen1 that controls state not implemented by a hart is read-only zero for that hart.
RULE 7: Any reserved bit of sstateen1 that has not been given a defined meaning is read-only zero.
RULE 8: For every bit that is zero in mstateen1, the same bit appears as read-only zero in sstateen1.
RULE 9: For every bit that is zero in hstateen1, the same bit appears as read-only zero in sstateen1 when accessed in VS-mode.
RULE 10: No bit of sstateen1 may be read-only one unless the same bit is read-only one in the matching mstateen1 CSR and, if present, in the matching hstateen1 CSR.
RULE 11: On reset, all writable bits of mstateen1 are initialized by hardware to zeros, and machine-level software that changes those bits must also initialize the corresponding writable bits of sstateen1 to zeros.
RULE 12: Bit 63 of mstateen1 controls access to the CSR sstateen1 (and to hstateen1).
RULE 13: Bit 63 of hstateen1 controls access to the CSR sstateen1.
RULE 14: Bit 63 of mstateen1 may be read-only zero only if the hypervisor extension is not implemented and the entire sstateen1 CSR is read-only zero; in that case, machine-level software should emulate attempts to access sstateen1 from S-mode by ignoring writes and returning zero for reads.
RULE 15: In M-mode, accessing sstateen1 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x10d; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 16: In S-mode, accessing sstateen1 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x10d; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: sstateen2
NUMBER: 0x10e
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=DATA
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: sstateen2 is SRW (supervisor read/write) accessible.
RULE 2: Any bit of sstateen2 that is defined to control a state that a hart does not implement shall be a read-only zero for that hart.
RULE 3: All reserved bits of sstateen2 that have not yet been given a defined meaning shall be read-only zeros.
RULE 4: If a bit in mstateen2 is zero, whether read-only zero or set to zero, the corresponding bit in sstateen2 shall be a read-only zero.
RULE 5: When accessed in VS-mode, any bit of sstateen2 that corresponds to a zero bit in hstateen2 shall be a read-only zero.
RULE 6: A bit of sstateen2 may be read-only one only if the same bit is read-only one in the matching mstateen2 and, if present, in the matching hstateen2.
RULE 7: On reset, hardware initializes all writable bits of mstateen2 to zeros.
RULE 8: If machine-level software changes writable bits of mstateen2, it must also initialize the corresponding writable bits of sstateen2 to zeros.
RULE 9: Bit 63 of mstateen2 may be a read-only zero only when the hypervisor extension is not implemented and all bits of sstateen2 are read-only zeros, and in that case machine-level software should emulate attempts to access sstateen2 from S-mode by ignoring writes and returning zero for reads.
RULE 10: In M-mode, accessing sstateen2 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x10e; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 11: In S-mode, accessing sstateen2 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x10e; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: sstateen3
NUMBER: 0x10f
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=DATA
EXTENSIONS: Smstateen, Ssstateen
RULE 1: sstateen3 has privilege SRW, indicating it is readable and writable in supervisor mode.
RULE 2: The upper 32 bits of sstateen3 are permanently read-only zero and no separate high-half CSR is defined for sstateen3.
RULE 3: Every bit of sstateen3 controls whether user-mode (U-mode or VU-mode) software may read or write the corresponding extension state.
RULE 4: Bits 63-32 of sstateen3 are permanently read-only zero, so only bits 31-0 may be used.
RULE 5: Any bit in sstateen3 that is an "encroaching" bit from the most-significant end of mstateen3 remains forever read-only zero.
RULE 6: Bits in sstateen3 that are defined to control state that a hart does not implement are read-only zero for that hart.
RULE 7: All reserved bits in sstateen3 that have not yet been given a defined meaning are read-only zero.
RULE 8: If a bit in mstateen3 is zero, the corresponding bit in sstateen3 is read-only zero.
RULE 9: If a bit in hstateen3 is zero, the same bit in sstateen3 is read-only zero when accessed in VS-mode.
RULE 10: A bit in sstateen3 cannot be read-only one unless the same bit is read-only one in mstateen3 and, when present, in hstateen3.
RULE 11: After reset, the writable bits of sstateen3 are initialized to zero because all writable mstateen bits are hardware-initialized to zero.
RULE 12: Bit 63 of mstateen3 controls whether S-mode (and VS-mode) may read or write sstateen3 (and hstateen3).
RULE 13: Bit 63 of hstateen3 controls whether VS-mode may read or write sstateen3.
RULE 14: Bit 63 of mstateen3 may be read-only zero only if the hypervisor extension is not implemented and sstateen3 is entirely read-only zero, which permanently disables S-mode access to sstateen3.
RULE 15: Bit 63 of hstateen3 is always writable, allowing VS-mode to modify bit 63 of hstateen3 and thereby control access to sstateen3.
RULE 16: In M-mode, accessing sstateen3 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x10f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 17: In S-mode, accessing sstateen3 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x10f; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 18: In U-mode, accessing sstateen3 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x10f; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 19: In M-mode, setting sstateen3.DATA (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x10f, a0; csrr a1, 0x10f; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
