RULE 22: In M-mode, accessing sstateen3 register while Ssstateen extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssstateen; csrr a0, 0x10f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: sstatus
NUMBER: 0x100
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: 63..63=SD, 33..32=UXL, 23..23=SPELP, 19..19=MXR, 18..18=SUM, 16..15=XS, 14..13=FS, 10..9=VS, 8..8=SPP, 6..6=UBE, 5..5=SPIE, 1..1=SIE
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: When determining whether a cache-block management (CMO) instruction may be permitted to access a cache block, the implementation checks the SUM and MXR bits in sstatus (together with the MPRV, MPV, and MPP bits in mstatus and the SUM and MXR bits in mstatus and vsstatus).
RULE 2: The permission for a CMO instruction to access a cache block may be granted or denied based on the states of the SUM and MXR bits in sstatus.
RULE 3: The sstatus register bits 10-9 are defined as a vector context status field named VS that is a shadow of the corresponding bits 10-9 in the mstatus register.
RULE 4: sstatus is readable and writable at supervisor privilege level.
RULE 5: When an MRET or SRET instruction is executed while the hart is in M-mode, the sstatus.MDT bit is set to 0.
RULE 6: If the new privilege mode after an MRET or SRET return is U, VS, or VU, the sstatus.SDT field is set to 0.
RULE 7: If the new privilege mode after an MRET or SRET return is VU, the sstatus.SDT field is set to 0 and the vsstatus.SDT field is also set to 0.
RULE 8: When the MNRET instruction is executed and the new privilege mode is not M, the sstatus.MDT bit is set to 0.
RULE 9: If the new privilege mode after an MNRET execution is U, VS, or VU, the sstatus.SDT field is set to 0.
RULE 10: If the new privilege mode after an MNRET execution is VU, the sstatus.SDT field is set to 0 and the vsstatus.SDT field is also set to 0.
RULE 11: If the Ssdbltrp extension is not implemented, the sstatus.SDT bit is read-only zero (and the vsstatus.SDT and henvcfg.DTE bits are also read-only zero).
RULE 12: The FS field in the sstatus register blocks access to the floating-point f registers.
RULE 13: The VS field in the sstatus register blocks access to the vector v registers.
RULE 14: Access to the vector v registers is blocked when the VS field in sstatus is initialized to zero, either at machine level or by the OS initializing sstatus.
RULE 15: The sstatus register is an SXLEN-bit read/write register.
RULE 16: When a trap is taken, the SPP bit in sstatus is set to 0 if the trap originated from user mode, or set to 1 otherwise.
RULE 17: When an SRET instruction is executed, the privilege level is set to user mode if the SPP bit in sstatus is 0, or set to supervisor mode if the SPP bit in sstatus is 1.
RULE 18: When an SRET instruction is executed, the SPP bit in sstatus is set to 0.
RULE 19: When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, the SPIE bit in sstatus is set to the previous value of the SIE bit in sstatus.
RULE 20: When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, the SIE bit in sstatus is set to 0.
RULE 21: When an SRET instruction is executed, the SIE bit in sstatus is set to the previous value of the SPIE bit in sstatus.
RULE 22: When an SRET instruction is executed, the SPIE bit in sstatus is set to 1.
RULE 23: In a straightforward implementation, reading any field in sstatus yields the same value as reading the homonymous field in mstatus.
RULE 24: In a straightforward implementation, writing any field in sstatus updates the homonymous field in mstatus with the same value.
RULE 25: When the sstatus register indicates that SXLEN=64, the UXL field is a WARL field that encodes the current value of UXLEN.
RULE 26: When the sstatus register indicates that UXLEN ≠ SXLEN, instructions executed in the narrower mode must ignore source register operand bits above the configured XLEN and must sign-extend results to fill the widest supported XLEN in the destination register.
RULE 27: When the sstatus register indicates that UXLEN < SXLEN, user-mode instruction-fetch addresses and load and store effective addresses are taken modulo 2^UXLEN.
RULE 28: When the sstatus register indicates XLEN < SXLEN and a HINT instruction is executed with destination-register bits SXLEN..XLEN not all equal to bit XLEN-1, it is implementation-defined whether those bits are unchanged or are overwritten with copies of bit XLEN-1.
RULE 29: The implementation-defined choice for HINT write-back is observable only by S-mode when the sstatus register reflects SXLEN > UXLEN and is invisible to U-mode.
RULE 30: When the MXR bit in sstatus is 0, only loads from pages marked readable (R=1) will succeed.
RULE 31: When the MXR bit in sstatus is 1, loads from pages marked either readable or executable (R=1 or X=1) will succeed.
RULE 32: The MXR bit in sstatus has no effect when page-based virtual memory is not in effect.
RULE 33: When the SUM bit in sstatus is 0, S-mode memory accesses to pages that are accessible by U-mode (U=1) will fault.
RULE 34: When the SUM bit in sstatus is 1, these accesses are permitted.
RULE 35: The SUM bit in sstatus has no effect when page-based virtual memory is not in effect.
RULE 36: The SUM bit in sstatus has no effect when executing in U-mode.
RULE 37: The SUM bit in sstatus does not permit S-mode to execute instructions from user pages.
RULE 38: The SUM bit in sstatus is read-only 0 if satp.MODE is read-only 0.
RULE 39: The SUM bit in sstatus does not grant S-mode software permission to execute instructions in user code pages.
RULE 40: The UBE bit in the sstatus register is a WARL (write-any-value-read-legal) field.
RULE 41: When the UBE bit in the sstatus register is 0, explicit load and store memory accesses made from U-mode are performed in little-endian order, and when the UBE bit is 1 they are performed in big-endian order.
RULE 42: The UBE bit in the sstatus register has no effect on instruction fetches, which are implicit memory accesses that are always little-endian.
RULE 43: For implicit accesses to supervisor-level memory-management data structures such as page tables, the endianness defined by S-mode applies and the UBE bit in the sstatus register is ignored.
RULE 44: When the V bit is 0, any access to the SPELP field in sstatus accesses the homonymous SPELP field in mstatus.
RULE 45: When the V bit is 1, any access to the SPELP field in sstatus accesses the homonymous SPELP field in vsstatus.
RULE 46: When an explicit CSR write sets the SDT bit in sstatus to 1, the SIE bit in sstatus is cleared to 0.
RULE 47: The clearing of the SIE bit occurs regardless of any value written to the SIE bit by the same CSR write.
RULE 48: The SIE bit in sstatus may be set to 1 by an explicit CSR write only if the same write sets the SDT bit to 0 or the SDT bit is already 0.
RULE 49: When a trap is to be taken into S-mode and the SDT bit in sstatus is 0, the SDT bit is set to 1 before the trap is delivered.
RULE 50: When a trap is to be taken into S-mode and the SDT bit in sstatus is already 1, the trap is classified as unexpected and a double-trap exception is delivered into M-mode.
RULE 51: An SRET instruction sets the SDT bit in sstatus to 0.
RULE 52: If a guest-page fault occurs while HS-mode invokes a hypervisor virtual-machine load or store instruction when the SDT bit in sstatus is 1, then the GPA will not be available in mtval2 when the double trap is delivered to M-mode.
RULE 53: An interrupt i will trap to S-mode when the current privilege mode is S, the SIE bit in the sstatus register is set, and bit i is set in both sip and sie.
RULE 54: The evaluation of interrupt trap conditions must occur immediately after an explicit write to the sstatus register.
RULE 55: Changes to the sstatus SUM field take effect immediately and do not require execution of an SFENCE.VMA instruction.
RULE 56: Changes to the sstatus MXR field take effect immediately and do not require execution of an SFENCE.VMA instruction.
RULE 57: If the SUM bit in sstatus is set, supervisor-mode software may also access pages whose PTE U bit = 1.
RULE 58: If the SUM bit in sstatus is clear, supervisor code will fault on accesses to pages whose PTE U bit = 1.
RULE 59: Irrespective of the SUM bit in sstatus, the supervisor may not execute code on pages whose PTE U bit = 1.
RULE 60: When V=1, the VS CSRs substitute for the corresponding supervisor CSRs, so vsstatus takes over all functions of sstatus except as otherwise specified.
RULE 61: When V=1, instructions that normally read or modify the sstatus CSR shall instead access the vsstatus CSR.
RULE 62: When V=1, an attempt to read or write the VS CSR that duplicates sstatus (vsstatus) directly by its own separate CSR address causes a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 63: The VS CSRs, including vsstatus which duplicates sstatus, can be accessed as themselves only from M-mode or HS-mode.
RULE 64: While V=1, the normal sstatus CSR retains its value but does not affect the behavior of the machine unless specifically documented to do so.
RULE 65: When V=0, the VS CSR that duplicates sstatus (vsstatus) does not ordinarily affect the behavior of the machine other than being readable and writable by CSR instructions.
RULE 66: When any trap is taken, the implementation sets the SPP bit in sstatus to the nominal privilege mode that was in effect at the time of the trap.
RULE 67: If the virtualization mode V equals 1 and a trap is taken into HS-mode, the implementation sets the SPP bit in sstatus to the nominal privilege mode at trap entry.
RULE 68: Executing an SRET instruction that transfers control to U-mode always clears the SPP bit in sstatus to 0.
RULE 69: An interrupt i will trap to HS-mode only if, when the current operating mode is HS-mode, the SIE bit in the sstatus register is set.
RULE 70: When the V bit in sstatus is 1, all instructions that normally read or modify sstatus instead access vsstatus.
RULE 71: When V=1, the floating-point status field FS in vsstatus and the FS field in the HS-level sstatus are both in effect.
RULE 72: When V=1, if either the FS field in vsstatus or the FS field in the HS-level sstatus is 0 (Off), executing a floating-point instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 73: When V=1, modifying the floating-point state sets both the FS field in vsstatus and the FS field in the HS-level sstatus to 3 (Dirty).
RULE 74: When V=1, the vector status field VS in vsstatus and the VS field in the HS-level sstatus are both in effect.
RULE 75: When V=1, if either the VS field in vsstatus or the VS field in the HS-level sstatus is 0 (Off), executing a vector instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 76: When V=1, modifying the vector state sets both the VS field in vsstatus and the VS field in the HS-level sstatus to 3 (Dirty).
RULE 77: The read-only SD field in sstatus summarizes the extension context status as it is visible to VS-mode only.
RULE 78: The value of the HS-level sstatus.FS field does not affect the vsstatus.SD field.
RULE 79: The read-only XS field in sstatus summarizes the extension context status as it is visible to VS-mode only.
RULE 80: During execution of hypervisor virtual-machine load and store instructions, the HS-level sstatus.SUM field is ignored.
RULE 81: When the HS-level sstatus.MXR field is set, execute-only pages become readable by explicit loads for both the VS-stage and G-stage of address translation.
RULE 82: If the FS field in sstatus is zero and this prevents an instruction from executing, the exception raised is always an illegal-instruction exception, never a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 83: If the VS field in sstatus is zero and this prevents an instruction from executing, the exception raised is always an illegal-instruction exception, never a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 84: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the sstatus.SPP field is set to 0 if the previous privilege mode was U-mode.
RULE 85: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the sstatus.SPP field is set to 1 if the previous privilege mode was HS-mode.
RULE 86: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the sstatus.SPP field is set to 0 if the previous privilege mode was VU-mode.
RULE 87: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the sstatus.SPP field is set to 1 if the previous privilege mode was VS-mode.
RULE 88: When a trap is taken into VS-mode, the HS-level sstatus register is not modified.
RULE 89: When the SRET instruction is executed in M-mode or HS-mode with V = 0, the architectural value of sstatus.SPP together with hstatus.SPV determines the new privilege mode as defined by the specification.
RULE 90: After SRET has determined the new privilege mode while executing in M-mode or HS-mode with V = 0, the instruction sets sstatus.SPP to 0.
RULE 91: After SRET has determined the new privilege mode while executing in M-mode or HS-mode with V = 0, the instruction sets sstatus.SIE to the current value of sstatus.SPIE.
RULE 92: After SRET has determined the new privilege mode while executing in M-mode or HS-mode with V = 0, the instruction sets sstatus.SPIE to 1.
RULE 93: sstatus includes the SPELP bit and any read or write of that bit accesses the same architectural field as mstatus.SPELP.
RULE 94: When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, the SPELP bit in sstatus is set to the current ELP value and ELP is subsequently set to NO_LP_EXPECTED.
RULE 95: If an SRET instruction transfers control to a privilege mode whose LPE field equals 1, then ELP is loaded from the SPELP bit in sstatus and the SPELP bit is subsequently cleared to NO_LP_EXPECTED.
RULE 96: If an SRET instruction transfers control to a privilege mode whose LPE field equals 0, then ELP is set to NO_LP_EXPECTED and the SPELP bit in sstatus is cleared to NO_LP_EXPECTED.
RULE 97: In M-mode, accessing sstatus register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x100; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 98: In S-mode, accessing sstatus register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x100; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: stval
NUMBER: 0x143
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: H, Ssdbltrp, Zicfilp, Zicfiss
RULE 1: The stval register is accessible with supervisor read/write privilege (SRW).
RULE 2: When a trap is delegated to S-mode (i.e., the trap occurs in S-mode or U-mode and the corresponding bit in medeleg or mideleg is set), the stval register is written with an exception-specific datum.
RULE 3: After a trap handler has saved the stval (along with scause and sepc) needed for resuming from the trap and the handler is reentrant, the implementation SHOULD clear the SDT bit.
RULE 4: The stval CSR is an SXLEN-bit read-write register.
RULE 5: When a trap is taken into S-mode, the implementation writes stval with exception-specific information to assist software in handling the trap.
RULE 6: Otherwise, the implementation never writes stval, though it may be explicitly written by software.
RULE 7: If stval is written with a nonzero value when a breakpoint, address-misaligned, access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception occurs on an instruction fetch, load, or store, then stval will contain the faulting virtual address.
RULE 8: On a breakpoint exception raised by an EBREAK or C.EBREAK instruction, stval is written with either zero or the virtual address of the instruction.
RULE 9: If stval is written with a nonzero value when a misaligned load or store causes an access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception, then stval will contain the virtual address of the portion of the access that caused the fault.
RULE 10: If stval is written with a nonzero value when an instruction access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception occurs on a hart with variable-length instructions, then stval will contain the virtual address of the portion of the instruction that caused the fault, while sepc will point to the beginning of the instruction.
RULE 11: If stval is written with a nonzero value when an illegal-instruction exception occurs, then stval will contain the shortest of the actual faulting instruction, the first ILEN bits of the faulting instruction, or the first SXLEN bits of the faulting instruction.
RULE 12: The value loaded into stval on an illegal-instruction exception is right-justified and all unused upper bits are cleared to zero.
RULE 13: On a trap caused by a software-check exception, stval holds the cause for the exception.
RULE 14: When the cause of a software-check exception is 0, stval is 0 to indicate no information provided.
RULE 15: When the cause of a software-check exception is 2, stval is 2 to indicate a Landing Pad Fault as defined by the Zicfilp extension.
RULE 16: When the cause of a software-check exception is 3, stval is 3 to indicate a Shadow Stack Fault as defined by the Zicfiss extension.
RULE 17: For other traps, stval is set to zero, but a future standard may redefine stval's setting for other traps.
RULE 18: stval is a WARL register that must be able to hold all valid virtual addresses and the value 0.
RULE 19: stval need not be capable of holding all possible invalid addresses.
RULE 20: Prior to writing stval, implementations may convert an invalid address into some other invalid address that stval is capable of holding.
RULE 21: If the feature to return the faulting instruction bits is implemented, stval must also be able to hold all values less than 2^N, where N is the smaller of SXLEN and ILEN.
RULE 22: When any trap (breakpoint, address misaligned, access fault, page fault, or guest-page fault) writes a guest virtual address to stval, the GVA field in stval is set to 1.
RULE 23: When any other trap into HS-mode writes to stval, the GVA field in stval is set to 0.
RULE 24: For breakpoint and memory-access traps that write a nonzero value to stval, the GVA field in stval is set to the same value as the SPV field.
RULE 25: If the explicit memory access of an HLV, HLVX, or HSV instruction causes a fault, SPV is set to 0 and GVA is set to 1 in stval.
RULE 26: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, hardware writes the stval register with exception-specific information.
RULE 27: For misaligned loads and stores that cause guest-page faults, the virtual address of the faulting portion of the access is reported in stval.
RULE 28: For instruction guest-page faults on systems that support variable-length instructions, the virtual address of the faulting portion of the instruction is reported in stval.
RULE 29: Ordinarily, the least-significant two bits of a faulting guest physical address are identical to the least-significant two bits of the faulting virtual address contained in stval.
RULE 30: For faults caused by implicit memory accesses during VS-stage address translation, the least-significant two bits of the virtual address reported in stval are zero.
RULE 31: When the V field is 1, any instruction that reads or modifies stval actually accesses the virtual supervisor trap value register vstval instead.
RULE 32: When the V field is 0, accesses to stval operate on stval itself and the virtual register vstval does not substitute for stval.
RULE 33: On a guest-page fault, the CSR stval is written with the faulting guest virtual address.
RULE 34: When a guest-page fault occurs during an instruction fetch or a misaligned memory access that straddles a page boundary, the faulting virtual address written to stval is the same as would be required for a regular page fault.
RULE 35: When a guest-page fault occurs during an instruction fetch or a misaligned memory access that straddles a page boundary, the faulting virtual address written to stval may be a page-boundary address that is higher than the instruction's original virtual address if the byte at that page boundary is among the accessed bytes.
RULE 36: When a guest-page fault is not due to an implicit memory access for VS-stage address translation, a nonzero guest physical address written to mtval2 or htval shall correspond to the exact virtual address written to stval.
RULE 37: On a virtual-instruction trap, the stval register is written with the same value that is written on an illegal-instruction trap.
RULE 38: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the implementation writes the CSR stval.
RULE 39: The write of the CSR stval is performed as part of the trap entry actions for a trap taken into HS-mode.
RULE 40: In all transformed instructions, the Addr. Offset field that replaces the instruction's rs1 field in bits 19:15 is the positive difference between the faulting virtual address written to stval and the original virtual address.
RULE 41: The positive difference between the faulting virtual address written to stval and the original virtual address can be nonzero only for a misaligned memory access.
RULE 42: When the hardware writes an address to the stval CSR during exception handling, pointer masking is applied to that write if pointer masking is applicable to that address.
RULE 43: During exception delivery, the hardware applies pointer masking to any address written into stval if pointer masking is applicable to that address.
RULE 44: In M-mode, accessing stval register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x143; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 45: In S-mode, accessing stval register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x143; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 46: In U-mode, accessing stval register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x143; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 47: In M-mode, setting stval.VALUE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x143, a0; csrr a1, 0x143; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 48: In M-mode, accessing stval register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x143; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 49: In M-mode, accessing stval register while Ssdbltrp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssdbltrp; csrr a0, 0x143; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 50: In M-mode, accessing stval register while Zicfilp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicfilp; csrr a0, 0x143; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 51: In M-mode, accessing stval register while Zicfiss extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicfiss; csrr a0, 0x143; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: stvec
NUMBER: 0x105
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..2=BASE, 1..0=MODE
EXTENSIONS: H, Ssdbltrp
RULE 1: stvec is a Supervisor-mode CSR.
RULE 2: stvec is readable and writable.
RULE 3: For a double trap that originates in VS-mode, M-mode should use an MRET to resume execution at the address contained in the stvec register.
RULE 4: stvec is an SXLEN-bit read/write register that holds trap vector configuration consisting of a vector base address (BASE) and a vector mode (MODE).
RULE 5: In the CSR layout, bits SXLEN-1 down to 2 of stvec hold the BASE field and are WARL, and bits 1-0 of stvec hold the MODE field and are WARL.
RULE 6: The BASE field of stvec must contain a 4-byte-aligned virtual or physical address.
RULE 7: The stvec CSR stores only bits XLEN-1 through 2 of the BASE address, and the lower two bits are implicitly zeroed to form an XLEN-bit address that is always 4-byte aligned.
RULE 8: When the MODE field of stvec is set to Direct, all traps into supervisor mode cause the program counter to be set to the address contained in the BASE field of stvec.
RULE 9: When the MODE field of stvec is set to Vectored, all synchronous exceptions into supervisor mode cause the program counter to be set to the address contained in the BASE field of stvec.
RULE 10: A supervisor-mode timer interrupt causes the program counter to be set to stvec.BASE plus 0x14.
RULE 11: When the V bit in mstatus is 1, any instruction that reads or writes the supervisor register stvec actually accesses the VS-mode register vstvec instead.
RULE 12: When the V bit in mstatus is 0, the VS-mode register vstvec does not affect the operation of the supervisor register stvec, which therefore functions normally.
RULE 13: The BASE field of vstvec, occupying bits VSXLEN-1 down to 2, defines the virtual supervisor trap vector base address that is used by the supervisor register stvec when V=1.
RULE 14: The MODE field of vstvec, occupying bits 1 down to 0, defines the virtual supervisor trap vector mode that is used by the supervisor register stvec when V=1.
RULE 15: The BASE field of vstvec is a WARL field.
RULE 16: The MODE field of vstvec is a WARL field.
RULE 17: Pointer masking is not applied when software writes to stvec.
RULE 18: Software may write a tagged or an untagged address to stvec.
RULE 19: During trap delivery, the address taken from stvec for the trap handler is used without pointer masking.
RULE 20: In M-mode, accessing stvec register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x105; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 21: In S-mode, accessing stvec register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x105; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 22: In U-mode, accessing stvec register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x105; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 23: In M-mode, setting stvec.BASE (bit 2) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x4) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4; csrs 0x105, a0; csrr a1, 0x105; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x4].
RULE 24: In M-mode, setting stvec.MODE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x105, a0; csrr a1, 0x105; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 25: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the stvec register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x105, a0; csrr a1, 0x105; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 26: In M-mode, accessing stvec register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x105; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 27: In M-mode, accessing stvec register while Ssdbltrp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssdbltrp; csrr a0, 0x105; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: tdata1
NUMBER: 0x7a1
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: XLEN
FIELDS: 63..60=TYPE, 59..59=DMODE, 58..0=DATA
EXTENSIONS: Zicbom, Zicbop, Zicboz
RULE 1: Type 6 address-match triggers, identified by tdata1.type = 6 and mcontrol6.select = 0, should be supported.
RULE 2: Type 2 address/data-match triggers, identified by tdata1.type = 2, should be unsupported.
RULE 3: When the Zicboz extension is implemented, implementing address-match triggers that satisfy tdata1.type = 6 and mcontrol6.select = 0 should be mandatory.
RULE 4: When the Zicbom extension is implemented, Type 6 data-match triggers, identified by tdata1.type = 6 and mcontrol6.select = 1, should be unsupported.
RULE 5: When the Zicboz extension is implemented, Type 6 data-match triggers, identified by tdata1.type = 6 and mcontrol6.select = 1, should be supported.
RULE 6: When the Zicbop extension is implemented, Type 6 data-match triggers, identified by tdata1.type = 6 and mcontrol6.select = 1, should be unsupported.
RULE 7: tdata1 is a Machine-Read/Write (MRW) control and status register (CSR).
RULE 8: In M-mode, accessing tdata1 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x7a1; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 9: In S-mode, accessing tdata1 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x7a1; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 10: In U-mode, accessing tdata1 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x7a1; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 11: In M-mode, setting tdata1.TYPE (bit 60) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1000000000000000; csrs 0x7a1, a0; csrr a1, 0x7a1; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1000000000000000].
RULE 12: In M-mode, setting tdata1.DMODE (bit 59) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x800000000000000; csrs 0x7a1, a0; csrr a1, 0x7a1; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 13: In M-mode, accessing tdata1 register while Zicbom extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicbom; csrr a0, 0x7a1; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 14: In M-mode, accessing tdata1 register while Zicbop extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicbop; csrr a0, 0x7a1; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 15: In M-mode, accessing tdata1 register while Zicboz extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicboz; csrr a0, 0x7a1; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: tdata2
NUMBER: 0x7a2
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: XLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=DATA
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The tdata2 CSR is a Machine-level Read/Write (MRW) register.
RULE 2: In M-mode, accessing tdata2 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x7a2; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 3: In S-mode, accessing tdata2 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x7a2; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 4: In U-mode, accessing tdata2 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x7a2; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 5: In M-mode, setting tdata2.DATA (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x7a2, a0; csrr a1, 0x7a2; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].

REGISTER: tdata3
NUMBER: 0x7a3
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: XLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=DATA
EXTENSIONS: Zicbom, Zicbop, Zicboz
RULE 1: tdata3 has MRW privilege, meaning it is machine-mode readable and writable.
RULE 2: In M-mode, accessing tdata3 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x7a3; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 3: In S-mode, accessing tdata3 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x7a3; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 4: In U-mode, accessing tdata3 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x7a3; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 5: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the tdata3 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x7a3, a0; csrr a1, 0x7a3; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 6: In M-mode, accessing tdata3 register while Zicbom extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicbom; csrr a0, 0x7a3; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 7: In M-mode, accessing tdata3 register while Zicbop extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicbop; csrr a0, 0x7a3; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 8: In M-mode, accessing tdata3 register while Zicboz extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicboz; csrr a0, 0x7a3; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: time
NUMBER: 0xc01
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The TIME CSR must be read-only and may be accessed using the csrrs canonical form or any of the read-only CSR instruction forms based on CSRRC, CSRRSI, or CSRRCI.
RULE 2: On implementations with XLEN ≥ 64, the RDTIME pseudoinstruction reads the full 64-bit TIME counter.
RULE 3: The 64-bit TIME counter increments by one for each tick of the real-time clock.
RULE 4: The real-time clocks of all harts must be synchronized to within one tick of the TIME clock.
RULE 5: Implementations must make it appear to software that the TIME values observed on different harts differ by no more than one tick.
RULE 6: Software must observe TIME values across harts to be monotonically nondecreasing.
RULE 7: Software reading TIME more frequently should observe monotonically nondecreasing values and should see a new TIME value at least once every 10 ns.
RULE 8: If the TW bit in mstatus is set, a WRS.NTO instruction is executed in any privilege mode other than M mode, and the instruction does not complete within an implementation-specific bounded time limit, then the WRS.NTO instruction causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 9: If execution is in VS or VU mode, the VTW bit in hstatus is set, the TW bit in mstatus is clear, and a WRS.NTO instruction does not complete within an implementation-specific bounded time limit, then the WRS.NTO instruction causes a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 10: When a WRS.NTO instruction is executed in U-mode and the governing TW bit is 0, the instruction does not cause an illegal-instruction exception regardless of any time limit.
RULE 11: The stall caused by a WRS.STO instruction is limited by an implementation-defined short time limit; the stall may continue only while the short duration since the start of the stall has not elapsed.
RULE 12: Once the short time elapses, the stall condition is no longer satisfied and the hart may resume execution, subject to other stall conditions.
RULE 13: A WRS.NTO instruction that does not complete within an implementation-specific bounded time limit, when the relevant TW or VTW conditions apply, triggers either an illegal-instruction exception or a virtual-instruction exception depending on the privilege mode and status bits.
RULE 14: The CSR at address 0xC01 named time is an unprivileged read-only register that provides the timer value for the RDTIME instruction.
RULE 15: The time CSR has URO privilege, meaning it is readable by unprivileged code and cannot be written by any privilege level.
RULE 16: The htimedelta CSR provides the lower 32 bits of the virtual supervisor time delta, is readable and writable in hypervisor mode, and is located at CSR address 0x605 (with the upper 32 bits at address 0x615 for RV64).
RULE 17: The vstimecmp CSR holds the lower 32 bits of the virtual supervisor timer compare value, is readable and writable in hypervisor mode, and resides at CSR address 0x24D.
RULE 18: When the time CSR is wider than XLEN bits, an explicit read of time returns its least-significant XLEN bits and an explicit write to time modifies only its least-significant XLEN bits, leaving the upper bits unchanged.
RULE 19: Accesses to the timeh CSR read or modify bits 63:32 of the corresponding 64-bit time CSR.
RULE 20: When XLEN = 64, an attempt to access the timeh CSR typically raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 21: The time register's TW bit is read-only 0 when no modes less privileged than M exist.
RULE 22: The MTIP bit in the mip register is read-only and is cleared by writing to the memory-mapped machine-mode timer compare register that holds a time value.
RULE 23: If the stimecmp (supervisor-mode timer compare) register is implemented, the STIP bit is read-only in the mip register and reflects the supervisor-level timer interrupt signal generated from the stimecmp time comparison.
RULE 24: The supervisor-level timer interrupt signal is cleared by writing the stimecmp register with a value greater than the current time value.
RULE 25: When the TM bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the time CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 26: When the TM bit in the mcounteren register is set, reading the time CSR in the next implemented lower-privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode) succeeds.
RULE 27: In harts that implement U-mode, the mcounteren register must be implemented, its fields are WARL and may be read-only zero, and a zero TM field causes a read of the time CSR in S-mode or U-mode to raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 28: Changing the accessibility settings of the time CSR does not affect the underlying time counter, which continues to increment even when the time CSR is not accessible.
RULE 29: Because the mtime counter can be shared between multiple cores, it cannot be inhibited with the mcountinhibit mechanism.
RULE 30: If the Sstc extension is not implemented, the time-related STCE bit is read-only zero.
RULE 31: When the time-related STCE bit is set to one, it enables the stimecmp time-compare register for S-mode.
RULE 32: When the Sstc extension is implemented and the time-related STCE bit in menvcfg is zero, an attempt to access the stimecmp register in any privilege mode other than M-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 33: When the Sstc extension is implemented and the time-related STCE bit in menvcfg is zero, the time-related STCE bit in henvcfg is read-only zero.
RULE 34: When the Sstc extension is implemented and the time-related STCE bit in menvcfg is zero, the STIP time-interrupt pending bits in mip and sip revert to their defined behavior as if the extension is not implemented.
RULE 35: If the H extension is implemented and the time-related STCE bit in menvcfg is zero while the Sstc extension is present, the hip.VSTIP time-virtual interrupt pending bit also reverts to its defined behavior as if the extension is not implemented.
RULE 36: Platforms must provide a memory-mapped machine-mode read-write time register called mtime that increments at a constant frequency.
RULE 37: The time register mtime will wrap around when its count overflows.
RULE 38: A machine timer interrupt becomes pending whenever the time register mtime contains a value greater than or equal to mtimecmp, treating the values as unsigned integers.
RULE 39: The machine timer interrupt remains pending until mtimecmp becomes greater than the time register mtime.
RULE 40: If the result of the comparison between the time register mtime and mtimecmp changes, the change is guaranteed to be reflected in MTIP eventually, but not necessarily immediately.
RULE 41: Software should be written to assume that a spurious timer interrupt may occur if an interrupt handler increments mtimecmp and then immediately returns, because the MTIP flag may not yet have cleared after the time register mtime change.
RULE 42: In RV64, naturally aligned 64-bit memory accesses to the time register mtime are supported and are atomic.
RULE 43: The time CSR is a read-only shadow of the memory-mapped time register mtime.
RULE 44: When the time register mtime changes, the updated value is guaranteed to be reflected in the time and timeh CSRs eventually, but not necessarily immediately.
RULE 45: While the privilege mode is M or S and siselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, an illegal-instruction exception is raised for any attempt to access a sireg when siselect equals 0x41, the selector for the time register.
RULE 46: When the Sstc extension is implemented, the sip.STIP bit reflects the timer interrupt signal that is generated based on the time register and the stimecmp value.
RULE 47: When the Sstc extension is implemented, writing stimecmp with a value less than or equal to the time register causes the sip.STIP bit to be set.
RULE 48: When the Sstc extension is implemented, writing stimecmp with a value greater than the time register causes the sip.STIP bit to be cleared.
RULE 49: When the TM bit in the scounteren register is clear, a read of the time CSR in U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 50: When the TM bit in the scounteren register is set, a read of the time CSR in U-mode is permitted.
RULE 51: If the TM bit in the scounteren register is read-only zero, a read of the time CSR in U-mode causes an exception.
RULE 52: U-mode may only access the time CSR when both the TM bit in scounteren and the TM bit in mcounteren are set.
RULE 53: When the Interrupt bit in scause is 1 and the Exception Code field equals 5, the scause register indicates a supervisor timer interrupt.
RULE 54: When the Interrupt bit in scause is 1 and the Exception Code field equals 13, the scause register indicates a counter-overflow interrupt, which is a time-related event.
RULE 55: A supervisor timer interrupt becomes pending, as reflected in the STIP bit in the mip and sip registers, whenever time contains a value greater than or equal to stimecmp, with the comparison performed as unsigned integers.
RULE 56: If the result of the comparison between time and stimecmp changes, the change is guaranteed to be reflected in STIP eventually, but not necessarily immediately.
RULE 57: The interrupt remains posted until stimecmp becomes greater than time, typically as a result of writing stimecmp.
RULE 58: The Sstc extension adds the stimecmp CSR at S-level as a time compare register.
RULE 59: The Sstc extension adds the vstimecmp CSR at VS-level as a time compare register.
RULE 60: The hip.VSTIP bit is set when vstimecmp is written with a value less than or equal to the sum of time and htimedelta, truncated to 64 bits.
RULE 61: The sum of time and htimedelta is truncated to 64 bits when determining whether a vstimecmp write value is less than or equal to that sum.
RULE 62: When the Sstc extension is not implemented, the time-enable STCE bit in henvcfg is read-only zero.
RULE 63: Setting the STCE bit to one enables the virtual time-compare register (vstimecmp) for VS-mode.
RULE 64: If the STCE bit in henvcfg is zero and V=1, any access to the stimecmp (vstimecmp) register raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 65: When the STCE bit in henvcfg is zero, the VSTIP field in hip reverts to its defined behavior as if the time-compare extension is not implemented.
RULE 66: When the TM bit in the hcounteren register is clear, an attempt to read the time register while V=1 will cause a virtual-instruction exception if the same bit in the mcounteren register is 1.
RULE 67: When the TM bit in the hcounteren register is set, access to the time register is permitted when V=1 unless prevented for some other reason.
RULE 68: In VU-mode, the time register is not readable unless the TM bit is set in both the hcounteren register and the scounteren register.
RULE 69: If a hcounteren TM bit is implemented as read-only zero, reads to the time register will cause a virtual-instruction exception when V=1.
RULE 70: The htimedelta CSR is a 64-bit read/write register that contains the delta between the value of the time CSR and the value returned in VS-mode or VU-mode.
RULE 71: Reading the time CSR while executing in VS-mode or VU-mode returns the sum of the actual time CSR value and the contents of htimedelta.
RULE 72: Overflow is ignored when summing the time CSR value and htimedelta, allowing large htimedelta values to represent negative time offsets.
RULE 73: When XLEN=64, the htimedeltah CSR does not exist, so the time CSR delta is accessed only via htimedelta.
RULE 74: A virtual supervisor timer interrupt becomes pending (the VSTIP bit is set) whenever the unsigned 64-bit sum of time and htimedelta, truncated to 64 bits, is greater than or equal to vstimecmp.
RULE 75: The virtual supervisor timer interrupt remains posted until vstimecmp becomes greater than the unsigned sum of time and htimedelta, typically after writing a new vstimecmp value.
RULE 76: The virtual supervisor timer interrupt will be taken according to standard interrupt enable and delegation rules while V = 1, based on the current time value used in the (time + htimedelta) comparison.
RULE 77: A supervisor timer interrupt, which is a time interrupt, is indicated by interrupt code 5.
RULE 78: A virtual supervisor timer interrupt, which is a time interrupt, is indicated by interrupt code 6.
RULE 79: A machine timer interrupt, which is a time interrupt, is indicated by interrupt code 7.
RULE 80: A counter-overflow interrupt, which may be raised when the time counter wraps, is indicated by exception code 13.
RULE 81: When XLEN>32, any attempt to access the high-half time CSR always raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 82: In VS-mode, an attempt to access the time CSR raises a virtual-instruction exception if the corresponding bit in hcounteren is 0 while the same bit in mcounteren is 1.
RULE 83: In VU-mode, an attempt to access the time CSR raises a virtual-instruction exception if either the hcounteren or scounteren bit for time is 0 while the mcounteren bit for time is 1.
RULE 84: In M-mode, accessing time register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc01; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 85: In S-mode, accessing time register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc01; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 86: In U-mode, accessing time register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc01; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 87: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the time register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc01, a0; csrr a1, 0xc01; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: tselect
NUMBER: 0x7a0
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: XLEN

EXTENSIONS: Sdtrig

REGISTER: vcsr
NUMBER: 0x00f
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 2..1=VXRM, 0..0=VXSAT
EXTENSIONS: V
RULE 1: vcsr has URW privilege.
RULE 2: The vector control and status register (vcsr) includes a field that reflects the vector fixed-point rounding-mode register (vxrm).
RULE 3: The vcsr register's least-significant bit (vcsr[0]) mirrors the vxsat bit, indicating whether a fixed-point instruction has saturated an output value to fit the destination format.
RULE 4: The register vcsr is an XLEN-bit-wide CSR.
RULE 5: Bits XLEN-1 through 3 of vcsr are reserved.
RULE 6: Bits 2 and 1 of vcsr implement the fixed-point rounding mode.
RULE 7: Bit 0 of vcsr implements the fixed-point accrued saturation flag.
RULE 8: The vcsr register has URW privilege, allowing user-mode read and write access.
RULE 9: If the v registers are implemented, the VS field, which encodes vcsr, shall not be read-only zero.
RULE 10: When VS = Off, any attempt to read vcsr raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: When VS = Off, any attempt to write vcsr raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: When VS is Initial, Clean, or Dirty, executing a read of vcsr succeeds and leaves the VS field unchanged.
RULE 13: When VS is Initial, Clean, or Dirty, executing a write to vcsr that changes its value causes the VS field to transition to Dirty (or remain Dirty).
RULE 14: In M-mode, accessing vcsr register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x00f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 15: In S-mode, accessing vcsr register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x00f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 16: In U-mode, accessing vcsr register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x00f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 17: In M-mode, setting vcsr.VXRM (bit 1) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2; csrs 0x00f, a0; csrr a1, 0x00f; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2].
RULE 18: In M-mode, setting vcsr.VXSAT (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x00f, a0; csrr a1, 0x00f; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].

RULE 20: In M-mode, accessing vcsr register while V extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: V; csrr a0, 0x00f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: vl
NUMBER: 0xc20
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The vl CSR has URO privilege, meaning it is unprivileged and read-only.
RULE 2: Any element in the tail of a mask result can also be written with the value the mask-producing operation would have calculated with vl = VLMAX, except for mask-load instructions.
RULE 3: For mask-logical instructions and the mask-manipulation instructions vmsbf.m, vmsif.m, and vmsof.m, any element in the tail of the result can be written with the value the mask-producing operation would have calculated with vl = VLEN, SEW = 8, and LMUL = 8.
RULE 4: The vl CSR is an XLEN-bit-wide, read-only register.
RULE 5: vl can only be updated by the vset{i}vl{i} instructions and by the fault-only-first vector load instruction variants.
RULE 6: A vector implementation with VLEN = 32 that supports SEW = 8 must implement at least six bits in vl to represent the values 0-32 because VLEN = 32, LMUL = 8, SEW = 8 yields VLMAX = 32.
RULE 7: The vector extension MUST ensure that after reset the value of vl can be read and later restored with a single vsetvl instruction.
RULE 8: At reset the implementation SHOULD set vl to zero.
RULE 9: The hardware writes to the vl CSR the number of elements it will process per iteration, which may be smaller than the AVL and is determined by the microarchitectural implementation and the current vtype setting.
RULE 10: The vset{i}vl{i} instructions set both the vtype CSR and the vl CSR according to their arguments and also write the resulting vl value into the destination register rd.
RULE 11: The vsetvli instruction writes the newly computed vl value to rd, takes the AVL from rs1, and uses the vtypei operand to specify the new vtype setting.
RULE 12: The vsetivli instruction writes the newly computed vl value to rd, takes the AVL from the immediate field uimm, and uses the vtypei operand to specify the new vtype setting.
RULE 13: The vsetvl instruction writes the newly computed vl value to rd, takes the AVL from rs1, and takes the new vtype value from rs2.
RULE 14: The hardware provides the vl value to software through a general-purpose register.
RULE 15: If the vtype value is not supported by the implementation, then the vl register is set to zero.
RULE 16: If rd is not a destination register and rs1 is not x0, the instruction performs normal strip mining and sets vl based on the AVL value in the rs1 register.
RULE 17: If rd is a destination register and rs1 is x0, the instruction sets vl to VLMAX.
RULE 18: If both rd and rs1 are x0, the instruction leaves vl unchanged (while vtype may change).
RULE 19: When rs1 is not x0, the instruction writes the newly computed vl value to the integer register specified by rd.
RULE 20: When rs1 is x0 and rd is not x0, the instruction writes VLMAX to vl and also writes VLMAX to the integer register specified by rd.
RULE 21: When both rs1 and rd are x0, the instruction uses the current vl as the AVL, computes a new vl value, writes it to vl, and does not write to any integer register.
RULE 22: The current vl value can be read from the vl CSR.
RULE 23: If AVL ≤ VLMAX then vl = AVL.
RULE 24: If AVL < 2 * VLMAX then ceil(AVL / 2) ≤ vl ≤ VLMAX.
RULE 25: If AVL ≥ 2 * VLMAX then vl = VLMAX.
RULE 26: For identical input AVL and VLMAX values, the resulting vl is deterministic on any given implementation.
RULE 27: If a value read from vl is later used as the AVL argument to vsetvl and the resultant VLMAX equals the VLMAX at the time vl was read, then the new vl equals the previously read vl value.
RULE 28: If AVL = 0 then vl = 0.
RULE 29: If AVL > 0 then vl > 0.
RULE 30: vl is never greater than VLMAX.
RULE 31: vl is never greater than AVL.
RULE 32: The hardware updates the destination integer register (a3) with the current vl, which equals the number of elements for that iteration.
RULE 33: The integer register supplied as the second operand to vsetvli (a0) provides the total element count that the hardware uses to compute vl for the iteration.
RULE 34: For the vector-unit-stride mask load (vlm.v) and mask store (vsm.v) instructions, the effective vector length evl is defined as the ceiling of vl divided by 8 (EMUL = 1).
RULE 35: The vlm.v and vsm.v instructions respect the vill field in vtype because they depend on vtype indirectly through its constraints on vl.
RULE 36: If element 0 raises an exception, vl must not be modified and a trap is taken.
RULE 37: If an element with an index greater than zero raises an exception, the corresponding trap is not taken and vl must be reduced to the index of that element.
RULE 38: If vstart = 0 and vl > 0, at least one element must be processed.
RULE 39: When a fault-only-first instruction takes a trap due to an interrupt, implementations should not reduce vl and should instead set a vstart value.
RULE 40: When a fault-only-first instruction would trigger a debug data-watchpoint trap on any element after the first, implementations should not reduce vl but should trigger the debug trap.
RULE 41: For fault-only-first segment loads, when an exception is detected partway through accessing a subsequent segment, vl is reduced to the index of that segment.
RULE 42: For fault-only-first segment loads, when an exception is detected partway through accessing the zeroth segment, a trap is taken and the architecture does not define any change to vl.
RULE 43: The csrr instruction that reads the vl CSR transfers the current vl register value to the destination integer register.
RULE 44: The vsetvli instruction with rd = x0 writes the value from the source integer register into the vl register, thereby restoring vl.
RULE 45: If vl equals 0, then any vector floating-point instruction that uses the frm field containing an invalid rounding mode—regardless of whether the instruction depends on the rounding mode—has a reserved effect.
RULE 46: If vstart is greater than or equal to vl, then any vector floating-point instruction that uses the frm field containing an invalid rounding mode—regardless of whether the instruction depends on the rounding mode—has a reserved effect.
RULE 47: The vfmerge.vfm instruction processes body elements starting at the index specified by vstart and continues through all indices that are less than the current vector length held in the vl register.
RULE 48: The selection of body elements for the vfmerge.vfm instruction is independent of the mask value and is limited only by the current vector length contained in the vl register.
RULE 49: If vl = 0, the instruction performs no operation and does not update the destination register.
RULE 50: When the source and destination scalar operands reside in different vector registers and vl = 0, the instruction does not copy the source into the destination.
RULE 51: The vfredosum instruction must sum the floating-point values in element order, starting with the scalar in vs1[0] and then adding the elements vs2[0] through vs2[vl-1], where vl is the current vector length.
RULE 52: If vl equals zero, no additions are performed and the scalar in vs1[0] is simply copied to the destination register without canonicalizing NaN values and without setting any exception flags.
RULE 53: When the vector mask vm is zero, elements that would be selected by the current vl are masked-off and do not affect the result or the exception flags.
RULE 54: When vl = 0, the vcpop.m instruction writes the value 0 to the integer register x[rd].
RULE 55: When vl = 0, the vfirst.m instruction writes the destination integer register with the value -1 because no mask elements are active.
RULE 56: After execution of the instruction `vsetvli x0, t0, e8, m8, ta, ma`, the register vl is set to the maximum-length vectors of bytes.
RULE 57: The instruction `csrr t1, vl` copies the current value of the register vl into integer register t1.
RULE 58: The vid.v instruction writes each element's index to the destination vector register group for element positions ranging from 0 up to vl-1 inclusive.
RULE 59: vmv.x.s performs its operation even if vstart ≥ vl or vl = 0.
RULE 60: vmv.s.x performs no operation and does not update the destination register when vstart ≥ vl.
RULE 61: vmv.s.x updates no elements in the destination vector register group when vl = 0, regardless of vstart.
RULE 62: vfmv.f.s performs its operation even when vstart ≥ vl.
RULE 63: vfmv.f.s performs its operation even when vl = 0.
RULE 64: vfmv.s.f performs no operation and does not update the destination register when vstart ≥ vl.
RULE 65: When vl = 0, vfmv.s.f updates no elements in the destination vector register group regardless of the value of vstart.
RULE 66: If vstart is greater than or equal to vl, the instruction performs no operation and leaves the destination vector register unchanged.
RULE 67: When vl is zero, no elements are updated in the destination vector register group, regardless of vstart.
RULE 68: For the vslideup instruction, the architectural register vl specifies the maximum number of destination elements that may be written.
RULE 69: If OFFSET is less than vl, destination elements whose indices range from OFFSET through vl-1 are written provided they are unmasked.
RULE 70: For any element index i satisfying 0 ≤ i < min(vl, max(vstart, OFFSET)), the destination element is left unchanged.
RULE 71: For any element index i satisfying max(vstart, OFFSET) ≤ i < vl, the destination element is written as vd[i] = vs2[i-OFFSET] when the corresponding v0.mask[i] bit is enabled.
RULE 72: For any element index i satisfying vl ≤ i < VLMAX, the tail handling policy defined by the architecture is applied.
RULE 73: For vslidedown instructions, vl specifies the maximum number of destination elements that may be written.
RULE 74: Elements with indices i satisfying vl ≤ i < VLMAX are handled according to the current tail policy.
RULE 75: If vstart < vl and 0 ≤ i + OFFSET < VLMAX, then src[i] is set to vs2[i + OFFSET].
RULE 76: If vstart < vl and VLMAX ≤ i + OFFSET, then src[i] is set to zero.
RULE 77: If vstart < vl and 0 ≤ i < vstart, then the destination element i remains unchanged.
RULE 78: If vstart ≤ i < vl and the mask bit v0.mask[i] is enabled, then vd[i] is written with src[i].
RULE 79: If vl ≤ i < VLMAX, then the destination element follows the tail policy.
RULE 80: The vl register specifies the maximum number of destination vector register elements that are updated with source values, and elements whose indices are greater than or equal to vl are handled according to the current tail policy.
RULE 81: For the vslide1up instruction, when vl > 0 and the element index i is less than vstart, the destination element remains unchanged.
RULE 82: For the vslide1up instruction, when vl > 0 and the element index i equals vstart, the destination element vd[i] is set to x[rs1] if the corresponding v0.mask[i] bit is enabled.
RULE 83: For the vslide1up instruction, when vl > 0 and max(vstart, 1) ≤ i < vl, the destination element vd[i] is set to vs2[i-1] if the corresponding v0.mask[i] bit is enabled.
RULE 84: For the vslide1up instruction, when vl > 0 and vl ≤ i < VLMAX, the element's behavior follows the current tail policy.
RULE 85: For the vslide1up instruction, the active vl − 1 elements are copied from index i in the source vector register group to index i + 1 in the destination vector register group.
RULE 86: The vl register specifies the maximum number of destination vector register elements that the vslide1down instruction may write with source values, with any elements beyond vl handled by the current tail policy.
RULE 87: The vslide1down instruction copies the first vl-1 active elements from index i+1 of the source vector register group to index i of the destination vector register group.
RULE 88: The vslide1down instruction writes the scalar x register argument to the destination vector element at index vl-1 when that element is active.
RULE 89: When the destination element at index vl-1 is not active, the vslide1down instruction updates that element according to the current mask-agnostic/undisturbed policy.
RULE 90: For every index i satisfying vstart ≤ i < vl-1, the vslide1down operation performs vd[i] = vs2[i+1] if the corresponding v0.mask[i] is enabled.
RULE 91: For the index i equal to vl-1 and satisfying vstart ≤ i, the vslide1down operation performs vd[vl-1] = x[rs1] if the corresponding v0.mask[i] is enabled.
RULE 92: For all indices i with vl ≤ i < VLMAX, the element in the destination vector register follows the current tail policy.
RULE 93: The source vector may be accessed at any element index that is less than VLMAX irrespective of the current value of vl.
RULE 94: When writing to the destination register, the number of elements written must not exceed vl, and any elements beyond vl are processed according to the current tail policy.
RULE 95: The usual property that no elements are written if vstart ≥ vl does not apply to these instructions.
RULE 96: The usual property that the instructions are reserved if vstart exceeds the largest element index for the current vtype setting does not apply to these instructions.
RULE 97: For these instructions, the reservation condition is vstart ≥ evl rather than any condition involving vl.
RULE 98: When an operand is a vector of element groups, the vl setting MUST correspond to an integer multiple of the element group size.
RULE 99: When an operand is a vector of element groups, any vl value that is not an integer multiple of the element group size is reserved.
RULE 100: When element group instructions are present and the AVL value is greater than VLMAX, the vl value MUST be set to either VLMAX or a positive integer multiple of EGSMAX, where EGSMAX is the largest element group size supported by the implementation.
RULE 101: The number of element groups operated upon by a vector instruction equals vl divided by the element group size (EGS).
RULE 102: When LMUL multiplied by VLEN is less than the Element Group Width (EGW) for an element-group instruction, the processor raises an illegal-instruction exception even if vl equals zero.
RULE 103: vl controls how many element groups are processed.
RULE 104: On implementations with VLEN = 64, the LMUL required for SHA-512 vector instructions (vsha2*) is expressed as vl divided by 2.
RULE 105: On implementations with VLEN = 32, the LMUL required for SM3 vector instructions (vsm3*) is expressed as vl divided by 4.
RULE 106: When EGS = 4 for SEW = 32, vl MUST be a multiple of 4.
RULE 107: The number of element groups to be processed equals vl divided by EGS.
RULE 108: vl MUST be set to the number of SEW-32 elements to be processed.
RULE 109: vl MUST be a multiple of EGS-4.
RULE 110: The eg_len value calculated from vl determines the number of element groups processed by the VAESZ.vs instruction.
RULE 111: During execution of the VROL_VV instruction, the current value of the vl register determines the upper bound of the element-wise loop, which iterates over element indices i from vstart up to vl-1.
RULE 112: During execution of the VROL_VX instruction, the current value of the vl register determines the upper bound of the loop, which iterates over element indices i from vstart up to vl-1.
RULE 113: In the execution of VWSLL.VV, the vl register is read to set the loop's upper bound so that element indices i iterate from vstart up to but not including vl.
RULE 114: In the execution of VWSLL.VX, the vl register is read to set the loop's upper bound so that element indices i iterate from vstart up to but not including vl.
RULE 115: In the execution of VWSLL.VI, the vl register is read to set the loop's upper bound so that element indices i iterate from vstart up to but not including vl.
RULE 116: For VWSLL.VV, VWSLL.VX, and VWSLL.VI, elements with indices i >= vl are not processed.
RULE 117: The vl CSR is classified as URO, meaning it is unprivileged read-only.
RULE 118: If VS is Off, a read of the vl CSR causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 119: If VS is Off, a write to the vl CSR causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 120: If VS is Initial, vl should contain its defined initial constant value.
RULE 121: If VS is Clean, vl contains the value saved at the most recent context save/restore.
RULE 122: The SD bit is read-only and is set when VS is Dirty; consequently, if vl makes VS Dirty, the SD bit will be 1.
RULE 123: In M-mode, accessing vl register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc20; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 124: In S-mode, accessing vl register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc20; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 125: In U-mode, accessing vl register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc20; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: vlenb
NUMBER: 0xc22
MODE: U-mode

FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: V
RULE 1: vlenb is a URO (unprivileged read-only) CSR.

RULE 3: The XLEN-bit-wide read-only CSR vlenb holds the value VLEN/8, which represents the vector register length in bytes.
RULE 4: Software can determine the number of bytes transferred by reading the vlenb register.
RULE 5: The vlenb CSR has privilege level URO, indicating that it is unprivileged and read-only.
RULE 6: If the vector registers v0-v31 are implemented, then the VS field, which encodes the state of vlenb, shall not be read-only zero.
