REGISTER: vscause
NUMBER: 0x242
MODE: VS-mode
WIDTH: VSXLEN
FIELDS: 63..63=INT, 62..0=CODE
EXTENSIONS: H
RULE 1: The vscause register is accessed at privilege level HRW (hypervisor-read/write).
RULE 2: When a virtual supervisor external interrupt with interrupt code 10 is delegated to VS-mode, the trap taken in VS-mode writes the supervisor external interrupt code 9 into the vscause register.
RULE 3: When a virtual supervisor timer interrupt with interrupt code 6 is delegated to VS-mode, the trap taken in VS-mode writes the supervisor timer interrupt code 5 into the vscause register.
RULE 4: When a virtual supervisor software interrupt with interrupt code 2 is delegated to VS-mode, the trap taken in VS-mode writes the supervisor software interrupt code 1 into the vscause register.
RULE 5: The translation of a delegated virtual supervisor interrupt to a supervisor interrupt, and the corresponding vscause write, occurs only when the interrupt is first delegated to HS-mode via the mideleg CSR and the corresponding hideleg bit is set.
RULE 6: The vscause register is a VSXLEN-bit read/write register.
RULE 7: When the V field equals 1, vscause substitutes for scause so that any instruction that normally reads or writes scause instead accesses vscause.
RULE 8: When the V field equals 0, vscause does not directly affect the behavior of the machine.
RULE 9: The vscause register is a WLRL register.
RULE 10: The vscause register MUST be able to hold the same set of values that the scause register can hold.
RULE 11: Bit position VSXLEN-1 of vscause encodes the interrupt flag.
RULE 12: Bits VSXLEN-2 down to 0 of vscause form the Exception Code field.
RULE 13: The Exception Code field of vscause is a WLRL field.
RULE 14: When a trap is taken into VS-mode, the implementation writes the vscause CSR (along with the vsepc and vstval CSRs).
RULE 15: The access type for vscause is supervisor read/write (SRW).
RULE 16: When a trap is delegated to S-mode, the vscause register is written with the trap cause.
RULE 17: The interrupt cause number i reported in the vscause register corresponds to bit i in both the sip and sie registers.
RULE 18: vscause is an SXLEN-bit read-write CSR.
RULE 19: When a trap is taken into S-mode, the implementation writes vscause with a code indicating the event that caused the trap.
RULE 20: When a trap is not taken into S-mode, the implementation never writes vscause, although software may write it explicitly.
RULE 21: The Interrupt bit of vscause is set to 1 if the trap was caused by an interrupt.
RULE 22: The Exception Code field of vscause contains a code that identifies the last exception or interrupt.
RULE 23: The Exception Code field of vscause is required to implement bits 4-0, thereby supporting values 0 through 31.
RULE 24: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 1 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 0, the vscause value is reserved.
RULE 25: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 1 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 1, the vscause value indicates a supervisor software interrupt.
RULE 26: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 1 and the Exception Code field of vscause is any value from 2 to 4, the vscause value is reserved.
RULE 27: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 1 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 5, the vscause value indicates a supervisor timer interrupt.
RULE 28: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 1 and the Exception Code field of vscause is any value from 6 to 8, the vscause value is reserved.
RULE 29: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 1 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 9, the vscause value indicates a supervisor external interrupt.
RULE 30: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 1 and the Exception Code field of vscause is any value from 10 to 12, the vscause value is reserved.
RULE 31: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 1 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 13, the vscause value indicates a counter-overflow interrupt.
RULE 32: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 1 and the Exception Code field of vscause is any value from 14 to 15, the vscause value is reserved.
RULE 33: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 1 and the Exception Code field of vscause is any value greater than or equal to 16, the vscause value is designated for platform use.
RULE 34: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 0, the vscause value indicates an instruction address misaligned exception.
RULE 35: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 1, the vscause value indicates an instruction access fault.
RULE 36: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 2, the vscause value indicates an illegal instruction.
RULE 37: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 3, the vscause value indicates a breakpoint.
RULE 38: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 4, the vscause value indicates a load address misaligned exception.
RULE 39: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 5, the vscause value indicates a load access fault.
RULE 40: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 6, the vscause value indicates a store/AMO address misaligned exception.
RULE 41: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 7, the vscause value indicates a store/AMO access fault.
RULE 42: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 8, the vscause value indicates an environment call from U-mode.
RULE 43: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 9, the vscause value indicates an environment call from S-mode.
RULE 44: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is any value from 10 to 11, the vscause value is reserved.
RULE 45: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 12, the vscause value indicates an instruction page fault.
RULE 46: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 13, the vscause value indicates a load page fault.
RULE 47: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 14, the vscause value is reserved.
RULE 48: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 15, the vscause value indicates a store/AMO page fault.
RULE 49: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is any value from 16 to 17, the vscause value is reserved.
RULE 50: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 18, the vscause value indicates a software check.
RULE 51: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is 19, the vscause value indicates a hardware error.
RULE 52: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is any value from 20 to 23, the vscause value is reserved.
RULE 53: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is any value from 24 to 31, the vscause value is designated for custom use.
RULE 54: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is any value from 32 to 47, the vscause value is reserved.
RULE 55: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is any value from 48 to 63, the vscause value is designated for custom use.
RULE 56: If the Interrupt bit of vscause is 0 and the Exception Code field of vscause is any value greater than or equal to 64, the vscause value is reserved.
RULE 57: The vscause register is a supervisor register.
RULE 58: When the virtualization mode bit V is 0, accesses to vscause operate on the real vscause register.
RULE 59: The most-significant bit of vscause (bit VSXLEN-1) is the Interrupt flag.
RULE 60: Bits VSXLEN-2 down to 0 of vscause hold the Exception Code, which is a WLRL field.
RULE 61: When the most-significant interrupt bit of vscause is 1, the exception-code field values 0-15 and ≥16 are defined as: 0 reserved, 1 supervisor software interrupt, 2 virtual supervisor software interrupt, 3 machine software interrupt, 4 reserved, 5 supervisor timer interrupt, 6 virtual supervisor timer interrupt, 7 machine timer interrupt, 8 reserved, 9 supervisor external interrupt, 10 virtual supervisor external interrupt, 11 machine external interrupt, 12 supervisor guest external interrupt, 13 counter-overflow interrupt, 14-15 reserved, and codes ≥16 are designated for platform use.
RULE 62: When the interrupt bit of vscause is 0, the exception-code field values are defined as: 0 instruction address misaligned, 1 instruction access fault, 2 illegal instruction, 3 breakpoint, 4 load address misaligned, 5 load access fault, 6 store/AMO address misaligned, 7 store/AMO access fault, 8 environment call from U-mode or VU-mode, 9 environment call from HS-mode, 10 environment call from VS-mode, 11 environment call from M-mode, 12 instruction page fault, 13 load page fault, 14 reserved, 15 store/AMO page fault, 16 double trap, 17 reserved, 18 software check, 19 hardware error, 20 instruction guest-page fault, 21 load guest-page fault, 22 virtual instruction, 23 store/AMO guest-page fault, 24-31 designated for custom use, 32-47 reserved, 48-63 designated for custom use, and codes ≥64 reserved.
RULE 63: An environment-call from HS-mode causes vscause to contain exception code 9, and an environment-call from VS-mode causes vscause to contain exception code 10.
RULE 64: When the V bit in hstatus is 1 and the attempted instruction is HS-qualified but is prevented from executing because of insufficient privilege or because a supervisor or hypervisor CSR such as scounteren or hcounteren disables it, vscause is set to the virtual-instruction exception code 22 instead of the illegal-instruction code 2.
RULE 65: In VS-mode, attempting to access a non-high-half counter CSR while the corresponding bit in hcounteren is 0 and the same bit in mcounteren is 1 causes vscause to contain exception code 22.
RULE 66: In VU-mode, attempting to access a non-high-half counter CSR while either hcounteren or scounteren has the corresponding bit 0 and mcounteren has the corresponding bit 1 causes vscause to contain exception code 22.
RULE 67: In VS-mode or VU-mode, attempting to execute a hypervisor instruction (HLV, HLVX, HSV, or HFENCE) causes vscause to contain exception code 22.
RULE 68: In VS-mode or VU-mode, attempting to access an implemented non-high-half hypervisor CSR or VS CSR in a way that would be allowed in HS-mode assuming mstatus.TVM=0 causes vscause to contain exception code 22.
RULE 69: In VU-mode, attempting to access an implemented non-high-half supervisor CSR in a way that would be allowed in HS-mode assuming mstatus.TVM=0 causes vscause to contain exception code 22.
RULE 70: In VS-mode, attempting to execute SRET when hstatus.VTSR=1 causes vscause to contain exception code 22.
RULE 71: In VS-mode, attempting to execute an SFENCE.VMA or SINVAL.VMA instruction or to access satp when hstatus.VTVM=1 causes vscause to contain exception code 22.
RULE 72: When vscause reports a virtual-instruction exception (code 22), the mtval or stval register is written with the same faulting instruction value as for an illegal-instruction trap.
RULE 73: If an instruction can raise multiple synchronous exceptions, the exception with the highest priority according to Table 51 is the one whose code is placed in vscause.
RULE 74: When an instruction is prevented from executing because the FS or VS field in sstatus or vsstatus is zero, vscause is set to the illegal-instruction exception code 2 rather than to the virtual-instruction exception code 22.
RULE 75: The TSR and TVM fields in mstatus are ignored when determining which exception code is placed in vscause for VS-mode traps.
RULE 76: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the implementation writes the vscause CSR together with the sepc, stval, htval, and htinst CSRs.
RULE 77: In M-mode, accessing vscause register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x242; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 78: In VS-mode, accessing vscause register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_virtual; csrr a0, 0x242; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 79: In U-mode, accessing vscause register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x242; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 80: In M-mode, setting vscause.INT (bit 63) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x242, a0; csrr a1, 0x242; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000].
RULE 81: In M-mode, setting vscause.CODE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x242, a0; csrr a1, 0x242; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 82: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the vscause register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x242, a0; csrr a1, 0x242; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 83: In M-mode, accessing vscause register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x242; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: vsctrctl
NUMBER: 0x24e
MODE: VS-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 60..63=CUSTOM, 47..47=DIRLJMPINH, 46..46=INDLJMPINH, 45..45=RETINH, 44..44=CORSWAPINH, 43..43=DIRJMPINH, 42..42=INDJMPINH, 41..41=DIRCALLINH, 40..40=INDCALLINH, 37..37=TKBRINH, 36..36=NTBREN, 35..35=TRETINH, 34..34=INTRINH, 33..33=EXCINH, 12..12=LCOFIFRZ, 11..11=BPFRZ, 8..8=STE, 7..7=RASEMU, 1..1=S, 0..0=U
EXTENSIONS: H
RULE 1: The vsctrctl register is accessed with hypervisor-read/write (HRW) privilege.
RULE 2: If the H extension is implemented, vsctrctl is a 64-bit read/write register that is VS-mode's version of supervisor register sctrctl.
RULE 3: When V=1, vsctrctl substitutes for the usual sctrctl, so instructions that normally read or modify sctrctl actually access vsctrctl instead.
RULE 4: The S field of vsctrctl enables transfer recording in VS-mode.
RULE 5: The U field of vsctrctl enables transfer recording in VU-mode.
RULE 6: The STE field of vsctrctl enables recording of traps to VS-mode when the S field is 0.
RULE 7: The BPFRZ field of vsctrctl sets sctrstatus.FROZEN on a breakpoint exception that traps to VS-mode.
RULE 8: The LCOFIFRZ field of vsctrctl sets sctrstatus.FROZEN on a local-counter-overflow interrupt that traps to VS-mode.
RULE 9: If mstateen0.CTR=0 and the current privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, any attempt to access vsctrctl raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: When mstateen0.CTR=1 and hstateen0.CTR=0, VS-mode accesses to vsctrctl raise a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 11: The vsctrctl.S field determines whether the source mode is enabled for recording.
RULE 12: The vsctrctl.U field determines whether the target mode is enabled for recording.
RULE 13: The vsctrctl.STE field determines whether an external trap is recorded.
RULE 14: For any ctrctl field not explicitly listed, the corresponding value is taken from the vsctrctl register.
RULE 15: When a trap from VU-mode to HS-mode occurs with vsctrctl.U = 1 and sctrctl.S = 1, the decision whether the trap is recorded depends on the CTR configuration in vsctrctl rather than on sctrctl.
RULE 16: When a trap originates in VU-mode and targets VS-mode, the vsctrctl STE bit must be set.
RULE 17: When a trap originates in VU-mode and targets HS-mode, the vsctrctl STE bit must be set.
RULE 18: When a trap originates in VU-mode and targets M-mode, the vsctrctl STE bit must be set.
RULE 19: When the H extension is implemented, the freeze behavior for LCOFIs that trap to VSmode is determined by the value of vsctrctl.LCOFIFRZ.
RULE 20: When the H extension is implemented, the freeze behavior for breakpoint exceptions that trap to VSmode is determined by the value of vsctrctl.BPFRZ.
RULE 21: The determination of freeze behavior for virtual LCOFIs pended by a hypervisor is also based on vsctrctl.LCOFIFRZ.
RULE 22: If vsctrctl.LCOFIFRZ=1 and a guest uses the SBI Supervisor Software Events extension, the HS-mode handler emulates the freeze by setting sctrstatus.FROZEN=1 before invoking the registered VS-mode LCOFI handler routine.
RULE 23: In M-mode, accessing vsctrctl register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x24e; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 24: In VS-mode, accessing vsctrctl register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_virtual; csrr a0, 0x24e; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 25: In U-mode, accessing vsctrctl register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x24e; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 26: In M-mode, setting vsctrctl.CUSTOM (bit 60) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1000000000000000; csrs 0x24e, a0; csrr a1, 0x24e; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1000000000000000].
RULE 27: In M-mode, setting vsctrctl.DIRLJMPINH (bit 47) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x800000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x800000000000; csrs 0x24e, a0; csrr a1, 0x24e; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x800000000000].
RULE 28: In M-mode, setting vsctrctl.INDLJMPINH (bit 46) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x400000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x400000000000; csrs 0x24e, a0; csrr a1, 0x24e; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x400000000000].

REGISTER: vsepc
NUMBER: 0x241
MODE: VS-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=PC
EXTENSIONS: H
RULE 1: The vsepc CSR is readable and writable only in hypervisor mode (HRW privilege/access).
RULE 2: vsepc is a VSXLEN-bit register.
RULE 3: vsepc is a read/write register.
RULE 4: When V = 1, vsepc substitutes for the usual sepc.
RULE 5: When V = 1, instructions that normally read or modify sepc actually access vsepc instead.
RULE 6: When V = 0, vsepc does not directly affect the behavior of the machine.
RULE 7: vsepc is a WARL register that must be able to hold the same set of values that sepc can hold.
RULE 8: When a trap occurs in VS-mode or VU-mode, is delegated by medeleg or mideleg, and is further delegated by hedeleg or hideleg, the trap entry into VS-mode writes the CSR vsepc.
RULE 9: The CSR vsepc is written on trap entry into VS-mode together with the CSRs vscause and vstval.
RULE 10: When the SRET instruction is executed in VS-mode (V = 1), the pc is set to the value of the vsepc register.
RULE 11: When a trap is delegated to S-mode, the vsepc register is written with the virtual address of the instruction that took the trap.
RULE 12: Setting a bit in medeleg or mideleg delegates the corresponding trap that occurs in S-mode or U-mode to the S-mode trap handler, and as a result the vsepc register is written with the virtual address of the instruction that took the trap.
RULE 13: When a double-trap exception is delivered to M-mode because the S-mode-disable-trap (SDT) bit is already 1, the hart writes the vsepc register with the same information that the unexpected trap would have written if it had been taken into M-mode.
RULE 14: vsepc is an SXLEN-bit read/write CSR.
RULE 15: The low bit vsepc[0] is always zero.
RULE 16: In implementations that support only IALIGN = 32, both low bits vsepc[1:0] are always zero.
RULE 17: Whenever IALIGN = 32, reads of vsepc mask bit vsepc[1] so that it appears to be zero.
RULE 18: The implicit read of vsepc performed by the SRET instruction also masks bit vsepc[1] when IALIGN = 32.
RULE 19: Even when IALIGN = 32 masks vsepc[1] on reads, software may still write to bit vsepc[1].
RULE 20: vsepc is a WARL register that must be able to hold all valid virtual addresses.
RULE 21: When a trap is taken into S-mode, the implementation writes vsepc with the virtual address of the interrupted or faulting instruction.
RULE 22: Apart from trap handling, the implementation never writes vsepc; it may only be written explicitly by software.
RULE 23: If stval is written with a nonzero value during an instruction access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception on a hart that supports variable-length instructions, then vsepc points to the beginning of the faulting instruction.
RULE 24: When an illegal-instruction exception occurs and the stval register is used to return the faulting instruction bits, then vsepc points to the faulting instruction in memory.
RULE 25: When a trap is taken into HS-mode after any delegation by medeleg or mideleg and after the virtualization mode V is cleared to 0, the implementation MUST write the CSR vsepc (together with the CSRs scause, stval, htval, and htinst).
RULE 26: The architectural effect of taking a trap into HS-mode is that the value of the vsepc register is updated as part of the trap entry sequence.
RULE 27: When the SRET instruction is executed in M-mode or HS-mode with V=0, the processor sets the program counter to the value contained in vsepc after the new privilege mode has been determined.
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing vsepc register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x241; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 29: In VS-mode, accessing vsepc register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_virtual; csrr a0, 0x241; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 30: In U-mode, accessing vsepc register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x241; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 31: In M-mode, setting vsepc.PC (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x241, a0; csrr a1, 0x241; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].

REGISTER: vsie
NUMBER: 0x204
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..16=WPRI, 15..14=RES10-11, 13..13=VSIE.LCOFIE, 12..12=RES9, 11..10=RES7-8, 9..9=VSIE.SEIE, 8..8=RES6, 7..6=RES4-5, 5..5=VSIE.STIE, 4..4=RES3, 3..2=RES1-2, 1..1=VSIE.SSIE, 0..0=RES0
EXTENSIONS: H, Shlcofideleg, Smaia, Smcdeleg, Ssaia, Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The vsie register has HRW privilege/access type.
RULE 2: An implementation that implements the hvip.LCOFI extension MUST implement bit 13 (the LCOFI bit) in the vsie CSR.
RULE 3: The vsie register is a VSXLEN-bit read/write register that serves as the VS-mode counterpart of the supervisor CSR sie.
RULE 4: When the V bit equals 1, the vsie register substitutes for the conventional sie register, causing any instruction that would read or modify sie to instead access vsie.
RULE 5: Bits 15 down to 0 of the vsie register constitute the standard portion.
RULE 6: If hideleg bit 13 is zero, the vsie.LCOFIE field is a read-only zero.
RULE 7: If hideleg bit 13 is non-zero, the vsie.LCOFIE field is an alias of the sie.LCOFIE field.
RULE 8: If hideleg bit 10 is zero, the vsie.SEIE field is a read-only zero.
RULE 9: If hideleg bit 10 is non-zero, the vsie.SEIE field is an alias of the hie.VSEIE field.
RULE 10: If hideleg bit 6 is zero, the vsie.STIE field is a read-only zero.
RULE 11: If hideleg bit 6 is non-zero, the vsie.STIE field is an alias of the hie.VSTIE field.
RULE 12: If hideleg bit 2 is zero, the vsie.SSIE field is a read-only zero.
RULE 13: If hideleg bit 2 is non-zero, the vsie.SSIE field is an alias of the hie.VSSIE field.
RULE 14: The vsie register is readable and writable in supervisor mode (SRW).
RULE 15: If an interrupt is delegated to S-mode by setting the corresponding bit in the mideleg register, then that interrupt can be masked using the vsie register.
RULE 16: If the corresponding bit in the mideleg register is not set, then the corresponding bits in the vsie register are read-only zero.
RULE 17: The supervisor can disable individual interrupt sources using the vsie CSR.
RULE 18: When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, SPIE is set to the value of SIE.
RULE 19: When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, SIE is set to 0.
RULE 20: When an SRET instruction is executed, SIE is set to the value of SPIE.
RULE 21: When an SRET instruction is executed, SPIE is set to 1.
RULE 22: Reading SIE in sstatus mirrors reading SIE in mstatus.
RULE 23: Writing SIE in sstatus mirrors writing SIE in mstatus.
RULE 24: vsie is an SXLEN-bit read/write register that contains interrupt-enable bits.
RULE 25: Interrupt cause number i corresponds with bit i in both sip and vsie.
RULE 26: An interrupt i will trap to S-mode only if the corresponding vsie bit i is set.
RULE 27: A write to vsie causes the interrupt-trap conditions to be evaluated immediately.
RULE 28: A bit in vsie must be writable if the corresponding interrupt can ever become pending.
RULE 29: Bits of vsie that are not writable are read-only zero.
RULE 30: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the vsie.LCOFIE bit is a read-only zero.
RULE 31: If a standard interrupt type (SEI, STI, SSI, or LCOFI) is not implemented, the corresponding vsie bit is a read-only zero.
RULE 32: All bits in vsie are WARL (Write-Any-Read-Legal) fields.
RULE 33: Implemented vsie bits can be discovered by writing one to every bit location in vsie and reading back to identify bits that retain a one.
RULE 34: Reading a vsie bit reads the corresponding mie bit, and writing a writable vsie bit writes the corresponding mie bit.
RULE 35: Bit 13 of the vsie register is assigned to the count-overflow interrupt.
RULE 36: In the vsie register, the LCOFIE bit is the interrupt-enable bit for the count-overflow interrupt.
RULE 37: The interrupt-enable bits for the count-overflow interrupt include the vsie LCOFIE bit.
RULE 38: Whether the count-overflow interrupt is enabled by the vsie LCOFIE bit depends on the delegation setting in the mideleg register.
RULE 39: For each writable bit in vsie, the corresponding bit in both hip and hie shall be read-only zero.
RULE 40: The nonzero bits in vsie and hie are always mutually exclusive, and the nonzero bits in sip and hip are always mutually exclusive.
RULE 41: An interrupt i traps to HS-mode if (1) the current operating mode is HS-mode and the SIE bit in the sstatus register is set, or the current operating mode has less privilege than HS-mode; (2) bit i is set in both sip and vsie, or in both hip and hie; and (3) bit i is not set in hideleg.
RULE 42: In M-mode, accessing vsie register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x204; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 43: In S-mode, accessing vsie register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x204; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 44: In U-mode, accessing vsie register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x204; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 45: In M-mode, setting vsie.WPRI (bit 16) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x10000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x10000; csrs 0x204, a0; csrr a1, 0x204; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x10000].

REGISTER: vsip
NUMBER: 0x244
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..16=WPRI, 15..14=OTHER_STD_INT, 13..13=LCOFIP, 12..10=OTHER_STD_INT, 9..9=SEIP, 8..6=OTHER_STD_INT, 5..5=STIP, 4..2=OTHER_STD_INT, 1..1=SSIP, 0..0=OTHER_STD_INT
EXTENSIONS: H, Shlcofideleg, Sscofpmf, Sstc
RULE 1: The vsip CSR has HRW privilege, allowing it to be read and written in hypervisor mode.
RULE 2: When V = 1, any instruction that would normally read or modify the sip register instead reads or modifies vsip.
RULE 3: When hideleg bit 13 is zero, the vsip.LCOFIP field is a read-only zero.
RULE 4: When hideleg bit 13 is one, the vsip.LCOFIP field is an alias of sip.LCOFIP.
RULE 5: When hideleg bit 10 is zero, the vsip.SEIP field is a read-only zero.
RULE 6: When hideleg bit 10 is one, the vsip.SEIP field is an alias of hip.VSEIP.
RULE 7: When hideleg bit 6 is zero, the vsip.STIP field is a read-only zero.
RULE 8: When hideleg bit 6 is one, the vsip.STIP field is an alias of hip.VSTIP.
RULE 9: When hideleg bit 2 is zero, the vsip.SSIP field is a read-only zero.
RULE 10: When hideleg bit 2 is one, the vsip.SSIP field is an alias of hip.VSSIP.
RULE 11: The vsip register is accessible with Supervisor-read/write privilege (SRW).
RULE 12: The vsip register provides a restricted view of the mip register for supervisor level.
RULE 13: If an interrupt is delegated to S-mode by setting a bit in the mideleg register, then that bit becomes visible in the vsip register.
RULE 14: If an interrupt is delegated to S-mode by setting a bit in the mideleg register, then that bit is maskable using the sie register.
RULE 15: If the corresponding bit is not set in the mideleg register, then the corresponding bits in the vsip register and the sie register are read-only zero.
RULE 16: When the Sstc extension is implemented and the STCE bit in menvcfg is zero, the STIP field in the vsip CSR reverts to its defined behavior as if the Sstc extension were not implemented.
RULE 17: The vsip register can be interrogated to determine the presence of any interrupt in supervisor mode.
RULE 18: vsip.LCOFIP is a field of the vsip register that can be cleared by software.
RULE 19: When vsip.LCOFIP is cleared before the LCOFI trap is raised, some or all CTR history may be overwritten while handling the LCOFI.
RULE 20: An interrupt i traps to S-mode if the current privilege mode is S and the SIE bit in sstatus is set, or if the current privilege mode has less privilege than S-mode, and bit i is set in both vsip and sie.
RULE 21: Each individual bit in vsip may be writable or read-only; when a bit i in vsip is writable, a pending interrupt i can be cleared by writing 0 to that bit; if bit i in vsip is read-only while interrupt i can become pending, the implementation must provide some other mechanism for clearing the pending interrupt.
RULE 22: If implemented, the SEIP bit in vsip is read-only and is set and cleared by the execution environment, typically through a platform-specific interrupt controller.
RULE 23: If implemented, the STIP bit in vsip is read-only; when the Sstc extension is not implemented, STIP is set and cleared by the execution environment; when the Sstc extension is implemented, STIP reflects the timer interrupt signal from stimecmp, being set by writing stimecmp with a value less than or equal to time and cleared by writing stimecmp with a value greater than time.
RULE 24: If implemented, the SSIP bit in vsip is writable and may also be set to 1 by a platform-specific interrupt controller.
RULE 25: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the LCOFIP bit in vsip is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request resulting from any mhpmevent n.OF bit being set; if the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, vsip.LCOFIP is a read-only zero.
RULE 26: A standard interrupt type (SEI, STI, SSI, or LCOFI) may not be implemented, and if it is not implemented the corresponding pending bit in vsip is a read-only zero.
RULE 27: Reading any implemented field of vsip or writing any writable field of vsip causes a read or write of the homonymous field of mip.
RULE 28: The STIP bit in the vsip register becomes pending whenever the unsigned integer value of time is greater than or equal to stimecmp.
RULE 29: When the result of the comparison time ≥ stimecmp changes, the STIP bit in the vsip register is guaranteed to eventually reflect the new comparison result, though the update need not be immediate.
RULE 30: The STIP bit in the vsip register remains set while stimecmp is less than or equal to time.
RULE 31: The STIP bit in the vsip register may remain set briefly after stimecmp is written to a value greater than time, which can cause a spurious timer interrupt.
RULE 32: In the vsip register, the new count overflow interrupt will be treated as a standard local interrupt.
RULE 33: The new count overflow interrupt is assigned to bit 13 in the vsip register.
RULE 34: The count-overflow-interrupt-request signal is treated as a standard local interrupt that corresponds to bit 13 of the vsip register.
RULE 35: Bit 13 of the vsip register, named LCOFIP, functions as the interrupt-pending bit for the count-overflow interrupt.
RULE 36: When an OF bit is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the vsip register.
RULE 37: The LCOFIP bit in the vsip register is cleared by software before servicing the count-overflow interrupt.
RULE 38: hip and hie are HSXLEN-bit read/write registers that supplement HS-level's vsip.
RULE 39: Nonzero bits in vsip and hip are always mutually exclusive.
RULE 40: An interrupt i traps to HS-mode when bit i is set in both vsip and sie, provided that either the current mode is HS-mode with the SIE bit in sstatus set or the current mode has less privilege than HS-mode, and bit i is not set in hideleg.
RULE 41: Active bits of hip must not be placed in HS-level's vsip.
RULE 42: In M-mode, accessing vsip register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x244; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 43: In S-mode, accessing vsip register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x244; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 44: In U-mode, accessing vsip register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x244; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 45: In M-mode, setting vsip.WPRI (bit 16) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x10000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x10000; csrs 0x244, a0; csrr a1, 0x244; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x10000].
RULE 46: In M-mode, setting vsip.OTHER_STD_INT (bit 14) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x4000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4000; csrs 0x244, a0; csrr a1, 0x244; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x4000].
RULE 47: In M-mode, setting vsip.LCOFIP (bit 13) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2000; csrs 0x244, a0; csrr a1, 0x244; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2000].

REGISTER: vsiselect
NUMBER: 0x250
MODE: VS-mode
WIDTH: VSXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: H, Smcdeleg, Smcntrpmf, Smcsrind, Smctr, Smstateen, Ssaia, Ssccfg, Sscofpmf, Sscsrind, Ssctr, Ssstateen
RULE 1: vsiselect has HRW privilege, allowing both read and write accesses.
RULE 2: The CSRIND bit in mstateen0 controls access to the vsiselect CSR (and also to siselect, sireg*, and vsireg* CSRs) provided by the Sscsrind extensions.
RULE 3: The CSRIND bit in hstateen0 controls access to the vsiselect CSR (noted in parentheses as "really vsiselect") provided by the Sscsrind extensions.
RULE 4: vsiselect is a virtual supervisor indirect register select CSR located at address 0x250, has HRW privilege, and its width equals XLEN.
RULE 5: vsiselect must support at least the value range 0 to 0xFFF.
RULE 6: Values of vsiselect with the most-significant bit clear are designated exclusively for standard use and are reserved until allocated to a standard architecture extension.
RULE 7: If XLEN changes, the most-significant bit of vsiselect moves to the new XLEN-1 position while retaining its previous value.
RULE 8: A virtual-instruction exception is raised for attempts from VS-mode or VU-mode to directly access vsiselect.
RULE 9: When vsiselect holds a value that is implemented at HS level but not at VS level, attempts to access sireg* (vsireg*) from VS-mode will typically raise a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 10: The widths of vsiselect and all vsireg* CSRs are always the current XLEN rather than VSXLEN.
RULE 11: If mstateen0[60]=0 and an instruction attempts to access vsiselect from a privilege mode less privileged than M-mode, the access results in an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: When execution is in M-mode, the value of mstateen0[60] does not affect the accessibility of vsiselect.
RULE 13: If mstateen0[60]=1, any direct access to vsiselect from VS-mode or VU-mode raises a virtual-instruction exception, regardless of any other mstateen bits.
RULE 14: If the Smstateen extension is implemented and bit 60 of CSR mstateen0 is zero, any attempt to access vsiselect from a privilege mode less privileged than M-mode must be prevented.
RULE 15: If the Smstateen extension is implemented and bit 60 of CSR hstateen0 is zero, any attempt to access vsiselect from VS-mode must be prevented.
RULE 16: If the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented, any direct access to vsiselect from VS-mode must raise a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 17: If the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented, any direct access to vsiselect from VU-mode must raise a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 18: While vsiselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, any attempt to access any vsireg from M-mode must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 19: While vsiselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, any attempt to access any vsireg from S-mode must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 20: While vsiselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, any attempt from VS-mode to access any vsireg must raise an illegal-instruction exception if menvcfg.CDE is zero.
RULE 21: While vsiselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, any attempt from VS-mode to access any vsireg must raise a virtual-instruction exception if menvcfg.CDE is one.
RULE 22: When the vsiselect register holds a value in the range 0x200 to 0x2FF inclusive, the vsireg* registers provide access to the same CTR entry register state as the analogous sireg* registers.
RULE 23: The vsiselect register does not provide a separate set of entry registers for V=1.
RULE 24: When mstateen0.CTR = 0, the current privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, and vsiselect holds a value in the range 0x200..0x2FF, any attempt to access a vsireg* register raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 25: When mstateen0.CTR = 1, hstateen0.CTR = 0, and execution is in VS-mode (V = 1), any VS-mode access to supervisor CTR state raises a virtual-instruction exception, and this applies to accesses to vsireg* when vsiselect is in the range 0x200..0x2FF.
RULE 26: If bit 60 of mstateen0 is clear or bit 60 of hstateen0 is clear, accesses to vsiselect from any privilege mode less privileged than M-mode are not permitted.
RULE 27: When vsiselect holds a value listed in Table 9, the indirect CSR mechanism accesses the CSR(s) named in the sireg, sireg2, sireg3, sireg4, sireg5, and sireg6 columns of that row.
RULE 28: When vsiselect contains the value 0x30, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = iprio0 and all other indirect-CSR slots (sireg2-sireg6) are none.
RULE 29: When vsiselect contains the value 0x3F, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = iprio15 and all other indirect-CSR slots (sireg2-sireg6) are none.
RULE 30: When vsiselect contains the value 0x40, the indirect CSRs accessed are sireg = cycle, sireg2 = cyclecfg, sireg4 = cycleh, sireg5 = cyclecfgh, while sireg3 and sireg6 are none.
RULE 31: When vsiselect contains the value 0x41, all indirect-CSR slots (sireg-sireg6) are none.
RULE 32: When vsiselect contains the value 0x42, the indirect CSRs accessed are sireg = instret, sireg2 = instretcfg, sireg4 = instreth, sireg5 = instretcfgh, while sireg3 and sireg6 are none.
RULE 33: When vsiselect contains the value 0x43, the indirect CSRs accessed are sireg = hpmcounter3, sireg2 = hpmevent3, sireg4 = hpmcounter3h, sireg5 = hpmevent3h, while sireg3 and sireg6 are none.
RULE 34: When vsiselect contains any value between 0x44 and 0x4F inclusive, the mapping of indirect CSRs is defined analogously by the corresponding table rows.
RULE 35: When vsiselect contains the value 0x5F, the indirect CSRs accessed are sireg = hpmcounter31, sireg2 = hpmevent31, sireg4 = hpmcounter31h, sireg5 = hpmevent31h, while sireg3 and sireg6 are none.
RULE 36: When vsiselect contains the value 0x70, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = eidelivery and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 37: When vsiselect contains the value 0x71, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = 0 and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 38: When vsiselect contains the value 0x72, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = eithreshold and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 39: When vsiselect contains the value 0x73, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = 0 and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 40: When vsiselect contains the value 0x7F, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = 0 and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 41: When vsiselect contains the value 0x80, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = eip0 and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 42: When vsiselect contains the value 0xBF, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = eip63 and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 43: When vsiselect contains the value 0xC0, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = eie0 and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 44: When vsiselect contains the value 0xFF, the indirect CSR accessed is sireg = eie63 and all other indirect-CSR slots are none.
RULE 45: When vsiselect contains the value 0x200, the indirect CSRs accessed are sireg = ctrsource0, sireg2 = ctrtarget0, sireg3 = ctrdata0, and sireg4-sireg6 are 0.
RULE 46: When vsiselect contains the value 0x2FF, the indirect CSRs accessed are sireg = ctrsource255, sireg2 = ctrtarget255, sireg3 = ctrdata255, and sireg4-sireg6 are 0.
RULE 47: If a hypervisor is oblivious to the AIA extension, it will not swap the vsiselect CSR on context switches, allowing vsiselect to be used as a covert channel between multiple guest OSes.
RULE 48: The CSRIND bit in mstateen0 controls access to the vsiselect CSR provided by the Sscsrind extensions.
RULE 49: The CSRIND bit in hstateen0 controls access to the vsiselect CSR provided by the Sscsrind extensions.
RULE 50: For an vsiselect value associated with counter X, the sireg and sireg2 registers can be used to access the mhpmcounterX and mhpmeventX CSRs.
RULE 51: For an vsiselect value associated with counter X, the sireg4 and sireg5 registers can be used to access the mhpmcounterXh and mhpmeventXh CSRs.
RULE 52: vsiselect will support the value range 0 .. 0xFFF at a minimum.
RULE 53: Ordinarily, when vsiselect holds a standard-defined and implemented value, each sireg_i will either access register state, access a read-only zero state, or raise an illegal-instruction exception unless execution is occurring in a virtual machine.
RULE 54: A virtual-instruction exception MUST be raised when a direct access to vsiselect occurs while execution is in VU-mode.
RULE 55: The vsiselect CSR is always XLEN bits wide (the current XLEN) and is not VSXLEN.
RULE 56: When the Smstateen extension and Smcsrind are implemented, bit 60 of the state-enable CSR mstateen0 controls access to the vsiselect CSR.
RULE 57: If mstateen0[60] = 0 and an attempt to access vsiselect is made from a privilege mode less privileged than M-mode, the attempt results in an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 58: If an attempt to access vsiselect is made while executing in M-mode, the state-enable CSRs do not affect accessibility and the access is allowed.
RULE 59: If mstateen0[60] = 1, a virtual-instruction exception is raised for all attempts from VU-mode to access vsiselect or any CSR accessed indirectly through vsiselect, regardless of any other mstateen bits.
RULE 60: If the hypervisor extension is implemented, bit 60 of the hypervisor CSR hstateen0 controls access to vsiselect and any CSR accessed indirectly through vsiselect.
RULE 61: vsiselect index values from 0x40 to 0x5F are reserved for delegated counter access.
RULE 62: When a counter i is delegated (mcounteren[i]=1 and menvcfg.CDE=1), vsiselect holds the value 0x40+i to access the counter's state via sireg*.
RULE 63: If the Smstateen extension is implemented and mstateen0[60]=0, any access to vsiselect from a privilege mode less privileged than M-mode must be prohibited.
RULE 64: If the Smstateen extension is implemented and hstateen0[60]=0, any access to vsiselect from VS-mode must be prohibited.
RULE 65: When vsiselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F and menvcfg.CDE=0, any M-mode or S-mode attempt to access sireg* must raise an illegal-instruction exception, provided access is not blocked by the mstateen0[60] or hstateen0[60] conditions.
RULE 66: When vsiselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, any M-mode or S-mode attempt to access sireg3 or sireg6 must raise an illegal-instruction exception, provided access is not blocked by the mstateen0[60] or hstateen0[60] conditions.
RULE 67: When vsiselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F and XLEN=64, any M-mode or S-mode attempt to access sireg4 or sireg5 must raise an illegal-instruction exception, provided access is not blocked by the mstateen0[60] or hstateen0[60] conditions.
RULE 68: When vsiselect equals 0x41, any M-mode or S-mode attempt to access sireg* must raise an illegal-instruction exception, provided access is not blocked by the mstateen0[60] or hstateen0[60] conditions.
RULE 69: When vsiselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F and the corresponding mcounteren bit for the selected counter is 0, any M-mode or S-mode attempt to access sireg* must raise an illegal-instruction exception, provided access is not blocked by the mstateen0[60] or hstateen0[60] conditions.
RULE 70: When vsiselect equals 0x41, the accessed register is the memory-mapped mtime register, which is not a performance-monitoring counter and therefore any access must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 71: For any vsiselect value defined in Table 25, if an extension required for the underlying counter state is not implemented, then any M-mode or S-mode attempt to access the associated sireg* must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 72: If the H extension is implemented, any attempt from VS-mode or VU-mode to directly access vsiselect must raise a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 73: When vsiselect is set to 0x200, the logical entry 0 accessed via sireg* always corresponds to the physical buffer entry immediately preceding the WRPTR entry.
RULE 74: For any vsiselect value that selects a logical entry X where X < depth, the physical buffer entry Y accessed via sireg* is computed as Y = (WRPTR – X – 1) mod depth, with depth defined as 2^(DEPTH+4).
RULE 75: When vsiselect selects a logical entry whose index is ≥ depth, reads of that entry return zero and the entry is read-only, so it cannot be written.
RULE 76: When vsiselect holds a value within 0x200-0x2FF, reads of sireg access the CTR logical entry field ctrsource.
RULE 77: When vsiselect holds a value within 0x200-0x2FF, reads of sireg2 access the CTR logical entry field ctrtarget.
RULE 78: When vsiselect holds a value within 0x200-0x2FF, reads of sireg3 access the CTR logical entry field ctrdata.
RULE 79: When vsiselect holds a value within 0x200-0x2FF, reads of sireg4, sireg5, and sireg6 return zero and these registers are read-only.
RULE 80: If mstateen0.CTR = 0 and the current privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, any attempt to access a sireg* register while vsiselect holds a value in the range 0x200 to 0x2FF raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 81: In M-mode, accessing vsiselect register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x250; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 82: In VS-mode, accessing vsiselect register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_virtual; csrr a0, 0x250; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 83: In U-mode, accessing vsiselect register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x250; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 84: In M-mode, setting vsiselect.VALUE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x250, a0; csrr a1, 0x250; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 85: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the vsiselect register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x250, a0; csrr a1, 0x250; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 86: In M-mode, accessing vsiselect register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x250; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 87: In M-mode, accessing vsiselect register while Smcdeleg extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smcdeleg; csrr a0, 0x250; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 88: In M-mode, accessing vsiselect register while Smcntrpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smcntrpmf; csrr a0, 0x250; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 89: In M-mode, accessing vsiselect register while Smcsrind extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smcsrind; csrr a0, 0x250; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 90: In M-mode, accessing vsiselect register while Smctr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smctr; csrr a0, 0x250; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 91: In M-mode, accessing vsiselect register while Smstateen extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smstateen; csrr a0, 0x250; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 92: In M-mode, accessing vsiselect register while Ssaia extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssaia; csrr a0, 0x250; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 93: In M-mode, accessing vsiselect register while Ssccfg extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssccfg; csrr a0, 0x250; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 94: In M-mode, accessing vsiselect register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0x250; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 95: In M-mode, accessing vsiselect register while Sscsrind extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscsrind; csrr a0, 0x250; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 96: In M-mode, accessing vsiselect register while Ssctr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssctr; csrr a0, 0x250; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 97: In M-mode, accessing vsiselect register while Ssstateen extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssstateen; csrr a0, 0x250; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: vsscratch
NUMBER: 0x240
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: XLEN
FIELDS: UNKNOWN..UNKNOWN=VSSCRATCH
EXTENSIONS: H
RULE 1: The vsscratch register has HRW (read/write) access permissions.
RULE 2: The vsscratch register is a VSXLEN-bit read/write register.
RULE 3: When V=1, vsscratch substitutes for sscratch so that instructions that normally read sscratch actually read vsscratch.
RULE 4: When V=1, vsscratch substitutes for sscratch so that instructions that normally modify sscratch actually modify vsscratch.
RULE 5: The vsscratch CSR is an SXLEN-bit read/write register that is dedicated for use by the supervisor.
RULE 6: When V=1, the contents of vsscratch are not read.
RULE 7: When V=1, the contents of vsscratch are not written.
RULE 8: In M-mode, accessing vsscratch register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x240; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 9: In S-mode, accessing vsscratch register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x240; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 10: In U-mode, accessing vsscratch register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x240; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 11: In M-mode, accessing vsscratch register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x240; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: vsstatus
NUMBER: 0x200
MODE: VS-mode
WIDTH: VSXLEN
FIELDS: 63..63=SD, 33..32=UXL, 23..23=SPELP, 19..19=MXR, 18..18=SUM, 16..15=XS, 14..13=FS, 10..9=VS, 8..8=SPP, 6..6=UBE, 5..5=SPIE, 1..1=SIE
EXTENSIONS: D, H, W
RULE 1: The permission for a CMO instruction to access a cache block may depend on the state of the SUM bit in vsstatus.
RULE 2: The permission for a CMO instruction to access a cache block may depend on the state of the MXR bit in vsstatus.
RULE 3: When the hypervisor extension is present, the vsstatus register includes a vector context status field VS located in bits 10:9.
RULE 4: When the V bit is 1, attempts to execute any vector instruction or to access any vector CSR raise an illegal-instruction exception if either vsstatus.VS or mstatus.VS is Off.
RULE 5: When V=1 and both vsstatus.VS and mstatus.VS are not Off, executing any instruction that changes vector state, including vector CSR accesses, changes both vsstatus.VS and mstatus.VS to Dirty.
RULE 6: If vsstatus.VS is Dirty then vsstatus.SD is 1; otherwise vsstatus.SD follows the setting defined by existing specifications.
RULE 7: If the hypervisor extension is implemented and the V bit is 1, the vsstatus.FS field is additionally in effect for vector floating-point instructions.
RULE 8: If vsstatus.FS or mstatus.FS is Off, any attempt to execute a vector floating-point instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 9: Any vector floating-point instruction that modifies any floating-point extension state must set both mstatus.FS and vsstatus.FS to Dirty.
RULE 10: The privilege level for vsstatus is HRW, indicating that it is readable and writable in hypervisor mode.
RULE 11: When an MRET or SRET instruction executed in M-mode changes the privilege mode to VU, the vsstatus.SDT field is set to 0.
RULE 12: When a MNRET instruction (provided by the Smrnmi extension) changes the privilege mode to VU, the vsstatus.SDT field is set to 0.
RULE 13: When menvcfg.DTE is zero, the vsstatus register behaves as though the Ssdbltrp extension is not implemented.
RULE 14: When the Ssdbltrp extension is not implemented, the vsstatus.SDT field is read-only and always reads zero.
RULE 15: When the V bit is 1, any access to the SPELP field added by the Zicfilp extension accesses the homonymous fields of vsstatus.
RULE 16: When V=1, any instruction that normally reads or modifies sstatus shall instead read or modify vsstatus.
RULE 17: When V=1, an attempt to read or write vsstatus directly by its own separate CSR address shall cause a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 18: When V=1, an attempt to read or write vsstatus directly from Umode shall cause an illegal-instruction exception as usual.
RULE 19: vsstatus can be accessed as itself only from M-mode or HS-mode.
RULE 20: When henvcfg.DTE is zero, the vsstatus.SDT bit is read-only zero.
RULE 21: vsstatus is a VSXLEN-bit read/write register that is VS-mode's version of the supervisor register sstatus.
RULE 22: When V=1, instructions that normally read or modify sstatus actually access vsstatus instead.
RULE 23: The UXL field controls the effective XLEN for VU-mode, which may differ from the XLEN for VS-mode.
RULE 24: When VSXLEN=64, the UXL field is a WARL field encoded the same as the MXL field of misa.
RULE 25: If VSXLEN is changed from 32 to a wider width and the UXL field is not restricted to a single value, the UXL field gets the value corresponding to the widest supported width not wider than the new VSXLEN.
RULE 26: When V=1, both vsstatus.FS and the HS-level sstatus.FS are in effect.
RULE 27: Attempts to execute a floating-point instruction when either vsstatus.FS or the HS-level sstatus.FS is 0 (Off) raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 28: Modifying the floating-point state when V=1 causes both vsstatus.FS and the HS-level sstatus.FS to be set to 3 (Dirty).
RULE 29: VS-level software can change vsstatus.FS arbitrarily; the hardware does not maintain it independently.
RULE 30: When V=1, both vsstatus.VS and the HS-level sstatus.VS are in effect.
RULE 31: Attempts to execute a vector instruction when either vsstatus.VS or the HS-level sstatus.VS is 0 (Off) raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 32: Modifying the vector state when V=1 causes both vsstatus.VS and the HS-level sstatus.VS to be set to 3 (Dirty).
RULE 33: The SD field of vsstatus is a read-only field that summarizes the extension context status as it is visible to VS-mode only.
RULE 34: The XS field of vsstatus is a read-only field that summarizes the extension context status as it is visible to VS-mode only.
RULE 35: The value of the HS-level sstatus.FS does not affect vsstatus.SD.
RULE 36: When V=0, vsstatus does not directly affect the behavior of the machine unless a virtual-machine load/store (HLV, HLVX, or HSV) or the MPRV feature in the mstatus register is used to execute a load or store as though V=1.
RULE 37: The SPELP field of vsstatus holds the previous ELP and is updated as specified in Section 23.1.2.
RULE 38: In vsstatus, SPELP encoding 0 indicates NO_LP_EXPECTED meaning no landing pad instruction expected.
RULE 39: In vsstatus, SPELP encoding 1 indicates LP_EXPECTED meaning a landing pad instruction is expected.
RULE 40: The vsstatus.MXR field affects only the first translation stage (VS-stage).
RULE 41: When MPRV=1, MPV=1, and MPP=0 (VU-level access with two-stage translation and protection), vsstatus.MXR makes pages marked executable at the VS translation stage readable only if those pages are also readable at the guest-physical translation stage.
RULE 42: When MPRV=1, MPV=1, and MPP=1 (VS-level access with two-stage translation and protection), vsstatus.MXR makes pages marked executable at the VS translation stage readable only if those pages are also readable at the guest-physical translation stage.
RULE 43: When MPRV=1, MPV=1, and MPP=1, vsstatus.SUM is used instead of the HS-level SUM bit.
RULE 44: The MXR field in vsstatus makes pages that are marked execute-only readable by explicit load instructions.
RULE 45: The MXR field in vsstatus only overrides virtual-supervisor (VS-stage) page protection.
RULE 46: Setting the MXR field in vsstatus at the VS privilege level does not override guest-physical page protections.
RULE 47: Setting the MXR field in vsstatus at the HS privilege level overrides both VS-stage and G-stage execute-only permissions.
RULE 48: If execution of an instruction is prevented because the FS or VS field in the vsstatus register is zero, the processor raises an illegal-instruction exception and never raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 49: When a trap is taken into VS-mode and the previous mode was VU-mode, the vsstatus.SPP field is set to 0.
RULE 50: When a trap is taken into VS-mode and the previous mode was VS-mode, the vsstatus.SPP field is set to 1.
RULE 51: When a trap is taken into VS-mode, the vsstatus.SPIE field is written (updated).
RULE 52: When a trap is taken into VS-mode, the vsstatus.SIE field is written (updated).
RULE 53: When the SRET instruction is executed in VS-mode (V=1), the vsstatus register's SPP field is set to 0.
RULE 54: When the SRET instruction is executed in VS-mode (V=1), the vsstatus register's SIE field is set equal to the value of the SPIE field.
RULE 55: When the SRET instruction is executed in VS-mode (V=1), the vsstatus register's SPIE field is set to 1.
RULE 56: If the Ssdbltrp extension is implemented, SRET is executed in HS-mode, and the new privilege mode after SRET is VU, then the vsstatus register's SDT field is set to 0.
RULE 57: If the Ssdbltrp extension is implemented and SRET is executed in VS-mode, then the vsstatus register's SDT field is set to 0.
RULE 58: The vsstatus register defines a SPELP bit that stores the previous ELP state on traps to VS-mode.
RULE 59: When a trap is taken into privilege mode x, the SPELP bit in vsstatus (the x PELP field for VS-mode) is set to the current ELP value.
RULE 60: When an x RET instruction is executed and the new privilege mode y has LPE = 1, the value of the SPELP bit in vsstatus is transferred to ELP; otherwise ELP is set to NO_LP_EXPECTED.
RULE 61: When an x RET instruction is executed, the SPELP bit in vsstatus is set to NO_LP_EXPECTED, thereby clearing the bit.
RULE 62: The permission for a CMO instruction to access a cache block may be granted or denied based on the states of the SUM and MXR bits in vsstatus.
RULE 63: The vsstatus register bits 10-9 are defined as a vector context status field named VS that is a shadow of the corresponding bits 10-9 in the mstatus register.
RULE 64: vsstatus is readable and writable at supervisor privilege level.
RULE 65: When an MRET or SRET instruction is executed while the hart is in M-mode, the vsstatus.MDT bit is set to 0.
RULE 66: If the new privilege mode after an MRET or SRET return is U, VS, or VU, the vsstatus.SDT field is set to 0.
RULE 67: When the MNRET instruction is executed and the new privilege mode is not M, the vsstatus.MDT bit is set to 0.
RULE 68: If the new privilege mode after an MNRET execution is U, VS, or VU, the vsstatus.SDT field is set to 0.
RULE 69: The FS field in the vsstatus register blocks access to the floating-point f registers.
RULE 70: The VS field in the vsstatus register blocks access to the vector v registers.
RULE 71: Access to the vector v registers is blocked when the VS field in vsstatus is initialized to zero, either at machine level or by the OS initializing vsstatus.
RULE 72: The vsstatus register is an SXLEN-bit read/write register.
RULE 73: When a trap is taken, the SPP bit in vsstatus is set to 0 if the trap originated from user mode, or set to 1 otherwise.
RULE 74: When an SRET instruction is executed, the privilege level is set to user mode if the SPP bit in vsstatus is 0, or set to supervisor mode if the SPP bit in vsstatus is 1.
RULE 75: When an SRET instruction is executed, the SPP bit in vsstatus is set to 0.
RULE 76: When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, the SPIE bit in vsstatus is set to the previous value of the SIE bit in vsstatus.
RULE 77: When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, the SIE bit in vsstatus is set to 0.
RULE 78: When an SRET instruction is executed, the SIE bit in vsstatus is set to the previous value of the SPIE bit in vsstatus.
RULE 79: When an SRET instruction is executed, the SPIE bit in vsstatus is set to 1.
RULE 80: In a straightforward implementation, reading any field in vsstatus yields the same value as reading the homonymous field in mstatus.
RULE 81: In a straightforward implementation, writing any field in vsstatus updates the homonymous field in mstatus with the same value.
RULE 82: When the vsstatus register indicates that SXLEN=64, the UXL field is a WARL field that encodes the current value of UXLEN.
RULE 83: When the vsstatus register indicates that UXLEN ≠ SXLEN, instructions executed in the narrower mode must ignore source register operand bits above the configured XLEN and must sign-extend results to fill the widest supported XLEN in the destination register.
RULE 84: When the vsstatus register indicates that UXLEN < SXLEN, user-mode instruction-fetch addresses and load and store effective addresses are taken modulo 2^UXLEN.
RULE 85: When the vsstatus register indicates XLEN < SXLEN and a HINT instruction is executed with destination-register bits SXLEN..XLEN not all equal to bit XLEN-1, it is implementation-defined whether those bits are unchanged or are overwritten with copies of bit XLEN-1.
RULE 86: The implementation-defined choice for HINT write-back is observable only by S-mode when the vsstatus register reflects SXLEN > UXLEN and is invisible to U-mode.
RULE 87: When the MXR bit in vsstatus is 0, only loads from pages marked readable (R=1) will succeed.
RULE 88: When the MXR bit in vsstatus is 1, loads from pages marked either readable or executable (R=1 or X=1) will succeed.
RULE 89: The MXR bit in vsstatus has no effect when page-based virtual memory is not in effect.
RULE 90: When the SUM bit in vsstatus is 0, S-mode memory accesses to pages that are accessible by U-mode (U=1) will fault.
RULE 91: When the SUM bit in vsstatus is 1, these accesses are permitted.
RULE 92: The SUM bit in vsstatus has no effect when page-based virtual memory is not in effect.
RULE 93: The SUM bit in vsstatus has no effect when executing in U-mode.
RULE 94: The SUM bit in vsstatus does not permit S-mode to execute instructions from user pages.
RULE 95: The SUM bit in vsstatus is read-only 0 if satp.MODE is read-only 0.
RULE 96: The SUM bit in vsstatus does not grant S-mode software permission to execute instructions in user code pages.
RULE 97: The UBE bit in the vsstatus register is a WARL (write-any-value-read-legal) field.
RULE 98: When the UBE bit in the vsstatus register is 0, explicit load and store memory accesses made from U-mode are performed in little-endian order, and when the UBE bit is 1 they are performed in big-endian order.
RULE 99: The UBE bit in the vsstatus register has no effect on instruction fetches, which are implicit memory accesses that are always little-endian.
RULE 100: For implicit accesses to supervisor-level memory-management data structures such as page tables, the endianness defined by S-mode applies and the UBE bit in the vsstatus register is ignored.
RULE 101: When the V bit is 0, any access to the SPELP field in vsstatus accesses the homonymous SPELP field in mstatus.
RULE 102: When an explicit CSR write sets the SDT bit in vsstatus to 1, the SIE bit in vsstatus is cleared to 0.
RULE 103: The clearing of the SIE bit occurs regardless of any value written to the SIE bit by the same CSR write.
RULE 104: The SIE bit in vsstatus may be set to 1 by an explicit CSR write only if the same write sets the SDT bit to 0 or the SDT bit is already 0.
RULE 105: When a trap is to be taken into S-mode and the SDT bit in vsstatus is 0, the SDT bit is set to 1 before the trap is delivered.
RULE 106: When a trap is to be taken into S-mode and the SDT bit in vsstatus is already 1, the trap is classified as unexpected and a double-trap exception is delivered into M-mode.
RULE 107: An SRET instruction sets the SDT bit in vsstatus to 0.
RULE 108: If a guest-page fault occurs while HS-mode invokes a hypervisor virtual-machine load or store instruction when the SDT bit in vsstatus is 1, then the GPA will not be available in mtval2 when the double trap is delivered to M-mode.
RULE 109: An interrupt i will trap to S-mode when the current privilege mode is S, the SIE bit in the vsstatus register is set, and bit i is set in both sip and sie.
RULE 110: The evaluation of interrupt trap conditions must occur immediately after an explicit write to the vsstatus register.
RULE 111: Changes to the vsstatus SUM field take effect immediately and do not require execution of an SFENCE.VMA instruction.
RULE 112: Changes to the vsstatus MXR field take effect immediately and do not require execution of an SFENCE.VMA instruction.
RULE 113: If the SUM bit in vsstatus is set, supervisor-mode software may also access pages whose PTE U bit = 1.
RULE 114: If the SUM bit in vsstatus is clear, supervisor code will fault on accesses to pages whose PTE U bit = 1.
RULE 115: Irrespective of the SUM bit in vsstatus, the supervisor may not execute code on pages whose PTE U bit = 1.
RULE 116: While V=1, the normal vsstatus CSR retains its value but does not affect the behavior of the machine unless specifically documented to do so.
RULE 117: When any trap is taken, the implementation sets the SPP bit in vsstatus to the nominal privilege mode that was in effect at the time of the trap.
RULE 118: If the virtualization mode V equals 1 and a trap is taken into HS-mode, the implementation sets the SPP bit in vsstatus to the nominal privilege mode at trap entry.
RULE 119: Executing an SRET instruction that transfers control to U-mode always clears the SPP bit in vsstatus to 0.
RULE 120: An interrupt i will trap to HS-mode only if, when the current operating mode is HS-mode, the SIE bit in the vsstatus register is set.
RULE 121: The read-only SD field in vsstatus summarizes the extension context status as it is visible to VS-mode only.
RULE 122: The read-only XS field in vsstatus summarizes the extension context status as it is visible to VS-mode only.
RULE 123: During execution of hypervisor virtual-machine load and store instructions, the HS-level vsstatus.SUM field is ignored.
RULE 124: When the HS-level vsstatus.MXR field is set, execute-only pages become readable by explicit loads for both the VS-stage and G-stage of address translation.
RULE 125: If the FS field in vsstatus is zero and this prevents an instruction from executing, the exception raised is always an illegal-instruction exception, never a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 126: If the VS field in vsstatus is zero and this prevents an instruction from executing, the exception raised is always an illegal-instruction exception, never a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 127: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the vsstatus.SPP field is set to 0 if the previous privilege mode was U-mode.
RULE 128: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the vsstatus.SPP field is set to 1 if the previous privilege mode was HS-mode.
RULE 129: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the vsstatus.SPP field is set to 0 if the previous privilege mode was VU-mode.
RULE 130: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the vsstatus.SPP field is set to 1 if the previous privilege mode was VS-mode.
RULE 131: When a trap is taken into VS-mode, the HS-level vsstatus register is not modified.
RULE 132: When the SRET instruction is executed in M-mode or HS-mode with V = 0, the architectural value of vsstatus.SPP together with hstatus.SPV determines the new privilege mode as defined by the specification.
RULE 133: After SRET has determined the new privilege mode while executing in M-mode or HS-mode with V = 0, the instruction sets vsstatus.SPP to 0.
RULE 134: After SRET has determined the new privilege mode while executing in M-mode or HS-mode with V = 0, the instruction sets vsstatus.SIE to the current value of vsstatus.SPIE.
RULE 135: After SRET has determined the new privilege mode while executing in M-mode or HS-mode with V = 0, the instruction sets vsstatus.SPIE to 1.
RULE 136: vsstatus includes the SPELP bit and any read or write of that bit accesses the same architectural field as mstatus.SPELP.
RULE 137: When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, the SPELP bit in vsstatus is set to the current ELP value and ELP is subsequently set to NO_LP_EXPECTED.
RULE 138: If an SRET instruction transfers control to a privilege mode whose LPE field equals 1, then ELP is loaded from the SPELP bit in vsstatus and the SPELP bit is subsequently cleared to NO_LP_EXPECTED.
RULE 139: If an SRET instruction transfers control to a privilege mode whose LPE field equals 0, then ELP is set to NO_LP_EXPECTED and the SPELP bit in vsstatus is cleared to NO_LP_EXPECTED.
RULE 140: In M-mode, accessing vsstatus register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x200; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 141: In VS-mode, accessing vsstatus register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_virtual; csrr a0, 0x200; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 142: In U-mode, accessing vsstatus register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x200; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
