REGISTER: vstart
NUMBER: 0x008
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: vstart is a control-and-status register located at address 0x008.
RULE 2: vstart has URW privilege, allowing unprivileged software to read and write it.
RULE 3: Hardware normally writes vstart on a trap on a vector instruction, storing the element on which the trap was taken and indicating where execution should resume after a resumable trap is handled.
RULE 4: All vector instructions begin execution with the element number given in the vstart CSR, leaving earlier elements in the destination vector undisturbed.
RULE 5: At the start of every vector instruction, including vsetvl, the implementation resets the vstart CSR to zero.
RULE 6: At the end of every vector instruction, the implementation resets the vstart CSR to zero.
RULE 7: Vector instructions that raise illegal-instruction exceptions do not modify the vstart CSR.
RULE 8: The vstart CSR contains only enough writable bits to represent the largest element index, which is one less than the maximum VLMAX for the current configuration.
RULE 9: Using a vstart value greater than the largest element index for the current vtype setting is reserved.
RULE 10: Certain vector instructions cannot be executed with a non-zero vstart value and will raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: At reset, the vstart CSR may contain any arbitrary value.
RULE 12: Executing the initial vsetvl instruction resets vstart.
RULE 13: Vector load instructions may generate a non-zero vstart value.
RULE 14: Vector load instructions may accept a non-zero vstart value.
RULE 15: Vector store instructions may generate a non-zero vstart value.
RULE 16: Vector store instructions may accept a non-zero vstart value.
RULE 17: For the vlm.v and vsm.v instructions, the architectural value of vstart is interpreted as a byte offset.
RULE 18: If vstart = 0 and vl > 0, then at least one element must be processed.
RULE 19: When a fault-only-first instruction takes a trap due to an interrupt, implementations should set a vstart value.
RULE 20: For whole-register load and store instructions, the effective vector length evl is defined as NFIELDS × VLEN / EEW, and this evl is the value compared with the vstart register to determine instruction reservation.
RULE 21: The usual property that no elements are written if vstart ≥ vl does not apply to whole-register load and store instructions.
RULE 22: The usual property that a whole-register load or store instruction is reserved if vstart exceeds the largest element index for the current vtype setting does not apply.
RULE 23: A whole-register load or store instruction is reserved when the value in the vstart register is greater than or equal to the effective vector length evl.
RULE 24: When vstart >= vl, the use of the frm field by any vector-floating-point instruction, including those that do not depend on the rounding mode, is reserved.
RULE 25: The vector-scalar floating-point merge instruction (vfmerge.vfm) operates on vector elements starting at the index indicated by the vstart register.
RULE 26: The vfmerge.vfm instruction operates on vector elements up to the current vector length specified in the vl register, beginning from vstart.
RULE 27: The vfmerge.vfm instruction operates on all elements from vstart to vl regardless of the mask register value.
RULE 28: When a trap is taken on a vector reduction instruction, vstart must be reported as 0.
RULE 29: A vector reduction operation must raise an illegal-instruction exception if vstart is non-zero.
RULE 30: During execution of a vector mask-logical instruction, elements whose indices are less than the current value of vstart are left unchanged.
RULE 31: After a vector mask-logical instruction completes, the architectural register vstart is reset to zero.
RULE 32: When a trap is taken on a vcpop.m instruction, the vstart register must be 0.
RULE 33: If vstart is non-zero when executing a vcpop.m instruction, the instruction must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 34: Traps on vfirst are always reported with a vstart value of 0.
RULE 35: The vfirst instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception if vstart is non-zero.
RULE 36: When a trap is taken on the vmsbf.m instruction, the architectural value of the vstart register must be zero.
RULE 37: The vmsbf instruction must raise an illegal-instruction exception whenever the vstart register is non-zero.
RULE 38: When a trap is taken on the vmsif.m instruction, the architectural value of vstart reported to software MUST be 0.
RULE 39: The vmsif instruction MUST raise an illegal-instruction exception whenever the architectural value of vstart is non-zero.
RULE 40: All traps that occur on a vmsof.m instruction are reported with vstart equal to zero.
RULE 41: The vmsof instruction will raise an illegal-instruction exception if vstart is non-zero.
RULE 42: A trap taken on a viota.m instruction shall report the architectural vstart register value as zero.
RULE 43: After handling a trap on a viota.m instruction, execution shall be restarted from the beginning, which requires the architectural vstart register to be zero.
RULE 44: An illegal-instruction exception shall be raised whenever the architectural vstart register holds a nonzero value.
RULE 45: The vmv.x.s instruction performs its operation even when vstart is greater than or equal to vl or when vl is zero.
RULE 46: The vmv.s.x instruction performs no operation and does not update the destination register when vstart is greater than or equal to vl.
RULE 47: When vl is zero, no elements of the destination vector register group are updated, regardless of the value of vstart.
RULE 48: vfmv.f.s performs its operation even if vstart ≥ vl.
RULE 49: vfmv.f.s performs its operation even when vl = 0, regardless of the value of vstart.
RULE 50: If vstart ≥ vl then vfmv.s.f performs no operation and the destination register is not updated.
RULE 51: When vl = 0, vfmv.s.f updates no elements in the destination vector register group, regardless of vstart.
RULE 52: For each vslideup, vslidedown, v[f]slide1up, and v[f]slide1down instruction, if the vstart register holds a value greater than or equal to the current vl, the instruction performs no operation and leaves the destination vector register unchanged.
RULE 53: When the current vl is zero, no elements of the destination vector register group are updated by any of the listed slide instructions, regardless of the value in the vstart register.
RULE 54: The vslideup instruction follows the described destination-element behavior only when vstart is less than vl.
RULE 55: For each element index i satisfying 0 ≤ i < min(vl, max(vstart, OFFSET)), the destination element may be written, subject to mask enable.
RULE 56: Destination elements with indices i satisfying max(vstart, OFFSET) ≤ i < vl remain unchanged.
RULE 57: When v0.mask[i] is enabled and i satisfies 0 ≤ i < min(vl, max(vstart, OFFSET)), the destination element vd[i] is assigned the value of vs2[i-OFFSET].
RULE 58: Satisfying the non-overlap constraint between the destination and source vector register groups enables restart of the instruction with a non-zero vstart.
RULE 59: The vslidedown instructions have defined architectural behavior only when the value of vstart is less than vl.
RULE 60: When vstart is less than vl, for each element index i in the slide such that 0 ≤ i + OFFSET < VLMAX, the source element src[i] is defined as vs2[i + OFFSET].
RULE 61: When vstart is less than vl, for each element index i in the slide such that VLMAX ≤ i + OFFSET, the source element src[i] is defined as zero.
RULE 62: When vstart is less than vl, for each element index i with 0 ≤ i < vstart, the destination element vd[i] remains unchanged.
RULE 63: When vstart is less than vl, for each element index i with vstart ≤ i < vl, the destination element vd[i] is set to src[i] if the corresponding mask bit v0.mask[i] is enabled.
RULE 64: When vstart is less than vl, for each element index i with vl ≤ i < VLMAX, the handling of vd[i] follows the current tail policy.
RULE 65: When vl > 0 and an element index i is less than vstart, the destination element vd[i] remains unchanged.
RULE 66: When i equals vstart (which is also the case i = 0 as specified in the source), the destination element vd[i] is set to the scalar x[rs1] if the mask bit v0.mask[i] is enabled.
RULE 67: When an element index i satisfies max(vstart,1) <= i < vl, the destination element vd[i] is set to the vector element vs2[i-1] if the mask bit v0.mask[i] is enabled.
RULE 68: The mask bit v0.mask[i] directly governs whether the update specified for a given vstart condition is performed.
RULE 69: If an element index i is less than the current vstart value, the corresponding destination element vd[i] is unchanged.
RULE 70: If an element index i satisfies vstart ≤ i < vl-1 and the mask bit v0.mask[i] is enabled, then the destination element vd[i] is written with the source element vs2[i+1].
RULE 71: If the element index i equals vl-1, vstart ≤ i, and the mask bit v0.mask[i] is enabled, then the destination element vd[vl-1] is written with the scalar register x[rs1].
RULE 72: If the element index i equals vl-1, vstart ≤ i, and the mask bit v0.mask[i] is not enabled, then the destination element vd[vl-1] remains unchanged according to the mask-agnostic/undisturbed policy.
RULE 73: When a trap is taken on a vcompress instruction, the architectural vstart value reported in the trap must be zero.
RULE 74: If a vcompress instruction is executed with a non-zero vstart, the implementation must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 75: For vmv<nr>r.v instructions, the condition vstart ≥ vl does not prevent writing vector elements.
RULE 76: For vmv<nr>r.v instructions, the instruction is not reserved when vstart exceeds the largest element index for the current vtype setting.
RULE 77: For vmv<nr>r.v instructions, the instruction is reserved if vstart ≥ evl, where evl = EMUL × VLEN/SEW (EMUL is the number of individual vector registers copied).
RULE 78: When a trap occurs during execution of a vector instruction, the vstart CSR contains the index of the vector element on which the trap was taken.
RULE 79: For precise vector traps, any operation within the trapping vector instruction that affects a result element whose index is less than the value in the vstart CSR MUST have committed its result.
RULE 80: For precise vector traps, any operation within the trapping vector instruction that affects an element whose index is greater than or equal to the value in the vstart CSR MUST NOT have altered architectural state unless restarting the instruction from the vstart index and completing it would still produce the correct final state.
RULE 81: Elements whose index is greater than the value in the vstart CSR are permitted to have been updated at the time the trap is reported only if re-executing the instruction from the vstart index will correctly overwrite those elements.
RULE 82: Implementations MUST eventually guarantee forward progress for the element or segment identified by the vstart CSR.
RULE 83: Imprecise traps shall report the faulting element in vstart for traps caused by synchronous vector exceptions.
RULE 84: vstart MUST be an integer multiple of the Element Group Size (EGS) for any Vector Crypto instruction that uses element groups.
RULE 85: If vstart is not an integer multiple of the required EGS for a Vector Crypto instruction, the instruction is reserved.
RULE 86: For Vector Crypto instructions matching the pattern vaes*, the required EGS for vstart is 4.
RULE 87: For Vector Crypto instructions matching the pattern vsha2*, the required EGS for vstart is 4.
RULE 88: For Vector Crypto instructions matching the pattern vg*, the required EGS for vstart is 4.
RULE 89: For Vector Crypto instructions matching the pattern vsm3*, the required EGS for vstart is 8.
RULE 90: For Vector Crypto instructions matching the pattern vsm4*, the required EGS for vstart is 4.
RULE 91: For vector GCM/GMAC instructions, vstart MUST be a multiple of EGS=4.
RULE 92: vstart must be a multiple of 4, which is the element group size (EGS) for Zvkned vector AES instructions.
RULE 93: vstart MUST be a multiple of the element grouping size (EGS), which is 4.
RULE 94: vstart MUST be a multiple of EGS, where EGS = 4.
RULE 95: vstart MUST be a multiple of the element group size (EGS), which is eight.
RULE 96: If the expression ((vstart % EGS) <> 0) | (LMUL*VLEN < EGW) evaluates to true, the implementation must raise an illegal-instruction exception by executing handle_illegal() and the instruction must retire with RETIRE_FAIL.
RULE 97: If the expression ((vstart % EGS) <> 0) | (LMUL*VLEN < EGW) evaluates to false, the implementation must set eg_start equal to (vstart / EGS).
RULE 98: In the vandn instruction, the element index i starts at the current value of the vstart register.
RULE 99: In the vandn instruction, the element index i iterates from the vstart register value up to the value of vl1.
RULE 100: The vstart register selects the first vector element index on which the VCLMUL instructions vclmul.vv and vclmul.vx perform carry-less multiplication and store the result.
RULE 101: The vclmulh instruction processes vector elements with index i beginning at the index value held in the vstart register.
RULE 102: The vclmulh instruction processes vector elements with index i from the vstart value up to the current vector length vl1.
RULE 103: The description provides no other conditions, exceptions, or effects on the vstart register for the vclmulh operation.
RULE 104: The vstart register determines the first element index processed by the vclz.v operation.
RULE 105: The vclz.v operation processes elements whose indices are greater than or equal to the current value of vstart and less than or equal to vl1.
RULE 106: The vcpop.v instruction reads the architectural register vstart to obtain the starting element index for its element-wise loop.
RULE 107: The vcpop.v instruction iterates over element indices i such that i ranges from the value in vstart up to and including the value in vl1.
RULE 108: In the execution of the vctz.v instruction, the element index i iterates from the value held in vstart up to vl1.
RULE 109: The value of the vstart register determines the first vector element processed by the vctz.v instruction.
RULE 110: In the operation of vghsh.vv, the value of vstart is divided by the element-group size (EGS) to compute eg_start.
RULE 111: The computed eg_start value derived from vstart is used as the starting index of the element-group loop in vghsh.vv.
RULE 112: The value of vstart determines the first element group (the iteration index) processed by the vghsh.vv instruction.
RULE 113: The vstart register value is divided by the element-group size (EGS) to produce the value eg_start used by the instruction.
RULE 114: The eg_start value, resulting from vstart divided by EGS, determines the first element-group index i of the instruction's processing loop.
RULE 115: For the VROR.VV, VROR.VX, and VROR.VI instructions, the element index i begins at the value contained in the vstart register.
RULE 116: For the VROR.VV, VROR.VX, and VROR.VI instructions, the element index i increments until it reaches vl-1, inclusive, using the vstart register as the lower bound.
RULE 117: The range of vector elements processed by VROR.VV, VROR.VX, and VROR.VI is defined by the vstart register as the starting index and by vl-1 as the ending index.
RULE 118: In the VSHA2c instruction, the start element-group index eg_start is computed as the architectural value of vstart divided by the element-group size EGS.
RULE 119: In the VSHA2c instruction, the iteration over element groups begins at the element group index derived from vstart (i = eg_start) and proceeds sequentially to i = eg_len-1.
RULE 120: When LMUL × VLEN < EGW, the architectural effect on vstart is that the instruction executes handle_illegal(), raises an illegal-instruction exception, and retires with RETIRE_FAIL.
RULE 121: The value of vstart is used to compute eg_start as the integer division of vstart by EGS (eg_start = vstart / EGS).
RULE 122: The vector-element loop iterates over indices i from the integer-division result of vstart by EGS up to eg_len-1, where eg_len is defined as vl divided by EGS.
RULE 123: The value of vstart determines the starting element index of the vector operation performed by the instruction.
RULE 124: The vstart CSR has URW privilege.
RULE 125: A read or write of the vstart CSR causes an illegal-instruction exception when the VS field is set to Off.
RULE 126: When the v registers are implemented, the VS field that includes vstart shall not be read-only zero.
RULE 127: If neither the v registers nor S-mode is implemented, the VS field that includes vstart is read-only zero.
RULE 128: If S-mode is implemented but the v registers are not, the VS field that includes vstart may optionally be read-only zero.
RULE 129: In M-mode, accessing vstart register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x008; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 130: In S-mode, accessing vstart register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x008; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 131: In U-mode, accessing vstart register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x008; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 132: In M-mode, setting vstart.VALUE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x008, a0; csrr a1, 0x008; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 133: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the vstart register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x008, a0; csrr a1, 0x008; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: vstval
NUMBER: 0x243
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: VSXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: H, Ssdbltrp, Zicfilp
RULE 1: The vstval CSR has privilege/access type HRW.
RULE 2: The vstval register is a VSXLEN-bit read/write register.
RULE 3: When the V field equals 1, vstval substitutes for the usual stval, causing instructions that normally read or modify stval to access vstval instead.
RULE 4: When the V field equals 0, vstval does not directly affect the behavior of the machine.
RULE 5: vstval is a WARL register that MUST be able to hold the same set of values that stval can hold.
RULE 6: When a trap is taken into VS-mode, the CSR vstval is written.
RULE 7: The write of vstval occurs as part of the trap-entry actions for a VS-mode trap, together with writes to the CSR vsepc, the CSR vscause, and the SPIE and SIE fields of vsstatus.
RULE 8: When a trap is delegated to S-mode (i.e., the trap occurs in S-mode or U-mode and the corresponding bit in medeleg or mideleg is set), the vstval register is written with an exception-specific datum.
RULE 9: After a trap handler has saved the vstval (along with scause and sepc) needed for resuming from the trap and the handler is reentrant, the implementation SHOULD clear the SDT bit.
RULE 10: The vstval CSR is an SXLEN-bit read-write register.
RULE 11: When a trap is taken into S-mode, the implementation writes vstval with exception-specific information to assist software in handling the trap.
RULE 12: Otherwise, the implementation never writes vstval, though it may be explicitly written by software.
RULE 13: If vstval is written with a nonzero value when a breakpoint, address-misaligned, access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception occurs on an instruction fetch, load, or store, then vstval will contain the faulting virtual address.
RULE 14: On a breakpoint exception raised by an EBREAK or C.EBREAK instruction, vstval is written with either zero or the virtual address of the instruction.
RULE 15: If vstval is written with a nonzero value when a misaligned load or store causes an access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception, then vstval will contain the virtual address of the portion of the access that caused the fault.
RULE 16: If vstval is written with a nonzero value when an instruction access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception occurs on a hart with variable-length instructions, then vstval will contain the virtual address of the portion of the instruction that caused the fault, while sepc will point to the beginning of the instruction.
RULE 17: If vstval is written with a nonzero value when an illegal-instruction exception occurs, then vstval will contain the shortest of the actual faulting instruction, the first ILEN bits of the faulting instruction, or the first SXLEN bits of the faulting instruction.
RULE 18: The value loaded into vstval on an illegal-instruction exception is right-justified and all unused upper bits are cleared to zero.
RULE 19: On a trap caused by a software-check exception, vstval holds the cause for the exception.
RULE 20: When the cause of a software-check exception is 0, vstval is 0 to indicate no information provided.
RULE 21: When the cause of a software-check exception is 2, vstval is 2 to indicate a Landing Pad Fault as defined by the Zicfilp extension.
RULE 22: When the cause of a software-check exception is 3, vstval is 3 to indicate a Shadow Stack Fault as defined by the Zicfiss extension.
RULE 23: For other traps, vstval is set to zero, but a future standard may redefine vstval's setting for other traps.
RULE 24: vstval is a WARL register that must be able to hold all valid virtual addresses and the value 0.
RULE 25: vstval need not be capable of holding all possible invalid addresses.
RULE 26: Prior to writing vstval, implementations may convert an invalid address into some other invalid address that vstval is capable of holding.
RULE 27: If the feature to return the faulting instruction bits is implemented, vstval must also be able to hold all values less than 2^N, where N is the smaller of SXLEN and ILEN.
RULE 28: When any trap (breakpoint, address misaligned, access fault, page fault, or guest-page fault) writes a guest virtual address to vstval, the GVA field in vstval is set to 1.
RULE 29: When any other trap into HS-mode writes to vstval, the GVA field in vstval is set to 0.
RULE 30: For breakpoint and memory-access traps that write a nonzero value to vstval, the GVA field in vstval is set to the same value as the SPV field.
RULE 31: If the explicit memory access of an HLV, HLVX, or HSV instruction causes a fault, SPV is set to 0 and GVA is set to 1 in vstval.
RULE 32: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, hardware writes the vstval register with exception-specific information.
RULE 33: For misaligned loads and stores that cause guest-page faults, the virtual address of the faulting portion of the access is reported in vstval.
RULE 34: For instruction guest-page faults on systems that support variable-length instructions, the virtual address of the faulting portion of the instruction is reported in vstval.
RULE 35: Ordinarily, the least-significant two bits of a faulting guest physical address are identical to the least-significant two bits of the faulting virtual address contained in vstval.
RULE 36: For faults caused by implicit memory accesses during VS-stage address translation, the least-significant two bits of the virtual address reported in vstval are zero.
RULE 37: On a guest-page fault, the CSR vstval is written with the faulting guest virtual address.
RULE 38: When a guest-page fault occurs during an instruction fetch or a misaligned memory access that straddles a page boundary, the faulting virtual address written to vstval is the same as would be required for a regular page fault.
RULE 39: When a guest-page fault occurs during an instruction fetch or a misaligned memory access that straddles a page boundary, the faulting virtual address written to vstval may be a page-boundary address that is higher than the instruction's original virtual address if the byte at that page boundary is among the accessed bytes.
RULE 40: When a guest-page fault is not due to an implicit memory access for VS-stage address translation, a nonzero guest physical address written to mtval2 or htval shall correspond to the exact virtual address written to vstval.
RULE 41: On a virtual-instruction trap, the vstval register is written with the same value that is written on an illegal-instruction trap.
RULE 42: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the implementation writes the CSR vstval.
RULE 43: The write of the CSR vstval is performed as part of the trap entry actions for a trap taken into HS-mode.
RULE 44: In all transformed instructions, the Addr. Offset field that replaces the instruction's rs1 field in bits 19:15 is the positive difference between the faulting virtual address written to vstval and the original virtual address.
RULE 45: The positive difference between the faulting virtual address written to vstval and the original virtual address can be nonzero only for a misaligned memory access.
RULE 46: When the hardware writes an address to the vstval CSR during exception handling, pointer masking is applied to that write if pointer masking is applicable to that address.
RULE 47: During exception delivery, the hardware applies pointer masking to any address written into vstval if pointer masking is applicable to that address.
RULE 48: In M-mode, accessing vstval register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x243; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 49: In S-mode, accessing vstval register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x243; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 50: In U-mode, accessing vstval register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x243; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 51: In M-mode, setting vstval.VALUE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x243, a0; csrr a1, 0x243; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 52: In M-mode, accessing vstval register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x243; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 53: In M-mode, accessing vstval register while Ssdbltrp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssdbltrp; csrr a0, 0x243; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 54: In M-mode, accessing vstval register while Zicfilp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicfilp; csrr a0, 0x243; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: vstvec
NUMBER: 0x205
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..2=BASE, 1..0=MODE
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The vstvec CSR is accessible in hypervisor mode with read-write permission.
RULE 2: vstvec is a VSXLEN-bit read/write register that provides VS-mode's version of the supervisor register stvec.
RULE 3: When the V bit equals 1, any instruction that reads or writes the supervisor register stvec instead accesses vstvec.
RULE 4: When the V bit equals 0, vstvec does not directly affect the behavior of the machine.
RULE 5: vstvec contains a field named BASE occupying bits VSXLEN-1 down to 2, and the BASE field is Write-Any-Legal (WARL).
RULE 6: vstvec contains a field named MODE, and the MODE field is Write-Any-Legal (WARL).
RULE 7: vstvec is readable and writable.
RULE 8: For a double trap that originates in VS-mode, M-mode should use an MRET to resume execution at the address contained in the vstvec register.
RULE 9: vstvec is an SXLEN-bit read/write register that holds trap vector configuration consisting of a vector base address (BASE) and a vector mode (MODE).
RULE 10: In the CSR layout, bits SXLEN-1 down to 2 of vstvec hold the BASE field and are WARL, and bits 1-0 of vstvec hold the MODE field and are WARL.
RULE 11: The BASE field of vstvec must contain a 4-byte-aligned virtual or physical address.
RULE 12: The vstvec CSR stores only bits XLEN-1 through 2 of the BASE address, and the lower two bits are implicitly zeroed to form an XLEN-bit address that is always 4-byte aligned.
RULE 13: When the MODE field of vstvec is set to Direct, all traps into supervisor mode cause the program counter to be set to the address contained in the BASE field of vstvec.
RULE 14: When the MODE field of vstvec is set to Vectored, all synchronous exceptions into supervisor mode cause the program counter to be set to the address contained in the BASE field of vstvec.
RULE 15: A supervisor-mode timer interrupt causes the program counter to be set to vstvec.BASE plus 0x14.
RULE 16: Pointer masking is not applied when software writes to vstvec.
RULE 17: Software may write a tagged or an untagged address to vstvec.
RULE 18: During trap delivery, the address taken from vstvec for the trap handler is used without pointer masking.
RULE 19: In M-mode, accessing vstvec register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x205; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 20: In S-mode, accessing vstvec register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x205; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 21: In U-mode, accessing vstvec register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x205; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 22: In M-mode, setting vstvec.BASE (bit 2) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x4) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4; csrs 0x205, a0; csrr a1, 0x205; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x4].
RULE 23: In M-mode, setting vstvec.MODE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x205, a0; csrr a1, 0x205; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 24: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the vstvec register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x205, a0; csrr a1, 0x205; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: vtype
NUMBER: 0xc21
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..63=VILL, 7..7=VMA, 6..6=VTA, 5..3=VSEW, 2..0=VLMUL
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The vtype CSR has privilege level URO, which is unprivileged and read-only.
RULE 2: vtype is a read-only XLEN-wide vector-type CSR.
RULE 3: vtype can only be updated by vset{i}vl{i} instructions.
RULE 4: Non-zero values in bits vtype[XLEN-2:8] are reserved.
RULE 5: Bit XLEN-1 of vtype, named vill, is illegal if set.
RULE 6: When vsew[2:0] in vtype is 000, the selected element width (SEW) is 8.
RULE 7: When vsew[2:0] in vtype is 001, the selected element width (SEW) is 16.
RULE 8: When vsew[2:0] in vtype is 010, the selected element width (SEW) is 32.
RULE 9: When vsew[2:0] in vtype is 011, the selected element width (SEW) is 64.
RULE 10: When vsew[2:0] in vtype matches the pattern 1xx, the encoding is reserved.
RULE 11: When the vlmul[2:0] bits in vtype are 1 0 0, the resulting LMUL encoding is reserved, the number of groups is undefined, VLMAX is undefined, and the register grouping is reserved.
RULE 12: When the vlmul[2:0] bits in vtype are 1 0 1, LMUL is 1/8, the vector register file is divided into 32 groups, VLMAX equals VLEN/SEW/8, and each group consists of a single register v n.
RULE 13: When the vlmul[2:0] bits in vtype are 1 1 0, LMUL is 1/4, the vector register file is divided into 32 groups, VLMAX equals VLEN/SEW/4, and each group consists of a single register v n.
RULE 14: When the vlmul[2:0] bits in vtype are 1 1 1, LMUL is 1/2, the vector register file is divided into 32 groups, VLMAX equals VLEN/SEW/2, and each group consists of a single register v n.
RULE 15: When the vlmul[2:0] bits in vtype are 0 0 0, LMUL is 1, the vector register file is divided into 32 groups, VLMAX equals VLEN/SEW, and each group consists of a single register v n.
RULE 16: When the vlmul[2:0] bits in vtype are 0 0 1, LMUL is 2, the vector register file is divided into 16 groups, VLMAX equals 2 × VLEN/SEW, and each group contains registers v n and v n + 1.
RULE 17: When the vlmul[2:0] bits in vtype are 0 1 0, LMUL is 4, the vector register file is divided into 8 groups, VLMAX equals 4 × VLEN/SEW, and each group contains registers v n through v n + 3.
RULE 18: When the vlmul[2:0] bits in vtype are 0 1 1, LMUL is 8, the vector register file is divided into 4 groups, VLMAX equals 8 × VLEN/SEW, and each group contains registers v n through v n + 7.
RULE 19: When LMUL derived from vtype equals 2, the vector register group contains registers v n and v n + 1, providing twice the vector length in bits.
RULE 20: When vtype encodes LMUL = 2, instructions that specify a vector register group with an odd-numbered base register are reserved.
RULE 21: When LMUL derived from vtype equals 4, the vector register group contains four consecutive registers.
RULE 22: When vtype encodes LMUL = 4, instructions that specify a vector register group using a base register number that is not a multiple of four are reserved.
RULE 23: When LMUL derived from vtype equals 8, the vector register group contains eight consecutive registers.
RULE 24: When vtype encodes LMUL = 8, instructions that specify a vector register group using a base register number that is not a multiple of eight are reserved.
RULE 25: Mask registers are always contained in a single vector register regardless of the LMUL value derived from vtype.
RULE 26: The use of vtype encodings that yield LMUL less than SEWMIN/ELEN is reserved.
RULE 27: Implementations MUST support all four possible combinations of the vta and vma bits in vtype.
RULE 28: When vta=0 and vma=0 in vtype, tail elements are undisturbed and inactive elements are undisturbed.
RULE 29: When vta=0 and vma=1 in vtype, tail elements are undisturbed and inactive elements are agnostic.
RULE 30: When vta=1 and vma=0 in vtype, tail elements are agnostic and inactive elements are undisturbed.
RULE 31: When vta=1 and vma=1 in vtype, tail elements are agnostic and inactive elements are agnostic.
RULE 32: Mask destination tail elements are always treated as tail-agnostic irrespective of the vta bit value in vtype.
RULE 33: If a set of destination elements is marked undisturbed by the vtype bits, those elements retain the value previously held in the vector register group.
RULE 34: If a set of destination elements is marked agnostic by the vtype bits, those elements may either retain the previous value or be overwritten with 1s.
RULE 35: Within a single vector instruction, the vtype bits allow each destination element to be either left undisturbed or overwritten with 1s in any combination, and the pattern is not required to be deterministic when the instruction is executed with the same inputs.
RULE 36: The vsetvli instruction includes mandatory flags that set the vta and vma bits in vtype: the flag ta sets vta=1, tu sets vta=0, ma sets vma=1, and mu sets vma=0.
RULE 37: If the vill bit in vtype is set, any attempt to execute a vector instruction that depends on vtype shall raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 38: vset{i}vl{i} instructions do not depend on vtype.
RULE 39: Whole-register loads and stores do not depend on vtype.
RULE 40: When the vill bit in vtype is set, all other XLEN-1 bits of vtype shall be zero.
RULE 41: The vector extension must have a consistent state at reset, and vtype must hold a value that can be read and then restored with a single vsetvl instruction.
RULE 42: When source and destination registers overlap and have different EEW, the instruction is mask-agnostic regardless of the setting of the vta and vma bits in vtype.
RULE 43: When source and destination registers overlap and have different EEW, the instruction is tail-agnostic regardless of the setting of the vta and vma bits in vtype.
RULE 44: The handling policy for destination vector register elements that correspond to masked-off elements is selected based on the setting of the vma bit in vtype.
RULE 45: Mask destination tail elements are always treated as tail-agnostic regardless of the setting of the vta bit in vtype.
RULE 46: When vtype.vma = 0, inactive elements do not raise exceptions and do not update any destination vector register group.
RULE 47: When vtype.vma = 1, inactive elements may be overwritten with 1s.
RULE 48: When vtype.vta = 0, tail elements do not raise exceptions and do not update any destination vector register group.
RULE 49: When vtype.vta = 1, tail elements may be overwritten with 1s, or may be overwritten with the result of the instruction for mask-producing instructions except mask loads.
RULE 50: When vstart ≥ vl, no elements are updated in any destination vector register group and tail elements are not updated with agnostic values, irrespective of vtype settings.
RULE 51: When vl = 0, no elements are updated in the destination vector register group, including any agnostic elements, irrespective of vtype settings or vstart.
RULE 52: All vset{i}vl{i} instructions update the vtype CSR with a value derived from their operands.
RULE 53: The vsetvli instruction uses its third operand vtypei as the new vtype setting that is written to the vtype CSR.
RULE 54: The vsetivli instruction uses its third operand vtypei as the new vtype setting that is written to the vtype CSR.
RULE 55: The vsetvl instruction uses its second source register rs2 as the new vtype value that is written to the vtype CSR.
RULE 56: When a vset{i}vl{i} instruction updates the vtype CSR, it also updates the vl CSR based on the same arguments.
RULE 57: In the vtype register, bit XLEN-1 is named vill and indicates an illegal value if set; for XLEN values other than 32, vill resides at bit XLEN-1.
RULE 58: Bits XLEN-2 through 8 of the vtype register are reserved and shall be zero; a non-zero value in these bits is reserved.
RULE 59: Bits 5 down to 3 of the vtype register form the vsew[2:0] field that encodes the selected element width (SEW) setting.
RULE 60: Bits 2 down to 0 of the vtype register form the vlmul[2:0] field that encodes the vector register group multiplier (LMUL) setting.
RULE 61: Assembler name e8 encodes SEW = 8 bits in the vsew[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 62: Assembler name e16 encodes SEW = 16 bits in the vsew[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 63: Assembler name e32 encodes SEW = 32 bits in the vsew[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 64: Assembler name e64 encodes SEW = 64 bits in the vsew[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 65: Assembler name mf8 encodes LMUL = 1/8 in the vlmul[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 66: Assembler name mf4 encodes LMUL = 1/4 in the vlmul[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 67: Assembler name mf2 encodes LMUL = 1/2 in the vlmul[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 68: Assembler name m1 encodes LMUL = 1 in the vlmul[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 69: Assembler name m2 encodes LMUL = 2 in the vlmul[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 70: Assembler name m4 encodes LMUL = 4 in the vlmul[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 71: Assembler name m8 encodes LMUL = 8 in the vlmul[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 72: Executing vsetvli with arguments e8, m1, ta, ma sets the vsew[2:0] field of vtype to encode SEW = 8 bits, sets the vlmul[2:0] field to encode LMUL = 1, and sets both the vta and vma bits of vtype to 1.
RULE 73: Executing vsetvli with arguments e8, m2, ta, ma sets the vsew[2:0] field of vtype to encode SEW = 8 bits, sets the vlmul[2:0] field to encode LMUL = 2, and sets both the vta and vma bits of vtype to 1.
RULE 74: Executing vsetvli with arguments e32, mf2, ta, ma sets the vsew[2:0] field of vtype to encode SEW = 32 bits, sets the vlmul[2:0] field to encode LMUL = 1/2, and sets both the vta and vma bits of vtype to 1.
RULE 75: If a vtype value is not supported by the implementation, the vill bit in vtype is set.
RULE 76: If a vtype value is not supported by the implementation, the remaining bits in vtype are set to zero.
RULE 77: If a vtype value is not supported by the implementation, the vl register is set to zero.
RULE 78: If any location within a vtype value contains an unsupported value, vill MUST be set.
RULE 79: When a vsetvli or vsetvl instruction is executed with rs1 = x0 and rd = x0, implementations MAY change the vtype register while preserving the current vl provided that VLMAX is not reduced.
RULE 80: After executing a vsetvli or vsetvl instruction with rs1 = x0 and rd = x0, implementations MAY set the vill field of the vtype register regardless of its prior value.
RULE 81: When both rd and rs1 are x0 in a vsetvli or vsetvl instruction, the existing vl must be kept while the vtype register may be changed.
RULE 82: vset{i}vl{i} instructions set VLMAX according to their vtype argument.
RULE 83: After setting VLMAX based on the vtype argument, vset{i}vl{i} instructions set vl in accordance with the constraints listed in Section 31.6.3.
RULE 84: When the instruction vsetvli a3, a0, e16, m4, ta, ma is executed, the vtype register is set to 16-bit integer vectors.
RULE 85: Masked vector loads do not update inactive elements in the destination vector-register group unless masked-agnostic operation is specified by setting vtype.vma to 1.
RULE 86: When vtype.vma is set to 1, masked vector loads update inactive elements, indicating that masked-agnostic behavior is in effect.
RULE 87: The SEW field encoded in vtype specifies the selected element width for the data values of vector indexed load and store instructions.
RULE 88: The LMUL field encoded in vtype specifies the selected group multiplier for the data values of vector indexed load and store instructions.
RULE 89: The vlm.v instruction respects the vill field in vtype.
RULE 90: The vsm.v instruction respects the vill field in vtype.
RULE 91: The vlm.v instruction depends on vtype indirectly through its constraints on vl.
RULE 92: The vsm.v instruction depends on vtype indirectly through its constraints on vl.
RULE 93: Whole-register load and store instructions compute their effective vector length as evl = NFIELDS * VLEN / EEW and do not consider the current vtype setting.
RULE 94: Whole-register load and store instructions are not reserved when vstart exceeds the largest element index defined by the current vtype setting.
RULE 95: The value of the vlmul field in vtype does not affect which vector register is used by vector mask-register logical instructions.
RULE 96: Vector mask-register logical instructions do not change the vlmul field of vtype.
RULE 97: In the masked viota.m example the vtype register's vma field is 0 (vtype.vma = 0).
RULE 98: The usual reservation rule that an instruction is reserved when vstart exceeds the largest element index defined by vtype does not apply to vmv<nr>r.v instructions.
RULE 99: vmv<nr>r.v instructions are reserved only when vstart is greater than or equal to evl, irrespective of the vtype-defined largest element index.
RULE 100: If the opcode statically encodes the EEW of all operands for a single-size operation, the vtype SEW field value is ignored.
RULE 101: The vtype CSR has unprivileged read-only (URO) privilege.
RULE 102: If VS is Off, a read of the vtype CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 103: If VS is Off, a write to the vtype CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 104: If the vector registers are implemented, VS must be writable and may not be permanently zero, indicating that the vtype CSR is present.
RULE 105: If neither the vector registers nor S-mode is implemented, VS is read-only zero and the vtype CSR is not present.
RULE 106: If S-mode is implemented but the vector registers are not, VS may be read-only zero and the vtype CSR is not present.
RULE 107: The setting of VS does not modify the contents of the vtype CSR.
RULE 108: When VS equals Initial or Clean, a write to the vtype CSR that leaves its value unchanged may (implementation-defined) cause VS to become Dirty.
RULE 109: In M-mode, accessing vtype register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc21; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 110: In S-mode, accessing vtype register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc21; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 111: In U-mode, accessing vtype register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc21; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: vxrm
NUMBER: 0x00a
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: V
RULE 1: The vxrm CSR is defined with URW privilege, meaning it can be read and written by unprivileged software.
RULE 2: The vxrm register holds a two-bit read-write rounding-mode field in the least-significant bits vxrm[1:0].
RULE 3: The rounding-mode value in vxrm is also reflected as a field in the vcsr register.
RULE 4: When vxrm[1:0] = 0b00, the rounding mode is round-to-nearest-up (add +0.5 LSB) and the rounding increment r used in (v >> d) + r is v[d-1].
RULE 5: When vxrm[1:0] = 0b01, the rounding mode is round-to-nearest-even and the rounding increment r used in (v >> d) + r is v[d-1] & (v[d-2:0] ≠ 0 | v[d]).
RULE 6: When vxrm[1:0] = 0b10, the rounding mode is round-down and the rounding increment r used in (v >> d) + r is 0.
RULE 7: When vxrm[1:0] = 0b11, the rounding mode is round-to-odd (OR bits into LSB, aka "jam") and the rounding increment r used in (v >> d) + r is !v[d] & v[d-1:0] ≠ 0.
RULE 8: The rounded result of a vector fixed-point operation is (v >> d) + r, where r is the rounding increment defined by the current vxrm encoding.
RULE 9: The function roundoff_unsigned(v,d) is defined as (unsigned(v) >> d) + r, where r is the rounding increment specified by the current vxrm encoding.
RULE 10: The function roundoff_signed(v,d) is defined as (signed(v) >> d) + r, where r is the rounding increment specified by the current vxrm encoding.
RULE 11: The vxrm register may also be accessed through a field in the XLEN-bit-wide vector control and status CSR named vcsr.
RULE 12: In the vcsr CSR, bits 2 down to 1 constitute the vxrm[1:0] field.
RULE 13: The bits 2:1 of vcsr are named vxrm[1:0].
RULE 14: The vxrm[1:0] field in vcsr specifies the fixed-point rounding mode.
RULE 15: For averaging add and subtract instructions, after the result is right-shifted by one bit, the rounding applied follows the rounding mode specified in vxrm.
RULE 16: The rounding operation that follows the infinite-precision computation and truncation uses the rounding mode selected by vxrm.
RULE 17: In signed fractional-multiply instructions such as vsmul.vv and vsmul.vx, after the 2 × SEW product is shifted right by SEW-1 bits, the bits that are shifted out are rounded according to the current value of the vxrm register.
RULE 18: The vector single-width logical right-shift scaling instruction vssrl rounds the shifted-out bits according to the current setting of the vxrm register.
RULE 19: The vector single-width arithmetic right-shift scaling instruction vssra rounds the shifted-out bits according to the current setting of the vxrm register.
RULE 20: For the vnclipu and vnclip instructions, the rounding mode is taken from the vxrm CSR.
RULE 21: Rounding that uses the mode specified in vxrm is performed around the least-significant bit of the destination.
RULE 22: Rounding that uses the mode specified in vxrm is performed before saturation.
RULE 23: The vxrm CSR has privilege URW, meaning it can be read and written in user mode.
RULE 24: When the VS field for the vector extension is set to Off, any instruction that attempts to read or write vxrm will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 25: If the VS field is read-only zero, any instruction that attempts to read or write vxrm will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 26: If neither the v registers nor S-mode is implemented, then VS is read-only zero, and consequently any attempt to read or write vxrm will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 27: If S-mode is implemented but the v registers are not, VS may be read-only zero, and when VS is read-only zero any attempt to read or write vxrm will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 28: If the v registers are implemented, the VS field shall not be read-only zero, thus accesses to vxrm are not prohibited by the VS-read-only-zero illegal-instruction rule.
RULE 29: In M-mode, accessing vxrm register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x00a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 30: In S-mode, accessing vxrm register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x00a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 31: In U-mode, accessing vxrm register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x00a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 32: In M-mode, setting vxrm.VALUE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x00a, a0; csrr a1, 0x00a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 33: In M-mode, accessing vxrm register while V extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: V; csrr a0, 0x00a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: vxsat
NUMBER: 0x009
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: V
RULE 1: The vxsat CSR resides at address 0x009 and has URW privilege.
RULE 2: The vxsat CSR contains a single read-write least-significant bit named vxsat[0].
RULE 3: The vxsat[0] bit indicates whether a fixed-point instruction has saturated an output value to fit into the destination format.
RULE 4: The vxsat bit is mirrored in the vcsr register.
RULE 5: The vxsat CSR can also be accessed as a field within the XLEN-bit-wide vector control and status CSR named vcsr.
RULE 6: At reset, the vxsat CSR may contain any value.
RULE 7: For the vsmul.vv instruction, if the signed fractional multiply operation produces a result that saturates after the 2 × SEW product is shifted right by SEW-1 bits and rounded according to vxrm, the vxsat bit is set.
RULE 8: For the vsmul.vx instruction, if the signed fractional multiply operation produces a result that saturates after the 2 × SEW product is shifted right by SEW-1 bits and rounded according to vxrm, the vxsat bit is set.
RULE 9: The vxsat register contains a single vxsat bit.
RULE 10: The vxsat bit is set in the vxsat register whenever any destination element is saturated.
RULE 11: For the vnclipu instruction, the shifted-rounded source value is treated as an unsigned integer and the operation saturates if the result would overflow the destination viewed as an unsigned integer, and such an overflow sets the vxsat bit.
RULE 12: For the vnclip instruction, the shifted-rounded source value is treated as a signed integer and the operation saturates if the result would overflow the destination viewed as a signed integer, and such an overflow sets the vxsat bit.
RULE 13: vxsat has URW privilege, meaning it is readable and writable in user mode.
RULE 14: When the vector registers are implemented, the VS field shall not be read-only zero, therefore the vxsat CSR shall not be read-only zero.
RULE 15: If neither the vector registers nor S-mode is implemented, the VS field is read-only zero, and consequently the vxsat CSR shall be read-only zero.
RULE 16: If S-mode is implemented but the vector registers are not, the VS field may optionally be read-only zero, and therefore the vxsat CSR may optionally be read-only zero.
RULE 17: Changing the VS field has no effect on the value of the vxsat CSR.
RULE 18: In M-mode, accessing vxsat register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x009; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 19: In S-mode, accessing vxsat register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x009; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 20: In U-mode, accessing vxsat register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x009; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 21: In M-mode, setting vxsat.VALUE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x009, a0; csrr a1, 0x009; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 22: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the vxsat register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x009, a0; csrr a1, 0x009; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 23: In M-mode, accessing vxsat register while V extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: V; csrr a0, 0x009; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
